stream-event.name: Stream Event
stream-event.description: Typed Decodable model of the claude --output-format stream-json NDJSON event stream (system/init, system task_started/task_progress/task_updated/task_notification, assistant, user/tool_result, result) — unknown shapes degrade to .unknown rather than throwing. System events route by subtype — task_* subtypes decode into SystemTaskEvent (task lifecycle), all others into SystemInit. SystemTaskEvent decodes the RICH (VERIFIED via live CLI raw capture, 2026-06) task fields — probes id/status/command/output/output_file/tool_use_id/parent_tool_use_id/task_type/description/subagent_type/prompt + the usage block (total_tokens/tool_uses/duration_ms) across flat + nested objects (patch carries task_updated {status,end_time}; usage carries task_notification metrics) — and keeps the full raw JSONValue (logged at debug). CRITICAL — task_* events cover BOTH background bash shells (task_type "local_bash") AND Agent/Task sub-agents (task_type "local_agent"); they emit identical shapes, so task_type is the DETERMINISTIC typing discriminator and tool_use_id is the DETERMINISTIC correlation key consumers use to split bash shells (#atrium-shells) from the sub-agent CHORUS (#sub-agent /

atrium-stop.name: Atrium Stop
atrium-stop.description: Stop control for the ATRIUM composer (#atrium-thread). Visible/enabled ONLY while the agent is mid-turn (status .running/.starting), coral/blocked-tinted stop.fill glyph beside Send. On click calls ClaudeStreamSession.interrupt(), which writes the stream-json CONTROL protocol line {"type":"control_request","request_id":"<uuid>","request":{"subtype":"interrupt"}} to the SAME claude stdin (does NOT close stdin). VERIFIED: the bare {"type":"interrupt"} line is IGNORED (a count-to-600 turn ran to completion); the control_request form halts the active turn (count stopped at 124) and emits {"type":"control_response","response":{"subtype":"success","request_id":"<same>"}} confirming it landed, then the turn ends with a terminal result subtype error_during_execution. The session stays alive; the next user turn is answered normally. interrupt() stops the in-flight caret immediately and tracks the pending request_id; applyControlResponse logs confirmation; applyResult settles status to .idle and treats the interrupt-initiated error_during_execution as a normal 'stopped' (NOT a scary error), with the silence watchdog as backstop. Logged under !claude-interrupt (e.g. 'interrupt control_request sent id=…', 'interrupt CONFIRMED — control_response success').

atrium-shells.name: Atrium Shells
atrium-shells.description: Background-shell inspector for the ATRIUM window. Background shells are commands the agent ran with run_in_background; Claude Code does NOT kill them on session exit (they orphan to PID 1), so the host tracks and reaps them. DETECTION: ClaudeStreamSession parses tool_result text 'Command running in background with ID: <id>' AND 'Output is being written to: <ABSOLUTE>.output' (correlating the command from the matching Bash tool_use id recorded in applyAssistant) AND/OR the system task_started/task_progress/task_updated/task_notification events (task_started gives early registration via task_id + tool_use_id correlation + description; task_updated carries patch.status); results upsert into @Published backgroundShells [BackgroundShell {id, command, startedAt, status running/finished/stopped/killed/failed, lastOutput, outputFile}]. SUB-AGENT FILTER (DETERMINISTIC, task_type-first): task_* events are emitted by BOTH background bash shells (task_type 'local_bash') AND Agent/Task sub-agents (task_type 'local_agent') with identical shapes — only REAL bash shells belong in this panel. On task_started for an untracked id, applySystemTask types by task_type: 'local_agent' routes to the CHORUS (#sub-agent), 'local_bash' admits to this panel; the originating tool_use name (traced via tool_use_id → toolNamesByToolUseId, recorded for EVERY tool_use in applyAssistant) is a FALLBACK only when task_type is absent (older CLI). A present-but-contradicting signal (task_type != local_bash, or fallback tool == 'Agent'/'Task') EXCLUDES the task (logged: 'ignoring non-bash task <id> type=<…> tool=<…>'). The temporal-adjacency FIFO is RETIRED. task_progress is a NON-TERMINAL running heartbeat (the model emits many per task) and is NEVER treated as terminal; only EXPLICIT terminal statuses (killed/stopped/failed/error/finished/completed/success/done/exited) move a shell out of .running — every other value (including empty/absent and progress-ish strings) stays running (the old 'unrecognized non-empty status → failed' rule was removed so progress can't falsely fail a live shell). There are NO pid files (verified) — only the .output file. UI: a right-aligned header button in AtriumThreadView shows a live count/'N live' and opens a popover (AtriumShellsPanel) listing each shell — command (mono, middle-truncated), id, status badge, startedAt, output, and [Inspect]/[Kill] actions; empty state when none. INSPECT (FIX 3, host-side): reads the shell's .output file directly via String(contentsOfFile:), stores it on the shell, and expands the row to a scrollable detail — NO message sent to the agent, NO thread mutation. KILL (FIX B, authoritative): the PRIMARY path is now a SUPPRESSED control turn (ConversationMessage.isControl 'Call the KillShell tool with shell_id <id>…') written to claude's stdin but EXCLUDED from the rendered thread by AtriumThreadView's filter — the agent owns the real task→PID mapping so it kills the CORRECT process. Status is NOT optimistically flipped (the old lsof-on-.output primary killed the file-writer wrapper, the WRONG PID, and LIED 'killed' while the real process lived → later exit 144/SIGURG); instead the real task_updated/task_notification patch.status (→killed/stopped) or the KillShell tool_result drives the panel status so it never lies. A non-authoritative best-effort host SIGTERM via `lsof -t -- <output_file>` remains only as a backstop and never sets the visible status. EXIT CLEANUP: shutdown() best-effort reaps the claude process tree BEFORE terminating claude — collectDescendants via pgrep -P, SIGTERM then SIGKILL survivors after a 300ms grace — preventing the orphan leak. Heavy ConductorLog under !background-shell (detection, raw task payloads, inspect/kill, lsof PIDs, reap).

conversation-model.name: Conversation Model
conversation-model.description: Observable projection of the stream-json event sequence into renderable ConversationMessage values (agent/user/system authors) with ToolCall chips (running/succeeded/failed) and an isControl flag for suppressed host→agent control turns (the authoritative KillShell control turn,

claude-stream-session.name: Claude Stream Session
claude-stream-session.description: @MainActor ObservableObject owning ONE headless claude process speaking stream-json over stdin/stdout. SPAWN ENVIRONMENT (FIX 1): because Conductor is a Finder-launched GUI/bundled app, it inherits a MINIMAL PATH; the spawned claude would fail to find node/paradigm/hooks (exit 127). loginShellEnvironment() runs the user's login+interactive shell (`$SHELL -lic env`, cached once) and overlays its full environment (PATH + nvm/asdf/homebrew exports) onto the child's environment, with a hardcoded-PATH fallback if the probe fails; the resolved child PATH is logged at startup under #claude-stream-session. Decodes the NDJSON OFF the main thread via a Sendable LineFramer in the readabilityHandler, then hops to @MainActor to project events into the conversation model. Buffers the first turn until system/init; keeps stdin open between turns. Traces every applied event type (system/systemTask/assistant/user/result/unknown) and surfaces claude stderr to ConductorLog so stalls/errors are visible. A silence watchdog settles the UI out of .running if a result is missed (caret off, status idle), and applyResult flips status to idle + records cumulative total_cost_usd and authoritative end-of-turn usage. interrupt() (#atrium-stop) writes the stream-json CONTROL protocol line {"type":"control_request","request_id":"<uuid>","request":{"subtype":"interrupt"}} to the SAME stdin (NOT closed) to halt the active turn while keeping the session alive — the bare {"type":"interrupt"} form is VERIFIED IGNORED. Decodes control_response (applyControlResponse confirms the matching request_id) and settles the interrupt-initiated terminal result (subtype error_during_execution) cleanly as a normal stop, logging under !claude-interrupt. Tracks background shells (#atrium-shells) in @Published backgroundShells by parsing tool_result 'Command running in background with ID: <id>' + 'Output is being written to: <path>' (command correlated from the Bash tool_use id) and system task events; inspectShell reads the .output file host-side; killShell (FIX B) uses the AUTHORITATIVE path — a SUPPRESSED isControl KillShell control turn so the agent kills the correct PID via its task→PID mapping (the old lsof-on-output-file primary targeted the file-writer wrapper, killed the wrong PID, and LIED 'killed' while the process lived) — status is NOT optimistically flipped; the real task_updated/task_notification (patch.status) or KillShell tool_result drives the panel; a non-authoritative best-effort host SIGTERM via lsof remains only as a backstop. shutdown() reaps the claude process tree (pgrep -P → SIGTERM/SIGKILL) before terminating claude to prevent orphan-to-PID-1 leaks.

atrium-theme.name: Atrium Theme
atrium-theme.description: Deep mono visual token system for the ATRIUM thread (void/surface/sunken surfaces, ink, amber/user/tool/running/blocked accents, monospaced body/chip/footer fonts) plus a Color(hex:) initializer.

atrium-thread.name: Atrium Thread
atrium-thread.description: Custom SwiftUI thread surface — a thin top header carrying the background-shell inspector affordance (#atrium-shells), a scrolling conversation pinned to bottom, agent turns with blinking amber caret + collapsible tool chips, right-aligned user capsules, reply composer (ALWAYS editable/focusable — never hard-disabled by session status; Send gated only on live-session + non-empty draft, so a stuck-running turn can never lock the founder out; mid-turn sends queue on claude stdin; a coral Stop button (#atrium-stop) appears beside Send while the agent is mid-turn), and a model·session·tokens·cost footer. THE CHORUS (#atrium-chorus): the body is an HStack of a conversation COLUMN + the right-side CHORUS RAIL using a PUSH layout — when ≥1 sub-agent is live (or the rail is pinned) the column narrows to make room and the rail slides in over 220ms ease (no overlay); it slides away when all sub-agents idle. The conversation column also renders the INLINE FAN-OUT block (#atrium-chorus) after the messages when subAgents is non-empty. Hosted in AtriumSpikeWindow (single-owner of its ClaudeStreamSession), launched from the menu bar — the window is resizable/zoomable/full-screen-capable (collectionBehavior .fullScreenPrimary) with a larger 1100x780 default, built toward the full-screen Conductor.

atrium-chorus.name: Atrium Chorus
atrium-chorus.description: THE CHORUS — sub-agents (#sub-agent) rendered as a chorus of parallel voices, across TWO surfaces over the same @Published subAgents data. SURFACE 1, the INLINE FAN-OUT block (AtriumFanOutBlock): born in the conversation when the model fans out, lists the spawned voices grouped, settles to a one-line summary ('✓ N sub-agents · 2m14s · ▸ expand') when all idle, and lives in history. SURFACE 2, the CHORUS RAIL (AtriumChorusRail): a right-side panel that AUTO-APPEARS while ≥1 sub-agent is live, SLIDES AWAY when all idle, and is PINNABLE (a pin control keeps it open when idle); the conversation column narrows to make room (PUSH layout, 220ms ease, no overlay). ROW ANATOMY (AtriumChorusRow, shared by both surfaces) — prose over mechanics: [state glyph] + TASK DESCRIPTION (system font, ink, leads) + subagent_type (mono, inkMuted, subtitle) + heartbeat SPARKLINE (Canvas, driven by real task_progress ticks) + elapsed (mono, right, ticking via a shared TimelineView clock). TEMPERATURE LAW (founder-baked): running = teal #4ED7A0 (autonomous work needs NO attention — never amber), completed/killed/stopped = inkMuted, failed = coral #FF6B6B, amber #F2B765 ONLY for needsHuman (a sub-agent blocked on the founder; v2 — not yet detected); blue #7CC4FF left-edge = drill/selection focus. SETTLED ROW + DRILL-IN: a settled row shows the status label plus real usage from the terminal task_notification ('done · 12.2k tok · 1.4s'); the inline fan-out summary aggregates tokens across the voices. Clicking a rail row expands it IN PLACE — drill-in shows description + subagent_type + status + elapsed + tokens/tool-uses/duration + the sub-agent prompt + live last-activity. Full nested per-tool transcript is still v2 (interleaved sub-agent tool calls don't yet carry parent_tool_use_id) and is NOT faked. STOP: a rail row's Stop sends a suppressed isControl TaskStop turn (reuses #atrium-shells sendControl); status reflects the real task_updated/notification, not optimistic.

sub-agent.name: Sub Agent
sub-agent.description: Observable record of a sub-agent the model spawned via the Agent/Task tool for parallel work (THE CHORUS, #atrium-chorus). SubAgent {id (taskId), description, subagentType, status (running/completed/stopped/killed/failed/needsHuman), startedAt, endedAt, lastActivity, progressTicks (sparkline heartbeats), originatingToolUseId, prompt, totalTokens, toolUses, durationMs; usageSummary computed → '12.2k tok · 1.4s'}. TYPING + CORRELATION ARE DETERMINISTIC (corrected 2026-06 from the earlier wrong temporal-adjacency conclusion): task_* events carry task_type ('local_agent' → sub-agent; 'local_bash' → bash shell) AND tool_use_id (ties the task to the EXACT spawning Agent tool_use) — the temporal-adjacency FIFO is RETIRED. POPULATION (ClaudeStreamSession @Published subAgents): an Agent/Task tool_use in applyAssistant caches description/subagent_type/prompt in agentSpawnsByToolUseId keyed by tool_use_id (FALLBACK only). applySystemTask routes a task to the chorus instead of the shells panel (#atrium-shells) when task_type == 'local_agent' (or, on an old CLI with no task_type, the originating tool is Agent/Task). applySubAgentTask populates the SubAgent DIRECTLY from the task_started fields (description + subagent_type + prompt — all on the event), sets originatingToolUseId from the event's tool_use_id, appends a sparkline tick per task_progress, updates lastActivity, captures usage (total_tokens/tool_uses/duration_ms) from the terminal task_notification via applyUsage, and freezes the sub-agent (endedAt) on terminal task_updated/notification. STATUS: 'completed' maps to .completed → muted ✓ (terminal SUCCESS, distinct from .killed/.stopped/.failed). parent_tool_use_id is still probed for forward-compat (interleaved sub-agent tool-call attribution → full nested drill-in, v2). subAgentTaskIds is sticky so signal-less follow-up events stay routed to the chorus. stopSubAgent sends a suppressed isControl TaskStop turn (authoritative; real status drives the UI). Bash shells (#atrium-shells) stay a SEPARATE list.

atrium-attachment.name: Atrium Attachment
atrium-attachment.description: Removable file-attachment chip for the ATRIUM composer — file-type SF Symbol + middle-truncated filename + ✕ remove, styled to the ATRIUM palette (surfaceRaised bg, tool-violet icon, mono ink filename). Files dragged onto the composer (.onDrop of .fileURL) become chips in a row above the field; on send the absolute paths are appended to the outgoing claude -p turn as a trailing "Attached files:" block so the agent can Read them, while the visible draft stays clean.

atrium-voice.name: Atrium Voice
atrium-voice.description: Keyword-driven voice dictation loop for the ATRIUM composer, modeled on a-aloud's reply-window loop. REUSES WhisperVoiceProvider (WhisperKit CoreML STT + AVCaptureSession mic) — no new STT dependency. Mic-button path AUTHORIZES FIRST — checks AVCaptureDevice.authorizationStatus(for:.audio), on .notDetermined awaits requestAccess (fires the TCC prompt; Info.plist has NSMicrophoneUsageDescription), on .denied/.restricted surfaces a `blocked` state whose next click opens System Settings › Privacy › Microphone — THEN loads the WhisperKit model (`loading` state) and starts continuous capture. State machine off→requesting→loading→armed→composing→sending→armed (+blocked) driven by forgiving word-boundary-anchored keyword grammar (normalize, last-occurrence match, multi-word phrases). Keywords are USER-CONFIGURABLE in Settings › Input › "Voice Composer (ATRIUM)" and persist in UserDefaults (atriumWakeKeyword / atriumSendKeyword / atriumCancelKeywords — cancel is a comma-separated list); they are re-read fresh at each arm (loadAndArm → refreshKeywordsFromDefaults) so a Settings change takes effect on the next arm. Defaults (seeds + fallbacks) wake="respond", send="send it", cancel="scratch that, never mind, nevermind". Uses its OWN WhisperVoiceProvider instance — fully decoupled from the orchestrator's global `voiceEnabled` pref, so the explicit mic-button action starts regardless of that setting. Live transcript streams into the composer's NSTextView via the

atrium-textview.name: Atrium Textview
atrium-textview.description: Custom NSViewRepresentable (AtriumTextView) wrapping an NSTextView subclass (AtriumNSTextView) in an NSScrollView — the ATRIUM composer's reply input. REPLACES the SwiftUI TextField that failed at runtime inside the manually-created AtriumSpikeWindow (NSHostingView in a bare NSWindow on an LSUIElement accessory app), where clipboard (⌘C/V/X) and .onKeyPress(.return) did not route. Clipboard/undo handled directly in performKeyEquivalent(with:) (menu-independent guarantee); Return-vs-Shift+Return handled by overriding insertNewline(_:) (plain Return → onSubmit callback, no newline; Shift+Return → real newline). Multiline, grows to ~6 lines then scrolls. ATRIUM styling (surface bg, ink text, monospaced 13, amber insertion point + selection). Two-way bound to the composer's draft via a Coordinator (textDidChange → binding); imperative AtriumTextViewHandle exposes appendText/clear/focus for the voice dictation path. A standard Edit menu is also registered via .commands in ConductorApp.swift as belt-and-suspenders.

gnomon-contracts.name: Gnomon Contracts
gnomon-contracts.description: Package entry (src/index.ts, re-exports every module) plus schemas/. probeResult:v1 = {probe, os, osVersion, arch, toolVersions{node,...}, verdict pass|fail|partial, evidence{}, specRefs[], at}; schemas/probeResult.v1.schema.json is its JSON Schema, src/probe-result.ts the TS type plus validateProbeResultV1 / isProbeResultV1. The PR-3 schemas in schemas/ are GENERATED from src/schemas.ts (`npm run schemas`, scripts/write-schemas.mjs) and a test keeps them a byte-identical fixed point. src/internal.ts holds the shared pure helpers (Checker with strict|tolerant modes, UTF-8, synchronous SHA-256, Crockford base32, canonical JSON, deepFreeze). Also home (no allowlisted sub-component yet; spec Appendix A has no node) of the M1.1-reserved (P8-D86–D88, §4.11) schemas: src/change-note.ts = change-note:v1 — agentClaims{testedHow{summary ≤1 KiB, refs[]}, risk{tier low|medium|high, why ≤512 B, blast[sym:]}, revert{how auto|command|manual, steps ≤1 KiB never executed, reversible}, draftedBy} UNTRUSTED and kept structurally apart from kernel{verified{n, of}, risk{floor, effective, reasons[]}, revert{how auto|none, ref?}} (B16); validateChangeNoteV1 needs an explicit form (no default): claim (contract.claim{note}: agentClaims only, a kernel part refused in every mode) or card (kernel required; strict: effective = max(floor, agent tier)); schemas/change-note.v1.schema.json publishes both as $defs/claim (kernel: false) and $defs/card, with x-gnomon-trust per part; failSafe* readings and changeNoteHasUnknownValue. src/review-finding.ts = review-finding:v1 {fid, round >= 1, class, severity important|nit|pre-existing (kernel-set), locus{path, lines?, symbol?}, instances[], claim, fingerprint}; `lines` = "n" or "from-to" (spec gives no grammar; judgment call); FINDING_RESPONSES fixed|wrong| intentional|immaterial + validateFindingResponses for contract.claim{responses}; schemas/review-finding.v1.schema.json. Tiers, hows, severities and responses are ADDITIVE with fail-safe readings (unknown tier ⇒ high, agent revert how ⇒ manual, kernel revert how ⇒ none, severity ⇒ important, response ⇒ no answer; round-2 ruling). They serve #approval-broker and ^certified convergence. M1.12 slice 1 (§4.5, §4.9, §9.1, §12.8), additive and NOT inputs to clientApiId (pin unchanged): src/display.ts = sanitizeDisplayText (the client-side §4.5 rules as amended by Aegis round 2 and M1.12 slice 2: a terminated OSC/DCS/SOS/PM/APC shown as ⟨OSC⟩payload⟨ST⟩ (payload visible, Aegis M2), CSI and other ESC sequences removed, an unterminated ESC shown as ⟨ESC⟩ with its tail visible; zero-width, tag, VS-supplement and filler characters stripped, misplaced U+FE00–FE0F (decided on the output, never after a mark) stripped, a kept U+FE00–FE0D flagged (only VS15/VS16 silent), U+2028/2029 ⇒ \n, all ⇒ hidden-chars; bidi controls and marks ⇒ visible glyphs ⇒ bidi; remaining C0/C1 removed ⇒ hidden-chars, CR unflagged; lone surrogates ⇒ U+FFFD; no normalisation; text idempotent, flags idempotent except that a kept U+FE00–FE0D re-flags hidden-chars; display.v1.json normative), eventRow (opaque {kind, principal, at} rows for modns.* and kinds newer than the package), renderDenominator ({n, of} or refused); src/conformance.ts = the conformance catalog (CONFORMANCE_CHECKS, run vs slice-2), the display vectors (conformance/display.v1.json, generated by `npm run conformance`, fixed point) and conformanceReportHash; src/client-types.ts = TYPE-ONLY params/results of the 12 verbs + 2 relays. M1.12 slice 3: src/client-api-doc.ts = renderClientApiDoc(), a pure render of the published surface (ids, verbs + access, relays, refusal codes + reasons, additive enums, kinds, schema files, kit, sanitizer sets, conformance catalog) into docs/specs/gnomon-client-api.md — generated by `npm run client-api-doc`, never hand-maintained; the committed file is its byte-identical fixed point (G-HON-04 rule, LF on every OS via .gitattributes); not an input to clientApiId (pin unchanged).

contract-event-v1.name: Contract Event V1
contract-event-v1.description: event:v1 envelope (§4.1) — P8-D98 (T-2026-10-19-001): reserves, tag 8.0:P8-D98, session.drained{uuid, reason} (DRAIN_REASONS = [upgrade], closed), permit.reattributed{permitId, hsid, drainedEventId, renewedByDrain:true, expiresAt} (founder carry-over ruling: a permit live at the drain gets a fresh window, never minted), approval.rule.revoked{ruleId, repoKey, tool, connId} and approval.effect.failed{cardId, decision, effect, reason}, each with a closed payload check (validateKindPayload; an extra field is refused, an unchecked kind is an error); reserved payload fields contract.claimed claimGen, approval.rule.learned match (ALWAYS_RULE_MATCHES = [exact], validateAlwaysRuleMatch, TD-2026-10-19-528 F2) and approval.expire why. Drain-and-resume (T-2026-10-19-014 B1/B2, Aegis M1 G-HON): reserved session.open resume{drainedEventId, outcome} + principalClass, session.sandbox resumedFrom/drainOutcome/note/drainedEventId, session.inject deadlineMs/deadlineSource/failed, session.refused resume; closed sets DRAIN_OUTCOMES, DRAIN_EXIT_REASONS [drain-clean, drain-interrupted], DRAIN_INJECT_CHANNELS [drain], DRAIN_DEADLINE_SOURCES, SANDBOX_D98_PHASES [resume-note], RESUME_NOTES, RESUME_REFUSALS — all in D98_CLOSED_VALUES. P8-D93 (T-2026-10-18-016): kernel-owned session.compacted{hsid, turn, reason, summaryHash, tokensBefore, tokensAfter} (summaryHash a sensitive field), KIND_PAYLOADS (published as x-gnomon-kind-payloads) and validateSessionCompactedPayload. P8-D89 (M1.4): reserves daemon.log.quarantined (evidencePath a sensitive field) and adds key.token.revoked{tokenId}, tag M1.4:P8-D89. EventV1 type, validateEventV1/isEventV1 (strict = registered kind + closed fields; tolerant = unknown kinds and fields accepted, opaqueEventView renders {kind, principal, at}), schemas/event.v1.schema.json. The kind registry EVENT_KINDS (§9.1, owner kernel|userland, M1.1 reservations tagged M1.1:P8-D58 / M1.1:P8-R9 / M1.1:P8-D86-D88 — the last: approval.strictness.raised| proposed|lowered|held, approval.mode.set, approval.auto, contract.review.returned|capped|extended|restarted, merge.reverted, merge.ref.rewritten, verdict.incident, request.strictness.set|mode.set| incident, all kernel-owned, private + normal) with RESERVED_PAYLOAD_FIELDS (oracle.result round/range/findings, contract.knot reopenOf, contract.built note/responses, verdict.founder override, session.inject briefId/peerRootKeyId, session.tainted taint), SESSION_TAINTS and APPROVAL_SUSPECT_REASONS (voice-* and strictness-class), and per-kind default labels: audience private, sensitivity per §9.1 (session.inject, turn.event, voice.turn.* sensitive; voice.enrol secret; field labels approval.request.tool_input and oracle.result.evidence sensitive). defaultLabelsFor(kind) returns undefined for an unregistered kind so the kernel refuses rather than guesses (S32 §6, L6, G-LOG-09 contract half). Serves #kernel-log and ~ample-internal-logs.

contract-project-hue.name: Contract Project Hue
contract-project-hue.description: The ONE project-hue function (critique 2026-10-20 S2.1): projectHue(key) = sha256(utf8(key))[0] mod PROJECT_HUES (6), the six pigments of design-system.yaml gnomon.colour. The kernel's Workshop feed (modhost/feed.ts session.open project) and the GUI's sessions rail both call it with the session.open cwd, so a project never gets two hues. A project hue is identity only, never state. Pure (in-house sha256), so it runs in the browser bundle too.

contract-workshop-cap.name: Contract Workshop Cap
contract-workshop-cap.description: The Workshop cap (critique 2026-10-20 S5.3): a closed, minimal shape a mod may put on a kit Text node, {shape tall|wide|floppy, hue 0..PROJECT_HUES-1, filled bool, state needs|working|idle|knot, label 1..40 code points, one line}. checkCap refuses any unknown, missing, mistyped or out-of-range field and returns a fresh five-key object. The kernel mod-block gate (modhost/block.ts) and the GUI renderer both call it; a client draws the hat from these fields only (no mod SVG, path, colour or attribute). Not an input to kitId, modAbiId or clientApiId.

contract-ids.name: Contract Ids
contract-ids.description: Ids (§4.2, §3.1, S32-13) — ULID (ulid, monotonicUlidFactory with in-ms increment and overflow refusal, isUlid, ulidTime) over globalThis.crypto.getRandomValues; prefixed ULID ids ev/log/conn/card/arm/ permit:v1/brief/msg/ds (mintId, isId); hsid:v1 (mintHsid, non-monotonic so hsid-short stays fully random), hsid:v1d derivation (deriveHsidV1d), hsid-short = lowercase Crockford of the ULID's 80 random bits, 16 chars (hsidShort); turn ids turn:<hsid>/<n> (turnId, parseTurnId); keyId, repo-scope and contract-id patterns. Serves #identity.

contract-principal.name: Contract Principal
contract-principal.description: Principals (§3.1, S32-02, P8-D75) — PRINCIPAL_KINDS human|agent|session| kernel|mod|voice|peer; p:<ns>/<name> and the foreign display form p:<ns>/<name>@<rootKeyId8> (parsePrincipalId marks it foreign, never local); samePrincipal compares full rootKeyId + name and never ns; isLocalPrincipal, foreignDisplayId, nsFromRootPublicKey, peerKernelPrincipal. Also the closed-kind row vocabularies of §3.1/§15.4: REGISTRY_ROW_KINDS (kernel, link), GRANT_ROW_KINDS (incl. reserved grant.voice-approvals, grant.peer), CAPABILITY_FORMS (incl. log.read:usage, the #mod-host usage feed grant, Aegis M1; paradigm.read:summary, the #paradigm-context-mod slice grant, K1) and FIRST_PARTY_ONLY_CAPABILITIES (link:send, knowledge:federate), GRANT_DERIVED_ONLY_CAPABILITIES (voice.approve:<class>) — not clientApiId inputs. Serves #identity and #peer-link (G-ID-08 contract half).

contract-ref-v1.name: Contract Ref V1
contract-ref-v1.description: ref:v1 grammar (§4.4, §3.7, §3.9) — scheme ":" id ["@" rev]; kernel and package scheme lists, peer reserved (M1.1, P8-R9), voice dropped; aliases # $ ^ ! ~ → sym:, TD-/L-/T- → td:/l:/t:; parseRef, formatRef, peerRef (peer:<logId>/<ref>, never nested), validateRefV1, schemas/ref.v1.schema.json. Serves #ref-resolver.

contract-refusal-v1.name: Contract Refusal V1
contract-refusal-v1.description: refusal:v1 Gnomon superset (§4.6) — P8-D89 (M1.4 slice 3) registers the read-token reasons (unknown-token, token-expired, token-revoked, token-in-use, token-not-yet-valid, token-store-untrusted), gone, the log.append ownership reasons (kernel-owned, ungranted, modns-not-own, bad-kind, bad-params), the slice-2 log.read / ref.resolve reasons (follow-needs-id, backlog-too-large, bad-since/until/limit/follow/kinds/ scope, since-ahead, subscription-cap, mod-principal-name, reader-unsupported, bad-ref, rev-not-applicable, unknown-scheme, peer-ref, no-resolver, not-found, row-integrity, closed) and CLIENT_LOCAL_REFUSAL_REASONS (hello-not-offered); log.append's verb refusals gain ENGINE. copied (not imported) from packages/warpline/src/fabric/refusal.ts: Warpline's 12 codes + BUDGET_DENIED, PERMIT_REQUIRED, CAS_LOST, BILLING_REFUSED, MODEL_UNAVAILABLE; gates + budget, billing, model, voice, link, and reserved review, strictness (P8-D86–D88); Retriability; next[] steps; verdict and contested[].rule widened to string|null; optional additive data{reason, offered, cardId}; voice and link reason lists (M1.1); reserved review-cap, strictness-presence|paused|mode|evidence, voice-strictness, note-missing with RESERVED_REASON_ROUTES naming each one's code and gate; SOCKET_REASON_ROUTES for the reasons the M1.4 kernel socket emits; exit codes and the JSON-RPC code map (§4.9); refuse() single constructor, refusalOf() accessor (+ the JSON-RPC error depth), RefusedError, validateRefusalV1, schemas/refusal.v1.schema.json. G-CON-02 partial: every Warpline-shaped refusal validates. P8-D98 (T-2026-10-19-001): D98_REASON_ROUTES reserve CAS_LOST stale-claim | claim-expired | claim-superseded (§7.4), BAD_REQUEST cursor-epoch (§5 log.read) and ENGINE draining (§2.4 rule 11), all in REFUSAL_REASONS.

contract-card-v1.name: Contract Card V1
contract-card-v1.description: card:v1 (§3.4, §14.7, §3.9) — P8-D98 (T-2026-10-19-001): kind daemon-stop (TD-2026-10-19-528 F3), CARD_EXPIRY_WHYS incl. session-drained (F4), decisionSig v2 layout (decisionMessageV2, first line DECISION_SIG_V2_MARKER gnomon:decision:v2, used for answer, carries the answer digest; the kernel signer adopts it in slice A2). Kinds incl. reserved voice-arm, grant, handoff, declassify, peer-pair, reconsider, strictness, incident; states incl. held; flags incl. voice-phrase, peer, irreversible, claim-mismatch; decisions incl. withdraw, extend, restart (reconsider cards only); fields note (change-note:v1, card form) and strictness{level L0-L3, mode manual|ask|auto-edits, reason} — level and mode ADDITIVE with fail-safe readings (unknown level ⇒ L3, mode ⇒ manual; no bypass mode); hasUnknownFailSafeValue ⇒ the card renders but is never decidable; strict producer checks: extend/restart (also as heldDecision) only on reconsider, claim-mismatch flag when agent tier < floor, irreversible flag when reversible:false (G-CHG-01/04); ROOT_CONFIG_RESERVED_SECTIONS; presence incl. voice-armed; via incl. voice, link; voice / voiceDecision blocks; signature domains gnomon:approve:v1 and gnomon:approve-voice:v1; CARD_RESERVED_VALUES; isCardDecidable (unknown state never decidable, held only withdraws); validateCardV1, schemas/card.v1.schema.json. Serves #approval-broker, ^voice-armed and ^peer-paired.

contract-gnomon-rpc-v1.name: Contract Gnomon Rpc V1
contract-gnomon-rpc-v1.description: gnomon-rpc:v1 (§4.9, §5, §12.3) — hello params/result types and validators, auth preimage helpers (authServerMessage / authClientMessage / authTokenMessage + their *Preimage forms, all binding the negotiated clientApi + canonical features; no unbound form; AUTH_TOKEN_DOMAIN gnomon:auth-token:v1 for read-token proof of possession — M1.4 slice 3, T-2026-10-17-017, P8-D89a); hello clientNonce (T-2026-10-18-016, P8-D93): HelloParams.clientNonce required (CLIENT_NONCE_PATTERN, base64url 22..86 chars, CLIENT_NONCE_BYTES = 32), echoed in HelloResult.clientNonce and bound into authServerMessage(nonce, clientNonce, endpointPath, negotiated) so a recorded hello cannot be replayed to another connection; client-local reason client-nonce-mismatch; negotiateHello (highest shared version, feature intersection, UNSUPPORTED{data:{offered[]}}); the frozen VERBS (12, with params, refusals and the §5 access matrix incl. the all-refused peer column; session.open runMode?, contract.claim note? / responses? + BAD_REQUEST, oracle.run FORBIDDEN per v3.9) and CLIENT_RELAYS (mod.view, mod.command); VERB_PARAM_VALUES, RESERVED_CONTENT_PARTS ({brief}), STATUS_RESERVED_FIELDS (links, strictness, review, unobservedRefWrites) and FAIL_SAFE_VALUES (in clientApiId); ADDITIVE_ENUMS + renderEnumValue implement the compatible-additive rule; schemas/gnomon-rpc.v1.hello.schema.json. P8-D98 (T-2026-10-19-001): HUMAN_DEVICE_VERBS gui.open{cwdHint?} (13) and rules.revoke{ruleId} (14) — human class only, access 'verified human device', every other class false; not among law 3's twelve kernel verbs; CLIENT_METHODS is 16; RESERVED_HELLO_FEATURES (journal.cursor, session.resume; the kernel advertises none until built); LogReadCursor {logId, seq} + validateLogReadCursor; D98_CLOSED_VALUES (always-rule match, drain reason); ADDITIVE_ENUMS gains approval.expire.why. Serves #socket and #web-endpoint.

contract-client-api-id.name: Contract Client Api Id
contract-client-api-id.description: kitId and clientApiId (§12.3, §12.8). TD-2026-10-20-086 F6 + T-2026-10-20-007 (one deliberate move) moved clientApiId sha256:ac22e72f26b673fae096b0495563c0c8029c8d37f9572526a1965b51eb0447e4 → sha256:795b342598244417473a3a8e77eb0ed5fea066ec337ce60511884f644ae6d63f: grant.standing / .used / .revoked, request.grant.standing / .revoke, approval.unlock.joined (Aegis M1; final id after the Aegis fold-ins below), approval.auto.miss (sensitive; why + inputHash sensitive), approval.auto{anchoredInputHash} (sensitive field), STANDING_TUPLES, STANDING_REVOKE_REASONS, STANDING_PRESENCE_PREFIX, STANDING_GRANT_MAX_MS (descriptor standingGrant); modAbiId unchanged (test/standing-grant.test.ts). TD-2026-10-19-063 (self-update pickup, founder ruling "ONE Touch ID", a deliberate move) moved clientApiId sha256:99d5c152…97d1 → sha256:ac22e72f26b673fae096b0495563c0c8029c8d37f9572526a1965b51eb0447e4 (AUTH_WIRE_DESCRIPTOR gains `resume`: the {resumeToken} web form, the gui.resume notification, its TTL, single use, via 'resume' and its refusals). Before it, TD-2026-10-19-194 (voice V0, founder ruling, the one deliberate voice move before any client ships) moved clientApiId sha256:f27ecb8b…11a4 → sha256:99d5c1527bbbfadd7dca9cfa115e3fbaca227029cecd44c95843a86eb08197d1 (descriptor gains voiceClosedValues = VOICE_CLOSED_VALUES: approval.voice.disarm.reason and refusal.voice-strictness.ceiling [null-level, manual]; statusFields gain arms, armCustody); kitId, modAbiId and abiId unchanged. P8-D98 (T-2026-10-19-001) moved clientApiId once (re-moved inside the same unreleased move for the drain-and-resume wire, Aegis M1, and once more for the #trace-capture wire, TD-2026-10-19-057 / Aegis M5: session.sandbox{traced, traceRefused} reserved, closedValues session.sandbox.traceRefused [trace-unsafe, trace-unavailable]): sha256:1faf47f5…8720 → sha256:f27ecb8b3ee5c1a4ad08d4c5eda427a63aebba8ba31963baed3c9d53e3e611a4 (descriptor gains humanDeviceVerbs — gui.open, rules.revoke and, with TD-2026-10-19-339 inside the same unreleased move, daemon.stop{reason?} with closedValues daemon.stop.reason [stop, upgrade] — helloFeatures.reserved, logReadCursor, closedValues and DECISION_SIG_DESCRIPTOR — the decisionSig v2 marker gnomon:decision:v2, its decisions [answer] and one fixed message vector); kitId and modAbiId unchanged. P8-D93 moved clientApiId once (hello clientNonce + session.compacted): sha256:fd576e6d… → sha256:1faf47f5…8720 (round 2: server-sig domain v2, closed compaction-reason enum; round 3: AUTH_WIRE_DESCRIPTOR — the three auth domains and one fixed preimage vector per auth form — is a CLIENT_API_DESCRIPTOR input, so a domain or layout change moves the id); kitId unchanged. kitId = sha256(canonicalJson(kit:v1 block list)); clientApiId = sha256(canonicalJson(CLIENT_API_DESCRIPTOR) + "\n" + kitId) where the descriptor = the 12 verbs + 2 relays, the JSON-RPC code map, ADDITIVE_ENUMS, every published client JSON Schema and the non-schema M1.1 reservations (verb param values, content parts, status fields); modAbiId is not an input. src/schemas.ts builds the schemas from the TS constants; schemas/client-api.ids.json pins the values per release.

contract-voice-allowlist.name: Contract Voice Allowlist
contract-voice-allowlist.description: The voice allowlist (spec §14.7 "The allowlist", D58, D61, D62, D66; TD-2026-10-19-194, T-2026-10-19-026 voice slice V0) — pure data plus pure functions, the AUTHORITATIVE hand-only mechanism for #gnomon-voice decisions in $voice-approval under ^voice-armed: VOICE_CLASSES reversible ⊂ gate ⊂ judgment (cumulative, as the D62 grant sets); VOICE_ALLOWLIST, one frozen row per CardKind {approve{class → decisions it adds}, deny[]}: reversible = permission allow|deny, ask-user answer, plan approve-plan; gate adds gate-class allow, fallback fallback-cloud, budget resume; judgment adds knot resolve, verdict accept|reject; deny[] = the D66 row (each kind's deny-direction decision, deny or reject, under any class, no hold; founder ruling: incident and daemon-stop have EMPTY deny rows — fully hand-only). Default deny: anything not named (incl. every unknown kind or decision) is hand-only; any card flag refuses every decision but withdraw, deny included (voice-ineligible); flags is a REQUIRED argument (Aegis M1). voiceDecisionCheck(class, kind, decision, flags) → {ok, hold, via} | {ok:false, reason voice-off|voice-class| voice-hand-only|voice-ineligible} (all reserved in refusal.ts); voiceMayDecide is its boolean form; voiceApprovingDecisions; voiceAllowlistCoversCardKinds. withdraw (undo during the hold) is ok on any kind with an approving row at any class, never blocked by flags; the caller checks state held under the same armId. Also reserved here (event.ts/rpc.ts): the closed VOICE_DISARM_REASONS (21 values, incl. daemon-exit, helper-exit) and status.arms / status.armCustody. Callers pass the EFFECTIVE class; the strictness overlay, null-level ceiling, manual-mode deny-only clamp and every runtime broker check live in #approval-broker (later voice slices). Not a clientApiId input (pin unchanged; test/voice-golden.test.ts pins the clientApiId literal, packages/gnomon/test/voice-golden.test.ts the abiId literal and that every allowlisted pair is a valid KIND_DECISIONS pair in classes.ts).

gui-model-picker.name: Gui Model Picker
gui-model-picker.description: Founder ask 2026-10-20 ("is there no way to change the model of what claude is in the tool?"). core/model-picker.ts (PURE): MODEL_CHOICES (contracts CLAUDE_MODEL_ALIASES + custom), openModelOf (route claude sends the alias/id or 'claude' for default; local/any unchanged), pickerProblem (contracts claudeModelProblem), the per-folder memory (localStorage gnomon.model.byFolder <= 64 folders + gnomon.model.last; a stored value failing the check is never restored), sessionModelOf (kernel rows only: the last session.model{outcome:switched}.to, else session.open.model), switchRequest = log.append{kind: request.session.model, payload:{hsid, model}}, switchConfirmText (the conversation continues, the prompt cache restarts, a larger model uses the plan faster; never says context is lost). ui/model-picker.ts (DOM, mounted once by app.ts): the "claude model" select + custom id field injected after #ns-model (hidden for the local route), the header chip (model + ▾ menu) after the backend in #chead-meta, the confirm sheet #model-switch-dialog that sends only once armed by a trusted click on its Switch key or a trusted Enter in its id field, recorded before the submit (Aegis L1; never the submit event's isTrusted), and the read-only Settings slot [data-gnomon-slot="session-model"]. Tests: test/model-picker.test.ts. 8.0:model-switch wiring: sessionModelOf also folds session.model{reconciled} (model = to) and {timeout} (uncertain = to, kept until reconciled, never after the session ended: a timeout before or after session.exited is not shown unconfirmed, Aegis L2); modelChipText shows "model: switching… (unconfirmed)" and disables the ▾ meanwhile; sessionModelText feeds the Settings Permissions row `session-model` (readonly, slot session-model, settings.ts SettingsInput.sessionModel); store.ts sessionModelLine writes one transcript line per outcome. Preview fixture `model-switch` (preview/fixtures.ts).

gui.name: Gui
gui.description: #gui (spec §11.1-§11.5, §4.5). #bare-entry (§2.4 rule 8): the fragment may carry an optional `cwd` folder hint (base64url UTF-8, ≤ 1024 bytes; a malformed one drops the hint, never the launch); core/launch.ts cwdHintOf escapes and caps it for display and applyCwdHint opens the new-session form, shows it as text in #ns-hint, prefills #ns-cwd only when clean and absolute, and never submits — session.open stays on the human's click (test/gui.test.ts). Aegis round 1: the hint is applied only inside attach() after the launch token verified (never on a failed attach or Reconnect); clearCwdHint on cancel, trusted submit and "+ new"; the prefill rule is the strict L/N/P/S-or-space rule minus Cf and default-ignorables, shared with the CLI via packages/gnomon/test/fixtures/cwd-hint.v1.json. static/boot.js reads the launch fragment (#launch=<token>&k=<spki>) and clears it with history.replaceState before any other script, handing it to app.js once. core/launch.ts decides the key pin (localStorage holds only the kernel public key; a changed fragment key re-pins visibly; Reconnect verifies against the pin; none ⇒ refuse); hostSurface() (T-2026-10-18-018 N1, M1.13) is 'wrapper' only for the frozen non-writable non-configurable window.gnomonSurface the #gnomon-wrapper document-start script defines (a plain browser cannot produce it under the kernel CSP), and then the page sends hello surface wrapper and hides the extension-risk badge (display only). core/server-sig.ts verifies hello.serverSig with WebCrypto Ed25519 over authServerPreimage and binds serverKeyId; each hello carries a fresh clientNonce (getRandomValues, 32 bytes) that the result must echo (client-nonce-mismatch) and the signature must cover (T-2026-10-18-016); card decision keys only for kernel-signed actions that verify. core/client.ts is a MINIMAL in-bundle gnomon-rpc:v1 client on gnomon-contracts (hello, sig check, auth {launchToken}|{reconnect}, calls, notifications, gnomonPost for POST /diag and /blob with X-Gnomon-Token and referrerPolicy same-origin; per-call timeout; id:null error frames surface as a notice + /diag; a call written and unanswered when the socket closes rejects DELIVERY_UNKNOWN{delivery-unknown}, a call after the close CLOSED{connection-closed} (B7: one client-local spelling with the kernel + TS clients), T-2026-10-19-009 item 6; setup treats both as stopped) - swapped for the published #client-ts (M1.12) in slice 2. The GUI defines NO sanitizer (Aegis C1): every string goes through gnomon-contracts sanitizeDisplayText (display.ts, tested with conformance/display.v1.json through the render path, plus a fence test); core/render.ts renders the closed kit and kernel cards as DOM TEXT NODES only (no innerHTML); a block kit.Button is not a decision key and is live only for BLOCK_SAFE_COMMANDS (never diag.send or gui.reconnect). Card decision keys only for kernel-signed actions whose keyId is the hello's serverKeyId, cached per (cardId, contentHash) and cleared when the verify key changes. A re-pin is a sticky kernel-owned notice with old/new keyIds and a /diag line. core/store.ts reduces log.read rows into sessions by project, per-hsid transcripts and the decision stack (order independent, per-project filter); core/virtual.ts is the Fenwick-tree virtualized transcript with per-width height caches; core/commands.ts the palette, layout presets and theme/motion resolution. ui/app.ts wires the page: launch, Reconnect, backlog paging + follow subscription, sessions sidebar with new session (session.open), composer (session.send), decision stack (approve on trusted gestures; an ask-user card with a verified `answer` key gets a picker built ONLY from askDetailOf: the card block's one {type:'ask-user', detail} node whose detail recomputes (with kind, requester, hsid, flags; cardContentHash) to the card's contentHash — display text is never parsed; missing/malformed/mismatched => no picker (Aegis C1); radio/checkbox per option plus a free-text field (aria-label, maxlength = detail.maxAnswerChars), askNote (null- prototype answers) builds the approve note: plain text for one question, JSON {answers} for several; a Bash permission card (TD-2026-10-20-294) splits `always` into "Always: this exact command" and one key per prefix choice, taken ONLY from prefixOptionsOf (the one {type:'bash-prefix', detail} node whose detail recomputes to the contentHash); approveParamsOf turns the clicked key's data-scope/data-prefix into approve{scope} (only for always; a malformed key sends no scope, so the exact rule); refusals shown verbatim until M1.3 presence), Shuttle view, the kernel-owned extension-risk badge, papercraft day / phosphor night / auto themes and reduced motion.

gui-setup.name: Gui Setup
gui-setup.description: #gui-setup (spec §11.1, §11.2 rule 11; T-2026-10-19-005 MVP-b) — the first-run setup screens over the #setup-endpoint's closed gnomon-setup:v1 protocol: a `#setup=<tok>&k=<spki>[&cwd=…]` fragment (core/launch.ts parseSetupFragment; never mixed with #launch=) runs src/setup instead of the app. route.ts is the state machine (welcome → preflight → name → identity 1 of 2 / 2 of 2 → success → handoff; any refusal or a closed socket → aborted); hello is verified against the fragment setup key with the launch path's verifyServerSig before auth, and that key is never stored as the kernel pin. screens.ts renders by textContent only; clicks only request steps; the page sends only the name and a server-listed gen. digest.ts: the digest is the kernel's setup.presence value, shown big and grouped; the copy says the Touch ID dialog's last line must BEGIN with `Gnomon Helper: root key signs 1: <d12>`, that exactly 2 prompts come, and that cancelling is safe.

gui-relaunch.name: Gui Relaunch
gui-relaunch.description: #gui-relaunch (T-2026-10-20-001) — a kernel restarted outside the self-update path (stop, then start) reopens the GUI with no terminal. (1) A start without a TTY opens it: printLaunch with no TTY hands the launch URL to the browser opener ONLY (osascript stdin; never printed), and `gnomon daemon start | --detach` / `gnomond` (activator) open it after a FRESH ready through cli/relaunch.ts openGuiAfterStart — the same gui.open path bare `gnomon` uses (home pin verifies the hello before the device signs; one shared launch-grant cap; single use, 60 s). `--no-open` / GNOMON_NO_OPEN=1 turn it off; `gnomond --foreground --no-open` is a usage refusal (the foreground kernel never opens anything). (2) NO remembered web port (Aegis H1, withdrawn from 945349a3): a port reused across stop/start lets a local squatter serve the old origin while Gnomon is down, so a reloaded stale tab could plant a service worker that the next auto-opened `#launch=` would load into. Every plain start binds an OS-chosen port and deletes any leftover `web-port.json` without reading it; the upgrade successor keeps its inherited fd. The stale tab cannot rejoin in place (each start has a new ephemeral key that only a launch fragment delivers); see gnomon-gui core/stale.ts.

gui-stop-speaking.name: Gui Stop Speaking
gui-stop-speaking.description: #gui Stop speaking (T-2026-10-19-026). A ⏹ "Stop speaking" button beside the mic pill (static/index.html #voice-stop), shown only for a human connection with the voice app connected (status.voice.clientConnected) and status.voice.playback.playing; a trusted click, or Esc when no menu or dialog is open and focus is not in the composer, sends ONE log.append request.voice.client{op:'stop-speaking'} (narrows: no card, no presence). core/voice.ts holds the pure decisions (playbackPlaying, stopSpeakingShown, speakPollWanted, escStopsSpeaking); app.ts re-reads status every 300 ms (SPEAK_POLL_MS) only while speech plays, plus a 4 s watch window after a voice row (playback reports are never logged, so the page cannot otherwise see a reply start).

gui-dictation.name: Gui Dictation
gui-dictation.description: #gui-dictation (TD-2026-10-20-262, T-2026-10-19-026) — voice dictation into the composer. core/dictation.ts is a PURE reducer: a live voice.turn.user row with the kernel-stamped `forwardable: true`, non-empty text, no `intercepted`/refusal, for the attached session and past the start seq (no backlog; each seq once) appends to the draft with one space. One countdown ring runs over the per-machine delay (localStorage gnomon.dictation.delayMs: 3/5/8/15 s/off, default 5 s; pill menu picks and voice.delay.* palette commands) while the draft is unheld, the voice app idle (status.voice.dictation.activity), the session not streaming, and the attached session is the GUI's focused one (else the pill says "draft waiting"); new speech, transcription, a new turn or streaming resets it to the full delay. Hold: [Hold]/[Resume], the voice app's ⌃⌥H (status.voice.dictation.holdToggles, by parity), typing in or clicking into a draft. [Send]/Enter/⌘Enter send now. The send is session.send{hsid, content: one part per turn | the edit as ONE part, source: voice}. The #gui store reads turn.sent voiceTurnSeqs (and the older voiceTurnSeq), shows 🎙 for voice and 🎙✎ for voice-edited, and a forwardable unsent turn as "in composer". Only a human-class connection (canAttach) gets these controls; a voice connection never. Aegis conditions: hold records who set it (gui | voice | detached; a voice toggle never clears a GUI-set or detached hold); no live attachment for the draft's session ⇒ held 'detached', never auto-sent; an edit while sending keeps hold and the edit; turn text is sanitized by the contracts sanitizeDisplayText (sent as the voice app's exact words only when sanitizing changed nothing); the holdToggles baseline resets per voice connection (connEpoch, else client.restarts); edited drafts echo as typed messages. TD-2026-10-20-125 (founder ruling): ambient speech NEVER auto-sends. A part whose turn's mode is not exactly 'ptt' (missing included) marks the draft ambient (ambientDraft); an ambient draft never arms the ring and only [Send]/Enter/⌘Enter sends it (note "draft · Enter sends (ambient never auto-sends)"). PTT drafts keep the countdown; the delay picks say push-to-talk.

gui-preview.name: Gui Preview
gui-preview.description: #gui-preview (DEV ONLY; never in the kernel-served bundle) - the GUI fixture preview for designers and agents. scripts/preview.mjs serves the REAL static/index.html, boot.js and styles.css on 127.0.0.1 only (default port 8790, loopback Host check) with an app.js bundled from src/preview/main.ts: the real ui/app.ts and core run over a fake kernel Transport (src/preview/fake-kernel.ts) that answers hello with a real Ed25519 serverSig from a per-page throwaway WebCrypto key, auth, status, log.read (backlog + follow), approve (emits approval.decide), log.append and session.send (no effect), and refuses session.open. Card actions are signed with the same key, so the real GUI verifies and renders the decision keys. Fixtures (src/preview/fixtures.ts: contracts LogRow chains of registered kinds plus the status result; desk, empty, voice-armed, voice-crashed, stack-heavy, workshop, spoken, choices) are chosen by URL ?fixture=&theme=day|night&motion=on|off[&surface=browser]; src/preview/env.ts stubs only the colour-scheme and reduced-motion media queries and the wrapper surface marker. The workshop fixture runs the real Workshop mod model (packages/gnomon-mods/workshop/model.mjs) over the feed projection and draws it with renderBlock. / lists every fixture x theme; --fixture-list prints the URLs. scripts/preview-shots.mjs writes <fixture>-<theme>.png at 1440x900 with Playwright or Puppeteer when one is already installed (none is added), or an installed Chrome with --chrome; otherwise it skips. Fixture paradigm-context (#paradigm-context-mod): status.mods.views lists the sidebar sheet; the fake kernel answers mod.view like the host (the GUI {focus:{hsid}} joined to a fixture K1 slice by hsid, other keys ignored) through the REAL mod model (src/preview/paradigm-context.ts), drawn by the real mod-panel path.

gui-voice-capture.name: Gui Voice Capture
gui-voice-capture.description: #gui-voice-capture (T-2026-10-20-005 A1, TD-2026-10-20-086 V3/V4) — live capture feedback. core/capture.ts is PURE: captureStatusOf is the one adapter over status.voice.capture{state, segId, reason?, level?, at} (the voice app's per-segment state, relayed by the kernel with a 5 s TTL); captureStep/captureDisplayOf give the pill words: idle keeps "Listening" / "Hold … to talk" (meter still), hearing "Hearing you…" (pulsing, the meter is the REAL level), transcribing "Catching that…", captured "Got it" (1.2 s flash), dropped the reason only for 2.5 s (no words, no count). capturePollMs is the V3 cadence (no push relay): ~1 s at rest, 175 ms while hearing or transcribing, null when off, detached, the voice app gone or disconnected; app.ts syncClientPoll runs the one attached poll at that cadence (single flight, pollStatusOnce) and stopStatusPolls clears every status poll and the flash timer on disconnect (Aegis L2 of 862ef85a). The composer ghost line "…" is its own element (#composer-ghost, never the textarea); the polite caption (#voice-caption) changes on a state change only. The decorative meter animation and row kick are gone, and the dead voice.turn.partial path is removed. B1 live words (T-2026-10-20-005, V1/V2): captureStatusOf reads capture.text{committed, tail} (hearing / transcribing only; ghostTextOf: strings only, whitespace collapsed, capped at GHOST_TEXT_MAX keeping the newest words), which the kernel projects to the human gui credential only; app.ts paintGhost puts the committed words solid (.ghost-committed) and the tail dim (.ghost-tail) as text nodes into #composer-ghost (never the textarea, so a send can never carry non-final words), "…" with no words, and clears on captured / dropped / idle. Reduced motion: the global rule makes the tail fade instant. Aegis follow-ups: a capture from a status received more than CAPTURE_STALE_MS (5 s) ago is never shown (freshCapture, page clock); a captured the kernel marks kernel:'unconfirmed' reads "Heard, not confirmed", never "Got it".

gui-offer-slip.name: Gui Offer Slip
gui-offer-slip.description: The Desk's margin slip (TD-2026-10-20-812 O1, Luna's comp .atelier/sessions/2026-10-20-gnomon-mod-invitations refs/flow.html). core/offers.ts (PURE): foldOffers folds ONLY the kernel's offer.shown / offer.decided / offer.kept rows of one conversation (principal p:<ns>/kernel, payload hsid = the conversation, offer:<ULID>, a turn:<hsid>/<n> replyTurnId, single-line question <= 240 code points), never reply text; slipViews mounts each slip under the last assistant item before its offer.shown row and makes only the newest undecided slip live, only while its reply is the latest and no human message follows; openStep is the two-step open (A5: first trusted click/Enter arms and shows "takes: <manifest contextIn> · ↵ to open", the second sends); decideRequest = log.append{kind:request.offer.decide, payload:{offerId, decision}}; offer.decided closes the slip, not-now quiets that mod for the rest of the conversation (L4), stop-here quiets all; voiceOfferIntent: a heard "not now" dismisses (one request per offer, live rows only), a heard "open" only shows "click or ↵ to open" (L1). Aegis fixes: M1 openStep refuses key repeats and multi-clicks, waits OFFER_ARM_GAP_MS (400) after the arm, and drops an arm after OFFER_ARM_TTL_MS (15 s); M2 only a forwardable, non-intercepted push-to-talk row (pttDismissable) dismisses, only the slip live when it arrived, only rows after offerLiveSince; ambient speech shows "click not now to dismiss"; M3 "takes:" comes from the row's kernel-copied contextIn (contracts CONTEXT_SOURCES labelled by CONTEXT_SOURCE_LABELS, unknown tokens shown as unknown, +N more past 8, missing = "unknown (not reported by the kernel)"); L1 devArmOfferOnce is dead code in the served bundle (__GNOMON_PREVIEW__ define false + minifySyntax in build.mjs). The offer kinds, patterns, CONTEXT_SOURCES and the isOfferTitle / isOfferQuestion text rules are imported from @a-company/gnomon-contracts. stripOfferBlocks (called by store.ts chatItems) hides a reply's trailing ```offer block (contracts offerBlockOf body) ONLY when a valid kernel offer.shown row anchors to that reply and the block names the same mod and kind; otherwise the reply text shows as-is (model text alone never hides anything). ui/offer-slip.ts: renderOfferSlip (dashed, soft shadow, never .key / data-decision; tab = glyph + offer · mod:<name>, no per-mod hue, L2; the question a text node) and wireOfferSlips (trusted click / Enter only). ui/app.ts mounts the slips in itemEl and syncs them in paintTranscript; styles.css .slip* (-0.7deg by day via --slip-tilt, flat at night, a slide-in of up to 320ms, instant under reduced motion). Preview fixtures offer-slip, offer-armed (devArmOfferOnce, DEV ONLY), offer-muted; the fake kernel answers request.offer.decide with offer.decided. Tests: test/offers.test.ts.

gui-table-talk.name: Gui Table Talk
gui-table-talk.description: #gui-table-talk (TD-2026-10-20-294) — a reply's first speak fenced block (store.ts splitSpeak, mirroring the kernel projector) shows as a highlighted "said aloud" line at the top of the reply and is removed from the body; a reply without one (heuristic) gets no highlight. Lines that start with a bold label, in whatever scheme the agent chose (letters, numbers, short names), render as subtle chips (replyParts). Aegis L3: when the kernel's speakable row (principal p:<ns>/kernel) for that reply exists, the line is its text (from block, "said aloud"; heuristic shows none); otherwise the GUI's own parse ("spoken part"). Aegis M1: a replayed user message always keeps content[0]; a later text block is hidden only when its sha256 is the kernel guidance hash (TABLE_TALK_GUIDANCE_HASH, pinned to the kernel's) or the turn.sent guidanceHash; a human-typed <gnomon-voice> stays visible. One spoken-aloud marker per reply (founder bug 2026-10-20): pipelined TTS logs one playback voice.turn.agent per sentence; chatItems (spokenFold/spokenText) opens ONE 🔊 marker at the kernel's speakable row (or the first playback row on an older kernel) and folds every later playback row and voice.bargein into it until the next assistant reply: "🔊 spoken aloud · 5s", "· stopped" when any chunk was cut off (interrupted, shorter than planned, or a barge-in); a barge-in with no marker stays the lone "🔊 interrupted". app.ts paintTranscript repaints a mounted row whose text changed in place. Preview fixture `spoken`. Clickable reply options (core/choices.ts, PURE): replyChoices finds 2..6 option lines keyed A..F or 1..6 in order (separator space ) . :, optional bold) at the END of a reply that asks a question (in the text above or the said-aloud line); labels go through the contracts sanitizer and are at most 120 chars, else no chips. liveChoiceKey: only the last assistant item of the focused session, while the human has not written after it; older replies render the chips disabled. Chips are dashed buttons (.choice, ink keycap by day, [A] at night) with data-choice / data-choice-item, never the key class or data-decision. pickChoice: trusted gesture only; the sent text is rebuilt from the parsed reply (`A — <label>`), put into the composer and sent via the composer form's requestSubmit (the typed-message path); a draft (typed or dictated) is kept and the option appended, nothing sent. Keys: letter/number pick inside the live group when the composer is empty, arrows move, Enter activates. Voice picking is out of scope. Preview fixture `choices`. Tests: test/choices.test.ts. Aegis review folded in: M1 a letter/number key only moves focus to its chip (Enter/Space confirms); a label over 60 chars, with a backtick or shell-like text needs a confirming second click/Enter (.choice.armed, "again to send"). M2 any option the contracts sanitizer flags ⇒ no chips. L1 night chips show a plain underlined letter, no [ ] brackets. L2 send() returns whether the kernel took the message; a chip is marked picked only then, and the composer clears only when the message went out (never on an early return). L3 onChoice recomputes liveness from currentItems(). L4 more than two combining marks on a base ⇒ no chips.

gui-settings.name: Gui Settings
gui-settings.description: #gui-settings (founder UI-first rule) - the header Day / Night / Auto theme switch and the Settings sheet (header gear key, Cmd-comma, the palette's "Settings..."). core/settings.ts is PURE: parseTheme / parseMotion (per-browser THEME_KEY / MOTION_KEY, like the Layout), themeSwitchEntries, unlockSeenOf (the cached unlock folded from kernel-principal approval.unlock / .dropped rows; daemon.start clears) and settingsModel (Appearance, Layout, Voice, Permissions, About). Every control names an existing GUI command in SETTINGS_RUNS (theme, motion, layout presets, pane toggles, workshop placement, mode.repo.*, voice app start/stop, enrol, dictation delay) or the standing Revoke (core/standing.ts revokeRequest); no new kernel verb. Kernel-owned values (mode ceiling, unlock and bounds, connection, bundle pin, voice hotkeys, the always-shown regions) are read-only rows with a how-to-change line, never a terminal-only path. ui/settings-sheet.ts paints with render.ts h() (text nodes, no inline style) and acts on trusted clicks only (G-GUI-04). settings.* is not block-safe. Aegis fixes: kernel rows are pinned to the connected home's kernel principal (standing.ts kernelPrincipalOf / isKernelPrincipal, also for the standing feed); an unseen unlock says only "no unlock seen since this page connected"; run(id, trusted) carries the gesture's isTrusted from every path and the header switch checks it; the standing feed sits under overlays (hidden while a dialog is open), its offer is not an ink key, and the stack pile reserves bottom room so it never covers a card key.

gnomon-helper.name: Gnomon Helper
gnomon-helper.description: Holds what the kernel must never hold. M1.3 slice 1: the root and approvals P-256 keys in the Secure Enclave (access group SW4BMQ8PNL.gnomon, .privateKeyUsage + .userPresence), a sign API over stdin/stdout (`serve` NDJSON loop, `once` for one request) speaking gnomon-helper:v1 — info, key.create/public/delete, sign (root: fresh presence per signature; approvals: fresh, or a per-connection cached unlock held here keyed by the request's connId string, bounded to 32, dropped 12 h after it opened or after 512 signatures under it, with no separate idle limit (TD-2026-10-20-086 F4, helper 1.7.0; 1.6.0 was 15 idle min / 60 min / 64; a kept fresh sign reports `bounds` so the broker opens the same caps, else it keeps the 1.6.0 ones; F5: the kernel sends the GUI device's `udev:` key there so the unlock survives a reconnect; UnlockBoundsTests.swift), on unlock.drop and on exit), unlock.drop(-all). Every fresh sign (root and approvals) returns `shown`, the helper's own prompt line, which the provisioner checks names the digest it displayed (helper 1.5.0; 1.4.0 omitted it for root, so guided setup failed helper-line-mismatch). M4: promptText strips every format (Cf), control and line/paragraph separator from the caller text before the OS prompt. Each key signs only its own domain prefixes (root: row-sig, presence; approvals: approve, presence). Inputs bounded before any key is touched. Refuses to run sandboxed (P8-D68). Never prints key material. Helper 1.6.0 (protocol gnomon-helper:v2, V5 of TD-2026-10-19-194, spec §14.7, S29-K5, G-BRK-06): voice ARMS in their own store (Custody.swift, cap Bounds.maxArms 8, separate from maxUnlocks 32), opened by arm.open (fresh presence bound to {humanConnId, voiceConnId}); arm.sign signs ONLY gnomon:approve-voice:v1 for that pair, and neither fresh nor cached signing ever accepts that domain; arm.close(-all); conn.close drops a connId's unlock and every arm naming it. SessionWatch.swift observes screen lock, screensaver, display sleep, system sleep and user switch (distributed + NSWorkspace notifications, IOKit power, a CGSession poll at a 250 ms cadence), invalidates every arm and unlock, bumps the epoch (a prompt open across the event is never kept), then pushes an unsolicited {push:'session', cause, arms, unlocks, seq} line. serve runs requests on a reader thread and the main run loop for the observer; Output serializes stdout. Aegis V5 fixes: arm.sign parses the frozen gnomon:voice-decision:v1 preimage (gnomon-contracts voice-decision.ts) and refuses unless it names this arm and pair; arm.open and arm.sign fail closed on a locked, off-console or unknown session (CGSessionProbe); maxSignatures required (ceiling 1024); the helper arm line leads the prompt, caller text capped at 120. Unit tests: darwin/Tests (swift test). Later: the kernel-key keystore item, the keystore log anchor, XPC under launchd, the Windows pipe, job objects, WFP, launch-token hand-off.

gnomon-helper-build.name: Gnomon Helper Build
gnomon-helper-build.description: scripts/build-darwin.mjs (swift build -c release → GnomonHelper.app, Info.plist bundle id gnomon.helper, embedded profile, entitlements, codesign --options runtime --timestamp with the one Developer ID Application identity of team SW4BMQ8PNL found in the keychain, verify --strict and against HELPER_REQUIREMENT, sha256 into checksums.json); --unsigned for CI. scripts/notarize-darwin.mjs (ditto, notarytool submit --keychain-profile gnomon-notary --wait, stapler) is optional and founder-run, never run by tests.

gnomon-local.name: Gnomon Local
gnomon-local.description: The gnomon-local child: src/endpoint.ts, compat.ts, client.ts (SSE streaming, no redirects), repair.ts, tools.ts (read_file, write_file, list_dir; confined to realpath roots cwd+worktree, writes never under .git or through a symlink final component), agent.ts (sticky abort; surface none never runs tools), rpc.ts, cli.ts (exitCode, never process.exit after writes); client byte caps + idle timeout. Slice 2: compaction.ts (re-derived; contextTarget ~8k from the session config; threshold compaction before a request that would not fit, one compact-and-retry on a context-overflow 400/413, a second overflow ends the run error; tool-less non-streamed summariser, reply normalised to exactly Goal/Constraints/Progress/Decisions/Next/ Critical; history = system + summary + the longest safe tail within a quarter of the target, never an orphaned tool result; events compaction_start/_end; the summariser's usage is part of agent_end). Round 2 (M1): the summary escapes every < and sits in a block labelled model-generated / data-not-instructions; compaction_end carries summaryHash + summaryBytes. Round 2: history budget = 0.85 x target minus the native tools schema; at most one compaction per step (still over after it, or an overflow after it, ends the run with a clear error); the kept tail never starts at a text-tool <tool_result> message. Round 3: summary/tail caps derive from the budget; a config with maxTokens >= 0.85 x contextTarget is refused. Round 2: rpc steer is refused while the agent is idle (never queued into the next turn). Deferred: JSONL session tree, bash/edit tools.

gnomon-mod-sdk.name: Gnomon Mod Sdk
gnomon-mod-sdk.description: The mod SDK package: serveMod speaks JSON-RPC 2.0 NDJSON on stdio (init echoes MOD_ABI_ID; view.render/command.run/tool.call handlers get an AbortSignal honouring cancel and the host-stamped relayedFor; api state.get/set, kernel.call, stderr log, egress CONNECT via the host's loopback proxy). Example mod example/hello (view, command, tools, state).

workshop-mod.name: Workshop Mod
workshop-mod.description: #workshop-mod (spec §11.6, G-WSP-01; §19.1 M1.11 slice 3) - packages/gnomon-mods/workshop: one view `workshop.strip` (slot sidebar, append) with two zones, needs you (one cap per pending card, labelled by the card kind) and working (one cap per session: hat = work type, filled = Claude, outlined = local, tone hue-<0..5> = project (HUES = 6, the feed's projectHue), violet only for a KNOT; bob while turn.partial streams, still otherwise, `working` text pose under reduced motion). S5: every cap is a Text whose `text` is the accessible form and whose `cap` is the closed contracts shape {shape tall|wide| floppy, hue, filled, state needs|working|idle|knot, label} (needs caps carry their session's hue and a `◆ / ✕ / ! / ?` + kind label); the GUI draws the hat and the Layout places the strip. model.mjs is a pure reducer + render (sessions and cards bounded at 256 each); index.mjs speaks mod-abi:v1 directly (no SDK import, so the pinned packageHash never depends on an SDK build) and echoes MOD_ABI_ID. State comes ONLY from the host's projected kernel-event feed (#mod-host feed.ts, granted by the log.read capability); a host-initiated fixture render may replay input.fixtureEvents, a relayed render never can. Declared effects: none beyond idle read; tier first-party; installs with `gnomon mod install packages/gnomon-mods/workshop` + the root-key card. Fixtures strip.json / strip-reduced.json with golden renders (test/workshop-mod.test.ts, every OS).

ledger-mod.name: Ledger Mod
ledger-mod.description: #ledger-mod - packages/gnomon-mods/ledger, the context and budget meter (mod #1 of the mods arc). Two views: `ledger.strip` (slot composer.footer, append) - one line for the focused session (relay input {hsid}, display only) or all sessions, `182k in · 9k out · 71% cache · $0.42 · ⇣ 2 compactions (190k → 41k)` (in = fresh + cache reads + cache writes; cache = the share read from cache; a local session shows its token total), the budget meter (the over-permit row `n of m`, else the highest budget.ladder rung `n of 100%`) and the alarms (breaker open, permit denied); `ledger.sheet` (slot sidebar, append) - a Table row per session plus the total, meter and alarms. Tones: quiet; warn (amber) at a rung >= 75% or an over-permit row; deny (vermilion) on a breaker or a denied permit; hue-<0..7> ONLY on the cap glyph, never as text. Reduced motion renders the meter as Text (no Progress fill at all). kit:v1 blocks only (Box, Text, Table, Progress). model.mjs is a pure reducer + render (MAX_SESSIONS 256, MAX_DIMENSIONS 32, every number re-clamped by count(), unknown kinds ignored); index.mjs is the #workshop-mod stdio loop verbatim but for the two views (no SDK import, echoes MOD_ABI_ID). State comes ONLY from the #mod-host feed projection v2 (numbers only, granted by log.read); a relayed render never replays fixtureEvents. requires log.read and log.read:usage (Aegis M1: the usage rows reach only that grant), egress none, no tools or commands; tier first-party (packageHash pinned in FIRST_PARTY_PACKAGE_HASHES). Fixtures strip, strip-reduced, over-budget, breaker, compacted with golden renders (test/ledger-mod.test.ts, light and dark); goldens regenerate with `npm run repin:first-party` in packages/gnomon.

paradigm-context-mod.name: Paradigm Context Mod
paradigm-context-mod.description: #paradigm-context-mod - packages/gnomon-mods/paradigm-context, Paradigm Context (mod #2 of the mods arc). One view `paradigm-context.sheet` (slot sidebar, append), read-only (no Button, no command, no tool): a head with the project swatch (tone hue-<0..7> on the ● cap glyph only, the name in ink), a stale line (warn) when the newest decision or lore entry is > STALE_DAYS (14) older than the slice's `at`, then three zones headed (Text tone head) with their {n, of} count - tasks (`tasks · n of m open · k high`), decisions, lore - each item a row with a FIXED type prefix (`task` / `task ▲` for high, `decision`, `lore <type>`), the id (+ date), then the title “quoted” (inner curly quotes flattened), every part tone quiet, so a repo title never supplies a status glyph (Aegis L2) - then the symbols touched as chips (tone chip, mono ink, never a hue), and a skipped line (malformed / refused / secret counts). Titles cut to 80 code points. Its ONLY input is the host-composed `input.paradigm` (#mod-host K1 paradigm-slice:v1 of the focused LIVE session's repo, joined server-side from {focus:{hsid}}, K3); model.mjs re-validates and bounds it (ids, dates, tokens, symbol shape, counts). requires paradigm.read:summary only (no log.read, so no feed), egress none (refused with that capability). index.mjs is the #ledger-mod stdio loop minus the feed (no SDK import, echoes MOD_ABI_ID). Fixtures empty, full, full-dark, stale, unfocused with goldens (test/paradigm-context-mod.test.ts, light and dark); regenerate with `npm run repin:first-party`; tier first-party once pinned in FIRST_PARTY_PACKAGE_HASHES (sha256:be0cce01…, repinned after Aegis L2).

neurons-mod.name: Neurons Mod
neurons-mod.description: #neurons-mod - packages/gnomon-mods/neurons-brain (the Desk, TD-2026-10-20-812 slice S2), mod name `neurons-brain`, because `neurons` is a kernel namespace token (the §9.1 `neurons.event` kind) and the validator refuses it as a mod name. View-less, with no process of its own (no index.mjs; the validator needs none). It declares one provides.mcp server `gnomon-neurons-brain` (generic default `neurons mcp`, a placeholder that is not absolute, so it fails closed until the user sets an absolute command through the per-user override; config {command, args, env [NEURONS_VAULT], the upstream server's own variable}; no personal path is committed), three offers (search-the-brain diverge → neuron_search, capture-a-learning synthesize → source_note, capture-a-decision commit → neuron_write; each offer's contextIn comes from CONTEXT_SOURCES, and the two capture restraints, like the playbook, require showing the exact text and waiting for the human to confirm or edit it, flagging fetched, tool-output or unverified content), and one skill, skills/neurons-desk/SKILL.md, a playbook that falls back to plain suggestions outside Gnomon. Every ```offer example in it resolves to a declared offer (tested). requires egress none, no capability. Fixtures are model replies with one ```offer block, and their goldens come from scripts/offer-golden.mjs (offerBlockOf plus the manifest's offer-spec), with one undeclared-kind negative. Tier first-party (packageHash pinned in FIRST_PARTY_PACKAGE_HASHES); tested in test/neurons-mod.test.ts.

constellation-mod.name: Constellation Mod
constellation-mod.description: #constellation-mod - packages/gnomon-mods/constellation (the Desk, TD-2026-10-20-812 slice S2). View-less, with no process of its own. It declares one provides.mcp server `gnomon-constellation` (placeholder default `constellation-mcp`, never launched: it is not absolute, so it fails closed until the user sets an absolute node and `<checkout>/mcp/server.ts` through the per-user override; config {command, args, env [CONSTELLATION_NO_AUTOSTART]}), two offers (map-the-idea diverge → apply, contextIn [recent-messages]; summarize-the-session synthesize → summarize; the automation offer is deferred to O2 behind a confirmation and a disabled save, Aegis H1), and one skill, skills/constellation-desk/SKILL.md, a playbook that falls back to plain suggestions outside Gnomon. requires egress none, no capability. The L3 "sky" world is not declared yet, because manifest:v1 has no world field. Offer fixtures plus goldens include a two-blocks negative. Tier first-party (packageHash pinned); tested in test/constellation-mod.test.ts.

gnomon-voice.name: Gnomon Voice
gnomon-voice.description: Dictation (TD-2026-10-20-262): accepted voice.turn.user rows carry a kernel-stamped forwardable (a client forwardable is BAD_REQUEST); a human session.send{source:'voice'} is hash-matched against the attachment's pending turns and tagged turn.sent{source voice|voice-edited, voiceSessionId, voiceTurnSeqs, voiceTurnSeq} (attribution never refuses); request.voice.report {dictation} is relayed as status.voice.dictation{activity, holdToggles, at}. #gnomon-voice kernel side, slices V1 talk-only and V2a ambient (TD-2026-10-19-298: the attachment mode is a ceiling, ptt under any, conversation only under conversation; widening to conversation takes one fresh-presence strictness card per GUI login; ambient turns need an aec claim, an enrolled speaker and a not-busy session by the supervisor's own turn state plus the echo tail (voice-playback, clock kernel); idle auto-off of a conversation ceiling after voice.ambientIdleMs, default ten minutes, written voice.session.end reason idle; receipt-refused and unknown-speaker turns are stored as a keyed text hash, duration and reason, never text; status.voice attached, hsid, ceiling, since, idleAt) (spec §14.1-14.4, §14.7 Forwarding guards and No level, run modes; §4.10; T-2026-10-19-026, TD-2026-10-19-194, TD-2026-10-19-677). src/kernel/voice/voice-control.ts: attachment ONLY by a human gesture (log.append voice.session.start|end on a first-party GUI/device connection; the kernel mints voiceSessionId and writes the row); voice session.send to the attached session only, source voice forced, riding the attaching human's turn permit (never its own), accepted only for the voice connection's latest voice.turn.user in this attachment from an enrolled speaker, not intercepted, push-to-talk, outside every voice.turn.agent playback window + echoTailMs (750). Refusals are FORBIDDEN gate voice with reserved reasons: voice-target, voice-conn, voice-stale-utterance, voice-speaker, voice-grammar, voice-echo, voice-off (conversation mode). session.stop interrupt only; voice.* shape-validated; the voice reader sees its attached session + voice.*, redacted. approve stays voice-off in every form; request.voice.arm stays refused (V7). src/kernel/voice/enrolment.ts + src/cli/voice-cli.ts: gnomon voice setup | enrol | forget, root-signed rows (enrolments.jsonl, voice device key). Aegis V1 conditions: kernel receipt time stamped on voice.turn.user|agent (receivedAt); a turn is forwardable for VOICE_TURN_MAX_AGE_MS (30 s) after receipt, never before the attachment, echo checked on kernel times too; per-turn client mode claim cross-checked against the attachment (ptt is a client claim, §A.4); voice follow subscriptions end on every attachment change (SubscriptionHub.endReaderClass); turn.sent / session.inject carry source voice + voiceSessionId, turnId, voiceTurnSeq (the link); the voice reader sees only its attached session's rows; enrolment order is the signed seq; windows bounded at VOICE_WINDOW_CAP.
