Slice V2e (spec §14.4.1): src/kernel/voice/voice-child.ts VoiceChildSupervisor spawns the voice client over an inherited socketpair (fd 3) the kernel authenticates itself as p:<ns>/voice (SocketServerHandle.adopt + dispatcher.adoptPreauthenticated, no hello/auth, no key in the child), allow-list env, backoff restarts, dies on every daemon exit and drain (TD-908). voice-install.ts copies + codesign-verifies GnomonVoiceIO.app into <home>/bin/voice and fetches models; the client entry resolves lazily, darwin only. Aegis M2: at DAEMON START createVoicePrepare checks the workspace gnomon-voice dist against dist/voice-client.manifest.json and that manifest against the loaded build stamp's voiceClientManifest (scripts/build-stamp.mjs; build gnomon-voice first), then copies all of dist, voice-models.manifest.json, a module package.json and the optional sherpa-onnx-node + platform packages into <home>/bin/voice/client (0700/0600), pins a sha256 of every file in memory, runs the model fetch and the spawn from the COPY, and re-verifies the pin last in every prepare; a changed, added or missing file is VoiceClientRefused, phase 'unavailable' with the reason, never retried. Every exit (signal, stop, idle, upgrade after its drain) goes through shutdown(), which awaits voiceChild.close(). voice-requests.ts: dispatcher-only request.voice.enrol (fresh-presence strictness card, detail.op voice.enrol, writes the root-signed row), request.voice.forget (no card), request.voice.report (client progress + notices relayed in status.voice; 2026-10-20 prints{stale: names} = speakers whose print predates the client's speech gate, held per voice connection with no TTL, cleared when it closes, relayed as status.voice.prints; T-2026-10-20-005 A1 capture{state idle|hearing|transcribing|captured|dropped, segId, reason? closed too-short|echo|not-attached|no-words|not-enrolled| barge-in|refused on dropped only, level? 0..1 on hearing only} relayed as status.voice.capture with VOICE_CAPTURE_TTL_MS 5 s; voiceStatusFor projects B1's capture.text{committed, tail} (the live partial words, hearing / transcribing only, voice principal only, sanitised, capped at CAPTURE_TEXT_MAX 600, in memory with the capture TTL, never a row) to a human-class connection on the gui credential only (V2; the shared CAPTURE_STATUS_KEYS never include text); voice.capture.level declared in status-numbers.ts. Aegis follow-ups: terminal states are marked claim:'client' and cross-checked against the kernel's own acceptances on that voice connection (VoiceControl onAccepted turn|send, 5 s window): a contradicted drop shows captured with kernel:'accepted' and clientReason, a captured with no acceptance is kernel:'unconfirmed'; text only for cls human on the gui credential; the slot remembers its connId and clears when that connection closes); request.voice.client start|stop is human only. speakable.ts KernelSpeakable appends voice.turn.agent{source kernel-speakable, turnSeq, items} for the attached session; the voice reader is narrowed to voice.* rows. speakerEnrolled is the kernel's call (readEnrolled). No §9.1 kind added; clientApiId unchanged. TABLE TALK (TD-2026-10-20-294, docs/guides/table-talk.md): the reply item prefers the first speak fenced block (markdown, URLs and long digit/hex runs stripped, 300-char sentence cap, unclosed fence = its first paragraph) as from:'block', else the gnome line / first paragraph as from:'heuristic'; kernel-written ask-waiting and edits items carry from:'kernel'. table-talk.ts holds the frozen guidance (at most 160 words, pinned hash); VoiceControl.guidanceFor(hsid) returns it only while voice is attached to that session, and the #supervisor writes it as a second <gnomon-voice> text block on every send (turn.sent guidanceHash; contentHash stays the human text, replay unchanged). The spoken scrub (scrubSpoken) also covers heuristic and ask items (Aegis L2); gnomon trace allows one extra prompt block only when turn.sent names its guidanceHash and the hash matches (Aegis M2).

gnomon-voice-io.name: Gnomon Voice Io
gnomon-voice-io.description: Hotkeys talk, mic-toggle, mode-toggle, hold-toggle (carbonId 4, default ctrl+alt+h, TD-2026-10-20-262 dictation hold) and stop-speaking (carbonId 5, default ctrl+alt+. — the period key, kVK_ANSI_Period 0x2F, spelled "." or "period"; T-2026-10-19-026: cuts the reply being read aloud). The voice child's audio I/O, mic only (no keychain group, no network, writes only stdout/stderr). Protocol gnomon-voice-io:v1, the same framing both ways: type:u8 length:u32le payload (max 1 MiB); 0x01 JSON (stdin commands, stdout replies and events), 0x02 capture (stdout: hostTimeNs:u64le sampleRate:u32le s16le, 16 kHz mono after voice processing), 0x03 playback (stdin: sampleRate:u32le s16le mono TTS, 8-48 kHz). Commands info, mic.on, mic.off, play.stop (barge-in flush), play.end, route.get, hotkeys.set {bindings}, quit; each gets one reply {type:'reply', id, op, ok}. Events (tUs monotonic µs, the capture clock): ready, mic, route {route, aec: vpio|headphones|none}, level {rmsDBFS, peakDBFS} ~15 Hz, playback.start {audibleAtUs}, playback.end {reason: drained|stopped|mic-switch|route-change|exit}, hotkey {action: talk|mic-toggle|mode-toggle|hold-toggle|stop-speaking, phase: down|up}, engine, error, exit. Mic on = one AVAudioEngine with inputNode.setVoiceProcessingEnabled(true) (VoiceProcessingIO AEC) and a player node in the same engine, so TTS is the echo reference; mic off stops and releases that engine (no orange dot) and TTS plays via an output-only engine that never touches inputNode. Route from CoreAudio (default output device transport + built-in data source, listeners on both). Hotkeys via Carbon RegisterEventHotKey, press and release, no Input Monitoring; defaults ctrl+alt+space (talk), ctrl+alt+m, ctrl+alt+a; reported only, the controller acts. Mic modes re-spawn with TCC responsibility disclaimed so the Microphone grant names GnomonVoiceIO (probe P1; --no-disclaim is the control). Aegis V2b fixes: MicGate (a mic.off during an open TCC prompt wins, generation counter; mic.on refused not-disclaimed unless disclaimed or --no-disclaim), DisclaimToken (disclaimed only when argv --disclaim-token equals the env token; a stray env var is ignored), ParentWatch (kqueue EVFILT_PROC NOTE_EXIT on the re-spawning and the original parent: the child exits with either), re-spawn path from _NSGetExecutablePath + realpath only, a tap generation so no capture or level frame follows mic:false, a bounded stdout queue (one writer thread, no lock held in write(2), capture frames dropped first with a capture.dropped event), transport in mic and route events. --version, --selftest (1 s smoke), --probe-aec <file> (P7); stdin EOF exits 0. VoiceIOCore (frame codec, command parser, hotkey config, level and route math, mic gate, disclaim token, parent watch) is pure or Darwin-only and covered by swift test (37 XCTests).

gnomon-voice-io-build.name: Gnomon Voice Io Build
gnomon-voice-io-build.description: scripts/build-voice-io.mjs: swift build -c release → GnomonVoiceIO.app (bundle id gnomon.voice-io, LSUIElement, NSMicrophoneUsageDescription "Gnomon voice listens only while the mic is on."), codesign --options runtime --timestamp with the one Developer ID Application identity of team SW4BMQ8PNL (looked up via the helper's signing.mjs), exactly one entitlement com.apple.security.device.audio-input, no provisioning profile and no keychain group; verifies --strict, the VOICE_IO_REQUIREMENT, the entitlement set and the runtime flag; sha256 into checksums.json (advisory). --unsigned for CI. No notarization (founder-run).

gnomon-voice-bench-partials.name: Gnomon Voice Bench Partials
gnomon-voice-bench-partials.description: scripts/bench-partials.mjs: the B0 benchmark for voice phase B (live words while speaking; T-2026-10-20-005, ruling V5 in TD-2026-10-20-086). Builds the Parakeet recognizer exactly as engines/sherpa.ts does (only numThreads varies), synthesises ~15 s of test speech in memory with Kokoro, and also uses the Parakeet archive's test_wavs/0.wav. It times 4, 6 and 8 s tail-window decodes at 2 and 4 threads, measures sync decode against decodeAsync (event-loop block), checks a worker_thread, and measures prefix stability and LocalAgreement-2 commits for decodes every 600 ms. Read-only on the model home (verifiedModelPaths); it writes nothing. Results are in PROBES.md, section B0. Dev tool only, not shipped.

gnomon-wrapper.name: Gnomon Wrapper
gnomon-wrapper.description: Package-level component (allowlisted in packages/gnomon/test/symbol-allowlist.json: Appendix A treats gnomon-wrapper as a package, not a spec node). Tauri pinned exact (=2.12.4; tauri-build =2.7.3). One window whose main frame is in exactly one phase the NATIVE side moves (src/nav.rs): the bundled status page (tauri://localhost) or the one kernel origin http://127.0.0.1:<port>; on_navigation refuses every other URL (another port, localhost, userinfo tricks, other schemes) and on_new_window denies. IPC is disabled for page content (src/surface.rs): invoke_system replaces Tauri's invoke script with a stub that holds no invoke key and throws, there is no command and no invoke handler, capabilities: [] (the generated gen/schemas/capabilities.json is {}), withGlobalTauri: false, freezePrototype: true. Devtools only in debug builds (no devtools feature). A document-start script defines a frozen window.gnomonSurface='wrapper' on the 127.0.0.1 origin only, which the GUI reads to declare hello surface wrapper and drop the extension-risk badge (display only). Hardened runtime with an EMPTY entitlements set. Double-click flow (src/main.rs): the app spawns `node --disable-sigusr1 <dist>/cli/gnomon.js up --wrapper` (src/kernel.rs: env_clear + HOME USER LOGNAME LANG TMPDIR SHELL + fixed PATH, no NODE_OPTIONS/GNOMON_*/DYLD_*). Trust root (Aegis C1, src/tree.rs shared with build.rs): the build records the node path as found plus the sha256 of its realpath target, and the gnomon-wrapper-kernel-tree:v1 hash of packages/gnomon/{dist,package.json}; check_trust_root re-hashes both before every spawn and refuses "built against a different node/kernel … Rebuild the app" (covers brew upgrade node). local.signed.json is not a node source (Aegis C2). Stderr to ~/Library/Logs/Gnomon/kernel.log (0600), reads gnomon-wrapper-channel:v1 (src/contract.rs; LaunchGrant Debug redacts token and key), and on a grant runs the native preflight (src/loopback.rs): channel bundleHash == the pin compiled from gui-bundle.ts (src/bundle.rs), its own WebSocket hello with surface wrapper verified natively (src/verify.rs: ed25519-dalek strict, exact SPKI, kernel keyId, sent clientNonce, gnomon:auth-server:v2), then every pinned file and / re-hashed — only then Phase::Kernel and navigate. Any refusal (unprovisioned shows `gnomon identity init`) stays on the status page. Window close hides (kernel keeps running), Dock click reopens, Cmd-Q sends quit, waits 10 s, kills. Tests: unit (nav, surface, contract, verify against TS-generated vectors, bundle, kernel env/argv), tests/live_kernel.rs (preflight vs a live dev kernel; a foreign key and another pin refused), tests/no_page_ipc.rs (config falsifiers). Round 2: the child is `node --disable-sigusr1 …` (NODE_FLAGS, first and only); the channel is #wrapper-channel; lines are capped at 64 KiB at read time; at stdout EOF the phase returns to Status and an EOF without a refusal/down line says "the kernel exited before starting" with the status; Cmd-Q prevent_exit + worker-thread stop (try_wait, 10 s, kill); src/logfile.rs opens kernel.log O_NOFOLLOW with fchmod/fstat checks and a 0700 dir; tests/crafted_ipc.rs (Tauri mock runtime: keyless messages dropped, keyed commands refused from both origins); subframes are excluded by the kernel CSP frame-src 'none' (falsified statically and on the live header). #setup-endpoint (T-2026-10-19-005 MVP-b): an unprovisioned home makes `up --wrapper` emit {t:setup,port,setupToken, setupPublicKey,bundleHash,expiresAt} (contract.rs SetupGrant, Debug redacted; ^setup-token exactly 43 base64url); loopback.rs setup_preflight runs the SAME pin and serverSig checks against the ephemeral setup key speaking gnomon-setup:v1; nav.rs Phase::Setup{port} locks navigation to that one origin; the page reaches no Tauri command (G-GUI-12). After success the channel's {t:up} continues into the normal launch. refusal_text no longer says "In Terminal".

gnomon-kernel.name: Gnomon Kernel
gnomon-kernel.description: The kernel package. ZERO runtime deps (G-SEC-01): package.json has no `dependencies` key; @a-company/gnomon-contracts is a devDependency that tsup bundles. Import fence (G-KRN-02): every import under src/kernel/** is node:*, relative, or @a-company/gnomon-contracts, and dist/ holds no bare import. src/kernel/ has the thirteen §18 modules (identity, log, runner, supervisor, broker, budget, scheduler, manifest, refs, socket, web, sandbox, modhost) as empty directories at PR-0. Placeholder bins write to stdio directly: the kernel cannot depend on the Paradigm logger (zero deps); #kernel-log brings its own logging at M1.2. PR-5 adds src/kernel/lifecycle/ — the $daemon-lifecycle core (spec §2.4): home resolution (~/.gnomon; GNOMON_HOME is a test seam only, a detached daemon gets --home in argv) created 0700 with the mode read back; the endpoint path (<home>/gnomon.sock, $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR fallback on Linux on sun_path overflow, never /tmp, refuse if nothing fits; win32 refuses pending the P8-D78 parity phase); the O_EXCL daemonPid:v1 pidfile lock lifted from warpline lifecycle.ts (live holder refuses, dead holder cleaned by rename-and-inode-check and re-raced, empty file = racer mid-write); the clean re-exec env (PATH fixed pending root-signed config, HOME/USERPROFILE, LANG, LC_*; NODE_OPTIONS and GNOMON_* dropped); the idle-exit monitor (holders = open #socket connections until sessions/subscribers exist). bins: `gnomond [--foreground] [--home] [--idle-ms]`, `gnomon daemon status|stop|--detach` (stop refuses not-implemented pending #approval-broker, M1.6). Lifecycle events are emitted to a callback using the spec §9.1 kinds daemon.start, daemon.exit{reason}, daemon.lock.refused (the kernel log takes them at M1.2); the spec declares no signals. SYMBOL CONVENTION (P8-D81, test/symbols-drift.test.ts): every source module names the symbol(s) it implements in its header (first 40 lines), one `@symbol <id>` per line, using the spec Appendix A id verbatim where the spec has one (e.g. `@symbol #kernel-log`, `@symbol $daemon-lifecycle`). Every .ts under src/kernel/** must carry a tag; every tag must be declared in a packages/gnomon*/.purpose; every declared symbol must be an Appendix A node or be listed in test/symbol-allowlist.json with a reason. G-WIN-05 MARKER ENFORCEMENT (T-2026-10-17-011): vitest.config.ts excludes every test file whose `// @gnomon-platform:` marker omits the running process.platform (test/platform-registry.ts excludedTestFiles); each such file has a registry row (sibling or n/a reason), and the registry test proves per platform that the excluded set equals the rows that omit it, and that each row's platforms equal its file's marker.

gnomon-probes.name: Gnomon Probes
gnomon-probes.description: M1.0 probe harness (spec §19.1, research 29 §2). `node packages/gnomon/probes/run.mjs <id> [--out-dir d] [--timeout ms]` imports probes/<id>/probe.mjs (zero deps, no build), runs its default export with {id, platform, arch, probeDir, signal}, and writes a probeResult:v1 record to probes/results/<id>.<platform>.json. Throws and timeouts become verdict `fail`. Exit codes 0 pass / 1 fail / 2 partial / 64 usage. Probe ids match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$ (no path traversal). p-harness is the self-test and its results are gitignored; real results are committed from hardware runs only. A `fail` on a ruling means a re-plan memo before dependent builds. Unsigned macOS probes: p10m-sbx-deny-mac (S29-03/04 sandbox-exec session denies + escape matrix), p11-ws-framing (RFC 6455 over node:http with a forked server child, 27 Autobahn-style raw cases, 4 MiB throughput, RSS and phys_footprint), p-noise-vectors (Noise IK/XX/XXpsk3 over node:crypto against a verbatim cacophony/snow vector subset in vectors.json, G-LNK-11) p-log-fsync (kernel-log head-anchor fsync stalls, arms A-G; arm G = the research 33 policy: coalesced anchor + forced fullfsync+anchor at 1/64, judged by the restated G-LOG-04; env P_LOG_FSYNC_ARMS accepts A,E,G) and p01-claude-cli (read-only `claude --version`/`--help` flag check; live items pending-manual). M1.0 batch 2 (probes/README.md lists them): unattended p06-local-caps (llama.cpp /slots n_ctx + live tool-call detection; no endpoint = partial, recorded not failed), p09-ed25519-matrix (WebCrypto Ed25519 in Node + every local engine under the §11.2 CSP; safari.html for Safari by hand, P09_SAFARI_LINE to record it), p12-excalidraw-csp (pinned Excalidraw bundled by esbuild in a temp dir, loaded under the §11.2 CSP; violations by phase, size, parse time), p14-link-outbound (default-deny sandbox-exec link profile); founder-run p00-sign-notary, p04-se-helper, p05-keychain-acl (signed GnomonHelperProbe.app from _shared/helper/ProbeHelper.swift; fail fast with a founder-steps pointer when the identity / provisioning profile / gnomon-notary profile is missing; prompt-free halves run unattended), p07-launch-token (NSWorkspace hand-off, eslogger + log stream + ps capture with an argv positive control, browser history grep incl. mozlz4), p01-claude-cli-manual (hook session_id, control_request interrupt, loopback-override observation, managed policy; claude by the path p01 recorded, never PATH). s29-10-voice-custody is a README stub pending the signed helper. p14b-link-fdpass (research paradigm-8/37): the kernel stand-in dials the peer and passes the connected socket over IPC to a deny-default child with no network* allow; full duplex 4 MiB, peer close, redial hand-off, child connect/UDP/listen/unix/file/exec all EPERM. p14b-web-handoff (T-2026-10-18-020): the inbound twin — the kernel stand-in listens on 127.0.0.1 (pauseOnConnect) and hands each accepted socket to a deny-default child with no network-* rule; full duplex 4 MiB, client close, 5 repeated hand-offs, every child bind/listen (0.0.0.0, ::, en0, 127.0.0.1, ::1, no host), UDP bind, outbound TCP and unix connect EPERM; pass on darwin. probes/_shared/ (browser.mjs, signing.mjs, abort.mjs — synchronous cleanups on SIGINT/SIGTERM/ctx.signal for founder-run probes, ask() rejects on abort — wkwebview-load.swift, helper/) is shared code, not a probe id. p12 pins its whole tree with a committed package-lock.json (npm ci). CI probe results go to $RUNNER_TEMP, never probes/results/.

socket.name: Socket
socket.description: #socket (spec §2.1, §4.9, §5) — the kernel's gnomon-rpc:v1 endpoint. T-2026-10-18-016 (P8-D93): hello carries a client-chosen clientNonce (validated, required); auth.ts echoes it in the result and signs serverSig over nonce + clientNonce + endpointPath + negotiated hello; connectGnomon (client.ts) sends a fresh 32-byte nonce, refuses a hello that does not echo it (client-nonce-mismatch) and verifyServerHello takes the SENT nonce, so a recorded genuine hello replayed from a squatted socket never reaches auth. PR-5 core: unix-socket server bound under a 0177 umask, chmod 0600 and the ACL read back before serving; byte-based NDJSON framing (4 MiB max inbound frame, UTF-8 safe partial lines, oversize discarded to its newline and answered BAD_REQUEST once, malformed lines BAD_REQUEST, connection kept); per-connection in-order replies; connIds are conn:<ULID>. M1.4 SLICE 1: errors carry contracts refusal:v1 in error.data with the §4.9 code map (rpc.ts). auth.ts — `hello` negotiation via contracts negotiateHello (highest shared gnomon-rpc version; none shared ⇒ UNSUPPORTED{offered[], supported[]}; tolerant param validation; client strings capped at 128 chars) answering {clientApi, features, nonce, serverKeyId, serverSig, clientApiId, kitId}; serverSig = kernel key over gnomon:auth-server:v2 + nonce + endpointPath; `auth {principal, deviceId, sig}` verified against the ROOT-signed device registry (#identity), nonce single-use (any attempt consumes it) and 30 s, accepted transcripts remembered so a replay is socket.auth.replay; {token}/{launchToken}/{reconnect} refused UNSUPPORTED (later M1.4 slices). Any failed auth = ONE AUTH refusal, then the connection is closed. dispatch.ts — before auth only hello and auth (every other name, known or unknown, AUTH{unauthenticated} then closed — Aegis L6: no pre-auth method enumeration; UNKNOWN_VERB only after auth); after auth the §5 verb × principal matrix (contracts VERBS.access; peer refused everywhere) then `status` served for real (principal, connId, surface, clientApi, clientApiId, kitId, abiId, nextLegalVerbs from the §5 table, verbs/relays with availability + milestone, daemon info, log head, sessions 0, cards 0, kernelKeyCustody partial, root state, authenticated clients) under 50 ms (G-ABI-03), every other verb/relay ENGINE{not-implemented, milestone} — no fake success, no extra verb (the PR-5 daemon.status / daemon.stop placeholders are removed). Kernel-log rows before the reply: socket.hello, socket.auth.ok, socket.auth.fail, socket.auth.replay (+ socket.connect, socket.frame.refused as diagnostics); a failed auth.ok write refuses the auth. client.ts — rpcCall, RpcConnection, verifyServerHello (serverSig against the registry's kernel key over the CLIENT-derived path), signAuth and connectGnomon (never sends auth to an unverified server; reason unverified-server). ROUND 2: both signatures also bind the negotiated clientApi + canonical features (downgrade-proofing; a deviation from the §4.9 preimage text, pending spec/contracts); the registry is cached by size+mtime+sha256; qualified matrix access (e.g. mod 'own view') is refused ENGINE not-implemented with its milestone, never the full view; hello/auth.ok log failures close the connection (fail rows are best-effort); pre-auth limits — no hello in 10 s or no auth by the 30 s nonce TTL closes, at most 64 pre-auth connections; flow control pauses reading at 32 queued requests or 1 MiB unsent replies; pre-auth diagnostics are coalesced into one signed counter row per window. ROUND 3: socket.hello and socket.auth.fail are rate-limited — the first 8 per 10 s window individually, the rest folded into that window's signed counter row (byOutcome / byReason); auth.ok/.replay stay individual; inbound frames capped at 16 KiB until auth succeeds; the client refuses a hello whose clientApi/features it did not offer (hello-not-offered, client-local); RegistryCache parses the bytes it hashed. Windows named pipe: parity phase (P8-D78). M1.4 SLICE 2 (log-read.ts): `log.read` and `ref.resolve` served for authenticated principals, each handled EXPLICITLY per reader class (never the generic 'full'): human → the §9.3 COMMUNITY-CLIENT projection (full minus sensitive and secret, sensitive-column kinds as {kind, hsid, at, hash} stubs, registered sensitive fields → {redacted, hash}) because a first-party surface / log.read:sensitive grant cannot be proven on the socket yet (result names projection + fullView.needs); mod → own modns.<name>.* + granted kinds (none yet); agent → UNSUPPORTED Move 2; voice → UNSUPPORTED Move 4; session → ENGINE not-implemented M1.7 (no principal → hsid binding); read tokens do not exist yet. Pages: {since, until?, kinds? (exact or ns.*), scope? {hsid, repo, loop, contract} applied to the PROJECTED view (a stub never matches a repo/loop/contract filter), limit? ≤ 1000} → {rows, next (last scanned seq, stable cursor), head, caughtUp, projection, withheld}; ≤ 10 000 rows scanned and ~2 MiB per page, a row > 1 MiB becomes {view: 'oversize', kind, hash, bytes}. Subscriptions (follow: true): reply {subscription, since, head, projection, backlogCap} written first (ctx.afterReply), then backlog + live rows as `event` notifications {subscription, row} in seq order, read lazily from the log; the pump writes only under the connection's write high-water mark and resumes on 'drain'; per subscription a queue of undelivered post-subscribe seqs (numbers only) — beyond 10 000 the subscription is dropped, the client gets event{subscription, end{reason:'dropped', lag, since}} and the kernel logs socket.subscription.dropped{subscription, lag, since} with the connId (deferred, never inside a commit); ≤ 8 subscriptions per connection, 256 per kernel; each holds the idle monitor ('subscriber'); subscriptions end with their connection. server.ts gains ctx.notify / writableLength / writeHighWater / onDrain / afterReply; client.ts RpcConnection.onNotification. status adds subscriptions{n, onThisConnection, perConnectionMax, backlogCap}. ROUND 2: limited views (community-client, mod, read-token) carry no hash/sig/prev, redacted fields are {redacted: true} and stubs {kind, hsid?, at} (no confirmation oracle; ref.resolve returns no hash to them); only rows at or below the log's RELEASED head are read or streamed (failed critical rows never); lag = committed head − cursor, a subscribe with head − since > 10 000 is BAD_REQUEST{backlog-too-large} (page first); the commit-path fan-out is one metadata check per subscriber (mayBeVisible + kind filter; no projection, copy or hash — projection happens lazily in the pump); writeHighWater is clamped to ≥ the socket's writableHighWaterMark; an unencodable frame ends the subscription with end{reason:'internal'}; follow on a JSON-RPC notification (no id) is refused follow-needs-id; queued requests of a closed connection never run (server `closed` flag) and dispatch refuses ENGINE{gone} for a closed ctx, so zombie pre-auth entries cannot fill maxPreAuth. ROUND 3: limited views also drop idem and refHash; lag = min(seq, released head) − cursor; subscribe admits at most cap/2 backlog measured against the released head (page until caughtUp, then follow). M1.4 SLICE 3 (round 2: P8-D89 / D89a): read tokens are PROOF OF POSSESSION — auth {tokenId, sig} (exactly those keys, after hello, inside the nonce TTL), sig = the token's Ed25519 key over gnomon:auth-token:v1 + contracts authTokenMessage(nonce, serverKeyId, tokenId, endpointPath, negotiated hello), verified against the public key in #identity's root-signed token file; a bearer {token} is auth-params; the seed never crosses the wire. The connection binds to the token's principal with credential 'read-token' and matrix class readToken: status, log.read (the §9.3 read-token projection), ref.resolve; every other verb and both relays FORBIDDEN{matrix}. Unknown / expired / not-yet-valid / revoked (sticky) / bad or replayed proof / in use (one live connection per token) / untrusted token file ⇒ AUTH + close; the token is re-checked on every call, at its expiry and every 5 s; a dead token closes the connection with a best-effort socket.disconnect{reason, tokenId}. A connection that closes during the awaited auth.ok write is refused ENGINE{gone} and gets no timers or lifted cap (timerCount() for tests). Rows carry only tokenId. connectGnomon({readToken}) validates options before connecting and proves possession only to a verified server. G-SOCK-01: a known verb before auth is AUTH and CLOSES the connection. log-append.ts — the §5 namespace-ownership gate (G-SOCK-04): unknown and kernel-owned kinds FORBIDDEN{kernel-owned} for every class, the human request.* exception too (needs: first-party human-class connection, unprovable until #web-endpoint); voice request.voice.arm and voice.* ENGINE Move 4; userland kinds FORBIDDEN{ungranted, M1.5 — grant.bind needs M1.3 grants over M1.5 manifests} for human/agent; a mod's own modns ENGINE M1.11, else modns-not-own; nothing is ever appended in M1.4. status adds credential, token{tokenId, expiresAt}, relay access, and nextLegalVerbs filtered to the caller's class. Preimages come from contracts (T-2026-10-17-017). abiId pinned in test/abi.ids.json (G-ABI-04). Suites: test/socket-abi.test.ts (G-ABI-01..05 incl. a literal §5 matrix fixture and the userland-namespace list, G-SOCK-02..04, the auth race; todos naming later milestones). ROUND 3: the PoP is verified before any token state is told (no valid proof ⇒ uniform unknown-token, no tokenId on the row); the daemon re-reads the token file at start and every 60 s (tokenRefreshMs) so revocations reach the chain with no live token connection, retrying a failed key.token.revoked write and keeping it pending (daemon.token.revocation.unrecorded event) — never dropped; every reason the kernel sends is registered (test/refusal-reasons.test.ts scans socket/, web/, refs/, redaction.ts). M1.4 #web-endpoint: auth.ts takes a `web` hook for {launchToken}/{reconnect} (credential 'gui', human class); on the unix socket those forms stay UNSUPPORTED web-auth-not-implemented. P8-D98 (T-2026-10-19-001 A0): the registry (methods.ts) also registers the three human-device verbs gui.open, rules.revoke and daemon.stop (human tier only, every other class false, deny by default); dispatch.ts refuses any non-human class FORBIDDEN{matrix}, refuses a human GUI launch-token connection the same way, and routes a human DEVICE connection to DispatcherOptions.humanVerbs (one handler module per verb, wired by the daemon so dispatch.ts does not change again) or ENGINE{not-implemented} when the port is absent; status lists them as humanDeviceVerbs. SERVER_FEATURES stays [] (no reserved hello feature advertised). abiId still hashes the twelve VERBS only.

web-endpoint.name: Web Endpoint
web-endpoint.description: #web-endpoint (spec §2.1, §4.9 WebSocket paragraph, §11.2, §15.5 `transport`, §2.4 linger; M1.4). The kernel half (src/kernel/web/) and the `gnomon-web` transport child (src/transport/). Listener (T-2026-10-18-020, §11.2 rule 1): the KERNEL listens on the 127.0.0.1 literal (OS-chosen ephemeral port, pauseOnConnect) and hands each accepted socket, unread, to the child with subprocess.send('conn', socket) over the child's IPC channel (stdio fd 3, WEB_CONN_MESSAGE); accept-and-forward only, so the child stays the only parser (A24-1). The listener outlives a child restart (same port); stop(), the restart cap and a failed respawn close it (the port is then ECONNREFUSED, and squattable by a local process, §A.7); a connection accepted while no child serves is closed. Hand-off bounds (round 2, Aegis C1): listener maxConnections WEB_MAX_PENDING_HANDOFFS = 128 (Node counts a socket until it is sent and queues later hand-offs behind an unACKed one); an ACK watchdog (handoffAckMs, default 5 s, ACKs seen via the undocumented 'internalMessage' NODE_HANDLE_ACK, FIFO) SIGKILLs a stalled child; any user IPC message and any internal one but NODE_HANDLE_ACK kills the child and closes an attached handle; an UNSOLICITED NODE_HANDLE_ACK (none in flight, or one more than sent) would make Node's own handler throw ERR_INTERNAL_ASSERTION in the daemon, so a prependListener (relies on the Node internal _handleQueue) gives Node an empty queue and kills the child (round 3); a failed send forgets its watchdog entry; a stop() during the exit-log write cancels the respawn and writes its stop row. Residual: Node's fd-3 JSON-line reader is unbounded (DoS-only, §A.7). A start that began before a stop() (stop generation counter) kills its child and never listens or writes a second socket.web.stop row; listenAddress() exposes the bound address. The CHILD listens on nothing and parses bytes only: node:http over the handed sockets (server.emit('connection')) with per-socket slowloris deadlines (a never-listening http.Server runs no headersTimeout/requestTimeout checker): headersTimeout 10 s from the hand-off and after each response, requestTimeout 30 s for the body; the ready record names no port (channel gnomon-web:v2), the RFC 6455 upgrade and zero-dep framing (ws-codec.ts: text only — binary 1003; no fragmentation — FIN=0/continuation 1009; no extension ever negotiated — RSV bits 1002; masking required 1002; invalid UTF-8 1007; >4 MiB 1009 from the header; close mirrored; pings every 30 s, closes after 2 missed pongs), and static serving of the bundle bytes it hashed at start (held in memory). It forwards {rid, method, path, headers} / {rid, data} records over stdio (protocol.ts) and writes back only what the kernel says; its import closure is framing + channel + bundle hash (test/seams-fence.test.ts). The KERNEL decides every rule (rules.ts): Host = 127.0.0.1:<port> else 421 (host) before routing; Origin = http://127.0.0.1:<port> on every upgrade and non-static request else 403 (origin); a present Sec-Fetch-Site same-origin|none else 403 (an absent one passes only an upgrade, and /diag and /blob, which then still need a live X-Gnomon-Token: Aegis finding 2); no cookies, no ACAO, the rule-6 CSP/COOP/CORP/nosniff/no-referrer on every response, no-store on non-static; traversal refused; /blob raster-only by content sniffing and verified content hash, GUI token in X-Gnomon-Token; /diag ≤ 64 KiB to <home>/logs/gui.log after redactDiagText (32-byte base64url tokens ⟨redacted⟩, contracts display sanitizer, Aegis C5); /blob and /diag are POST (a same-origin GET carries no Origin; the page sends them with referrerPolicy same-origin), GET/HEAD 405; /rpc and /diag match exactly, only /blob/ is a prefix; no HTTP RPC. Every child record is validated against the closed shape set (protocol.ts validateChildRecord) and the child is SIGKILLed on the first violation or on any throw in record handling (Aegis C1); a compromised child is a compromise of the GUI sessions it relays (spec §A.7). Child-written 503/404 carry the rule-6 default headers. Per connection: the child starts at a 16 KiB inbound cap, raised by a kernel `limit` record on authentication; unsent bytes are reported as pressure/drain (the dispatcher's writableLength/onDrain are per connection) and over 8 MiB the child closes 1008; more than 32 queued requests close 1008. Read tokens do not authenticate on the web endpoint (Aegis C3). WebSocket: hello then auth within 5 s else 1008, frames before auth never dispatched as verbs; ≤ 64 live (non-closing) connections, at the cap the oldest live unauthenticated one is closed (1013), never an authenticated GUI one (503 instead); ≤ 5 auth attempts/min/connection. Its own dispatcher (authenticator signs ws://127.0.0.1:<port>/rpc) with a `web` auth hook (launch.ts): a single-use 60 s launch token minted in-process for an authenticated human device connection (DaemonHandle.requestWebLaunch — §5 names no verb for `gnomon open`), exchanged for a 32-byte GUI token held as a digest; a second presentation inside the TTL is theft (refused, the consuming session revoked, socket.auth.theft + socket.gui.session.ended {theft}); after the TTL a replay (socket.auth.replay only); both answer `replayed-transcript`. Reconnect logs socket.auth.reconnect.requested and is refused UNSUPPORTED web-auth-not-implemented {milestone M1.3, cause presence-unavailable} until the signed helper's presence. GUI sessions live as long as their socket (≤ 12 h; revoke-all; daemon exit). Bundle pin (bundle.ts): gnomon-bundle-tree:v1 hash; since M1.10 slice 1 the #gui bundle (packages/gnomon-gui, embedded as opaque base64 in the GENERATED gui-bundle.ts, read by gui-pin.ts outside the child closure) pinned by the GUI_BUNDLE_HASH literal until the root-signed `gnomon gui pin` (M1.3), materialized under <home>/gui/bundle/ (the placeholder bundle stays a fixture); a mismatch logs socket.web.bundle.mismatch and never opens. Supervision: restart cap 3/10 min (socket.web.transport.exited, then socket.web.stop {transport-restart-cap}; a failed respawn ⇒ {transport-restart-failed}; both clear the timers); 2-min linger after the last GUI session (socket.web.linger, socket.web.stop{no-sessions}). Production spawn only through the platform's `transport` sandbox profile (#oracle-sandbox; on macOS that profile has no network-* rule, so the child opens no network socket of its own — every bind, listen and outbound connect is EPERM, P14b-web, T-2026-10-18-020); the unsandboxed child exists only via the internal seam `web` (testing.ts createWebEndpointForTest). Event kinds emitted (§9.1 socket namespace): socket.web.listen, socket.web.bundle.mismatch, socket.web.linger, socket.web.stop, socket.web.transport.exited, socket.gui.token.issued, socket.gui.session.ended, socket.auth.theft, socket.auth.replay, socket.auth.reconnect.requested, socket.auth.fail {origin|host|sec-fetch-site|gui-token}. The spec declares no signals.

oracle-sandbox.name: Oracle Sandbox
oracle-sandbox.description: #oracle-sandbox (spec §15.5) — the kernel's sandbox profiles. M1.4 lands the `transport` profile for gnomon-web (src/kernel/sandbox/ transport.ts): profile data, the darwin sandbox-exec SBPL generator (default-deny; read of `/`, /usr/lib, /System/Library, the node binary and its install's lib/ — never the prefix — plus Homebrew's Cellar, opt and etc/openssl@3; refused `sandbox-unavailable` if any granted read subpath equals or contains $HOME, the gnomon home or its keys dir (Aegis C2); the child's entry dir and package.json ancestors, the pinned bundle; metadata of their ancestors; sysctl-read; exec of node only; NO network-* rule at all (no bind, no inbound, no outbound — the kernel listens and hands connected sockets over the IPC channel, T-2026-10-18-020); no fork, no write, no mach-lookup; every path realpath'd; env empty; TRANSPORT_PROFILE v2). Platform registry TRANSPORT_BACKENDS (G-WIN-05): darwin only; win32 is the Windows parity phase (P8-D78); any platform without a backend refuses `sandbox-unavailable` (fail closed). Residuals: ancestor metadata is visible; node may re-exec itself; the child reads and writes the sockets it is handed. T-2026-10-18-017 (measured): SBPL accepts only `*` or `localhost` as a network host, and `(local ip "localhost:*")` matches every address configured on this host's interfaces (LAN and wildcards included), so no listen rule can be loopback-only. T-2026-10-18-020 (Aegis ruling) therefore removed every network-* rule: the kernel listens on 127.0.0.1 and passes the CONNECTED socket (never the listening fd, whose listen() would be re-checked). Falsifiers in web-sandbox.test.ts: every child bind/listen/UDP/outbound/unix attempt EPERM against an unsandboxed control; a handed socket serves HTTP + a WebSocket round trip; the en0 address at the endpoint port is refused; the SBPL names no network rule. The T-017 loopback-listen retry is gone (nothing left to flake). The other seven profiles land with their milestones (session M1.7, oracle M2.3, …).

ref-resolver.name: Ref Resolver
ref-resolver.description: #ref-resolver (spec §3.7, §4.4, §5 verb 12; M1.4 slice 2) — src/kernel/refs/resolve.ts, the kernel's read-only resolver for its built-in schemes. Served: `ev:<ULID>` → {ref, target: the §9.3 projected view for the caller's reader class, hash}; every row is re-hashed (mismatch ⇒ ENGINE{row-integrity}, withheld); a missing row and an invisible one are the same NOT_FOUND (no existence oracle); an @rev on an event is BAD_REQUEST. Validated then ENGINE{not-implemented, milestone}: turn:<hsid>/<n> and hsid: (M1.7), cc (M1.7), gkey/dev (M1.3), permit/card (M1.6), contract/node (M2.1), pev (Move 2 — the spec names none). UNSUPPORTED: peer: (only a brief's copy, §3.9), package schemes (no-resolver: userland), unknown schemes. Malformed refs, dropped schemes (voice) and refs over 512 chars are BAD_REQUEST.

identity.name: Identity
identity.description: #identity (spec §3.1; M1.4 slice of it — hardware custody is M1.3, blocked on the founder's provisioning profile). root-authority.ts — the RootAuthority seam: UnprovisionedRootAuthority is the production default (verifies nothing, signRow refuses UNSUPPORTED{root-unprovisioned, milestone M1.3}; never a software fallback); DevTestRootAuthority is a software P-256 root constructible only with the literal DEV_TEST_ROOT_ACK, never from env/argv (§15.3), reported as root state `dev-test` in status and daemon.start; RootVerifier verifies rows from a pinned root public key (the client side). Row sigs: gnomon:row-sig:v1 over canonical JSON, P-256 IEEE-P1363. device-key.ts — the Ed25519 device key at <home>/keys/device.key: written O_EXCL 0600, loaded only if a regular owner-only file in an owner-only keys/ dir; a device signer cannot approve. registry.ts — <home>/keys/registry.jsonl, append-only {row, signer, sig} rows (kind kernel | device); fail-closed reader: untrusted signer, bad signature, keyId ≠ sha256(PEM), principal or deviceId outside the root's ns, foreign principals and peer/kernel kinds never resolve and are surfaced in rejected[]; first row pins a deviceId and a keyId. The kernel principal is p:<root ns>/kernel, or p:00000000/kernel while no root exists (UNPROVISIONED_NS). kernel-pub.ts — PUBLIC halves of every kernel key the home ran with (<home>/keys/kernel-pub.jsonl, 0600), loaded into the log's key ring and kernelKeyIds so verify works across restarts; same-user writable and not root-signed, so across restarts kernel signatures prove nothing against a same-user forger until M1.3 (custody partial). presence.ts (T-2026-10-17-009(c), Aegis S34-10) — PresenceToken, a branded type minted only by this module: private constructor guarded by a module-private mint key, a `#state` private field and a `unique symbol` brand (nominal by type; `PresenceToken.is` is a `#state in v` runtime brand check no copy, prototype object or Proxy passes); bound to one purpose (`log.gap.acknowledge`; M1.5 adds `mod.install` and `mod.rollback`), single-use and fresh for 60 s (`consumePresence` → ok | not-a-token | wrong-purpose | stale | used). `requestPresence` refuses UNSUPPORTED{presence-unavailable, M1.3} until the signed helper's prompt exists; the only mint before then is the internal test seam (method `test-seam`). read-token.ts (M1.4 slice 3, P8-D89a) — <home>/keys/read-tokens.jsonl, append-only root-signed rows {op: mint, tokenId rtk:<26>, keyId, publicKeyPem, principalId (root ns, not kernel, not foreign), createdAt, expiresAt (default 1 h, ≤ 24 h)} and {op: revoke, tokenId}; PUBLIC keys only. mintReadToken (library only: no verb, no argv; now within 5 min of the real clock and clamped to it, so expiresAt ≤ real now + ttl) returns grt:v1:<id>.<seed> once; parseReadToken gives the client a readToken-class signer that signs only gnomon:auth-token:v1. ReadTokenStore: fail-closed reader; not valid before createdAt − 60 s; revocations STICKY for its life and seeded from key.token.revoked rows on the chain (daemon.ts records each newly seen revoke); the file must grow append-only — shrinking or a lost/rewritten line, or more than 1 MiB / 10 000 rows, makes it untrusted for the store's life (nothing resolves; key.registry.malformed{file, reason}). Open questions (spec silent; most restrictive reading chosen): the CLI verb that mints, the revocation re-check period. M1.3 slice 1 (hardware custody, the signed #gnomon-helper): helper.ts — pinHelper resolves the path once (realpathSync.native), refuses missing / non-executable / group- or world-writable files, verifies `codesign --verify --strict` + HELPER_REQUIREMENT (Developer ID Application, team SW4BMQ8PNL, identifier gnomon.helper), records inode/size/mtime/sha256 and RE-CHECKS them synchronously before every spawn; HelperProcess runs `gnomon-helper serve` (NDJSON, one request in flight, ≤ 16 queued, 1 MiB lines, timeouts kill it; out-of-order or oversized replies kill it — fail closed); SupervisedHelper restarts it on demand; helperOnceSync runs `once` for synchronous root signatures. The unsigned verifier exists only behind DEV_TEST_HELPER_ACK. Round 2: the pin is hash → verify → re-hash (H5); after spawn the RUNNING child is code-sign-verified by pid and must answer `info` with gnomon-helper:v2 (helper 1.6.0) and version ≥ MIN_HELPER_VERSION before any request (H1 c — a version floor, not a CDHash allowlist, because timestamped signatures change every build); the platform check is src/platform/helper-verifier.ts (R6); SupervisedHelper never restarts after close() and backs off 1 s doubling to 30 s (R5). hardware.ts — HardwareRootAuthority (state `hardware`; verifies with the pinned root; signRow sync via `once`, signRowAsync via the daemon's helper; fresh presence per signature; a signature that does not verify under the pinned root is refused); HelperApprovalsKey (ApprovalsKey whose decisionSig the helper makes after presence: fresh, optionally kept as the connId's cached unlock IN THE HELPER, or cached; the same touch signs a kernel presence challenge so the broker gets a bound `helper-se` PresenceToken; every helper signature verified before use; approver must be the key's human). presence.ts — production mint = hardware attestation: beginHardwarePresence (single-use challenge, ≤ 64 outstanding, 120 s) / completeHardwarePresence (mints only on a `gnomon:presence:v1` signature that verifies in the pinned ring). provision.ts — <home>/keys/identity.json (identity:v1, public only: gen, root key + ns, root-signed approvals binding to the human, device, helperPath) and keys/identity.jsonl journal; openHardwareIdentity opens it for gnomond only when the pinned helper confirms both SE public keys and the binding verifies under the root, else the daemon refuses to start (identity-<reason>), never a software root. cli/identity-cli.ts — `gnomon identity init` provisions the real root once (refused from a kernel-spawned shell, while the daemon runs, and when identity.json exists unless `--rotate` on a TTY with the typed confirmation, logged to stderr and a journal line signed by the OLD root; old registry moved aside as evidence, old SE keys retired): pins the helper, creates root + approvals in the SE under a fresh generation, two root signatures with presence (approvals binding, device row), identity.json last; a failure deletes the keys it made. Round 2: rotate needs the OLD root in the SE to sign a gnomon-root-rotate:v1 statement the helper demands before it creates the new generation (H4/H2); `--recover` (typed `recover`) replaces a LOST root with a new namespace, journalled as not signed by it; init asks the helper (key.list) and refuses while another generation is held; every touch's expected digest is printed (H3); the device row is signed first and appended only after identity.json (R3); a failure before the record restores moved files (R2) and deletes its keys via the live helper or a fresh one with presence (R4), never after; Ctrl-C stops at the next step and cleans up. `gnomon identity purge-keys --gen <g>` deletes another generation's keys, one touch each. registry.ts gains deviceRowFor + appendSignedRegistryRow. `gnomon identity status`. Founder hardware test: GNOMON_HW_TESTS=1 test/identity-hw.test.ts (it.todo in CI).

dev-launch.name: Dev Launch
dev-launch.description: #dev-launch (spec §2.4 rule 6) — the UNSIGNED, DEV-ONLY dogfood launch path until #identity M1.3. src/cli/dev-home.ts + src/cli/dev-cli.ts. `gnomon dev init [--home <abs>]` provisions a DEV home (default ~/.gnomon-dev): a software P-256 dev-test root (DevTestRootAuthority behind DEV_TEST_ROOT_ACK, persisted 0600 as keys/DEV-ONLY-root-p256.pem), a software kernel key (keys/DEV-ONLY-kernel-ed25519.pem), the device key and the root-signed registry rows for the kernel key and ONE human device (p:<ns>/founder); the marker DEV-ONLY-gnomon-home.json is written LAST. Refuses (falsifiers in test/dev-launch.test.ts): the production home ~/.gnomon, anything inside or containing it (production-home); a home holding a registry it did not write (production-root); any other non-empty unmarked home (home-not-empty). The production-home check (Aegis C1) covers ~/.gnomon lexically and realpath'd, its symlink target (dangling included), and on darwin compares case-folded (~/.GNOMON); a symlinked dev home is refused (unsafe-home). TRIPWIRE: gnomond (both paths) and `gnomon daemon start` refuse loudly a home holding the marker (daemon-cli.ts refuseDevHome). Loading (dev up) refuses a home without the ack-bearing marker (not-a-dev-home) and one whose keys do not match the marker or whose registry has ANY rejected row (dev-home-damaged). gnomond and a bare startDaemon never read these files: the production root stays unprovisioned (falsifier: device auth on a dev home without the dev root is refused root-unprovisioned). No command prints key material. `gnomon dev up [--home <abs>]` (startDevKernel) runs startDaemon IN THE CLI'S OWN PROCESS with the dev root and dev kernel key, connects as the registered human device through the published TS client (kernel key pinned, serverSig verified before the device signs), and mints the launch token through the existing in-process `gnomon open` path (DaemonHandle.requestWebLaunch, §11.2 rule 2; the web endpoint's rules are untouched). The URL is printed ONLY to an interactive terminal (a pipe or file gets the port and no token); Enter mints a fresh one (Reconnect is UNSUPPORTED until M1.3), q / Ctrl-C stop the kernel. The CLI's device connection is held open, so the kernel does not idle out while dev up runs. SMOKE (test/dev-launch-session.test.ts, darwin): dev init → startDevKernel → launch URL → a second device client → session.open on the FAKE claude under the real session profile → session.send → turn.result, with no approval card on the path. The one seam is the internal-seams `daemon` slot (lifecycle/daemon.ts registers it; only testing.ts's startDaemonForTest reads it): the supervisor's test-rig options (script claude, its path, a throwaway user home and env) and the fuse's law-7 billing source. A socket device connection is a community-client reader, so turn.event (the reply text) reaches it as {kind, hsid} stubs; the GUI's launch-token session is the first-party surface that sees it.

wrapper-channel.name: Wrapper Channel
wrapper-channel.description: #wrapper-channel (spec §19.1 M1.13 row, Appendix A; G-GUI-12, G-WEB-01..06, G-GUI-03) — the gnomon-wrapper-channel:v1 launch contract between Gnomon.app (#gnomon-wrapper) and `gnomon up --wrapper` / `gnomon dev up --wrapper`. The app spawns `node --disable-sigusr1 <gnomon.js> up --wrapper` with a clean env; the child writes NDJSON on its stdout pipe (up, launch{port, launchToken, kernelPublicKey, bundleHash, expiresAt}, launch-failed, refused{code, reason, message, next}, down) and reads `launch` | `quit` on stdin (EOF = quit). The token is on that pipe only. Child side: src/cli/launch-tty.ts (serveWrapperChannel, wrapperChannelProblem, channelRefused, WRAPPER_LAUNCH_CAP 8/min with one mint in flight, stopping re-checked after each mint, WRAPPER_UNSAFE_ENV_NEXT). Wrapper side: packages/gnomon-wrapper/src/contract.rs (parse_line, read_line_capped at 64 KiB, redacting Debug).

update-watch.name: Update Watch
update-watch.description: #update-watch (TD-2026-10-19-063, flow 2) — self-update pickup. The build writes dist/build-id.json {version, commit, distHash, guiBundleHash} (scripts/build-stamp.mjs); at boot the kernel writes <home>/kernel-build.json (0600) with what it loaded (lifecycle/build-stamp.ts). lifecycle/update-watch.ts polls the stamp on the configured cadence UPDATE_POLL_MS (30 s) and, once per distinct new stamp, the kernel raises its OWN daemon-stop{reason:'upgrade'} card (broker/daemon-stop.ts raiseUpgrade, UPGRADE_CARD_TIMEOUT_MS 24 h, first line "Gnomon was updated: v→v′ (commit)"; at most one per UPGRADE_CARD_COOLDOWN_MS 1 h per kernel (Aegis L); it shares the one-card slot with a launcher's daemon.stop{reason:'upgrade'}). Accept takes one Touch ID (F3), drains (§2.4 rule 11), releases the lock and socket, and runForeground spawns ONE detached successor (lifecycle/successor.ts: reexecArgs + cleanReexecEnv + --prefer-port <old web port>, 127.0.0.1 only, exclusive; a taken port falls back and status reports web.portFallback). The helper binary is watched on the same tick (identity/helper.ts HelperRepin): changed + nothing in flight ⇒ re-pinned through pinHelper and `serve` recycled, no card; unsigned, unverifiable or not holding this identity's keys ⇒ fail closed.

gui-resume.name: Gui Resume
gui-resume.description: #gui-resume (TD-2026-10-19-063, founder ruling "ONE Touch ID") — the `{resumeToken}` web auth form (kernel/web/resume.ts). Minted only when an upgrade card is accepted from a live GUI session: 32 random bytes sent to THAT connection alone (gui.resume notification); the digest, bound to the session's principal, device id and root ns, is handed to the successor on its STDIN pipe together with its kernel key (Aegis M: never a file; a record planted in the home is never read, and none is read without --kernel-key-stdin). The successor serves on the old kernel's listening socket, inherited as fd 3 (--web-listen-fd), so the port is never unbound (Aegis H); on any other port the record is dropped. The GUI checks the successor signs a fresh nonce with the delivered key before it reloads. Refused if malformed, expired or with a TTL above RESUME_TOKEN_TTL_MS 60 s; accepted ONCE: replay, expiry, a device no longer that principal's human device, or another root ns are refused; RESUME_MAX_MISSES wrong tokens burn it. It authenticates a GUI connection only — never presence, never a card decision.

bare-entry.name: Bare Entry
bare-entry.description: #bare-entry (spec §2.4 rule 8) — bare `gnomon` in a folder, like `claude`: src/cli/bare-cli.ts runs #gnomon-up's runUp (every guard unchanged and in order: unsafe-env, unprovisioned → `next: gnomon identity init`, dev-home, …) with refusal code GNOMON and a FOLDER HINT — folderOf(cwd) = the nearest ancestor holding .git, else the cwd (said so) — carried ONLY as a launch URL fragment parameter `&cwd=<base64url utf-8>` appended after the token on the same TTY line (launch-tty.ts printLaunch urlSuffix; never argv, env, a file, the wrapper channel or another line; over HINT_MAX_BYTES 1024 it is not carried). displayPath escapes every code point that is not a letter, number, punctuation, symbol or plain space, plus Cf, default-ignorables (fillers, variation selectors, tags), U+FFFD and backslash, as \u{..}, and caps at 240 code points (shared vectors test/fixtures/cwd-hint.v1.json, Aegis L3); the GUI (#gui, core/launch.ts cwdHintOf/applyCwdHint) applies the same rule, prefills only a clean absolute path and never submits. A kernel already running on the home: no second one starts. On an interactive terminal bare `gnomon` asks it for a launch grant over the P8-D98 human-device verb `gui.open {cwdHint}` (up-cli.ts requestRunningLaunch: this home's device key + root-signed human row checked like startUpKernel's deviceOf, the kernel hello verified against the home's pin via kernelPinOf, then device auth; T-2026-10-19-001 A3) and prints/opens that URL with the same `&cwd=` fragment (ATTACHED readout). Not a terminal: the TTY check runs BEFORE the RPC, nothing on stdout, no gui.open call, `REFUSED GNOMON already-running`, exit 3 (BARE_EXIT_ALREADY_RUNNING), naming the instance from the pidfile pid classified via `ps -o command=` (diagnostic only). The kernel side is #socket src/kernel/socket/gui-open.ts (createGuiOpenHandler, wired in DispatcherOptions.humanVerbs by the daemon): verified human device only; cwdHint ≤ 1024 UTF-8 bytes else BAD_REQUEST{cwd-hint-too-long}, returned verbatim, never read or logged; the grant is the in-process requestWebLaunch's (single-use, at most 60 s) under the ONE shared launch-grant cap src/kernel/web/launch-cap.ts (LaunchGrantCap on WebEndpoint.requestLaunch: one in flight, 8 a minute across the terminal, the wrapper channel and gui.open — shared, not added on top; ENGINE{web-launch-capped}). Fairness (Aegis M2): gui.open is a `socket` asker that may hold at most LAUNCH_GRANT_SOCKET_SHARE (4) of the 8 window slots, so the in-process asker (terminal, wrapper) always keeps the rest; a socket mint in flight (a cold start) makes ONE in-process asker wait and go next, never refuses it; a mint that throws refunds its slot (the token is the mint's last throwing step). The human-device verbs are UNIX-SOCKET ONLY (Aegis L1): the daemon builds them as their own `humanVerbs` object and hands it only to the unix dispatcher (daemon.ts dispatcherOptionsFor), so the web dispatcher reports them unavailable and refuses them. A grant whose caller's connection closed during the mint is withdrawn (GuiAccess.withdraw via WebEndpoint.withdrawLaunch, Aegis L2), never left pending. Falsified in test/gui-open.test.ts and test/human-device-verbs.test.ts. Hardening: requestRunningLaunch refuses a gui.open grant whose url fails isOpenableUrl (gui-open-bad-grant) and sanitizes the server's refusal text (sanitizeDisplayText); bare entry builds `&cwd=` from its own capped folder, never the kernel's echoed cwdHint (Aegis L3, L4). log.read's one-page since-ahead is judged against releasedHead(), as subscribe does (Aegis L6). Also `gnomon help|--help|-h` (GNOMON_HELP, one line per verb) and an unknown verb → usage exit 64 without echoing it. scripts/install-darwin.mjs is the idempotent installer (build, link `gnomon` into /opt/homebrew/bin or /usr/local/bin, refuse a non-symlink or a link elsewhere, NODE_OPTIONS check, next steps; no sudo, never touches ~/.gnomon). AUTO-OPEN (spec §2.4 rule 10): src/cli/open-browser.ts openInDefaultBrowser hands every terminal launch/setup URL to the default browser via LaunchServices — it runs /usr/bin/osascript - (absolute, no shell, EMPTY env) and writes `open location "<url>"` on its STDIN, so the token is on no argv or env (`open <url>` is forbidden: argv is readable by ps); the URL is validated first (loopback, fragment [A-Za-z0-9_=&%.-] only), 5 s timeout, never throws. The TTY shows `opened in your browser` with the URL kept below as the fallback, or the old copy line on failure / non-darwin. Covers bare `gnomon`, `gnomon up`, `gnomon setup`, the Enter fresh URL, the setup re-link on expiry and the setup→up hand-off. Off with `--no-open` (all three verbs) or GNOMON_NO_OPEN=1; never without a TTY; never on the wrapper channel (`up --wrapper`).

provisioner.name: Provisioner
provisioner.description: #provisioner (spec §3.1 Provisioner; T-2026-10-19-005 MVP-a) — the ONE engine behind `gnomon identity init|--rotate|--recover|purge-keys` (identity-cli.ts, a thin renderer, byte-identical output) and the guided #first-run (and the GUI setup phase, MVP-b). An EventEmitter with an AbortSignal: events step / presence {n, of, purpose, digest12} / done / aborted; it renders nothing. Enforces Aegis I1 (a root signature is accepted only when the helper's own prompt line, reply.shown, names the digest shown: helperLineShows; HardwareRootAuthority.signRowShown), I5 (helper path pinned, from the caller default or identity.json), I6 (a generation it did not create is never adopted; purgeGeneration takes presence per key), I7 (ROOT_PROMPT_BUDGET init 2 / rotate 3 / recover 2 / complete 0), I8 (O_EXCL `<home>.provisioning.lock`, provisioning-locked, before key.list), I9 (pre-commit failure restores moved files and deletes only keys it created), I10 (after identity.json, keys are never deleted; completeDevice() appends the device row the root signed during that provisioning, saved in identity.json as pendingDeviceRow with deviceKeyId — verified under the root, keyId === device key on disk === deviceKeyId, deviceId/principalId === the record's; ZERO new signatures, budget 0; no saved row → no-saved-device-row, use --rotate; Aegis HIGH-1), I12 (validates name/host itself).

setup-endpoint.name: Setup Endpoint
setup-endpoint.description: #setup-endpoint (spec §11.2 rule 11, §2.4 rule 9; T-2026-10-19-005 MVP-b) — the SETUP MODE loopback endpoint: a #web-endpoint (same gnomon-web transport child, rules.ts, 127.0.0.1 only, the SAME pinned #gui bundle) whose dispatcher is the closed gnomon-setup:v1 protocol (gnomon-contracts setup.ts, own SETUP_API_ID; clientApiId unchanged): hello / auth {setupToken} / setup.preflight / setup.name / setup.begin / setup.purge {gen} / setup.complete (I10, the saved row, 0 prompts) / setup.finish, events setup.state and setup.presence {n,of,purpose,digest12}. No gnomon-rpc verb is reachable. An ephemeral Ed25519 setup key signs serverSig. One setup connection; a closed socket aborts the #provisioner at its next step boundary. Exact params key sets: the page carries only name, a server-listed gen, and clicks. Entry: bare gnomon / gnomon setup on a TTY print the setup URL (and every expected digest: the terminal is the surface to trust); gnomon setup --cli keeps the prompts; up --wrapper emits {t:setup,...} and then continues into {t:up}. Falsified in test/setup-endpoint.test.ts (G-SET-08..14) and test/wrapper-channel.test.ts. Never hangs: it settles on finish (also for an already-set-up home), token expiry, a 10 min idle cap, socket close, transport stop or token reuse; a refused purge (GNOMON_HOME guard, in-use / identity-malformed) or a failed begin returns to the checks. The checks are read-only: setup state lives in a private scratch dir and the home is created at begin. stop() removes that scratch dir BEFORE it waits for a running step, so the wrapper's quit / stdin EOF (Gnomon.app Cmd-Q, which kills the kernel at most 10 s later) cleans it even with a Touch ID prompt held open; an EOF that came before waitSetup listened also stops it. A failed rm (e.g. EACCES) never rejects stop(); the next run sweeps it.

setup-preflight.name: Setup Preflight
setup-preflight.description: #setup-preflight (spec §2.4 rule 9) — READ-ONLY first-run checks (no key, no file write, no prompt; only key.list): helper signed+pinned and not from a sandboxed shell, touch-id (helper 1.4.0 presence.available: LAContext canEvaluatePolicy, never a prompt; pass or fail), macos, sip (csrutil; off = warn), claude (resolved, pin none/match/mismatch → `gnomon session repin-claude`), law-7 billing env, runtime (NODE_OPTIONS / node flags), node floor, leftover generations (purge, never adopt), home state (dev marker, symlink, malformed identity.json: shown, never touched). Each check {id, status pass|warn|fail, detail, fix}. INFORMATIVE only (Aegis I12): #provisioner and #gnomon-up enforce on their own.

first-run.name: First Run
first-run.description: #first-run (spec §2.4 rule 9) — the guided first run. Default: the setup SCREENS (#setup-endpoint, #gui-setup; `gnomon setup` and bare `gnomon` print a one-shot setup URL and every expected digest, the terminal being the surface to trust; Gnomon.app runs it in its window). `gnomon setup --cli` keeps the plain readline prompts (no in-terminal UI, P8-D51): welcome paragraph, #setup-preflight results with fixes, leftover generations offered for purge, a name prompt prefilled from $USER (PRINCIPAL_NAME_PATTERN, re-checked by #provisioner), "exactly 2 Touch ID prompts; a third is an attack", then 1 of 2 / 2 of 2 each preceded by the expected digest shown big and grouped on the terminal (I2), a summary (root keyId, principal, device, files) and the hand-off to #gnomon-up's runUp in the same process. Bare `gnomon` (#bare-entry) on a TTY with an unprovisioned default home runs it first, then continues with the folder hint. Home strict (I4: never GNOMON_HOME, lstat, symlink refused — the raw `gnomon identity init` still honours GNOMON_HOME/--home). Gated by ^unprovisioned-only. `up` / `up --wrapper` unprovisioned refusals now name the first run. On a terminal each setup URL (and each re-link after expiry) is also opened in the default browser (#bare-entry's open-browser.ts, osascript stdin; `gnomon setup --no-open` or GNOMON_NO_OPEN=1 prints only, and --no-open carries into the up hand-off); the wrapper path never opens.

gnomon-up.name: Gnomon Up
gnomon-up.description: #gnomon-up (spec §2.4 rule 7) — `gnomon up [--home <abs>] [--wrapper]`, the production counterpart of `gnomon dev up`: the REAL-HOME GUI launcher. M1.13 (#gnomon-wrapper): `--wrapper` (also on `gnomon dev up`) is the mode Gnomon.app spawns: launch-tty.ts serveWrapperChannel speaks gnomon-wrapper-channel:v1 NDJSON on stdout (up / launch{port, launchToken, kernelPublicKey, bundleHash, expiresAt} / launch-failed / refused{code,reason,message,next} / down) and reads `launch` | `quit` on stdin (EOF = quit); human lines go to stderr; a stdout or stdin that is a terminal or a regular file is refused `wrapper-channel` before any kernel starts. The token is on that pipe only — never argv, env, a file or a log (test/wrapper-channel.test.ts, P07-style ps argv+env sampler with a positive control). src/cli/up-cli.ts; the in-process launcher and terminal loop are shared with #dev-launch in src/cli/launch-tty.ts (attachInProcess, printLaunch, serveInProcess: one copy of the launch rules). Runs startDaemon IN THE CLI'S OWN PROCESS on a PROVISIONED home (default ~/.gnomon; never GNOMON_HOME, like gnomond) with the hardware identity opened by openHardwareIdentity — the same path gnomond takes (root + approvals key behind the pinned signed helper; the helper is closed on every failure and at shutdown) — connects as the home's registered human device (loadDeviceCredential: one owner-only read) with the kernel key pinned in-process, and mints the launch token through DaemonHandle.requestWebLaunch. URL ONLY to an interactive terminal; Enter re-mints; q / Ctrl-C stop. Approvals from the GUI: broker → HelperApprovalsKey.signDecision (fresh presence, Touch ID) → decisionSig + helper-se presence token. DESIGN (lore): in-process, NOT `gnomon open` against a running gnomond — that needs a new wire verb and moves clientApiId. GUARDS on a home resolved once (lstat plain directory, then realpath), each with a falsifier in test/up-cli.test.ts: FIRST (Aegis C1, also in dev up) a non-empty NODE_OPTIONS or any node interpreter flag (process.execArgv) other than exactly --disable-sigusr1, or that flag MISSING (T-2026-10-18-030: the bin shebang `env -S node --disable-sigusr1` passes it) → unsafe-env — refused, not re-executed, so no second process holds the helper (scope: an AMBIENT unsafe runtime, not a hostile preload already running as the user); a stdout/stderr 'error' (EIO after SIGHUP) is handled as a stop so the shutdown sweep runs; the device key opens O_NONBLOCK (a swapped-in FIFO cannot hang it, test/device-key-fifo.test.ts); missing home / no identity.json → unprovisioned; symlink / non-directory → unsafe-home; DEV-ONLY marker → dev-home; a live pidfile holder or an answering socket → daemon-running (and the O_EXCL lock as backstop); any IdentityError → identity-<reason> (fail closed); a registry row this root does not verify → registry-damaged; a device key without its matching human row → device-unregistered. Never prints a key or a token. Known gap: the kernel key is still ephemeral per start with no root-signed row, so OTHER socket clients report serverVerified:false (the keystore item). Seams (UpDeps: start, verifier, startHelper, userHome) are programmatic only; gnomon.ts passes none (falsifier). END TO END (test/up-launch-session.test.ts, darwin): identity init with the FakeHelper → gnomon up → launch URL → the GUI WebSocket authenticates with the launch token → session.open on the fake claude raises a plan card → GUI approve → one helper prompt → approval.decide{presence:fresh, via:gui} whose decisionSig verifies under the approvals key.

manifest-loader.name: Manifest Loader
manifest-loader.description: #manifest-loader, the Desk (TD-2026-10-20-812). manifest.ts: provides.offers (offer-spec:v1 from gnomon-contracts, at most 6, unique kinds, needs a provides.mcp server since reach is mcp) and 'offers' in WIDENING_FIELDS (key kind@phase→handoffTool; a text-only change is no widening); a provides.mcp entry may declare a closed per-user override surface config{command?:true, args?:true, env?:[names]} (env names never PATH/HOME/NODE_OPTIONS/… nor LD_/DYLD_/ANTHROPIC_/ CLAUDE_/GNOMON_/NPM_CONFIG_/GIT_; a config is part of the mcp widening key); validateMcpUserConfig + resolveMcpLaunch admit only what it declares, under COMMAND_UNSAFE (first-party servers launch as node <absolute path> from other repos; a user-set command is an absolute path, spawn with shell:false). Env names: MCP_ENV_DENY + MCP_ENV_DENY_PREFIXES (Aegis M1), and below first-party <NAME>_* or *_API_KEY / *_TOKEN only. Each offer contextIn source is its own widening key (kind:in:src). Not yet wired into a launch path. RESERVED_MOD_NAMES (kernel, gnomon, system, paradigm, claude, …; NAME at every tier), FIRST_PARTY_MOD_NAMES and FIRST_PARTY_NAME_PREFIXES (gnomon-, paradigm-, claude-, anthropic-) first-party only. install.ts surfaceOf: one 'offer:' card line per offer and a 'user may set:' suffix on an mcp line; both absent when undeclared, so pre-812 card detail hashes are unchanged. #manifest-loader + policy (spec §3.6, §4.3, §12.5, §15.4, §15.5, §15.7, §16; §19.1 M1.5). src/kernel/manifest/. manifest.ts — manifest:v1 validation, producer-strict and fail-closed (wire form: the JSON subset of the §4.3 YAML in gnomon-manifest.json, zero deps): unknown keys and trust:/source:/postinstall refused; kind: mod needs abi mod-abi:v1, an unknown abi refused; a name equal to a kernel namespace token refused; kind adapter/provider first-party only, a provider ships only provides.knowledge; tool effects ⊆ read|write|network|spend; card.* and status.mod slots append-only; events under modns.<name>.*; keybindings bind declared commands, never the reserved decision keys; capabilities are §15.4 forms (approve/band:write never; voice.approve:<class> never from a manifest; knowledge:federate/link:send first-party only; log.append only on its own modns); provides.knowledge needs knowledge:provide and never egress. manifestHash = sha256(canonical JSON); detectWidening = additions by field (effects, egress, capabilities, events, tools, views, commands, keybindings, knowledge). egress.ts — Anthropic hosts (anthropic.com, claude.ai, claude.com and subdomains, and any wildcard covering them) refused in manifests and grant rows (G-MAN-01). snapshot.ts — the snapshot copier: copies a package or linked folder to <home>/mods/<name>/pinned/<hex>/ (owner-only, read-only), packageHash over the sorted tree of the COPY (exact bytes, .git skipped unread), refusing symlink/junction, hardlink (nlink > 1), .node addon, a path escaping the folder, special files, case-colliding paths and a swap between walk and read (fstat dev/ino), emitting mod.snapshot.refused + manifest.refuse{SNAPSHOT}; lockfile rule (node_modules needs an npm lockfile, the card lists every package@version; other formats refused, LOCKFILE); lifecycle install scripts refused (POSTINSTALL); diffTrees for the re-approve card. grants.ts — <home>/grants.jsonl, root-signed rows through the RootAuthority seam (production refuses until M1.3), fail-closed reader (unsigned, untrusted signer, bad signature, unknown kind, malformed, Anthropic egress, egress beside knowledge:provide → rejected[]); grant.install carries `name` beside the §15.4 fields; the effective pin is the last grant.install row. install.ts — stageInstall (package or linked) raises a PENDING card:v1 kind install with its detail (name, source, tier, effects, egress, capabilities, events, tools, views, read paths, package@version list, widening, file diff, stagedBy) and signs nothing (manifest.staged). The kernel-composed line `runs commands: N mcp server(s), M hook(s)` follows the packageHash line, before any manifest-controlled line (Aegis round 2 C2); mcp.command, mcp.args, hooks.command and hooks.event refuse SCHEMA on C0/C1, Zl, Zp and Cf (U+2028/U+2029 would otherwise draw a fake card line, C1); a linked source whose realpath has such a character is refused SCHEMA at stage and INTEGRITY at re-derivation, and the header is one display line (version and source middle-truncated for display; contentHash keeps the full detail), so the count line is always index 2 (Aegis round 3). The card's lines put every mcp server and every hook on its OWN line and are sanitized and WRAPPED by code points under the broker's MAX_LINE (continuations `  ↳ `), never cut, so a long mcp argument list cannot push a hook out of sight; the sanitizer flags travel with the lines (blockFor → rederiveInstallDetail → the broker), and contentHash still covers the full detail (T-2026-10-18-015 item 2); loadMod loads only from a pinned snapshot under a root-signed grant.install, re-hashes it (INTEGRITY), checks grants, and for a linked folder re-hashes the source: a change pauses the mod (mod.paused) and stages one re-approve card (manifest.widened when widened). The card DECISION and the human rollback (re-pin a previously approved snapshot, mod.rolled-back) are module-private and registered only on the internal seam channel (slot `manifest`), reached only through src/kernel/testing.ts (decideInstallCard, rollbackModSnapshot) until the M1.6 approval broker owns cards; both need a PresenceToken (mod.install / mod.rollback) and a signing root. layers.ts — layersHash (managed, user settings*.json + CLAUDE.md + skills/plugins/agents/commands listings, project and worktree .claude/** + CLAUDE.md + CLAUDE.local.md) and gitHash (.git/config, hooks/**, info/** in the common dir, a worktree's .git file followed, .gitattributes), CRLF→LF and case-folded NFC path keys on every platform (G-WIN-04). policy.ts — the per-session policy DATA for the `session` profile (keys/Warpline-token/browser read denies, ~/.gnomon + settings layers + linked folders write denies, endpoint-port loopback deny, process-info deny-others, launchers deny; realpath'd; policyHash) and the matching policy.json permissions block — the platform profile is generated by M1.7. generate.ts — plugin.json, .mcp.json, hooks.json and .gnomon/.gitignore from a kind: distro manifest into the repo's .gnomon/, each with a marker and a ledger; a fixed point; never overwrites a file that is not ours; uninstallRepo removes exactly the ledger's unedited files and the dirs it created (project.yaml stays); uninstallHome removes ~/.gnomon or returns it as the export path. ROUND 2 (review + Aegis F1–F11): generate.ts confines every path to the fixed generated set under <repo>/.gnomon (lstat each component, refuse links/junctions, realpath inside .gnomon, temp file O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW + rename) and keys ownership on the manifestHash marker plus the kernel-held record <home>/generated/<sha256(realpath repo)>.json (the repo holds no ledger); the session policy write-denies the whole ~/.claude/** and ~/.claude.json (both also hashed into layersHash — a gap in spec §3.3/§15.5 to amend) and .git/hooks|config|info (gitHash inputs; §15.5 amendment), and carries the platform-neutral deny classes (tmux/screen sockets, helper IPC, sysmond, AppleEvents, service manager, mic/camera, launchers) mapped per platform in src/platform/session-denies.ts; widening covers mcp and hooks and the card lists commands, keybindings, knowledge, mcp, hooks and opaque array counts; the lockfile rule is case-folded, applies at any depth and cross-checks shipped package.json versions; the tier is derived (linked ⇒ local, first-party only from a bundled packageHash allowlist, empty for now; a signed claim is refused until trusted keys exist); decideInstall validates the cardId, recomputes contentHash, re-derives the detail from the pinned snapshot, appends grant.install LAST and is idempotent; egress refuses ports, numeric hosts, single labels and local/private names; symlinked layers hash the target bytes and .claude/worktrees/ is excluded. The case-collision oracle is exercised on Linux CI (a case-insensitive FS cannot hold the pair). Events: §9.1 kinds only (manifest.*, mod.*); the spec declares no signals. Refusals are refusal:v1 with data.manifestCode (not data.reason, which would move clientApiId).

kernel-log.name: Kernel Log
kernel-log.description: #kernel-log (spec §3.2, M1.2; research 29 §4 PR-4) — the one hash-chained, append-only, segmented kernel log. node:sqlite; active segment <home>/kernel.db, sealed segments <home>/log/segments/NNNNNN.db (0600, dirs 0700; read-denied to every session by the session profile, T-2026-10-18-010); a session reader (redaction.ts) sees only its own hsid rows at every label, and voice.turn.*.audioRef never (SESSION_NEVER_FIELDS, limited view); `chain` table per §3.2 plus a write-once `meta`; BEFORE UPDATE/DELETE triggers abort (L1). hash = sha256(canonical(envelope minus hash, sig)), prev(1) = sha256("gnomon-log-genesis:" + logId), seq computed inside the write txn and checked against the in-memory tip. Envelope = contracts event:v1, validated strict with default-label check; unregistered kinds refused (never guessed), labels tighten-only (L6), kernel/userland ownership enforced (L7), daemon.segment reserved to the log, session.inject must carry {origin, hash, bytes}; session.compacted (T-2026-10-18-016, P8-D93) must pass contracts validateSessionCompactedPayload (closed, typed) else bad-payload; replay folds its summaryHash as a RECORDED host hash. Signer seam (signer.ts): Signer.sign(domain, message) prepends the §3.1 domain (gnomon:event-sig:v1 etc.), key classes limited to their domains; SoftwareEd25519Signer = the in-memory kernel key (keyId gkey:v1:<sha256(spki PEM)>); root/approvals keys are hardware-only and plug in after probes P04/P02; KeyRing verifies Ed25519 and P-256. Unsigned rows only for daemon/socket/schedule; the §3.2 mandatory list refuses unsigned (unsigned-mandatory). Segments rotate at 10⁶ rows with a signed daemon.segment closing row and an unbroken chain across files; crash mid-rotation is completed on open. Anchors: file <home>/head (atomic tmp+rename; fsync only at genesis/rotation/close) and a KeystoreAnchorStore SEAM that reports `unavailable` until the helper exists (AnchorStore.write may be async; keystore writes are serialised). ANCHOR POLICY (anchor-policy.ts; research 33 S33-05..07, P8-D82): `append` is async and resolves {seq, hash, anchored, event}. Bulk rows coalesce the file anchor (renamed when 63 rows are un-anchored or 50 ms after the first, unref'd timer + inline check, and on checkpoint) and queue the keystore anchor every 1023 rows / 1 s off the append path. CRITICAL_ANCHOR_KINDS (approval.decide/suspect/presence.denied/ rule.learned/voice.arm/voice.disarm, key.*, grant.*, config.*, manifest.*, billing.*, verdict.*, link pair/renew/revoke, session.inject{origin:'peer'}, socket.auth.theft) commit with the bulk durability (no fullfsync since S33-10 / P8-D83), then rename the file anchor, then AWAIT the keystore write (it starts only after COMMIT returned), and only then resolve {anchored: true}; no effect may be released before that (a failed keystore write rejects ENGINE{anchor-failed}). This is an ordering guarantee against a same-user process, not a power-loss guarantee. Close writes durable anchors (file AND keystore) carrying the clean-close marker `closed: true`; open rewrites them without. BOOT SESSION (boot.ts, S33-10): every anchor records `boot` = kern.bootsessionuuid (macOS, spawned /usr/sbin/sysctl once per process) / boot_id (Linux) / `unknown` (Windows until the parity phase); only the keystore copy is authoritative. An anchor ahead of the db is INTEGRITY_BROKEN{truncated} with data.cause `tamper` (same boot, clean close, or no comparable keystore boot — fails closed) or `unclean-reboot` (boot changed, not a clean close); a forged file-anchor boot/closed changes nothing. The recovery open (an internal seam, see SEAM HARDENING) opens such a log refusing every append and writing no anchor; acknowledgeGap ({presenceToken}) (a branded PresenceToken, identity/presence.ts; unclean-reboot only) appends one kernel-signed daemon.log.gap{lostFrom, lostTo, lostHash, bootPrev, bootNow, fileLag} (contracts kind added, reserved to the log) and re-anchors durably; the chain verifies across it.
