ROUND-2 HARDENING (research 33 S34-xx): every non-recovery open re-stamps the keystore anchor with the current boot and the first append waits for it (S34-01; cause semantics = "power loss OR tampering"); non-ahead anchors get the full check even in recovery, and a file-only lead with a present keystore cannot be acknowledged (FORBIDDEN{unauthenticated-lead}, S34-04); any lag behind a clean-close KEYSTORE anchor is anchor-lag (S34-05); acknowledgeGap leaves recovery only after both anchors succeed (S34-12) and rotates a daemon.segment tip first (S34-13). ANCHOR FAULTS (S34-02): a post-COMMIT failure on a critical row (file anchor, rotation, keystore reject or `keystoreTimeoutMs` timeout, default 5 s, S34-11) rejects ENGINE{anchor-failed} and faults the log — bulk continues, critical appends re-anchor first or refuse ENGINE{anchor-faulted}; on recovery one kernel-signed daemon.anchor.failed{seq, kind} per failed row is appended (contracts kind added, reserved); projections must treat that seq as not having taken effect. `append` resolves anchored false | 'both' | 'file-only' (stub keystore), also in anchorStatus.anchoring (S34-03); live `integrity` getter (ok | truncated | anchor-faulted); close() resolves a CloseReport surfacing a failed keystore write. Verify (S34-06): daemon.log.gap / daemon.segment / daemon.anchor.lag / daemon.anchor.failed / socket.auth.theft are signature-mandatory, and kernel-principal rows must carry a kernel key id (signer + kernelKeyIds) — failure code `kernel-key`. Boot ids are validated as UUIDs; sysctl is spawned with an empty env (S34-09). ROUND 3: the daemon.anchor.failed marker is committed IMMEDIATELY in the post-commit failure path (durable fault, S34-17); the fault clears only when every failed row has a marker AND both anchors cover a head at/after it (S34-19); close() records pending markers before its closing anchors and reports `fault` (none|recovered|pending) in CloseReport; on open every critical row above the keystore anchor without a marker gets one. An interrupted acknowledgeGap (tip = kernel-signed daemon.log.gap naming the keystore head as lostTo/lostHash) is re-anchored on open and openForRecovery. RESERVED_KINDS exported; verify binds reserved-kind rows to the kernel principal + key (`reserved-binding`) and VerifyReport.kernelBinding is ok|failed|not-checked (standalone verify without kernel identity) — S34-18. Keyless logs are non-rotating and diagnostic-only: the boundary append and open-time lag/marker rows refuse before commit with FORBIDDEN{kernel-key-required} (S34-22). Boot ids are normalised on both sides; `unknown` is not cached and emits onDiagnostic `boot.unknown` (S34-21). `fileAnchorMaxMs` test seam (S34-23). Keystore timeout runs from dequeue; while a timed-out write is unsettled new writes refuse at once (order kept, no hang). KNOWN GAPS — DECIDED: (a) P8-D84 — accepted dev-only until T-2026-10-17-009: with the stub keystore (until M1.3) every truncation classifies `tamper` and cannot be acknowledged — a no-recovery window; recovery path = the quarantine command; (b) P8-D85 — the S33-07 file-anchor lag > 63 bound is not power-loss-safe (un-fsynced renames can roll back), so at open, after the truncation check, it is relaxed ONLY when the keystore anchor is present, not closed, passes the full anchor check, and records a known boot that differs from this known boot, and the file anchor's hash still matches its row; a relaxed open appends a kernel-signed daemon.anchor.lag{rows, which: 'file', bootPrev, bootNow} (keyless ⇒ FORBIDDEN{kernel-key-required}); every other case (same boot, unknown boot, stub/absent/malformed/pre-D83/closed keystore, closed file anchor; pre-D83 ⇒ relax boot-unknown) refuses anchor-lag with `data.relax` naming why. The file anchor's own boot is never consulted. A relaxed lag defers every open-time anchor write (file rewrite, marker/keystore-lag re-anchor) until the signed row is committed (evidence first); rotation completion runs first but writes no anchor. S34-24: keystore anchor ahead + any file lag ⇒ truncated (cause from the keystore boot); the file anchor still gets the hash and clean-close checks, only the > 63 bound is skipped, and its lag is TruncationReport.fileLag and daemon.log.gap.fileLag (additive). S34-30 CHECKS BEFORE WRITES: on open every integrity check (file anchor + lag bounds / relax, keystore anchor + clean-close lag, keyless refusals for the open-time marker / keystore-lag rows) runs before the first anchor write, rotation completion or row append; a crashed rotation is completed with NO anchor writes (the file rewrite and the closing keystore re-stamp anchor the head), so a refused open leaves both anchors byte-for-byte as found and no queued keystore write lands after the throw. OPEN-PATH FOLLOW-UPS (T-2026-10-17-012/013/015): S34-31 the keystore anchor is read before the create branch — a home with no db but a present/malformed keystore anchor refuses missing-db with no file written; the durable file-anchor rewrite runs BEFORE a crashed rotation is completed (non-relaxed), so a crash after the seal rename reopens as a rotation window; S34-25 a relaxed (P8-D85) open whose rotation crashed after the seal rename (lagging file anchor, no kernel.db) is accepted iff the same relaxation holds against the sealed closing row (pure pre-check, keyless refuses kernel-key-required), the segment is created and the relaxed row appended there first, the file anchor second; acknowledgeGap completes a rotation with no anchor write of its own (the closing row never overwrites the ahead keystore anchor). ROTATION FAILURE (T-013(a)): any failure after the active db is closed (fsync/fsyncDir EIO, seal rename, next kernel.db) halts the instance — closed, timers stopped, append / acknowledgeGap refuse ENGINE{rotation-failed} (in-process reason; reads refuse `closed`), close() reports keystore 'failed' and writes no anchor; reopen completes the rotation. Round 2: the halt starts at the closing-row commit (durable file anchor, TRUNCATE checkpoint, journal switch), so no row ever follows daemon.segment; a critical append rotates only after its anchors settled and resolves anchored even if the rotation then halts (surfaced on the next call / close). Stated residual: a rotation halt inside acknowledgeGap after the seal rename turns the acknowledgeable truncation into missing-db (fail-closed; quarantine). S34-29 (documented): a genesis fsyncDir(home) failure leaves kernel.db without a head file ⇒ anchor-missing on every later open; manual wipe / quarantine, never auto-recreated. `forcedAnchorRate` / `anchorStatus` = status.log telemetry (forced anchors per row over the last 10⁴ rows; > 1/64 = outside the measured envelope). Open refuses INTEGRITY_BROKEN on missing-db (with anchor, sealed segment or keys present), truncated (either anchor ahead of the db, with the S33-10 cause), anchor-mismatch, anchor-missing, and anchor-lag (file anchor > 63 rows behind unless relaxed across a boot change per P8-D85, or any lag behind a clean-close anchor); a smaller lag is accepted only as a chain prefix and repaired; keystore lag > 1023 appends a kernel-signed daemon.anchor.lag{rows, which} (contracts kind added; bootPrev/bootNow additive for which: 'file'). Fsync policy: WAL + synchronous=FULL (default 'process-crash'); 'power-loss' adds fullfsync per commit, which costs more than the 5 ms falsifier allows (the M1.2 figure carries no recorded method or machine, so no number here). G-LOG-04 (test:perf, one attempt): bulk p99 < 5 ms / ≤ 0.1 % over 5 ms, critical at 1/s under bulk load (60 events in the unit pass) p99 < 25 ms; the ≥ 600-event 1/s oracle is the manual 10⁶ probe run. verify(): full chain (segment links, genesis, anchors) or one segment; detects tamper, re-hash forgery, truncation, reorder, stripped or bad signatures, unknown keys, relaxed labels. read(): §9.3 projection per reader class (human, read-token, community-client, session, mod, peer; agent/voice refuse UNSUPPORTED pending M1.7/M4.x). M1.4 SLICE 2 READ SIDE: projection uses the EFFECTIVE sensitivity = strictest of the registered default, the envelope label and the stored column label (an unknown label ranks secret) — labels never widen, and nothing in a payload is consulted; readPage({reader, afterSeq, untilSeq?, maxScan, kinds?, match?, visit}) re-hashes every envelope (mismatch or seq/kind/id column disagreement ⇒ withheld + diagnostic read.withheld), returns {lastScanned, scanned, withheld, head, caughtUp}; getById (the UNIQUE id index) for ev: refs; onCommit(listener) — tail observers called after COMMIT in seq order, exceptions reported as diagnostic commit.listener.failed, never reaching the appender; sealed segment infos cached (immutable). read() is now built on readPage. ROUND 2: releasedHead() = highest seq with no unresolved critical row at or below it (a critical row is pending from COMMIT until its anchors resolve; failure ⇒ FAILED, withheld forever; failed seqs also loaded from daemon.anchor.failed markers); readPage and getById never return rows above it; onRelease(listener) wakes tails. readPage projects BEFORE hashing for non-human readers, checks prev linkage across contiguous rows (prev-mismatch ⇒ withheld) and states the residual (a consistent same-user rewrite of a row and every later prev/hash passes without signature verification). getById decides visibility before the hash (row-integrity only for a row the reader could see). Redaction: limited views drop hash/sig/prev, fields → {redacted: true}, stubs drop the envelope hash; mayBeVisible(e, reader) = metadata-only visibility; projectionStats counter. ROUND 3: limited views drop idem and refHash too (contracts FIELD_LABELS gain the content-digest audit: approval.auto.inputHash, turn.sent.contentHash, approval.voice.arm.phrasesHash, approval.voice.intent.handleHash / challengeHash, link.msg.out.hash, inject.receipt.shas / source_hash / frozenSliceHash); #hashAt uses the sealed-info cache. RESIDUAL until M1.3 (header): with the stub keystore, a critical row left unanchored by a crash in a previous run is not held out of the released head on restart. Not yet: async hardware signers, helper anchor, blobs/TTL pruning, projections tables, wiring $daemon-lifecycle events into the log. Durable-write platform seam (anchor.ts fsyncFile / fsyncDir, the one place a path is fsynced; T-2026-10-17-011): on win32 a file is reopened 'r+' because FlushFileBuffers needs a writable handle (a read-only one is EPERM), and the directory fsync is skipped (Windows cannot open a directory for flush). STATED RESIDUAL (spec §16, S34-26): on win32 a rename is atomic but NOT durable at return — node's renameSync has no MOVEFILE_WRITE_THROUGH, so a power cut can undo it; a durable Windows rename is parity-phase work (P8-D78). macOS/Linux: the file is reopened 'r' and fsync(2)ed, the directory fsync(2)ed; an unsupported directory fsync (EINVAL/ENOTSUP/EOPNOTSUPP/EISDIR/EBADF, isBenignDirFsyncError) is a no-op and any other error (EIO, …) is rethrown (S34-28). SEAM HARDENING (T-2026-10-17-009(c), Aegis S34-10, §19.1 release gate): `keystoreAnchor` and `bootSession` are no longer KernelLogOptions keys (KernelLog.open refuses them at runtime with a TypeError; the private constructor demands a module-private construct key held only by open and the registered seam closures, so a cast call throws; verifyLog has no keystoreAnchor option and always reads the kernel's own store, and refuses the key at runtime), and the recovery open and acknowledgeGap are no longer public members. The log registers them once (class static block) with the internal seam channel src/kernel/internal-seams.ts, read only by the internal test entry src/kernel/testing.ts (openKernelLog, openKernelLogForRecovery, acknowledgeGap, mintTestPresence). test/seams-fence.test.ts proves: no src file imports the test entry; only presence.ts, kernel-log.ts, manifest/install.ts (M1.5) and testing.ts import the channel; the closure of every tsup entry excludes the test entry; no src/cli or $daemon-lifecycle file (nor any other src file but the owners) names acknowledgeGap / openForRecovery; dist/ carries no test-entry marker and its KernelLog / KernelLogOptions types expose no seam. QUARANTINE (T-2026-10-17-009(a), P8-D89, quarantine.ts + src/cli/log-cli.ts): `gnomon log quarantine [--home]` moves the whole home aside intact to the sibling <home>.quarantine-<YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ>-<hex> (Windows-safe name) and installs a new home whose log's genesis (seq 1) is the reserved, kernel-signed daemon.log.quarantined{quarantinedLog, quarantinedHead{seq, hash, segment}, evidencePath, authorizedBy} (KernelLog.createQuarantineSuccessor is the only writer; append refuses it; verify flags it anywhere but seq 1 and binds it to the kernel key). Identity: EVERY head source (db tip, newest sealed segment, file anchor, keystore anchor when one exists) is read — dbs from a private scratch COPY (kernel.db + -wal, never -shm), so the evidence is never written — and the HIGHEST seq is the quarantined head (a truncated db behind its anchor is not hidden); all observed heads go in the journal and the CLI readout, with a disagreement WARNING before the prompt. Crash-safe: daemon lock (acquireDaemonLock) held across steps 1-4 and released through the evidence path; build in <evidence>.new, journal, rename home→evidence, rename staging→home (ENOENT there = installed by another process). completePendingQuarantine (run by every quarantine, by the CLI first and by startDaemon before it creates a home) installs an interrupted quarantine ONLY if the unsigned journal checks out: staging = evidence + '.new', evidence a quarantine-named sibling, both plain dirs owned by this uid (no symlink/junction), the evidence holds the journal's quarantinedLog, and the staging log's row 1 is a verified daemon.log.quarantined matching newLog / evidencePath / quarantinedLog; anything else is abandoned (reported, never deleted). These checks stop accidents and planted junk; they are NOT authenticity (the journal is unsigned and the staging keys are its own) — that waits for M1.3. The staging genesis is checked on rows/chain/signature only, never via verifyLog (which reads the per-user keystore anchor; M1.3 tripwire test → T-2026-10-18-007), and the keystore anchor is consulted only for the default home (spec §22 OPEN 19). Unreadable dbs are reported (`unreadable: copy failed: CODE`), ENOSPC refuses no-space; EPERM/EBUSY on the install refuses install-busy (retry; the pending install finishes). A crash between the step-4 rename and the lock release leaves our pidfile in the evidence, reported as lockResidue. An interrupted install is reported as outcome completed-pending (CLI: COMPLETED). Refuses daemon-running, not-a-home, nothing-to-quarantine, quarantine-pending, home-busy (EPERM/EBUSY/EACCES on the move), kernel-key-required. The genesis principal comes from kernelPrincipalOf (the daemon's root-authority source). CLI output: src/cli/readout.ts (#gnomon-kernel; instrument-readout voice — readout rows, `REFUSED  CODE reason`, indented `next:`); canConnectSocket shared in lifecycle/endpoint.ts. RESIDUALS: authorizedBy 'interactive-confirm' is NO PROOF OF PRESENCE — an interactive TTY + typed last 8 chars of the log id, passable by any same-user process owning a terminal, until presence lands at M1.3; at M1.3 the keystore anchor item must move with the evidence; a stale pidfile of a dead daemon is DELETED from the evidence by the lock acquisition, its bytes kept in the journal (stalePidfile, base64) — the only change to the old home. `npm run test:perf` = scripts/test-perf.mjs (cmd.exe-safe; --passWithNoTests on win32 only, a missing perf file fails loudly elsewhere).

gnomon-ts-client.name: Gnomon Ts Client
gnomon-ts-client.description: #gnomon-ts-client (spec §4.9, §5, §12.8; §19.1 M1.12 slice 2). src/clients/ts/ — the published TypeScript client, built ONLY on @a-company/gnomon-contracts + node:* (fenced by test/m112-conformance): hello with a fresh 32-byte clientNonce that the result must echo (client-nonce-mismatch) and serverSig verified against the PINNED kernel key over the SENT nonce before any credential is sent (T-2026-10-18-016); device-key auth (gnomon:auth:v1) or read-token proof of possession (gnomon:auth-token:v1); call() typed for the 12 verbs + 2 relays (ClientMethodParams/Results); refusals reject with RefusedError; subscribe() = log.read{follow} with rows in seq order and a visible end; logging through an injected ClientLogPort (Paradigm-logger shaped). Re-exports the one §4.5 sanitizer for UIs.

client-conformance.name: Client Conformance
client-conformance.description: #client-conformance (spec §12.8, G-CLI-02; M1.12 slice 2). src/clients/conformance/ — driver.ts: the language-neutral JSON-lines driver protocol (connect/call/subscribe/events/closed/close/sanitize/ row/denominator), TsClientDriver (in-process, JSON round-tripped) and SubprocessDriver (any language over stdio); runner.ts: runs every CONFORMANCE_CHECKS `run` check against a live kernel, `slice-2` checks reported todo, report + conformanceReportHash; hello.server-sig-mismatch runs an impostor endpoint that REPLAYS a real recorded hello (genuine serverSig) verbatim and with clientNonce rewritten to the victim's (T-2026-10-18-016): a conformant client refuses both, zero auth frames (falsifier: a client that trusts the echoed nonce fails it); the impostor listens on a private socket file (POSIX) or a random named pipe (Windows) and a listen error fails the check instead of crashing the runner. auth.device-refused also requires that the client keeps no live connection after the AUTH refusal. subscribe.since checks the backlog against a non-follow page (since+1, no gaps); contiguity assumes the fixture's full-visibility principal, a restricted principal must use the oracle-page comparison only. Falsifiers (T-2026-10-18-015): a client that checks the pin's PEM hash and keyId but never serverSig fails only hello.server-sig-mismatch, at case (c); a client that keeps a connection after the refusal fails auth.device-refused. status.clients[] copies only {suite, version, reportHash} (sanitized, capped) and labels a declared tuple `declared` and reports clientConformance{n, of} (G-OBS-01). M1.12 SLICE 3 honesty CI: test/honesty.ts scanners + test/honesty.test.ts (the gate over packages/gnomon*/src, manifests and package docs, plus a planted-violation falsifier per rule): G-HON-02 fabrication grep (Math.random outside ids, simulated/simulation, sleep()/delay(), hardcoded gains, mechanism words the code lacks), G-HON-05 no Task-steering descriptions, G-HON-06 unscoped guard names refused, G-HON-07 (round 2, B2): every ms/µs number in package docs — prose, wrapped paragraphs and Markdown table cells, keyword or not — names a concrete machine (chip, versioned OS or arch) and a named method in its sentence or table row, unless it is a budget, bound or configured interval (the BUDGET EXEMPTION, pending founder ratification); the live status of a spawned kernel (device + read-token views) passes checkStatusNumbers (#socket) in test/m112-conformance.test.ts.

standing-grant.name: Standing Grant
standing-grant.description: TD-2026-10-20-086 F6 (spec §3.4 "Standing grant"). The grant card is raised with RaiseInput.standingGrant: its allow is FRESH class (one presence, no root signature; Aegis open point 1); other grant cards stay root. src/kernel/broker/standing-grant.ts. ONE root-class `grant` card (request.grant.standing{tuples, repos} from the human on the GUI only, detail.op 'standing') mints grant.standing{grantId (= the cardId), cardId, tuples, repos, device (the GUI device's udev: unlock key), expiresAt ≤ 12 h, by}; the same touch keeps the device's cached unlock so later uses can be signed by the helper. While it stands, a human GUI decision on the same device that a tuple covers (STANDING_TUPLES: mode.loosen:auto-edits, permission:always, voice.widen, voice-arm:allow, daemon-stop:restart with detail.binaryUnchanged and no update; NOT reconsider:extend, Aegis M2; repo-scoped ones only with a non-null granted repo) takes no prompt: approval.decide {presence:'standing:<grantId>'} then the notify row grant.standing.used{grantId, cardId, tuple, decision, repo, hsid}. Never standing: root class, hand-only, install, gate-class, fallback-cloud, declassify, peer-pair, api-token, grant, handoff, peer-flagged or irreversible cards (standingTupleOf + broker checks). Ends: expiresAt, Revoke (request.grant.standing.revoke{grantId} → grant.standing.revoked{grantId, by, reason:'human'}, a tighten, no presence), the next screen lock / sleep / user switch or a helper exit (broker.helperSessionEnded/helperExited → endAll). StandingGrantBook folds kernel-signed rows only (forged rows ignored), like RuleBook / RunModeBook; status.standing{built, tuples, active[], pendingCardId}. No new signal (events are the §9.1 grant.standing* kinds).

approval-broker.name: Approval Broker
approval-broker.description: STANDING GRANT (TD-2026-10-20-086 F6): StandingSeam (setStanding) is asked before any presence; a match is signed under the device unlock (or a verified client decisionSig) with presence 'standing:<id>' and #standing-grant writes grant.standing.used after approval.decide. RUN MODES: approval.auto modeRef is mode:auto-edits (file edits) or mode:auto-edits:read-only / mode:ask:read-only (a Bash command #shell-readonly proves read-only; TD-2026-10-20-294 part 1, F1 TD-2026-10-20-086; path = the anchored root's realpath, inputHash the request's) or rule:<cardId>. Not built (would move clientApiId, founder gate): approval.auto.miss and an anchoredInputHash field. PREFIX SCOPE (TD-2026-10-20-294 part 3): approve{decision:'always', scope} — {kind:'exact'} is the v1 exact rule; {kind:'prefix', prefix} (1-3 words) is accepted only on a Bash permission card whose SHOWN command parses via simpleArgv as one literal simple command whose argv starts with exactly those words (else BAD_REQUEST); decisionSig is the v2 layout whose last line is scopeDigest(scope) (signer decisionMessage {scopeDigest}), the presence binding carries scopeDigest, the prompt names the prefix, approval.decide records scope and approval.rule.learned records {match:'prefix', prefix}. replay.ts verifies a scoped always ONLY over the scope layout. A Bash card whose command is one literal simple command carries detail.prefixOptions (first 1-2 argv words) + a {type:'bash-prefix', detail} block node the GUI verifies against contentHash. #approval-broker (spec §3.4, §5 verb 8, §3.1 approvals key; §19.1 M1.6). Voice (TD-2026-10-19-194): whether voice may take a decision is gnomon-contracts' VOICE_ALLOWLIST (#contract-voice-allowlist, §14.7), not classes.ts; test/voice-golden.test.ts pins abiId and checks the list against KIND_DECISIONS. src/kernel/broker/. Helper 1.6.0 (V5, TD-2026-10-19-194, §14.7, S29-K5): arm-custody.ts VoiceArmCustody keeps voice-arm REFERENCES only (the unlock is in the helper per armId) and appends approval.voice.disarm {armId, reason, cause?} for every arm on a helper session push (reason per cause from contracts VOICE_DISARM_REASONS: screen-lock (also screensaver), display-sleep, system-sleep, user-switch), helper exit (helper-exit) or a pair connection closing (conn-closed). A push also drops every cached-unlock reference (helperSessionEnded); connectionClosed sends conn.close. HelperApprovalsKey gains openArm, signUnderArm, closeArm, closeAllArms, connectionClosed and onHelperPush; HelperProcess parses the v2 push (a malformed one kills the helper); MIN_HELPER_VERSION 1.6.0, HELPER_PROTOCOL gnomon-helper:v2 (test/voice-arm-custody.test.ts, test/identity-helper-pin.test.ts). T-2026-10-18-028: M2 — UnlockStore ends a cached unlock at UNLOCK_IDLE_MS idle, UNLOCK_ABSOLUTE_MS (60 min) after it opened, or after UNLOCK_MAX_SIGNATURES (64) uses (approval.unlock. dropped{reason: idle|expired|exhausted}); M3 — unlock.drop goes to the helper on every close and failure path (connectionClosed always, a lost keep-sign reply, a close during the keep-sign, a failed cached sign, an ended unlock), and HelperApprovalsKey.dropUnlock escalates a drop the helper does not answer to unlock.drop-all, then recycles the helper process (HelperTransport.running / recycle); helper floor MIN_HELPER_VERSION 1.3.0 (test/unlock-bounds.test.ts). M4 — the presence prompt (drawn by the OS, not a conformant client) gets the card line through promptSafe (every Cf, Cc, Zl, Zp removed) and the summary QUOTED with quote/backslash escaped (quoteSummary, card.ts); the helper strips the same set from the caller text (Protocol.swift promptSafe). M5 (#session-runner, platform/darwin/session-sbpl.ts, profile v4): every session profile ends with helperDenySbpl() — deny process-exec of /GnomonHelper.app(/|$) and /gnomon-helper$, deny file-read* of the bundle (no copy out), regexes on resolved paths; backstop: the helper refuses serve/once under any sandbox (test/session-helper-deny.test.ts). L2 — #freshPrompt: at most ONE outstanding fresh presence prompt per connection (FORBIDDEN{presence, why: prompt-outstanding}), and PROMPT_COOLDOWN_MS (3 s) after a prompt the human declined (why: prompt-cooldown, retryAfterMs); an accepted prompt or an unavailable helper starts no cooldown; PromptRateLimited passes the presence error mapping unchanged (test/prompt-rate.test.ts). P8-D96: RaiseInput.decisions limits a card's signed actions (permission slice cards: allow|deny, no always); approve refuses any other decision bad-params; expire(cardId, why) logs approval.expire{into:'deny', why}; noteOf; suspect (approval.suspect from kernel observation). Aegis A3: approve claims the decision synchronously after its last re-check (CardRecord.claim); expire() refuses a claimed card and defers while #deciding (applied in approve's finally if the decision did not settle). classes.ts (P8-D98: the reserved daemon-stop kind is accept|reject, both fresh presence — Touch ID, TD-2026-10-19-528 F3) — valid decisions per card kind and the BASE presence class of each (cached: allow/deny on permission, answer, approve-plan, reject on plan/reconsider/inbound handoff, deny on strictness, incident; fresh: everything else the spec names, incl. always; root: install, use-api-token, peer-pair, grant; none: withdraw); irreversible and peer flags raise a cached decision to fresh; a decision the spec does not class is fresh (fail closed). card.ts — the card is composed from the broker's own record: lines sanitized (hidden-chars / bidi → visible escapes + card flags, §4.5), contentHash over {kind, requestedBy, hsid, detail, flags}, actions[] kernel-signed per valid decision (domain gnomon:card-action:v1), and the presence prompt composed from the card record (kind, requester, contentHash summary, connId, open GUI sessions {n}, the class reason) and signed by the kernel key (domain gnomon:presence-prompt:v1); verifyPresencePrompt checks text = the record's composition. Line cap MAX_LINE (512 code points, exported for #manifest-loader's install-card wrapping); the presence summary takes the first line's first 120 code points, never splitting a surrogate pair. install-card.ts passes the install card's pre-sanitized lines together with their sanitizer flags. unlock.ts — the cached unlock (TD-2026-10-20-086 F4/F5, superseding S25-H1 and the M2 60 min / 64): created only by a fresh presence on a GUI connection, never for a CLI connection; KEYED BY THE GUI DEVICE (broker unlockKeyOf: `udev:` + 40 hex of sha256 over the launch-token deviceId; a gui context without a deviceId keeps its connId) so it survives a reconnect and is shared by the device's GUI sessions; ends at screen lock / sleep / user switch (helper push), helper exit, 12 h (UNLOCK_ABSOLUTE_MS = UNLOCK_IDLE_MS) or 512 signatures, each bound LOWERED to the helper's: helper 1.7.0 reports `bounds` on a kept sign (helperBoundsOf), 1.6.0 reports none and is held to LEGACY_HELPER_BOUNDS (15 min idle, 60 min, 64). Dropped rows name the last connection and scope:'device' (test/unlock-device.test.ts). broker.ts — ApprovalBroker: raise (approval.request before the card exists; permission cards time out into deny, fallback and api-token never expire), approve (human only, B4; voice FORBIDDEN gate voice `voice-off` for every form, G-ABI-02 voice row; via link refused `peer-via`; held ⇒ withdraw only; peer-flagged always refused `peer-always`; decisionSig by the approvals key over approveMessage — bad ⇒ AUTH bad-signature, no approvals key ⇒ UNSUPPORTED presence M1.3; presence per class with a PresenceToken BOUND to {cardId, contentHash, decision} on the kernel-trusted clock (T-2026-10-18-003); always under a cached unlock ⇒ FORBIDDEN presence when no fresh presence comes; root class signs the decision with the root key; approval.decide {decisionSig, presence, via, connId, cli provenance} BEFORE the effect; always ⇒ approval.rule.learned; approval.suspect{why, provenance} for unknown CLI provenance / no TTY / CLI pgid inside a live session / unlock beyond class), expireDue, decisionOf (silence and unknown cards ⇒ deny, B6), connectionClosed, status. Production presence is PRESENCE_UNAVAILABLE, the approvals key NO_APPROVALS_KEY and the root unprovisioned until M1.3: every presence-taking decision refuses. install-card.ts — the M1.5 install-card decision moved under the broker (T-2026-10-18-008): the card is rendered from the detail RE-DERIVED from the pinned snapshot (manifest/install.ts rederiveInstallDetail) and kept in kernel memory; presence is a mod.install token bound to {cardId, contentHash} handed unburned to decideInstall. api-token.ts — the per-use billing api-token card (human-only request, root+fresh use-api-token, never expires), keystore injection into exactly one child env (takeEnvFor, single use; KEYSTORE_UNAVAILABLE until M1.3), billing.api.card.requested / active (activation and every turn) / ended / refused and the status indicator API CREDITS ACTIVE. port.ts — the #socket port: approve, permit.reserve (+ release), connection close, status cards / budget / billing, guiSessions[].unlock. The spec declares no signals; events are §9.1 approval.* / billing.* kinds. Round 2 (Aegis C1): GUI vs CLI is decided by the authenticated credential (only a launch-token GUI session may hold an unlock), never by the hello surface; expiry skips a card being decided and the decision re-checks the card and the connection after its last await (one terminal row); the sanitizer strips tag characters and escapes C0/C1 controls; the install card is rendered by the broker from re-derived lines, readPaths and linked source validated, presence bound to the decision; effect failures are recorded as exactly one approval.effect.failed{cardId, decision, effect: the card kind, reason: a kebab-case code} and no approval.suspect row; the card stays pending (approval.decide is a record, never authority; P8-D98 slice A2), so replay folds decide -> approval.effect.failed -> decide for one card with no divergence (the last decide stands). raise refuses a card carrying both a ruleScope and an effect BAD_REQUEST (Aegis M3: a learned rule auto-allows without running an effect). decisionSig v2 (P8-D98 slice A2): an `answer` signs the v2 message (signer decisionMessage, first line gnomon:decision:v2, last line answerDigest = the noteHash) and its presence binding carries answerDigest. With a client-supplied decisionSig an answer rewritten on the wire after signing fails AUTH bad-signature; on the helper-signs path the kernel computes answerDigest from the note it received, so v2 binds the text the kernel received, not the text the human saw (Aegis M2); an answer with no note is refused BAD_REQUEST; every other decision stays v1. Replay verifies both layouts given decisionKeys (replay.ts checkDecisionSigs) with a per-log cutover MARKER ROW: the first v2 answer or any 8.0:P8-D98 kind; a v1 answer after it is decision-sig-v1-after-cutover. The helper prompt line (gnomon-helper Protocol.swift helperLine) parses the v2 marker so it still shows the decision, card and content hash, plus the answer digest. Slice 2: with no approvals key (before M1.3) approve answers UNSUPPORTED{presence} before the decisionSig shape check, so the GUI (no signing path yet) sees the presence refusal (T-2026-10-18-018 item 2); status.cards per F4 — the human gets pendingForYou + byKind, every other class counts only {n, pendingForYou: 0, held}; theft-card.ts — a logged socket.auth.theft (#socket dispatch → port.authTheft) raises ONE fresh-presence gate-class card per revoked connId naming it, no timeout, no effect (the revocation stands either way). Round 2 (Aegis C2): the card's promise is stored before the raise awaits (concurrent theft rows for one connId raise one card), at most MAX_OPEN_THEFT_CARDS (8) theft cards are open — past that a theft coalesces into the newest open card — a failed raise is forgotten so the next theft row retries, and #socket raises only after the socket.auth.theft row was written. The path #web-endpoint (revokes, reports theft) → #socket (writes the row) → #approval-broker (raises the card) is a one-row relay with no state of its own, documented here and in theft-card.ts rather than as a $flow node (a new spec node moves Appendix A's count; see lore). M1.3 slice 1: with a helper-held approvals key (#identity HelperApprovalsKey) an `approve` WITHOUT decisionSig has the helper make it: a cached-class decision on a GUI connection with a live unlock signs `cached` (no prompt; a helper that lost the unlock ⇒ approval.unlock.dropped{helper-lost} and a fresh touch); otherwise one fresh touch signs the decision and the bound presence challenge, keeping the unlock in the helper for cached-class GUI decisions only. Unlock drops (idle, closed) propagate to the helper; a helper exit drops every unlock (approval.unlock.dropped{helper-exit}). A helper that is down or returns a signature that does not verify ⇒ UNSUPPORTED / FORBIDDEN presence, card stays pending. Root-class decisions use the root's signRowAsync. A client-supplied decisionSig is still verified as before. No new wire reason or event kind. T-2026-10-19-009 item 5 (Orca audit Adopt 5): deny-safe settlement pinned by falsifiers, no code change — an undecodable request is denied (permission-malformed ⇒ deny line; bad approve params ⇒ BAD_REQUEST, card stays pending; answerFor: only a decoded allow allows); a cancel (control_cancel_request ⇒ expire 'cancelled') settles into deny once and answers the session nothing; a late answer on a non-pending card is refused before presence with no approval.decide row; an unknown card is NOT_FOUND. Tests: test/broker-deny-safe.test.ts (every platform). F3 (TD-2026-10-20-086): RunModeControl configDefault = the root-signed config `runModes.default` (budget/config.ts parseRunModesSection; any fallback ⇒ null): a repo with no mode of its own takes it (view source 'config') when its folder is known and not home / above home / `/` (else ask; a repo key with no live session ⇒ ask, fail safe); the ceiling still applies; status.runModes .configDefault (test/run-mode-default.test.ts). RUN MODES (P8-D86/D87, src/kernel/broker/run-mode.ts + supervisor/ auto-edits.ts): manual | ask (default) | auto-edits, per repo and per session, folded from KERNEL-signed approval.mode.set and session.open{runMode} rows (RunModeBook, catchUp over modeSourceOf; a repo's mode persists across sessions and restarts). A session takes its repo's mode unless set for it. Effective = stricter(chosen, ceiling); ceiling L0/L1 auto-edits, L2 ask, L3 manual; strictness levels are NOT built (no level source ⇒ ceiling auto-edits; status.runModes.strictness .built false). RunModeControl.request serves log.append request.mode.set from a human on a gui or device credential only (dispatch.ts `requests`): BAD_REQUEST on an unknown mode/keys, NOT_FOUND on a dead hsid, FORBIDDEN{gate strictness, strictness-mode} over the ceiling; writes request.mode.set, then tightening ⇒ approval.mode.set{scope, from, to, by, presence:'none'} at once; loosening ⇒ a strictness card (allow fresh/hand-only, deny cached; decisions allow|deny so never always; 2 min ⇒ deny) whose effect re-checks the ceiling and writes approval.mode.set{presence:'fresh'}; one pending loosening card per scope. session.open{runMode}: no looser than the repo ⇒ set by the open row; looser ⇒ opened at the repo's mode + a loosening card (result.runModeCard). Supervisor: manual denies Bash/PowerShell/Edit/ Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit, WebFetch and mcp__* (manualHolds) with no card until a plan card in that session is approved (reset whenever manual begins; RunModeControl onChange → supervisor.noteModeChange records every applied change on each live session at once, Aegis L2); auto-edits passes Edit/Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit whose path is absolute with no `..` (M4), under a root that is not the user's home, above it or / (M3, isHomeOrAbove; also refused at admitOpen and request.mode.set), with NO symlink component below the root (every component lstat'd, the final one too; H1), not gate-class (layers.ts gateClassPathRule, incl. editor/toolchain dirs, lint/format configs, task/build files, other agents' steering files, non-ASCII and win32 alias names; H2; TD-2026-10-20-294 re-check C2: .gitconfig, .git-credentials, .netrc, curl/pip/conda config, interpreter and toolchain pins, build entry points, shell rc files, .env/.env.*) and whose card has no hidden/bidi flags, after broker.auto ⇒ approval.auto{hsid, tool, path (real), inputHash, modeRef:'mode:auto-edits'} (a failed row falls through to the card); everything else cards as in ask. Tightening a REPO pulls every live session whose own mode is looser down to it with its own approval.mode.set and withdraws a pending loosening card for it (M1). permission.ts deniedWrite also tests policy.ts realpathFollow (where a write lands, dangling links followed) and denies an unresolvable path (H1).

desk-guidance.name: Desk Guidance
desk-guidance.description: #desk-guidance (TD-2026-10-20-812 A1, slice S1; spec §12.9). src/kernel/desk/desk-guidance.ts: the frozen DESK_BODY (pinned DESK_BODY_HASH) and a kernel-composed roster from manifest fields only (mod name, offer kind, phase, title; A7), wrapped in <gnomon-desk>. composeGuidance(voice, desk) returns ONE block (voice first, blank line, desk) so table talk and the Desk share the single extra text block under one turn.sent{guidanceHash} that trace-cli extrasAgree admits (Aegis M2); voice alone is exactly TABLE_TALK_GUIDANCE. The supervisor's setTurnGuidance takes the composite (setVoiceGuidance is its alias).

offer-router.name: Offer Router
offer-router.description: #offer-router (TD-2026-10-20-812, slice S1; spec §12.9). src/kernel/desk/offer-router.ts: a fold over committed rows (daemon log.onCommit, like the speakable projector; seed() replays offer.* and request.offer.mute at boot). At turn.result it parses the turn's main-chain assistant text with offerBlockOf; at most one per reply, none while another turn is outstanding, none while the session has a pending card; the mod must be installed, granted, unpaused (DeskMods), not muted for the hsid (offer.decided not-now / stop-here) nor its repo (request.offer.mute, repo:<16 hex> from the session's repoKey), and the kind one of its declared offers; phase, title and contextIn are copied from the manifest (Aegis D3). It returns the kernel offer.shown row (the daemon appends it). decide(): request.offer.decide from the human on a gui/device connection only (Aegis D1), offer live (session running and owned by the asker), latest for the hsid, undecided (exactly one decision; a concurrent replay is refused before the row commits); writes request.offer.decide + offer.decided and on open sends the kernel template "Open <title>: use the <handoffTool> tool." as the human (session.inject origin kernel). offer.kept once per offer when the declared handoffTool on mcp__gnomon-<mod>__ completes without error after open. mute(): request.offer.mute row as the kernel. Aegis S1 fixes: open names the fully qualified tool mcp__<server>__<handoffTool>; only kernel-principal rows fold; the next turn.sent retires the shown offer; decided once the request row commits (a retry is a replay, no second request row), send failures reported (diag send.failed); a mod paused or muted after open never counts as kept (diag kept.refused); mutes survive session exit until the bounded state is evicted. Pause and mute stop offers at once; removing the server applies to new sessions. CLI `gnomon desk stats` (src/cli/desk-cli.ts) folds shown/open/not-now/ stop-here/kept per mod from the verified log.

mcp-passthrough.name: Mcp Passthrough
mcp-passthrough.description: #mcp-passthrough (TD-2026-10-20-812 A2, slice S1; spec §12.9). src/kernel/desk/mcp-passthrough.ts: DeskMods / readDeskMods (installed, pinned snapshot verifies, manifest matches its grant, capabilities and egress granted, not paused; cached on the grant table) and mergeDeskMcp, wired as SupervisorOptions.deskMcp into the session mcp.json: gnomon-<mod> (gnomon-<mod>-<entry> for extra entries), never a repo server name nor an earlier mod's, repo-muted mods skipped. Per-user launch override (Aegis D2): kernel state only (<home>/desk/mcp-overrides.json, 0600), never a repo file; `gnomon mod config <mod> --command <abs> --args … --env N=v` writes a request under <home>/mods/<mod>/ (session sandboxes cannot write the home); McpConfigCards raises a root-class grant card showing command, args, env NAMES and the launch hash; only allow writes the store. Accepted only for what provides.mcp[].config declares (validateMcpUserConfig) and an absolute command; a store entry failing the checks falls back to the manifest launch. Fail closed (Aegis S2): a server whose RESOLVED command is not absolute (isAbsoluteCommand: POSIX /… or a Windows drive path; // and UNC refused) is never added (skipped needs-config, daemon diag daemon.desk.mcp.unconfigured with the gnomon mod config hint); both shipped first-party defaults fail it until configured. Names come from ONE helper, serverNameOf: an entry named <mod> or gnomon-<mod> is gnomon-<mod>, else gnomon-<mod>-<entry> (gnomon-neurons-brain); #offer-router's kept check uses the same helper. Aegis S1 fixes: repo servers named with a reserved desk prefix (RESERVED_DESK_PREFIXES gnomon-, gm_, gx_) are dropped (diag mcp.reserved); the daemon records the servers added per hsid and the router offers and counts kept only through them; no desk server before the router is bound (mcp.unbound); per added server a diag mcp.added {server, launchHash, overridden}; launchHashOf is an HMAC under the kernel key <home>/desk/launch-hash.key; overrides refuse secret-marked env names (manifest provides.mcp[].config.secret), non-.exe commands on win32 and args the card would truncate (MCP_CARD_ARGS_MAX); the card says env values land in the session's mcp.json and labels the requester "a request file under the Gnomon home".

budget-fuse.name: Budget Fuse
budget-fuse.description: #budget-fuse as a METER (spec §3.4, §4.8, §10 laws 1/7; §19.1 M1.6; founder ruling P8-D92 "track everything, enforce nothing"). Only law 7 is enforced: permit.reserve of every kind but tool.permission (Aegis L1) on claude-code runs the billing scan (env, settings env blocks, apiKeyHelper, mcp.json env blocks, any *_BASE_URL incl. loopback; unreadable layers are hits) and refuses BILLING_REFUSED, unless the kernel's own spawn of the card's hsid holds the per-use api-token (scan still run, only the injected key ignored). Every other reserve is granted with a kernel-signed permit:v1 (attribution, law 1). Removed by P8-D92: day caps, compute and concurrency caps, the window threshold and 30 % human reserve, the breaker pause, the armada pause and budget card, the resume allowance. Tracked per UTC day: tokens + USD per user (P8-D91: an agent's spend in its human's bucket; before M1.7 attributed to the root's human principal, recorded attributed: root-human on permit.reserve), repo, loop, session, model, backend; local-LLM sessions with model and projects; subscription-window usage; quota errors (budget.window {quotaError}); ladder rungs 50/75/90/100 % as informational budget.ladder rows; over-permit usage recorded once (budget.usage {overPermit}). Usage only via recordStreamUsage(turn.usage|turn.result); malformed ⇒ budget.usage{malformed} and dropped. status.budget exposes the spend breakdown (byUser/byRepo/byLoop/bySession/byModel/byBackend, local, subscriptionWindow, quotaErrors). config.ts: root-signed tracking/display keys only (reference amounts, window shape) with a version high-water mark (sidecar ⊔ last signed config.loaded on the chain); unsigned/invalid/older/missing-after-signed ⇒ defaults + a logged row; project.yaml fuse/budget/strictness/review keys ignored and logged. parseReserveParams: no usage params; agents never name repo/loop/session/machine (kernel-bound, M1.7). Slice 2: restore(rows) at boot rebuilds today's counters, the window, local sessions and the announced rungs from budget.usage rows joined to their permit.grant (grant-less, malformed, over-permit and non-stream rows count nothing); day and window from the chain's last event time (S-L2, KernelLog.lastEventAt), never the wall clock. Round 2: restore counts only rows whose principal is a kernel principal AND whose keyId is a kernel key (KernelLog.isKernelKey; Aegis C1 — these kinds are not reserved), and a usage row's user must equal its grant's scope.user; a turn counts under its own budget.usage row's `at` (the row is written first; runtime and restore agree); chain times beyond wall + MAX_CLOCK_SKEW_MS (5 min) are clamped to the wall clock and reported once (onClockSkew → daemon event daemon.fuse.clock.skew, no row); restore runs before daemon.start, so its "today" is the day of the chain's last event. M1.7 note: api-token session turn permits are labelled subscription; per-turn billing.api.active needs usage against the spawn permit (G-SUB-03).

scheduler.name: Scheduler
scheduler.description: #scheduler (spec §3.5, §2.4 rule 3, §9.1 schedule.*, §10 law 5; M1.9) in src/kernel/scheduler/. Log-derived timers (timer:v1, never stored): the last fired due instant of a key is the max dueAt of its schedule.automation.due rows, so start() rebuilds every timer from the records + the log and no instant fires twice (G-SCH-01). automation:v1 {id, trigger: {at} | {every, anchor}, model: local|claude|any, attended} is a LOCAL shape (not a wire object yet; moving it into gnomon-contracts would move clientApiId). Every automation is attended: attended:false is REFUSED (schedule.dropped{reason: 'unattended-unavailable'}) until an #approval-broker decision (M1.6) and the run step (M1.7/M1.8) exist (law 5). Instants are strict ISO-8601 with Z or ±hh:mm; every is 1 min..10 years. Rebuild trusts only kernel-principal due rows whose dueAt is not after their own at (kernel principals = the unprovisioned p:00000000/kernel and the current one, so root provisioning at M1.3 does not refire timers). One daemon ⇒ one timer per key: duplicates (N worktrees) are dropped {reason:'duplicate-key'} (G-LAW-05b). An instant due while down — or older than one period capped at the horizon (a slept host) — fires as an attended event (late:true); several missed instants coalesce (schedule.dropped{reason:'coalesced', count}). A due row spends nothing; the run step is hard-wired to refuse ENGINE{not-implemented} (session.refused) — no spawn, no permit (G-LAW-05). Wakes are capped at 60 s; a failed append releases the hold and retries in 5 s; stop() is a latch returning the in-flight tick, which the daemon awaits before stopping children; the scheduler starts before the idle monitor. While the next due instant is inside 10 min the scheduler holds idle exit ('timer' holder). Clock and wake are seams (now, arm), so the 24 h soak is a unit test. Daemon wiring: DaemonOptions .automations (none by default; root-signed config later), handle.scheduler.

session-runner.name: Session Runner
session-runner.description: #session-runner (spec §3.3 Preflight/Environment, §3.4 law 7, §16; M1.7 slice 1) in src/kernel/runner/. preflight.ts: the claude binary by explicit path (root-signed config) else the platform registry's known locations (src/platform/claude-code.ts), NEVER PATH (p01); realpath + sha256; claude_binary_changed on a changed sha; version >= 2.1.288; `auth status` = claude.ai/firstParty. law7Layers: EVERY layer the child reads for THIS spawn's cwd (T-009 / Aegis C5) — managed sources per OS (+ managed-settings.d/*.json; unscannable sources such as Windows policy keys are hits), user settings*.json, project + worktree .claude/settings(.local).json and .mcp.json, ~/.claude.json mcpServers AND projects.<cwd>.mcpServers, the session's own policy.json/mcp.json — scanned over the CHILD env (scanApiBilling). env.ts: allowlist + scrub + GNOMON_HSID/SOCK/SESSION_KEY, envKeys names only (G-RUN-02). The darwin `session` profile generator is src/platform/darwin/session-sbpl.ts (from the M1.5 SessionPolicy + session-denies registry; T-008 git denies: .git pointer file, config.worktree, modules/**/{hooks,config, info}; launchers open/osascript/lsregister/launchctl by realpath), SLICE 2 (T-2026-10-18-010): the WHOLE Gnomon home is read-denied (keys/ incl. the device key, kernel.db*, log/** segments, every other session dir, the pin); policy.ts homeReadable carves back only the session's own sessions/<short> dir and the exec'd bin/ copy (or the runners/<tree> copy), refusing anything outside HOME_READABLE_ROOTS by realpath; SBPL order deny home, allow own, metadata on ancestors, re-deny keys + kernel log (profile v3; test/session-sandbox EPERM rig). registered in src/kernel/sandbox/session.ts (no backend => refused sandbox-unavailable; status fidelity per platform, G-WIN-06). p10m-claude-compat-generated (probes/) re-ran real Claude Code 2.1.302 under the GENERATED profile with the adapter argv: PASS, with writes to the whole ~/.claude/** and ~/.claude.json denied and NO per-session CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (a custom CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR loses subscription auth). ROUND 2 (Aegis H1/M1/M2/L2): binary.ts pins the claude sha256 in <home>/claude-pin.json on first use (logged session.sandbox{phase: 'binary-pin'}); another hash is claude_binary_changed until an explicit repinClaudeBinary (CLI/test seam until the gate-class card); the kernel executes only a private copy <home>/bin/claude-<sha> written from the same verified buffer, and preflight --version / auth status run that copy UNDER the session profile. The profile also write-denies the binary realpath, its versions dir and every known-location link (supervisor binaryDenies) and the user persistence paths (policy.ts PERSISTENCE_PATHS: LaunchAgents, shell rc files, git config, ~/.ssh); shortcuts/automator join the launcher exec denies; copied Apple launchers die by launch constraints (137, spec §A.2(iv)). Law 7 also flags ~/.claude.json primaryApiKey / customApiKeyResponses.approved and forceLoginMethod 'console' (billing.ts). The p10m re-run with the private copy and the new denies: PASS. ROUND 3: trust on first use — the pin is written only after the sandboxed preflight passes (N1); the copy (not the source) is hashed, streamed, and not re-hashed when size+mtime match the pin record; script installs (#!, the npm cli.js) are refused claude_binary_unsupported; `gnomon session repin-claude` (src/cli/session-cli.ts: TTY + typed last 8 of the new sha, daemon stopped) writes a re-pin the supervisor logs session.sandbox{binary-pin, by:'repin', from, to} at the next open; PERSISTENCE_PATHS adds .bash_login, .zlogout, ~/.config/fish. macOS FLOOR (P8 note, CI run 39100281741): SESSION_SANDBOX_MIN_MACOS = 15 (platform/darwin/session-sbpl.ts, read via platform/darwin/macos.ts sw_vers); below it the darwin session backend refuses sandbox-unavailable {floor:macos, have, need} and status shows the session sandbox unavailable — on macos-14 a copied osascript reached System Events from inside the profile. CI tests macos-15 (enforcement) and macos-14 (floor refusal). SIP FLOOR (CI run 39100811385, GitHub macos-15 runner, SIP off: a copied launchctl not SIGKILLed): darwinSipEnabled (platform/darwin/macos.ts, csrutil status, cached; Custom Configuration counts as disabled) — SIP not plainly enabled ⇒ sandbox-unavailable {floor:sip, have:disabled| unknown}, status unavailable reason sip-disabled; test seam SupervisorOptions.sipEnabled / sessionLaunchPlan's 4th arg. Profile v2 adds (deny mach-lookup (global-name "com.apple.coreservices.appleevents")) beside (deny appleevent-send) (APPLEEVENT_MACH_SERVICES); Claude verified working (p10m-claude-compat-generated pass). Its coverage of a non-Apple AppleEvent sender is UNPROVEN (spec OPEN 5): the existing copied-osascript check (`get name` of System Events) is answered without sending an event, so its exit is only RECORDED (test annotation), never asserted; the 137 launch-constraint kill is asserted on SIP-on macOS 15+ only. Aegis conditions: darwin automation:apple-events fidelity is 'partial' while spec OPEN 5 is open (status must not overclaim); inherited TCC grants of the responsible process + the reachable pasteboard are spec §A.2(v) / OPEN 22 (recommend launching gnomond by launchd or the signed app); the csrutil parser test keeps the exact macOS 15 stdout fixture. TRANSCRIPTS (TD-2026-10-19-814 item 1, probe p-resume darwin; profile v6): a Claude Code session (supervisor claudeTranscripts: true; local sessions never) gets policy.allowWrite = [<userClaudeDir>/projects, subpath], rendered (allow file-write* ...) AFTER the ~/.claude write deny (SBPL last match wins), then (deny file-write* ...) again on policy.denyWriteAlways + the T-008 git regexes; no later rule allows writes. denyWriteAlways = the projects dir itself as a LITERAL (Aegis M1: no rm/rename/symlink swap of it; children still match the allow; the supervisor's ensureTranscriptDir creates it before the spawn, never over an existing entry), the denies inside it, and the steering regex re-rooted AT projects (Aegis L3; the home-rooted one would re-close ~/.claude). Hardlinks (Aegis M2): measured on macOS 15 that link(2) into projects from a write-denied source (~/.claude/settings.json, ~/.claude.json) is refused by the source's write deny; no file-link rule needed, tests assert it. ~/.claude/settings*, plugins, CLAUDE.md, the rest of ~/.claude and ~/.claude.json stay denied. The allow is derived from the user Claude dir only (a flag, never an input path: no manifest can widen it) and WITHHELD fail closed (allowWriteRefused, logged session.sandbox{phase:'transcripts-withheld'}) when projects resolves elsewhere (symlink) or another deny covers it. policy.json's Edit deny on ~/.claude/** is unchanged. Residual, ACCEPTED by the founder (TD-2026-10-19-814): (a) a session can write (and delete) memory and transcripts for ANY cwd's projects/<enc>/, not only its own; (b) it can forge transcript history a later --resume loads; (c) the readers include the user's own unsandboxed Claude Code; (d) a link planted inside projects (e.g. MEMORY.md -> ~/.zshrc) can redirect a later write by the host's Claude Code outside projects. Linux/Windows: data only, no backend. repin-card.ts (TD-2026-10-19-063): the GUI re-pin of the claude binary — ClaudeRepinCards pre-stages ONE #approval-broker gate-class card per new sha (on an open refused claude_binary_changed, and on a poll of the resolved source at REPIN_POLL_MS cadence that never writes a pin); allow = fresh presence (one prompt), card TTL 24 h, a deny suppresses the sha; the publisher is checked on the private copy by src/platform/claude-verifier.ts (codesign, team Q6L2SF6YDW) and anything else sets claim-mismatch; the effect re-hashes the copy and writes the pin with signer + approval {cardId, contentHash, decisionSig}; live sessions keep their copy. Aegis fixes: the effect refuses unless the pin still equals the card's `from` (no rollback) and expires every other pending re-pin card; the card is voice-hand-only (broker, §14.7); binaryKind runs on the copy; a denied sha's refusal says "re-pin denied; restart Gnomon to re-offer"; the offline CLI prints the codesign signer (loud on a mismatch).

supervisor.name: Supervisor
supervisor.description: AUTO-EDITS READ-ONLY BASH (TD-2026-10-20-294 part 1): auto-edits.ts autoBashReadOnly passes a Bash request with no card, after approval.auto{modeRef:'mode:auto-edits:read-only'} (log before effect), only when its input keys are command/description/timeout, no root is home-or-above, the card is not flagged and #shell-readonly proves the command read-only; in auto-edits and (F1, TD-2026-10-20-086) ask (modeRef mode:ask:read-only), never in manual. K1 ANCHOR: classified with ctx.cwd = realpath(s.cwd); the allow sends updatedInput.command = anchorCommand(command, root, shellFlavour(session env SHELL)); approval.auto{path: root, inputHash: the request's}; the session.inject row of the allow carries inputHash and anchoredInputHash. F7: the kernel-written policy.json carries env CLAUDE_BASH_MAINTAIN_PROJECT_WORKING_DIR=1 (manifest/policy.ts CLAUDE_SESSION_ENV). Misses are not logged yet (approval.auto.miss needs a clientApiId move). session.send accepts source 'voice' from a human only, as a dictation attribution hint for #gnomon-voice (TD-2026-10-20-262). #supervisor (spec §3.3, §6.1, §5 verbs 2-4; M1.7 slice 1) in src/kernel/supervisor/. P8-D96 PERMISSION CHANNEL (probe p01b): sessions run --permission-prompts host --permission-prompt-tool stdio; each can_use_tool request is answered exactly once (pending map per session, cap 64, entry deleted before the answer; card raised inside the stdout queue, decision awaited outside it). permission.ts (pure) composes the card (Bash full command; Edit path + old/new; Write path, bytes, excerpt, inputHash; other tools capped canonical JSON; detail {tool, toolUseId, requestId, inputHash, repo, path?}), auto-denies writes under denyWrite and malformed AskUserQuestion input, and maps the outcome: only allow / approve-plan / answer allow. ASK-USER (gui-complete item 1): AskUserQuestion is an `ask-user` card (cached class, decision `answer` only, 10 min timeout => deny "no answer"); the questions are validated (<= 8, <= 16 options, one-line bounded text) and shown in a fixed line grammar (question N / option N.M) the GUI picker reads; approve{decision:'answer', note} carries the plain answer (one question) or JSON {answers:{question: answer}}, checked by parseAskAnswer against the KERNEL-held questions before presence (broker RaiseInput.checkNote, BAD_REQUEST bad-params); the allow is updatedInput = {...kernel-held input, answers}; approval.decide logs noteHash/noteBytes only (privateNote). ROUND 2 (Aegis C1/L1/L4): the AskUserQuestion schema is closed (an extra key at any level is bad-input); the questions are structured card detail (inside contentHash) carried in one {type:'ask-user', detail} block node the GUI verifies against contentHash; answers are null-prototype objects; every multi-line field body is fenced by fieldLines (FIELD_BODY_PREFIX + an end marker; model-chosen keys JSON-quoted), the shared helper that replaces the hardening lane's T-032(2) copy. Accepted risk (spec §3.4, Aegis C3, T-2026-10-19-001): the note is in neither the decisionSig nor the presence binding. PLAN TEXT (item 3): claude 2.1.302 sends ExitPlanMode with input:{} (p01b planMode, after a plan-file Write the session policy denies); the supervisor keeps the assistant tool_use ExitPlanMode input.plan (by tool_use id, bounded) and the last `.claude/plans/*.md` Write content, and the plan card shows it labelled "not in the request" with detail.planHash (so the contentHash covers it); a plan in the request wins. updatedInput is the kernel-held input; never updatedPermissions. Deny on no broker, raise failure, expiry, cancel (control_cancel_request => expire 'cancelled'), duplicate requestId (both + approval.suspect), exit/stop (expire 'session-exited', nothing written). Every answer is logged session.inject{origin:'kernel', hash, bytes} first. A permit never means allow (P8-D92). ROUND 2 (Aegis): the card block is wrappedBlock (never cut); every input field shown (key=value); MultiEdit per edit, NotebookEdit source in full, Write the only excerpt; auto-deny sandbox-escape / bad-input / too-large; deniedWrite case-folds on darwin+win32; policy.json permissions.ask for ALWAYS_ASK_TOOLS; control_request turn.event rows hash-only; a malformed body under a valid id is denied, a bad id logs approval.suspect malformed-permission-request; the ungated-tool-use detector (tool_result of a gated tool with no request); pending entries carry closedWhy (the expire why); repo-hook cards for PreToolUse / PermissionRequest carry TOOL_APPROVAL_WARNING. P8-D94 / G-SUB-07 (M1.7 slice 2, founder ruling): repo-hooks.ts extracts the repo's project/local hooks (strict; O_NOFOLLOW + fstat; events allow-listed to CLAUDE_HOOK_EVENTS; COMMAND_UNSAFE, unknown keys, non-command types refused by id; symlinked/oversized/unparseable layer or >64 hooks => none run; roots deduped by realpath), raises one gate-class card per undecided hook (install-card rendering via wrappedBlock, with the kernel warning line REPO_HOOK_WARNING), pins decisions to (repoKey, setHash) — read back by repoHookDecisionsFrom from KERNEL-signed gate-class.decided rows only (allow|deny; a withdraw records nothing) — and writes only approved hooks into the session's policy.json under --setting-sources user (hooks mode `audited`, the default; probe p10m-repo-surfaces). Pending cards bounded (MAX_PENDING_HOOK_CARDS). P8-D97 / G-SUB-08 (founder ruling 2026-10-18; probe p10m-repo-context, real claude 2.1.303, pass): repo-context.ts loads the repo's CONTEXT in `audited` — memoryDirsOf (cwd up to the git top-level holding CLAUDE.md / .claude/CLAUDE.md / .claude/rules, never the user home) -> --add-dir + REPO_CONTEXT_ENV (CLAUDE_CODE_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORIES_CLAUDE_MD=1); buildRepoContext copies .claude/{skills,agents,commands} into <session dir>/context, a --plugin-dir named `project`, frontmatter ALLOW-LISTED (sanitizeFrontmatter: hooks, allowed-tools, permissionMode, mcpServers, unknown keys dropped; tabs/quoted/flow/merge/duplicate keys or unterminated blocks refuse the file); symlinks refused; caps MAX_CONTEXT_FILES / MAX_CONTEXT_BYTES / MAX_CONTEXT_FILE_BYTES. Frontmatter hooks are stripped and listed, never approvable. The repo's non-hook settings are NOT loaded: repoSettingsInfo / repoSettingsLines put counts and key names (never values) on each repo-hook card and on gate-class.detected{what:'repo-context'}. ROUND 2 (Aegis): auditMemoryDir refuses a memory dir with a symlinked memory file or an @ import (importTargets, Claude's grammar, depth 5) reaching outside the git top-level (memoryRefused, on cards via repoContextLines); hasShellPreprocessing refuses skills/commands with !`...` or ```! and policy.json gets REPO_CONTEXT_SETTINGS (disableSkillShellExecution); every SKILL.md at any depth sanitized; M3 continuation/control-character rules; memoryChainOf feeds the policy's memoryDirs write-denies (M1); dotfiles skipped, readdir failures refused. ROUND 3 (Aegis): memoryFilesUnder audits each memory dir's whole SUBTREE (claude.md any case/depth, .claude/rules/**; symlinked claude.md/.claude refuse; VCS dir + node_modules not walked; cap MAX_SUBTREE_DIRS; outer walk reused by nested dirs); the policy's `steering` match (memorySubtree) write-denies CLAUDE*.md and .claude/** below the git top-level in any case (SBPL regex + Edit globs); imports leaving the repo refuse before lstat, % tokens and entity-encoded @ refuse, an import still pending at depth 5 refuses; every .md in a skill tree (SKILL.md any case) is sanitized and written sanitized. FOLLOW-UPS (Aegis F1-F3): symlinked dirs in the subtree are realpath'd (outside the git top or into node_modules refuses); `dep-steering` read-denies CLAUDE*.md and .claude/** under any node_modules (SBPL regex + Read rules); every in-repo import target (existing or not) is a write-deny literal (memoryImports, MAX_IMPORT_TARGETS) and the repo context is staged before the policy; permission.ts deniedWrite matches `steering`, so those writes are auto-denied with no card. F3a: an SBPL-inexpressible import target refuses only its dir; F4: the subtree audit collects /^claude[^/]*\.md$/i (CLAUDE.local.md too); F1a: dangling symlinked dirs resolved lexically (outside/node_modules refuse). Residual: carded Bash can restructure ancestor dirs mid-session. M1.8 slice 2: port.ts serves session.send{steer} (boolean; local sessions only, a Claude session refuses BAD_REQUEST); probeLocal() is the daemon-start local probe; the daemon passes the root-signed local config. The one place `claude -p` starts. Slice 1: ATTENDED HUMAN-started Claude Code sessions only (others FORBIDDEN; the scheduler run step still refuses). open: session.open -> preflight -> session dir policy.json/mcp.json from generated plugin bytes VERIFIED against the kernel-held record (T-008, manifest/generate.ts verifiedGenerated) -> per-spawn law-7 scan (hit => billing.api.refused + session.refused{api_billing_refused}, BILLING_REFUSED, before any permit) -> permit.reserve{session.spawn, claude-code, kernelSpawn} -> assertClaudePermit (Aegis: never claude without a live law-7-scanned claude-code session.spawn permit for this hsid) -> generated session profile -> DaemonChildren.intend (intent row BEFORE fork) -> spawn detached -> track (boot + start-time witness) -> session.sandbox{hashes}. stdout: every line a turn.event first (S2); usage only from stream events against the SPAWN permit (fuse.recordStreamUsage); ask-user / plan cards via the broker; init.apiKeySource != none kills the group; quota recorded (P8-D92 tracking-only fuse). send: a turn permit (caller's validated or kernel-reserved), law 7 re-scanned, session.inject{client} -> turn.sent -> stream-json user line. stop: interrupt = control_request only; else staged (control message, stdin close, DaemonChildren.stop SIGTERM -> SIGKILL on the group). Mid-session watch (G-SUB-05): layersHash + gitHash polled every 500 ms; a law-7 hit stops the session within 2 s. port.ts: the dispatcher's session port (human class only); daemon.ts wires it. ROUND 2: the exit listener is attached synchronously at spawn (an early-exiting child is cleaned up: watch cleared, permits released, moved to a bounded history); one catch from reserve to track releases the permit, kills a stray child, removes the session dir; layers hashed before the law-7 scan and re-checked right before spawn; child HOME forced to the scanned user home; caller turn permits must be live, unexpired, subscription and single-use; turn permits FIFO; the watch hashes ~/.claude.json only through its law-7 projection; stdout paused above a queue high-water mark and lines over 64 KiB logged as {lineHash, bytes}; init without apiKeySource logged absent. ROUND 3: 'exit' only resumes paused stdout; the release path runs on 'close' so a result written just before exit is recorded; #wire runs before the post-track log row, and a failure after track stops the group (the exit path releases the permits); a stray child before track is SIGKILLed as a group; preflight spawns are async; used turn-permit ids are pruned on expiry; status shows the claude pin.

shell-readonly.name: Shell Readonly
shell-readonly.description: #shell-readonly (spec §3.4 run modes, TD-2026-10-20-294 part 1, Aegis re-check C1 C2 H1-H4 M1-M3 + Low closed) in src/kernel/supervisor/shell-readonly.ts. Side-effect free, fails closed; reads the filesystem (realpath, readdir) only to check symlinks and expand globs. parseShell is a real tokenizer/parser for a shell subset (quotes, escapes, line continuations, $NAME/${NAME}, $(...), backticks, <(...), globs, tilde, comments, ; && || | & newline, subshells, for-in loops, redirections with IO numbers, heredocs); it refuses $((...)), $'...', $"...", >(...), |&, ;& and ;;&, ;; outside a case, (Aegis C1) any line of an UNQUOTED heredoc (<< or <<-) ending in an odd run of backslashes (the shell joins it before the delimiter match), braces other than the safe brace expansion, ~user, zsh $= $~ $^ forms and every other compound. TD-2026-10-20-086 grammar (each fail-closed): brace expansion {a,b} (two or more safe literal items, no nesting, no $, = or ~) and {N..M} (non-negative integers, at most 200), never right after a $NAME; case WORD in pat) list ;; esac (patterns literal + glob chars only, bodies walked, the subject is text); a local assignment name=$(...) or name=lit with no command word (lowercase, not LOOP_VAR_DENY, not a zsh hook array *_functions, not mapfile or a lowercase proxy variable (Aegis L2; deniedVarName, also for loop names), not a loop variable) makes name TAINTED text for the later items of its list when it ran unconditionally (first or after ; / newline): "$name" only where a substitution may be (echo/printf args, <<<), unquoted only as the case subject; X=1 cmd and uppercase/special names stay refused. classifyReadOnly proves read-only: allowlisted command names with per-command flag rules; C1 a $(...) or backtick word is only echo/printf text or a <<< word, never a path, and a for loop iterates only literal words and literal globs (expanded now, each value one safe token), so every path a reader gets is concrete and checked; C2 printf takes no flag (printf -v), echo only -n/-e/-E, test only POSIX operators, pwd/which/basename/dirname/tr tight flags; H1 awk runs one `[PATTERN] { print ITEMS }` program; H2 globs expanded against the filesystem with a superset matcher, every match realpath-checked, > 200 matches or a match starting with - refused, no recursive or symlink-following reader flags (grep -r/-R/-S/-O/-d/-D, ls -L/-R, du -L, stat -L, diff -r, find -L/-follow), rg removed, diff takes no directory operand, a leading unquoted = (zsh =cmd) is refused, test -a FILE is path-checked; H3 + K1 (TD-2026-10-20-086) ctx.cwd is the anchored root's realpath (the caller runs anchorCommand: builtin cd [-q] -- 'root' && builtin unset CDPATH && {\n<cmd>\n}); a cd is a whole top-level item to an absolute path or (with a known cwd) a relative existing directory, no .. segment, never -, + or = led, inside a session root as given and at realpath; the top-level list tracks the SET of possible cwds (only the cd target along an unbroken && run, every cwd seen after ; newline or ||; at most 8) and walks each item once per cwd; git only while the cwd is a session root; H4 reads only inside the session roots and /usr /opt/homebrew /etc /tmp /private/tmp /private/etc (as given and at the deepest-existing-ancestor realpath; ctx.readRoots may only narrow that system list), plus the device/protected-root deny; M1 date display only; M2 the cwd is known only along an unbroken && chain from that cd, else relative paths, implicit-cwd reads and git raise the card; M3 no git remote -v, no credential-bearing git config key; Low git branch NAME only after the long --list. RC3 git also: show-ref ls-tree rev-list shortlog merge-base for-each-ref, worktree list, stash list (flags only), reflog show, cat-file -t/-s/-p OBJECT, tag -l/--list (listing flags only); all through gitOptBad. Aegis H1 (both modes): git is refused when the repo git would use from the cwd (nearest .git dir or gitdir: file, its config, config.worktree, the commondir config, every include/includeIf path) names an exec-class key (core.fsmonitor unless false, core.pager sshCommand hooksPath alternateRefsCommand askPass gitProxy, diff.external, diff.*.textconv/command, filter.*, pager.*, remote.*.uploadpack/receivepack, gpg[.*].program, uploadpack.packObjectsHook, credential.helper; repoGitExecKey); and anchorCommand exports command-scope GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/KEY_n/VALUE_n (ANCHOR_GIT_CONFIG: core.fsmonitor=false, core.pager=cat, core.hooksPath=/dev/null, core.sshCommand=false, log.showSignature=false, gpg[.ssh|.x509].program=false, credential.helper=) plus GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 and GIT_PAGER=cat. Prelude hardening (Aegis M2, L1): zsh unfunction chpwd cd, chpwd_functions=(), setopt no_ignore_braces; bash unset -f cd, set -B; then a runtime guard (set -- x{a,b}; test $# -eq 2) so the command runs only with brace expansion really on. No background/negation/env assignment, output redirection only to /dev/null. simpleArgv returns the argv of a single literal simple command (prefix always rules; signature unchanged).

always-rules.name: Always Rules
always-rules.description: #always-rules (spec §3.4 S-L1, S25-C2; gui-complete item 2) in src/kernel/supervisor/rules.ts. Permission cards offer allow | deny | always; `always` is fresh presence EVERY time (classes.ts, G-BRK-05) and needs the card's ruleScope {repoKey} (else bad-params). The broker logs approval.rule.learned{cardId, tool, matchExact, presence, repoKey}. RuleBook folds KERNEL-signed rows only (kernel principal + kernel key): approval.request (permission card, tool, tool_input) + approval.decide{always} + approval.rule.learned (presence != cached, same tool) => a rule keyed (repoKey, tool, inputHash of the canonical tool_input); forged rows of any kind are ignored. The supervisor answers an EXACT match allow with no card after broker.auto => approval.auto{hsid, tool, inputHash, modeRef:'rule:<cardId>'}; a different input, tool or repo raises the card. updatedInput is the kernel-held input; never updatedPermissions. Bounded (MAX_RULES 1024, MAX_TRACKED_REQUESTS 4096; dropping fails closed). The daemon folds via catchUp over ruleSourceOf(log) (Aegis C2: lastSeq advances to the captured head, past every scanned row; Aegis H1: that head is the RELEASED head, never the committed tip, so rows hidden behind a critical row pending on its anchors are folded once released, never skipped; repoKey is repo-hooks.ts repoKeyOf, pinned in a test; a failed approval.auto falls through to the card) incrementally from the chain (fromSeq). The learned row matches EXACT only (TD-2026-10-19-528 F2: matchExact:true or match:'exact'; any other match value forms no rule). Revoke (P8-D98, F1): a KERNEL-signed approval.rule.revoked{ruleId, repoKey, tool, connId} removes the rule and forgets the card's always decision (a replayed learned row never resurrects it); a forged revoked row is ignored; a fresh always on a new card learns a new rule. get(ruleId) serves #rules-revoke. Not built: the strictness L1 suspension of rules (M2.10). PREFIX RULES (TD-2026-10-20-294 part 3, F2 amended): a learned row {match:'prefix', prefix:[1..3 words]} forms a rule ONLY when the kernel-signed request is a Bash card whose command is one literal simple command (#shell-readonly simpleArgv) starting with the prefix AND the kernel-signed approval.decide{always} carries the same scope{kind:'prefix', prefix}; an exact learned row after a scoped decision (or vice versa) forms nothing. match(repoKey, tool, hash, input) answers a prefix rule only for a Bash input whose command is again one literal simple command (no ; && || | & newline, substitution, parameter, glob, tilde, redirection or assignment) whose argv starts with the prefix word for word, same repoKey and tool, input keys within command/description/ timeout. A prefix rule widens only within a single literal simple command. gnomon rules list shows match + prefix. Aegis H1/M2/M3: the fold forms no rule from a prefix #prefix-policy refuses, and match(..., ctx{prefixRules, roots}) answers a prefix rule only with a context (none => no prefix match), never in manual mode (prefixRules:false; exact rules still match) and only when #prefix-policy passes the argv against the session roots. RC5 (TD-2026-10-20-086): an exact Bash rule also matches by bashCommandHash = sha256 over canonical {command} (no description or timeout), folded from the kernel-signed request (so older rules match too), when both the learned and the later input have only command, description, timeout keys; run_in_background or any other key on either side leaves only the whole-input hash.

prefix-policy.name: Prefix Policy
prefix-policy.description: #prefix-policy (TD-2026-10-20-294, Aegis H1/M1/M3) in src/kernel/supervisor/prefix-policy.ts. Which prefixes may be a prefix-scoped always rule, enforced at the card offer (permission.ts), the broker accept (approve scope, bad-params before presence), the rule fold and every match. Default deny: 2-3 printable-ASCII words, never one; argv0 no path, never a shell/interpreter/runner; NO package manager or build tool is ever a prefix rule (BUILD_TOOL_PREFIX_ALLOW is empty after the second Aegis BLOCK: yarnPath, rustc-wrapper, go env -w, .pnpmfile and npm view --registry make every subcommand code or exfiltration; an entry needs a malicious-config falsifier; ALLOW_NPM_TEST_PREFIX default off); git exactly two words with a read-ish subcommand. prefixMatchRefusal re-checks at match time: gitPrefixOptBad models git's option parsing (a --name that prefixes any GIT_REFUSED_LONG option, so abbreviations like --outp/--ext-d/--open; any short bundle containing O c C p u; plus shell-readonly gitOptBad), non-listing git branch args, -C-style directory/config options, paths that leave the session roots (.., ~, \, out-of-root absolute), and gate-class paths (layers gateClassPathRule: .git/**, .claude/**, package.json ...). shownPrefixWords renders each word quoted with non-ASCII escaped \uXXXX for the presence prompt (M1; the GUI mirrors it). Residual: Claude's persistent Bash cwd is unknown to the kernel; git trusts repo config written before the rule or by a carded command.

trace-capture.name: Trace Capture
trace-capture.description: #trace-capture (src/kernel/trace/): a CORE per-project audit mode, on every home and build (TD-2026-10-19-057, amends TD-2026-10-19-139). The human switches it on per project folder (mode.ts; CLI `gnomon trace on|off|status|path`); state lives ONLY in <home>/trace-folders.json (0600, keyed by realpath). The supervisor reads the mode at every session.open and resume for the session cwd and, when on, tees every stdin and stdout line plus kernel ctl notes to <home>/trace/<project key>/<hsid with ':' as '-'>.jsonl, one {t, dir, line} per LF line. Project key = slug of the folder name + '-' + 12 hex of sha256(realpath); project.json in the key dir records the realpath (a mismatch refuses trace-unsafe). NOTHING is written into the project tree. The session profile's gnomon-home deny covers <home>/trace, renames included; no project-tree deny exists for the trace (Aegis L7). Dirs 0700, files 0600, lstat + O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK (+O_EXCL to create): a link, FIFO or device refuses trace-unsafe without hanging (Aegis M3). Refusals (TRACE_REFUSALS, published in gnomon-contracts D98_CLOSED_VALUES) are reported on session.sandbox{traced:false, traceRefused}; traced:true otherwise (both reserved under P8-D98). Never blocks a session: bounded queue, out dropped first, in/ctl evict queued out and have a reserve, drops counted in ctl notes. Aegis M1: per-record bound 64 KiB (truncated copy + hash + bytes); past the 50 MiB file bound a capped note, then in/ctl in full and out as skeletons; past 4x out is only counted. Aegis M2/L4: span redaction on the decoded value ([redacted:<kind>]: PEM, grt:v1:, sk-ant-, ghp_, github_pat_, AKIA, xox[bp]-, secret env values). Aegis L3: prior-close-unclean note on a resume after an unclean close; a drain flushes with a 2 s deadline. Residuals: prompt and tool text in the clear, readable by the user's own account outside Gnomon; exact-folder match only (a session in /proj/sub is untraced when /proj is traced, follow-up); in/ctl past the hard bound are unbounded; win32 has no POSIX modes (sessions refuse sandbox-unavailable). Zero deps: no logger; visibility is the kernel log row.

rules-cli.name: Rules Cli
