rules-cli.description: #rules-cli `gnomon rules list [<home>] [--json]` / `gnomon rules revoke <id>` (src/cli/rules-cli.ts). list verifies the home's kernel log read-only (verifyLog with the home's kernel pubs, like gnomon replay) and folds the verified rows through #always-rules; an unverified log is refused INTEGRITY_BROKEN; the kernel principal is namespaced by the home's root (homeTrust ns), as the daemon's is. revoke (`gnomon rules revoke <id> [--home <abs>] [--json]`) asks the RUNNING daemon: the hello's key id is pinned from the home (kernelPinOf; an unpinned server gets nothing), it authenticates as the home's human device (device.key + its root-signed human registry row) and calls rules.revoke (#rules-revoke); kernel refusals (NOT_FOUND, BAD_REQUEST, FORBIDDEN) are printed as they come; no daemon => REFUSED ENGINE{not-running}.

mode-cli.name: Mode Cli
mode-cli.description: #mode-cli `gnomon mode [manual|ask|auto-edits] [--session <hsid>] [--repo [<abs>]] [--home <abs>] [--json]` (src/cli/mode-cli.ts; spec §3.4 run modes, P8-D86/D87). Connects to the RUNNING daemon exactly as `gnomon rules revoke` does (hello key id pinned from the home via kernelPinOf, an unpinned server gets nothing; auth as the home's human device, humanDeviceOf). No mode: prints status.runModes (default, strictness built or not, repos with a mode, every live session's chosen/source/ceiling/effective and a pending loosening card). A mode: log.append{kind:'request.mode.set', payload:{to, hsid | repo}} (repo = --repo <abs>, default the cwd; the kernel turns a path into its repo key). Tightening prints the applied change; loosening prints the strictness card id to allow in Gnomon with Touch ID and does not wait. An unknown mode is refused locally (BAD_REQUEST usage, exit 64); kernel refusals print as they come.

rules-revoke.name: Rules Revoke
rules-revoke.description: #rules-revoke (P8-D98 human-device verb 14, TD-2026-10-19-528 F1) in src/kernel/socket/rules-revoke.ts: the rules.revoke{ruleId} handler the daemon wires into DispatcherOptions.humanVerbs['rules.revoke'] (one key per verb in daemon.ts `humanVerbs`). Reached only for a verified human device connection (dispatch.ts refuses every other class, and a connection whose credential is not explicitly 'device', Aegis L3); no presence prompt (revoking only narrows). Params exactly {ruleId} (RULE_ID_PATTERN) else BAD_REQUEST; the rule must stand in the daemon's RuleBook (kernel-signed rows only, shared with the supervisor's exact-match check via syncRuleBook) else NOT_FOUND; then the kernel appends approval.rule.revoked{ruleId, repoKey, tool, connId} (connId stamped from THIS connection; a CRITICAL kind, anchor-policy.ts Aegis M1, so the append resolves only once anchored) and re-folds, so the next exact match raises the card. Revokes run one at a time (a concurrent double revoke writes one row). Result {ruleId, revoked: true}.

gnomon-guide.name: Gnomon Guide
gnomon-guide.description: #gnomon-guide `gnomon guide [<topic>]` (src/cli/guide-cli.ts, src/cli/guide-topics.ts; spec §5 "gnomon guide" paragraph and §9.7, TD-2026-10-19-648 item 10, T-2026-10-19-015). A CLI-only, pull-only verb: not a socket method, so abiId and clientApiId do not move (§3.1 I3). Topics spawn, claims, cards and refusals are COMPILED IN: built in guide-topics.ts from literals and from the frozen @a-company/gnomon-contracts descriptors (verb refusal lists, card kinds, decisions, refusal codes with gate, retriability, exit code and default next step), bundled by tsup; no topic file exists on disk, in the home or in a repo, and the guide modules read no file, env or cwd (threat 11). Every rendered topic carries the abiId and clientApiId this binary was built with. No topic lists the topics (exit 0); an unknown topic or extra arguments are refused BAD_REQUEST usage, exit 64, without echoing the argument. Nothing injects a guide into a session, prompt, envelope or card, and a guide grants nothing; status stays the man page (F4). Honesty check G-HON-08 (test/honesty.ts scanGuides, gated in test/honesty.test.ts): a topic naming a verb, param, refusal code or reason, or CLI flag the frozen descriptors lack fails the build; durations go through the G-HON-07 docs scan. The id G-HON-08 is named in the tests only; the spec assigns it when amended.

gnomon-trace.name: Gnomon Trace
gnomon-trace.description: #gnomon-trace `gnomon trace [--home <abs>] [--last | --session <hsid> | --since <ISO>] [--json] [--full]` (src/cli/trace-cli.ts) — a CLI-only, READ-ONLY audit timeline of a session for dogfood audits by the founder and by Claude. Not a socket method: abiId and clientApiId do not move. Joins per hsid (a) the kernel-log rows of the session (envelope session or payload hsid, approval rows of its cards by cardId, the daemon.start before and daemon.exit after), read from the segment files with a write-free open (immutable=1 when no -wal exists; readOnly beside a live -wal) and a hash-chain check (envelope hash + prev link; signatures are left to gnomon replay and the output says so); (b) the Claude Code transcript <claude dir>/projects/<realpath cwd, non-alphanumerics to '-'>/<uuid>.jsonl (prompts, replies, tool_use, tool_result); (c) the raw capture traceDirOf(home, <realpath cwd>)/traceFileName(hsid) — that is <home>/trace/<project key>/<hsid with ':' as '-'>.jsonl (TD-2026-10-19-057) — when present and a regular file (unparsable lines skipped; span redactions read [redacted:<kind>]; a legacy {redacted, hash, bytes} record is shown as [redacted], never reconstructed). The header shows whether the session was traced, from its session.sandbox row (traced / traceRefused). src/kernel/trace/capture.ts mirrors the capture builder's traceFileName/traceDirOf. Ordered by time, stable per source. Each turn.sent contentHash is checked against the transcript prompt with the supervisor's own turnContentHash: "✓ matches log" / "✗ hash mismatch"; a prompt the log never sent is "not in log". Human output uses the readout helpers and sanitizeDisplayText on every shown string, truncated unless --full; --json is one {session:{hsid,uuid,cwd,principal}, log, transcript, capture, turns, usage, events:[{t, source: log|transcript|capture, kind, ...}]} per session per line. The output contains prompt text (help says so). `gnomon trace path [--home] [--folder]` prints where the folder's captures live and writes nothing; `on` says they live in the home and hold prompt and tool text in the clear (Aegis L8). Subcommands `gnomon trace on | off | status [--home] [--folder]` keep per-project trace mode in <home>/trace-folders.json (0600, keyed by realpath) via src/kernel/trace/mode.ts (setTraceMode, traceModeOf, tracedFolders — a minimal copy reconciled at merge with the capture builder's module); they are the only writes, and only to that file.

local-runner.name: Local Runner
local-runner.description: #local-runner (spec §13, §3.3, §6.1 step 2; M1.8 slice 1). Kernel side: local-session.ts maps a SUCCESSFUL compaction_end (summaryHash + both token counts, no error) onto the typed session.compacted{hsid, turn, reason, summaryHash, tokensBefore, tokensAfter} row (compactedPayloadOf; T-2026-10-18-016, P8-D93) after the raw turn.event line, which stays; src/kernel/local/endpoint.ts (loopback/LAN rule on the normalised host; hostnames, Anthropic hosts, link-local/metadata, public, userinfo, forbidden web-endpoint port refused — G-SUB-06 BILLING_REFUSED via config.ts), config.ts (compat names = gnomon-local allowlist, no cloud; assertNotClaude: law 7 never runs claude under a backend:local permit), probe.ts (/slots n_ctx, else /props; tools only on a live tool call), routing.ts (local|claude|any; capable = probe ok + tools (or text-tool opt-in) + n_ctx >= floor 8192), src/adapters/local/runner.ts (pi rpc JSONL driver, tolerant parse, LocalUsageMeter no double count), src/kernel/supervisor/local-session.ts (LocalLane: incapable local => fallback card via the broker + model.fallback.requested + MODEL_UNAVAILABLE{cardId}, no spawn; fallback-cloud decision opens Claude, S7; any => session.routed; capable => local session.spawn permit recorded with model + repo (P8-D92 meter, never capped) -> session profile -> intend/track kind local-runner; stdout turn.event first, model.capabilities/model.repair, usage against the spawn permit). Round 2: tools confined to realpath roots (no .git, no symlink final component), probe bodies capped 1 MiB, configured model id preferred, assertNotClaude on realpaths + @anthropic-ai/claude-code, explicit backend pins the route, launchPlan TEST-RIG seam (test/local-lane-spawn.test.ts). Slice 2: config.ts loadLocalConfig reads the ROOT-SIGNED <home>/local.signed.json (schema gnomon-root-local:v1; unsigned, tampered, unparseable, invalid or older than the sidecar/chain high-water mark => NO local config, logged config.unsigned / config.loaded{file, fallback:'none'}; a signed public endpoint is applied and refuses every open BILLING_REFUSED), wired by the daemon; round 2 (Aegis H1): the runner pin is MANDATORY (node + nodeSha256, package dir + treeSha256, entry) — runner-pin.ts copies the tree into <home>/runners/<treeSha256>/, hashes the COPY, verifies node and execs <realpath node> <realpath copied entry> (PERMIT_REQUIRED runner-pin-mismatch{part}); residual: node is not copied (Homebrew node loads ../lib) — round 3: EVERY session profile (Claude and local) denies writes to node, its install prefix and the pinned source dir (policy.ts localRunnerDenies, fed from the loaded local config), and node is re-hashed synchronously right before spawn; a concurrent staging rename (EEXIST/ENOTEMPTY) is success iff the dest verifies; turn.event rows for compaction lines keep summaryHash/summaryBytes even over the line cap; a signed config with maxTokens >= 0.85 x contextTarget is invalid; round 2 (M3): roots resolved ONCE by native realpath (fail closed) and only the resolved paths reach the policy, child config, darwin extras, repo id and spawn cwd; re-checked right before spawn; per-task endpoint choice = first endpoint in signed order capable for the floor; probeAll at daemon start records model.probe/model.capabilities; roots inside the Gnomon home refused; the child gets contextTarget min(~8k, n_ctx); session.send{steer} with a turn in flight writes the steer line under that turn's permit (session.inject + turn.steer, no new permit), idle it is a plain send; round 2: the steer needs the in-flight turn permit live (else PERMIT_REQUIRED); the child refuses a steer that reaches it idle and the kernel logs turn.steer{phase:refused, by:child}; Claude sessions refuse steer BAD_REQUEST. Deferred: darwin sandboxed e2e rig (G-LCL-01 fake half, G-LCL-06, 6-child G-LAW-01c), gnomon probe local CLI verb, the claude estimate on the card, attended/unattended local automations (law 5).

claude-adapter.name: Claude Adapter
claude-adapter.description: Generate slim CLAUDE.md (~150 lines) with core identity, session lifecycle, on-demand guidance pointers to paradigm://guidance/{topic} MCP resources, a Native Memory Hygiene redirect (Memory Steward B1 — route durable facts to lore/habits/decisions/tasks, keep native MEMORY.md ephemeral), and agent contributions section from high-priority .agent context

mod-host.name: Mod Host
mod-host.description: #mod-host (spec §3.8, §12.1-§12.3, §15.5 row mod; §19.1 M1.11 slice 1) in src/kernel/modhost/. host.ts ModHost - one child per mod, started ONLY via #manifest-loader loadMod (root-signed grant.install, snapshot integrity, manifestHash, grants; a changed linked folder pauses and stages the re-approve card instead of loading, G-MOD-08); effects in force = union of tool effects, capped at read while grant.install{dev} is live, an expired dev period pauses (mod.dev.expired, fail closed); spawns node <index.mjs|index.js> from the pinned snapshot under the default-deny mod profile (sandbox/mod.ts registry + platform/darwin/mod-sbpl.ts; same floor as sessions: macOS 15+ and SIP; other platforms refuse sandbox-unavailable), env GNOMON_MOD_NAME + GNOMON_EGRESS_PROXY only; tracked by DaemonChildren kind mod IN MEMORY (no mod.spawned/mod.exited kind: adding one moves clientApiId); init must echo mod-abi:v1 and MOD_ABI_ID. channel.ts - JSON-RPC 2.0 NDJSON over stdio (1 MiB frames, stderr tail). Calls serialized per mod so mod->host requests are attributed exactly; effects.ts enforces state.get=read, state.set=write, kernel.call by verb (approve never, log.append only own declared modns, session.send only inside a tool call with the caller hsid) => FORBIDDEN + mod.effect.refused. Timeout => cancel{cancelToken}, unhonoured => restart; crash => mod.health{ok:false} + restart (cap 3/10 min). block.ts closed kit:v1 gate (256 KiB / 2000 nodes, sanitizeLine, Button command id only, Image alt + sha256 blob, Canvas names a ds; S5: Text may carry a `cap`, the closed contracts shape {shape, hue 0..5, filled, state, label <=40} checked by checkCap, any other field refused, label sanitized; kitId/modAbiId/clientApiId do not move). relayView/relayCommand stamp relayedFor from the caller. egress-proxy.ts per-mod loopback CONNECT proxy (443 only; granted declared hosts; IP literals, private names, Anthropic hosts, private resolutions and calls lacking network refused). state.ts per-mod KV <home>/mods/<name>/state.db (sibling of state/, never granted; O_NOFOLLOW reads, random O_EXCL tmp; JSON in slice 1). Round 2 (Aegis): state/ and blobs/ must be real dirs at their expected paths before every profile build; tunnels closed at call end; proxy head deadline, connection cap, idle timeout, resolve-check-connect, wider non-public ranges; explicit verb-effect table; session.send pinned to the caller hsid, permitId stripped; channel caps in-flight mod requests at 16 with backpressure. Test seams (unsandboxed launcher, egress dialer) only via kernel/testing.ts createModHostForTest. SLICE 2: call-id binding (host mints callId on view.render/command.run/tool.call, the SDK echoes it on state.get/state.set/kernel.call; a foreign or ended callId is FORBIDDEN modCode CALL + mod.effect.refused{why:call-id}; none = idle; modAbiId moved 00ae702b -> 7aaf92f4, clientApiId unchanged); bridge.ts createModKernelCall (log.append own modns clamped to kind/payload<=16 KiB/audience/sensitivity, Aegis C2, appended under the mod principal; every other verb via dispatcher.callAs as a connection-less mod principal) and createModRelayPort (mod.view / mod.command start the mod on first use; relayedFor stamped by the dispatcher from the caller connection; GUI mod.command refused until a gesture proof, M1.10); startDaemon constructs the host, status.mods + status.modAbiId, stopAll before the children sweep at every exit; folder watch on a running linked mod (fs.watch recursive, .git ignored, 500 ms debounce => stop{changed} + loadMod pause + re-approve card). Round 2 (review + Aegis): own-modns appends go as:'userland' under the mod principal, kernel-key-signed as an attestation (attributed by principal, never keyId; spec §3.2 L7); relay admission ModHost.admit (name/id shapes refused BAD_REQUEST in dispatch; an uninstalled name NOT_INSTALLED with manifest.refuse folded past 8 per 10 s; paused answered from memory; relay starts count against RESTART_CAP; DOWN until an operator start); per-mod append budget (20 rows/s, 64 KiB per call) and 8 mod->host requests in flight per mod; status.mods full to the human class only, counts otherwise; watcher unarmed on exit/timeout/pause/cap and re-armed on a successful start; a lost mod.paused / mod.effect.refused row surfaces as daemon.mod.row.unrecorded. Round 3 (Aegis R2-1/R2-2): fold.ts RowFold - mod.effect.refused (per mod, keyed effect|why|verb, verb clipped) and relay-miss manifest.refuse rows: 8 individual per 10 s window, the rest one coalesced row on the timer / next window / stop / stopAll, at most 16 keys + other<Field>s + distinct (exact to 1024, then distinctCapped); the bridge drops a call's byte tally on the host's onCallEnd and prunes past idle seconds (never a wholesale clear); kernel-side refusals reach a mod as code + reason only (generic message, no wrapped data). Slice 3: the gnomon mod CLI and its control surface (#mod-cli, below); a <home>/mods/<name>/paused marker makes every start return paused{why:user}. feed.ts: ModHost.feed (startDaemon queues committed rows, bounded 4096, and feeds only rows at or below the log's released head; turn.partial coalesced to one edge per hsid; ModChannel.notify drops past 256 KiB unread stdin, counted in inspect droppedNotifications) forwards a fixed projection of session.open/exited, turn.partial/result, approval.request/decide/expire and warpline.knot (kernel fields only; project = a hue index from sha256(cwd)) to running mods requiring log.read - the #workshop-mod input. Projection v2 (#ledger-mod input; Aegis M1: ONLY to mods granted the narrower log.read:usage capability, named on the install card; log.read alone gets v1 and turn.result as {hsid}; feedAccessOf/feedReaches; a local-tier manifest may not combine log.read:usage with egress, #manifest-loader validateManifest) adds NUMBERS-ONLY rows: turn.usage/turn.result {hsid, tokens, tokensIn/tokensOut/cacheRead/cacheWrite from the turn.result split the supervisor now records from Claude's result.usage, costMicros}, session.compacted {hsid, tokensBefore, tokensAfter}, budget.usage {dimension, n, of?, usdMicros?, over?}, budget.ladder {dimension, scope, rung %}, budget.pause/resume/ breaker.open/close and permit.deny {dimension}; every number clamped (feedCount), strings only ids or enum tokens (test/mod-feed-v2.test.ts property test); seq/at validated. status() lists views of running mods ({name, viewId, slot, placement, dev}) for the #gui mod panels. FIRST_PARTY_PACKAGE_HASHES pins the Workshop, the Ledger and Paradigm Context. Still to come: spend from the caller permit, dev-mode cards/re-pin, gnomon-mods MCP bridge, /blob (C4), Tier 0. K1 (#paradigm-context-mod): paradigm-slice.ts, the paradigm-slice:v1 kernel projection of a LIVE session's repo (.paradigm/tasks/entries, decisions/TD-*.yaml, lore/entries/**): open/high task counts, top 5 tasks, last 5 decisions {id,title,date}, last 5 lore {id,title,type}, symbols touched; zero-dep strict YAML subset (malformed files skipped and counted), symlinks and realpath escapes refused, files capped, titles §4.5-sanitised, path-redacted, ≤120 chars; sensitivity secret dropped; no absolute path in the slice (hue + basename only). Granted by paradigm.read:summary (CAPABILITY_FORMS; not an id input; a manifest holding it may list no egress, any tier). Aegis review (H1/M2/M3/L1/L3): no super-linear regex over file text (key lines split by indexOf, trailing comments found by a linear scan, scalars and titles capped at SCALAR_MAX 4 KiB before any regex); the root walk runs in realpath space (cwd and home realpath'ed, case-folded on darwin/win32, never at or above the home); bounded opendir iteration (MAX_ENTRIES), MAX_TASK_PARSED 512, SLICE_BYTE_BUDGET 3 MiB; the cache is keyed by the .paradigm realpath (hue per cwd, sync read = single-flight; a worker is a follow-up); files: dev+ino match, nlink>1 refused, re-realpath + stat(realpath) vs fstat after open; realpath(cwd) and realpath(home) scrubbed. K3: a RELAYED render's input is host-composed (host.ts composeRelayedInput, HOST_INPUT_KEYS focus/hsid/paradigm): the client names only {focus:{hsid}} (or the K0 {hsid}); the host joins that hsid SERVER-SIDE to the live session cwd (ModHostOptions.focusCwd; daemon: supervisor.scopeOf) and gives a paradigm.read:summary mod exactly {hsid?, paradigm: slice | unfocused}; a forged repo/path/cwd/paradigm is ignored (test/mod-focus.test.ts). Other mods get their non-host keys + {hsid}. Local-lane sessions are not joined yet (unfocused). Aegis M1: the join checks the CALLER. The dispatcher stamps relayedFor{principal, connId, principalClass}; the host keeps the class host-side (the mod's relayedFor stays {principal, connId}). Human: any live hsid. Agent/session: only its OWN session (ModHostOptions. focusPrincipal; daemon: supervisor.principalOf(hsid) === caller). Voice, mod, unknown: unfocused (peer/read-token never reach mod.view: RELAY_TIERS false). Falsifier: test/mod-focus.test.ts (agent naming another session's hsid). HOST-LEVEL FALSIFIERS (test/mod-capability-falsifier.test.ts, real stub children; mutation-checked): log.read-only mods get no usage kind and turn.result exactly {hsid}; a mod without paradigm.read:summary never receives the slice (relayed, forged, or via the feed).

mod-cli.name: Mod Cli
mod-cli.description: #mod-cli (spec §12.4, §12.5, §3.1 I3; §19.1 M1.11 slice 3) - src/cli/mod-cli.ts `gnomon mod install|link|list|status|pause|start| uninstall` over #manifest-loader, plus the kernel half in src/kernel/modhost/control.ts. §5 has no install/pause/start verb and adding one moves clientApiId, so the CLI and the kernel meet in the home: install/link run stageInstall in the CLI (snapshot + pending card record, signs nothing; staging from a session is NOT available yet: the darwin session profile denies writes under the home, so it waits for the gnomon-mods bridge; a GNOMON_HSID in the env is recorded only as a claim, and the CLI's GNOMON_HSID refusals are advisory, the SBPL is the boundary) and print the card lines from rederiveInstallDetail (the hardened install path: one line per entry, kernel-composed count line at index 2, COMMAND_UNSAFE linked-path refusal, linked-source re-hash); a url source is refused. The daemon's StagedCardPickup (scan every 2 s) raises every pending staged card through #approval-broker raiseInstallCard (re-derived from the pinned snapshot; install = fresh presence + root key, Touch ID via the M1.3 helper), logs manifest.staged{via:cli} for cards the kernel did not stage itself, starts the mod on mod.installed; bounded (MAX_PICKUP_CARDS 32 raised, 256 remembered refusals keyed by file stamp so a tampered record is not retried until it changes; Aegis C5: files are listed by readdir + lstat only (≤ 1024), raised / settled / refused-unchanged ids are skipped before any read, ≤ 64 records READ per scan, 64 KiB per record, manifest.refuse carries the ManifestRefusal code and is folded 8 per 10 s, and the grant table is read once per scan). pause writes the paused marker (narrows; allowed from a session), the pickup stops a running paused mod (mod.paused{reason:user}); start clears it and writes start.request (operator start, lifts DOWN); uninstall writes uninstall.request naming the pin, the pickup raises a root-class `grant` card (allow|deny) whose allow appends a root-signed grant.uninstall row (GRANT_ROW_KINDS, not a clientApiId input; pin rows are stamped max(now, newest pin plus one millisecond) and read back - the reader rejects a non-newer pin as replay - and the uninstall effect reports nothing unless it took effect; junk staged files are remembered by stamp; manifest.staged logs by/hsid under claimed), stops the mod and logs manifest.uninstall{diff} (+ mod.unlinked); effectiveInstall = the last install/uninstall pin row naming the mod. start and uninstall are refused from a kernel-spawned shell. list and status read the grant table offline (trust from identity.json or a DEV home's root).

Wired into orchestrator.ts solo + DAG paths; every call best-effort (a bridge write failure never breaks the CLI run). Imports paradigm-mcp via the established relative-path precedent (core/habits/evaluator.ts).

calibration.name: Calibration

Wired into orchestrator.ts at both per-agent actual sites — faceted (result.relay.metrics.tokens_used, keyed by step.agent + classifyTask(task).type) and solo (agentName + classifyTask(task).type). The estimate itself is NOT recorded (the learned table is actuals-only → no cross-package coupling to the MCP constant). Capture is best-effort — a write failure is logged and swallowed, never alters the run. Aggregated by `paradigm calibrate` into .paradigm/learned/token-estimates.json, which the MCP planner reads learned-first.

calibrate-command.name: Calibrate Command
calibrate-command.description: v7.1 — `paradigm calibrate` aggregation command (the analysis half). Reads .paradigm/events/estimate-actuals.jsonl, groups by (archetype, taskType), and for each group with n>=8 samples computes a robust band (min=p10 of total, max=p90 of total) and writes .paradigm/learned/token-estimates.json as a nested archetype→taskType→band map of {min,max,n}. Groups under the 8-sample floor are NOT written (still use the constant cold-start prior). Reports learned vs. below-floor groups via cli-output helpers (header/kv/success/dim/warn). aggregateActuals + percentile are exported pure functions for testing.

git-exec.name: Git Exec
git-exec.description: Thin, READ-ONLY wrappers over git (merge-base, rev-parse, commit meta, merge-tree). ABSORB materializes a ref's tree via `git archive | tar` into a temp dir — NO worktree, no .git/worktrees lock — so absorbs run concurrently (T-2026-06-23-003). worktreeAdd/Remove remain only for the cold git<2.38 merge-tree fallback, which needs real merge machinery and is serialized per-repo via #repo-lock. WORKTREE LEAF NAMES ARE UNIQUE (T-2026-08-11): git registers a worktree under `.git/worktrees/<basename-of-path>`, resolving collisions by CHECKING the name then creating it — a TOCTOU window. Every worktreeAdd used to name its leaf `tree`, so N concurrent adds against ONE repo proposed the same registry name, raced in that window, and surfaced as `failed to read .git/worktrees/tree/commondir` on the loser plus ENOTEMPTY on teardown. It read as random unrelated failures across the git-era suite (divergence-proof, oracle, absorb) whenever the machine was loaded. The leaf now carries the mkdtemp suffix, which is already unique, so the race cannot form. materializeTree keeps a fixed leaf deliberately: it is `git archive | tar` into a plain directory and registers no worktree. gitUserName reads `git config user.name` (read-only) to seed the default ACTOR of a fabric #pick — coexistence only, never written back. The user's HEAD/index/worktree are never touched. PERF PLUMBING (T-2026-07-04-003): catFileBatch streams many blobs through ONE `git cat-file --batch` process (fail-closed on any missing object — a partial snapshot must never look complete; previously one `git show` spawn per file made whole-tree snapshots O(minutes) on a real monorepo), and diffRaw returns full-sha (--no-abbrev — raw-format abbreviation is NOT governed by --full-index) per-path change records (--raw -z --no-renames) — the changed-path inventory the INCREMENTAL native snapshot overlays onto a parent tree. NUL-DELIMITED PATHS (soundness audit C-2): changedPaths runs `-z` like its siblings diffRaw/lsTree. `core.quotePath` defaults TRUE, so without `-z` git returned `café.txt` as the octal-escaped literal `"caf\303\251.txt"` — that phantom path entered the merge plan as a DELETE (absent on all three sides), the REAL path never entered, and the merged tree silently kept the BASE version: a wrong merge with zero conflicts, on the default path, for any accent/CJK/Cyrillic/emoji/space/quote/backslash in a filename. NUL-delimited output is deliberately NOT trimmed — a path may legitimately begin or end with a space. FAIL-CLOSED PRESENCE (soundness audit C-8): treeEntryMode no longer swallows git errors. The discriminator is STRUCTURAL, not prose — `ls-tree` exits 0 with EMPTY output for a genuinely absent path and non-zero for a bad ref, a corrupt object DB, EMFILE or ENOMEM — so only empty output yields null and every error propagates. Returning null on error meant "deleted on that side" to #materialize and "not a stake, allow" to #stake-guard.

repo-lock.name: Repo Lock
repo-lock.description: A per-repo, in-process async mutex (withRepoLock(repoRoot, fn)). Serializes the one remaining git-worktree user — the cold git<2.38 merge-tree fallback — per resolved repo root so concurrent calls can't race the .git/worktrees lock; distinct repos run free. A predecessor's rejection never blocks later callers. In-process only (cross-process would need a .git flock; the parallel-absorb path no longer needs a worktree at all).

canonical-json.name: Canonical Json
canonical-json.description: Strict, dependency-free canonical serializer (sorted keys, NFC strings, no whitespace ambiguity) that produces the byte stream the essence hash digests.

essence-hash.name: Essence Hash
essence-hash.description: The load-bearing wall — essence(symbol) -> contentId. Hashes the Canonical Normal Form ⟨kind, normalized contract, edgeBag⟩, Merkle by TARGET essence (so rename is free), excludes name/path/prose/timestamps. Tarjan SCC for cycles; stable-id fold for generic-contract aliasing. .purpose contentId = "essence:v0:" + sha256(canonical). STAGE 3a: a code-unit branch in localCNF (detected by componentType==='code-unit') replaces the sorted edgeBag with the CCNF body and SUBSTITUTES each positional f:N token INLINE with the essence of codeLocalTargets[N]'s edge (via the SAME edgeEssence resolver, so intra-SCC targets become @scc-internal and a cross-symbol rename frees the chain); extern/builtin free:name tokens stay untouched; edgeBag is []. The version tag is read off entry.data.essenceTag (default ESSENCE_VERSION) so a code-unit contentId is "essence:<algo>:ts<exact>:"+sha256(canonical) (algo currently v1.1) and SCC members carry the same tag — mixed v0/v1.1 graphs interoperate because Merkle substitutes the target's full TAGGED string. essence-hash never imports the lens; the tag travels on the node. THE WALK IS ITERATIVE (T-2026-08-10). computeEssences used to resolve through a MUTUAL recursion with two entry arms — essenceOf reached itself via the singleton edge resolver AND via hashSCC's out-of-unit resolver, with essenceOf calling hashSCC in turn — so JS call depth equalled the longest chain in the SCC CONDENSATION and threw "Maximum call stack size exceeded" at roughly a THOUSAND (measured 1,050 ok / 1,080 throws; seal-path 1,000 ok / 2,000 throws). NOT an object-count ceiling: a real seal of 125,010 objects succeeded on the recursive code, because a shared gate back-links every component and Tarjan folds a naive fixture into ONE SCC the walk never nests into. resolve() now walks the condensation with an explicit heap stack (unitOf / dependenciesOf / hashUnit); `open` is the former `computing` guard, and a dependency already open reads back as @scc-internal exactly as before. tarjanSCCs was ALREADY iterative and was left alone. Content addresses are byte-identical: pinned against a pre-change golden in test/essence-iterative.test.ts, and differentially checked over this repo's own 25,336-symbol live graph, where the only two ids that moved were the code-units lifted from essence-hash.ts itself.

warp-object.name: Warp Object
warp-object.description: A WarpObject — a SymbolEntry stripped of labels and reduced to ⟨kind, contract, sorted outgoing edges, contentId⟩. liftEdges derives outgoing, typed, deduped, sorted edges from the live SymbolIndex (the single edge source the essence hash agrees on).

warp-state.name: Warp State
warp-state.description: A WarpState — the whole symbol graph of one ref lifted to MEANING. stateId = sha256 over the sorted contentIds; treeSha/absorbedAt are provenance, not identity. WarpObject.filePath is normalized REPO-RELATIVE to the absorb root (temp-worktree or cwd, with macOS /private↔/var alias handling) so a path-prefix difference never masquerades as a rename.

warp-store.name: Warp Store
warp-store.description: Content-addressed store for WARP objects + states and the .warpline/oracle.jsonl ledger appender. In-mem primary with a .warpline/ disk cache; loadState(stateId) rehydrates a persisted state back from .warpline/states/ (the Phase-2 write path needs the PARENT state across CLI runs when the in-mem map is cold) — faithful because diff reads only stableKey/contentId/contract, all preserved by serializeState. The ONLY thing Warpline writes to disk is under .warpline/. M1a — the NATIVE OBJECT STORE (byte authority, the replacement build): blob.ts (raw-byte blob, blobId=sha256 over git-style "blob <len>\0<bytes>" framing + shadow gitBlobOid), tree.ts (sorted directory manifest, git TREE-ORDER, fixed- width binary ids parseable by mode, treeId=sha256 + shadow gitTreeOid), object- store.ts (loose zlib blobs/ + trees/ under .warpline/objects/ with git fan-out, write-tmp+rename, idempotent put, verify()), snapshot.ts (snapshotDir walks a tree writing every object → root treeId + shadow gitOid; restoreTree rebuilds a byte-faithful tree with git ABSENT — binary/exec/symlink/empty-dir parity, and returns the entry count). IGNORE SEMANTICS (T-031/HIGH-3, the dogfooding unblock): the WORKTREE walk (snapshotDir, behind worktree pick/admit) honors ignore-rules.ts — .warplineignore at the root when present (gitignore syntax via the `ignore` package: dir patterns, globs, negation !, anchored /), else .gitignore, plus ALWAYS-ignored .git/.warpline/.loom/node_modules at any depth (.loom = the Loom-era engine's own state dir, tool state never meaning — T-2026-07-17-007) — so dependency trees and secrets never enter the permanent no-gc store; ignored dirs are PRUNED (no re-inclusion inside an excluded dir, gitignore parity). NATIVE IGNORE (TD-2026-08-12-218): snapshotDir's worktreeIgnoreMatcher COMPOSES #warpignore (`.warpignore` + the `.git`/`.warpline`/`.warpline-judge`/`node_modules` defaults — governs skips with git ABSENT) OVER the legacy ignore-rules matcher, so the worktree filter is a SUPERSET of the ref/projection filter (the recover invariant) and the absorb it feeds can never lift an ignored path as a symbol. Every reserved-name decision — the snapshotDir/ref-walk filters AND restoreTree's refusal — goes through #reserved-names, so the two can never disagree (a tree that could be sealed but never restored is the T-033 asymmetry). THE TREE SEMANTICS DECISION (T-2026-07-18-005; fixes the F3 drill-#1 recover false-refusal T-2026-07-18-004): WORKTREE SEMANTICS ('worktree:v1' — the snapshotDir rules above) is THE canonical tree semantics for ALL NEW bindings; the REF path (snapshotRef, full AND incremental) filters by the ref's OWN committed root ignore rules, so ref tree ≡ worktree tree of the same clean checkout (tracked-but-gitignored files OUT — git's view, not the walk's). New bindings carry additive binding.treeSemantics:'worktree:v1' (OUTSIDE the pickId preimage in both epochs; the founder-signed v3 preimage untouched); ABSENT = legacy-git semantics, grandfathered — every strand is judged under ITS OWN recorded semantics. projectTreeWorktreeSemantics(store, treeId) = the pure deterministic projection of any store tree to its worktree-semantics view (filtered by the tree's own root ignore blobs; zero writes) — how #stake cut/recover derive a legacy binding's honest recovery expectation. A root ignore-rule change between anchor and ref falls OPEN to the full walk. Pinned by test/tree-semantics.test.ts + snapshot-ignore.test.ts. TRUST FLOOR (MEDIUM-1): getBlob/getTree are VERIFIED READS — always-on, they recompute the content-address of the raw framed bytes just inflated and FAIL CLOSED on a mismatch, so restore/materialize/verify can never consume a tampered loose object (one uniform rule, no trusted/untrusted read fork). T-033 (root-ignore symmetry): snapshotRef skips .git/.warpline path components at ANY depth — a repo that TRACKS its own fabric ledger (this one does) would otherwise bind a ref tree that never matches the worktree snapshot and that restoreTree refuses to write. M1c PATH-HARDENING (Aegis C3, CVE-2021-21300 class): restoreTree FAILS CLOSED on a forged/corrupt entry name (assertSafeEntryName rejects empty/./../slash/backslash/NUL/absolute/drive-letter + reserved .git/.warpline), asserts the parent dir is a real non-symlink directory, and never writes THROUGH a pre-existing symlink — the #restore verb consumes it. The shadow gitOid EQUALS `git rev-parse <ref>^{tree}` for a clean worktree (a free byte-faithfulness proof during coexistence). Names use RAW bytes not NFC (A5). CLI: `warpline objects snapshot <dir>` / `objects verify`. Sha256 (one hash across meaning + bytes) — spec packages/warpline/docs/native-object-store-design.md. DELTA-NATIVE SNAPSHOTS (T-2026-07-04-003 byte layer, the Move-3 full-run unblock): snapshotRef has two byte-IDENTICAL paths — FULL (ls-tree inventory + ONE catFileBatch stream; was one git-show spawn per file, ~30s on this monorepo, now ~2s) and INCREMENTAL (a verified SnapshotAnchor {ref, treeId} → `git diff --raw` overlay onto the anchor tree via writeMergedTree, so an admit snapshot costs the DIFF, not the universe; sub-second warm). The incremental path applies the T-033 .git/.warpline skip identically and falls OPEN to the full walk on any anomaly (never fail-closed on the anchor). strandSnapshotAnchor is the verification gate: only a non-merge strand tagged binding.treeSemantics:'worktree:v1' whose binding.gitOid still equals `rev-parse <provenance.gitCommit>^{tree}` and whose native tree is present anchors — a merge strand's gitCommit is one parent, worktree/backfilled seals carry gitOid null, LEGACY-semantics (untagged) bindings must never seed a worktree-semantics overlay: all rejected (the first post-cutover seal walks full once, then re-anchors). captureMerge anchors base on the base strand's verified binding and ours/theirs on the just-built base tree (three universe snapshots → three diffs). Equivalence pinned by test/snapshot-incremental.test.ts (full treeId === incremental treeId on real fixtures incl. tracked-.warpline, mode flips, symlinks, deletes; plus a path-taken proof so fail-open can't mask a broken incremental path). I5 — THE WORKTREE INDEX (NATIVE-FIRST phase 0, T-2026-07-17-008): the WORKTREE walk gets the same delta discipline via worktree-index.ts, a git- style stat cache (`.warpline/index.d/<sha256(worktree)[:40]>`, worktreeIndex:v2, atomic tmp+rename, ONE FILE PER WORKTREE holding [mtimeMs,size,ino,mode,blobId,gitSha] tuples). snapshotDir(store, dir, {indexRoot}) trusts an entry only when the full stat key matches (mode included — a bare chmod is a miss), the recorded mtime clears the RACY_WINDOW_MS guard against builtAt (git's racy- timestamp lesson), and the cached blobId is still present in the store (a doctored index can never invent bytes); every anomaly fails OPEN to the full read+hash walk, and the refreshed index is written back after every walk. Warm walk on this monorepo (23k files): 7.1s full → 0.7-1.6s indexed, byte-identical treeId+gitOid (pinned with mutation-detection touch/edit/add/delete/chmod + path-taken + racy-guard + fail-open tests in test/worktree-index.test.ts). Wired behind native propose/resolve, worktree pick/admit (snapshotState indexRoot), and `objects snapshot`. DURABILITY (soundness audit C-7): writeLoose no longer hand-rolls write-tmp+rename — it goes through #warp-durable, so a loose object's bytes AND the fanout directory entry that publishes them are on the medium before put returns (git has hardened loose objects by default since 2.36, `core.fsync`). The worktree INDEX is deliberately NOT hardened: it is a self-declared cache whose corrupt read already falls open to a cold walk. D-G — ONE SHARD PER WORKTREE, NOT ONE SHARED FILE (soundness audit 2026-07-31, Arky): worktreeIndex:v1 was a SINGLE `.warpline/index` holding every worktree's section, and save was an UNLOCKED read-modify-write of the whole file called from snapshotDir OUTSIDE the fabric lock — two concurrent snapshots interleave and the last writer silently drops the other agent's section. Nothing ever pruned a dead worktree, so one stress run left 54 MB / 308,497 entries / 82 sections that every subsequent propose re-read and re-serialized (which also widened the clobber window from microseconds to hundreds of ms). Cost per save was O(all worktrees ever seen). git is per-worktree AND locked (index.lock); Warpline was weaker on both halves. THE CHOICE: shard, do not lock — sharding removes the SHARING, so there is no critical section to get wrong, whereas a lock leaves the 54 MB re-serialize in place and then serializes every agent's snapshot behind it; a lock also adds a timeout/staleness policy, i.e. a way for a CACHE to fail CLOSED, and a cache that can fail closed is worse than one that can be stale. Pruning becomes unlink, decidable per file (each shard records the absolute worktree path it caches), and a corrupt shard now costs ONE worktree a cold walk instead of all 82. saveWorktreeIndex reads/writes NOTHING but its own shard; pruneWorktreeIndex(root, keep?) unlinks shards whose worktree is gone using a BOUNDED 4 KB header read (the `worktree` field is serialized before `entries` for exactly this — a full parse would reintroduce the O(all worktrees) wall it removes: measured 172.9 ms vs 1.4 ms). Staging residue (`.tmp.*`) and headers that yield no worktree are never deleted — a `.tmp.*` may be another writer's mid-publish file. MIGRATION: an existing v1 file is ADOPTED, not orphaned — load falls back to its section so the first walk after the upgrade is still warm, and the first save splits EVERY section into shards (skipping any that already has one, so a fresher shard always wins) then deletes the v1 file, so no worktree suffers a cold-walk storm and the 54 MB is reclaimed once. MEASURED at the audit's 82 sections / 308,497 entries / 62.3 MB: 404.2 → 4.2 ms per save (96x), bytes touched 62.3 MB read + 62.3 MB re-serialized → 0.32 MB read + 0.76 MB re-serialized, and two real concurrent OS processes go from 1/2 survivors to 2/2 (bench/worktree-index-dg.mts; pinned by test/worktree-index-sharding.test.ts).

warp-durable.name: Warp Durable
warp-durable.description: The ONE durable-write discipline for every Warpline write a verb later claims succeeded (soundness audit C-7 + C-15) — durable.ts. C-7: `grep -rnE "fsync|fdatasync|O_SYNC" src` returned ZERO matches, so "PICK sealed → exit 0" was a claim about the PAGE CACHE. tmp+rename is atomic against process death and silent about power loss: without an fsync on the staging fd BEFORE the rename the rename can outrun the data (the file is atomically published as garbage), and without an fsync on the PARENT DIRECTORY AFTER it the rename itself can simply be lost — the half people forget. atomicWriteSync does mkdir → unique `wx` staging file → write → fsync(file) → rename → fsync(dir); appendDurableSync fsyncs the ledger append (and the directory only when the append CREATED the file). COVERED: the ledger append + whole-ledger rewrite (#fabric), both tip pointers (#fabric writeSelvage and #fabric-refs writeRef), the per-agent #scratch refs, and #warp-store loose objects. NOT covered, deliberately: the worktree index shards (a cache) and the shadow/grade/audit sidecars (observational telemetry — a lost last row is not a false success claim). THE macOS CALL, STATED: Apple's fsync(2) does not flush the drive's own write cache and F_FULLFSYNC does, at ~50x the cost; git exposes the choice (core.fsyncMethod) — WE DO NOT GET IT. Node has no fcntl binding and libuv's uv__fs_fsync on __APPLE__ already issues F_FULLFSYNC (falling back to F_BARRIERFSYNC then plain fsync only when the filesystem rejects it), so fs.fsyncSync IS the hardware flush here. Measured on APFS: 3.66 ms per file fsync, 3.79 ms per directory fsync, against 0.17 ms for the whole unhardened tmp+rename — the ~50x signature of F_FULLFSYNC, and fdatasyncSync measured identically, so there is no cheaper Node-reachable rung. The choice is therefore "hardware flush or nothing", which is why the escape hatch is real: WARPLINE_FSYNC=none makes every fsync a no-op and changes NOTHING else (same bytes, same atomic rename, same unique staging names). Default is `all`, INCLUDING for an absent, empty or UNRECOGNIZED value — a durability toggle fails SAFE. It is an ENV var and deliberately not a .warpline/config.json key: config.json lives inside the directory this module hardens, so the toggle would be less durable than the thing it governs. setFsyncPolicy() is the seam for a future explicit CLI flag. syncDir's tolerance is narrow ON PURPOSE — only a Windows directory-open failure (no directory fsync exists there) and only EINVAL/ENOTSUP/ENOSYS from the fsync itself ("this filesystem does not implement it"); ENOENT, EACCES, EIO, ENOSPC and EBADF all PROPAGATE, because durability that silently is not there is the bug being fixed. C-15: tmpNameFor is the single source of the staging name, `<target>.tmp.<pid>.<n>` — the pattern object-store.ts and stake-git.ts already used correctly, now shared so a fixed `${p}.tmp` cannot reappear. A SHARED staging name defeated the very CAS the ref writers publish (the CAS runs BEFORE the write): two writers that both passed it raced on one path, and A renamed B's VALUE into place and returned SUCCESS while B's rename failed ENOENT (Arky D-B, demonstrated; reproduced deterministically in test/staging-name-collision.test.ts by queueing the renames rather than racing threads). isTmpResidue is the shared predicate #fabric-refs uses so staging residue can never be read as — or minted as — a ref. NOT closed by this: fsync does not make an APPEND atomic; a torn tail line on a full disk (audit C-13) remains open. FOLLOW-UP: a cold genesis pays ~10 ms per NEW loose object (2.2s → 22.9s for 2,000 objects, measured); git's answer is core.fsyncMethod=batch, which needs a batch boundary the ObjectStore does not currently have.

warpignore.name: Warpignore
warpignore.description: Warpline's OWN, git-INDEPENDENT ignore mechanism (warp/warpignore.ts; T-2026-08-12-002, founder correction TD-2026-08-12-218). A native-first tool that "never touches git" cannot govern its own skips through git's `.gitignore` — so Warpline owns the `.warpignore` file + a pure hand-rolled gitignore-style handler (no third-party matcher on the native path). loadWarpignore(root) reads `<root>/.warpignore` (v1: root-level only) and returns a WarpignoreMatcher with isIgnored(relPath, isDir?); parseWarpignore is the pure content seam. Syntax: `#` comments + blank lines skipped, `!` negation (last match wins), trailing `/` = dir-only, `*`/`**`/`?` globs, leading (or non-trailing) `/` = root-anchored else any-depth. BUILT-IN DEFAULTS, always ignored at any depth and NOT un-negatable by a stray `!`: `.git`, `.warpline`, `.warpline-judge` (the Judge's witness/sandbox dir) and `node_modules` — matched through #reserved-names so `.GIT`/`GIT~1` spellings are covered too. WIRING: #snapshot's worktreeIgnoreMatcher and #lens-walk COMPOSE (OR) this native matcher OVER the legacy ignore-rules matcher — never replace it — so the worktree filter stays a SUPERSET of the ref-snapshot / worktree-semantics projection filter (the invariant recover relies on), and `.warpignore` only ever ENLARGES the exclude set. CANONICAL-WITH-LEGACY-FALLBACK (T-2026-08-12-002): `.warpignore` is canonical and `warpline init` only ever writes it; when it is ABSENT the deprecated legacy `.warplineignore` is read through THIS handler too (loadWarpignore) so existing repos never break, and `noteWarpignoreDeprecation` returns a one-time-per-root stderr notice the CLI emits on init/status/diff. A present `.warpignore` SHADOWS the legacy alias for this handler (canonical wins). Ignored paths never enter a tree, so they never become symbols and never enter the fabric — this is what kills the `fork --into <dir-under-repo-root>` phantom-symbol footgun (a nested worktree absorbed as `#cfg:wt-*/...` on the next root propose). Pure + deterministic (no clock, no ambient state); rules precompile once per load. Pinned by test/warpignore.test.ts (defaults, dir-only/globs/negation/anchoring, the dogfood regression asserting phantom symbols absent from the absorbed state, and the `!.git` safety case).

reserved-names.name: Reserved Names
reserved-names.description: The ONE normalizer behind every reserved-path-component decision — the fix for soundness-audit C-3 (git's CVE-2014-9390 class). `restore` writes tree bytes to disk, so a tree entry named `.git` overwrites a real repo and `.git/hooks/post-commit` is arbitrary code execution on the victim's next commit. The guard was an exact-match, case-SENSITIVE Set — the 2013 version of git's — so on a case-insensitive filesystem (macOS by default, Windows always) `.GIT` sailed through: the audit wrote a hook into the real `.git` and watched it FIRE, and `.WARPLINE` overwrote a live ledger. Reachable on case-SENSITIVE hosts too (Linux CI, Docker): an agent commits `.GIT/hooks/`, the strand is legitimately sealed, correctly hashed and verify-clean, and it detonates on a macOS box. normalizeReservedName folds a component before any lookup — NFC, drop HFS+-IGNORABLE codepoints (U+200C-200F/202A-202E/206A-206F/ FEFF — HFS+ ignores them when comparing, so `.gi<ZWNJ>t` really opens `.git`, git's next_hfs_char), strip trailing dots and spaces (Win32 strips them when RESOLVING), case-fold — and matchesReservedName additionally recognizes `~N` 8.3 SHORTNAMES (Win32 takes the long name minus leading dots, truncates to 6 chars, appends ~N: `.git`→GIT~1, `.warpline`→WARPLI~1). Deliberately NOT over-broad — .gitignore/.gitattributes/git-notes.md/g~1 stay ordinary files, because these same predicates decide what a SNAPSHOT ingests and a false positive silently drops a real file from the tree. Consumed by #warp-store (restoreTree's assertSafeEntryName, snapshotRefFull, snapshotRefIncremental) and by ignore-rules' ALWAYS_IGNORE, so snapshot and restore agree by construction. KNOWN GAP: NTFS *hashed* shortnames (GI7EBA~1, emitted only on an 8.3 basis collision) are not modeled. Pinned by test/reserved-name-normalization.test.ts (every spelling REFUSED at restore and never ingested by snapshotDir; legitimate names still allowed).

code-lens.name: Code Lens
code-lens.description: The TS code-lens interface surface (spec §2 / warpline-code-lens.md). Types ONLY (stage 1): CodeUnit — a SymbolEntry-shaped synthetic node keyed #code:<rel-path>::<qualified-name>, carrying the identity-bearing codeEssence (CCNF) body slot, resolved free-reference edges, and a visible reducedFidelity marker — and the CodeLens registry contract (extensions + lift()). Declares no behavior; pins the shape the lift machinery (ts-lens, stage 2) is built against. componentType 'code-unit' lets code-units flow through the EXISTING WARP (essence-hash/sem-delta/predict/oracle) as nodes in the same universe, never a parallel graph.

code-essence.name: Code Essence
code-essence.description: The pure-syntactic Code Canonical Normal Form (CCNF) producer — codeCNF(node) -> canonical token string for one declaration. The SYNTACTIC HALF of the lens: structure + WRITTEN annotations only, NO ts.Program/checker. Hardens the AST-absorb spike: (1) scope-correct alpha-normalization honoring JS hoisting (var/fn-decl -> nearest function scope; let/const/class -> block; params/type-params -> unit scope; catch var -> catch scope) with bindings as (depth, ordinal) coordinates and shadowing-correct use resolution, replacing the spike's unsound flat first-declaration-order map; (2) separate b:/t:/L: namespaces (the spike ignored type-params, so f<T> vs f<U> falsely DIFFERed); (3) the false-EQUAL guard (§3.2), FAIL-CLOSED since CCNF v1.1 (amendment 2026-07-02): EVERY modifier present is serialized (canonical token name, sorted — accessibility/override/readonly/accessor/declare/async/static/ abstract/export and any future modifier), decorators are serialized on function-likes AND parameters in SOURCE order (order is semantic) with their expressions through the standard expression path so decorator refs join the §4 frontier, type-param modifiers (<const T>) included; plus generator*/get-set/optional?/default-presence/rest.../definite!/ optional-chain?./nullish?? each produce a DISTINCT cnf. Exports CCNF_ALGO_VERSION ('v1.1') — bumped on ANY serialization change so cross-version essence comparison is impossible; test/false-equal-probes.test.ts is the per-TS-release ship gate; (4) literal normalization (§3.3) — integers (hex/oct/bin) -> exact decimal, bigint -> decimal+n, non-integer numerics -> raw source lexeme NOT an IEEE-754 round-trip (0.1 != 1e-1 by design), strings/templates NFC; (5) directive comments (@ts-ignore/@ts-expect-error/ @ts-nocheck/eslint-disable) hashed, free prose dropped. An optional freeRefClassifier strips free names to positional f:{idx} edge tokens (default emits free:{name}, keeping stage 1 self-contained and spike-equivalent). Stage 2 adds codeCNFDetailed(node,opts) -> {cnf, freeRefs[]}: the SAME first-appearance ordering drives both the body's f:{idx} tokens and the freeRefs index, so freeRefs[idx] (name + a representative ts.Identifier node) aligns 1:1 with the f:idx token. codeCNF now delegates to it and returns .cnf (the stage-1 signature is unchanged). This positional alignment is the input the lens hands the checker for §4 resolution; call order is meaning, so a sorted edge-set would be wrong.

code-symbol.name: Code Symbol
code-symbol.description: Pure string builders for a code-unit's WARP key and structural stable key (spec §2). codeSymbol(relPath, qualifiedName) -> "#code:"+relPath+"::"+ qualifiedName (the SymbolIndex key); codeStableKey(relPath, structuralPath) -> relPath+"::"+structuralPath where structuralPath is the (scopeKind#ordinal) chain (e.g. class#0/method#2). Both are LABELS — provenance + rename tiebreakers — NEVER hashed; pure functions of their inputs (no I/O), so trivially deterministic across machines.

ts-lens.name: Ts Lens
ts-lens.description: The TS/TSX code-lens (stage 2, spec §4/§5) — the checker-dependent half. TsLens.lift(rootDir) enumerates .ts/.tsx files (sorted, .d.ts excluded), builds ONE ts.Program over them against a FIXED, HARDCODED compiler-options baseline (ESNext target/module, Bundler resolution, strict, skipLibCheck, noEmit, allowJs:false — NEVER a discovered tsconfig, §5.2), and lifts each code-unit (FunctionDeclaration, arrow/fn-expr const, class + its method/ctor/ getter/setter/field members; default-export -> qualifiedName 'default'; overload sets -> the implementation signature, bodiless overloads skipped). Per unit it computes codeEssence via codeCNFDetailed and resolves each free VALUE ref to one of four §4 classes, ALIGNED to the body's f:idx slots: (a) module-local lifted code-unit -> 'local' edge (edgeKind calls/reads) carrying the target #code: symbol (body emits f:idx); (b) imported name -> 'extern' id extern:<specifier-as-written>#<exportName> derived from the SYNTACTIC import statement, NOT checker module resolution (§5.3 — deterministic with no node_modules); (c) builtin/global -> 'builtin' name; (d) unresolved -> set reducedFidelity. Checker is used for identity resolution ONLY (getSymbolAtLocation + getAliasedSymbol), never inferred types (§5.1). lift() returns CodeUnit[] sorted by symbol (determinism). Exports TS_LENS_VERSION (the exact pinned ts version) for stage 3 to stamp into the essence tag. File enumeration is delegated to #lens-walk (shared pruning + the repo's own ignore rules).

lens-walk.name: Lens Walk
lens-walk.description: The SHARED source-enumeration walk behind every code-lens. enumerateLensFiles(rootDir, accept, extraSkipDirs) prunes directories and returns the accepted files sorted by absolute path (determinism §5). A file is lifted only when BOTH agree: it is not under a BASELINE_SKIP_DIRS name (dependency/build output + VCS/tool state — node_modules, .git, .warpline, .loom, dist, build, .build, .next, coverage) AND the composed root ignore matcher admits it: #warpignore (native `.warpignore` + defaults, governs skips with git absent, TD-2026-08-12-218) OR'd OVER #warp-store loadIgnoreMatcher (.warplineignore preferred, else .gitignore) — the SAME superset the worktree snapshot uses, so a nested worktree listed in `.warpignore` is pruned here too. Extracted because each lens carried its OWN denylist and neither ever consulted the repository's own ignore semantics: cfg-lens was lifting every JSON key under Swift's .build/ as a symbol — 14,168 of 25,341 IN A WORKTREE ABSORB (name the surface: seals ride `git archive`, which carries git-tracked files only, so the sealed LEDGER never saw this junk — the measured seal delta across the fix was +2, not a mass retirement) absorbed symbols (55.9%), one output-file-map.json alone yielding 927 — with ABSOLUTE machine paths inside the ids, making the state's content-address machine-dependent. Sharing the snapshot path's matcher means what a lens lifts and what a snapshot seals can no longer disagree by construction. SCOPE (v1, inherited from #warp-store): root-level ignore files only — nested .gitignore files are not collected, which is why .build is in the baseline rather than left to packages/conductor/.gitignore.

lens-registry.name: Lens Registry
lens-registry.description: The code-lens registry (spec §9). lensFor(ext) -> CodeLens | undefined maps a file extension (incl. leading dot) to the responsible lens. Registered: TsLens (.ts/.tsx) and CfgLens (.json/.yml/.yaml — #cfg-lens, P3 GAP-1). The single seam per-language lenses plug into without touching the lift/absorb path.

cfg-lens.name: Cfg Lens
cfg-lens.description: The structured-data lens (P3 Lane A, GAP-1) — JSON/YAML key-trees lifted to CodeUnit-shaped nodes so config files (the census-proven agent-collision center of mass: package.json, tsconfig, CI yaml) get MEANING verdicts instead of falling silently to the byte tier. GRANULARITY (cfg-v1): one file-root marker unit per parsed file (key '/'); a top-level key whose value is a non-empty map lifts ONE UNIT PER CHILD (/dependencies/react) so disjoint dep adds COMMUTE (autoClean) while the same dep at different versions is a same-unit divergent body → KNOT via predict's scalar 'body' slot rule; a top-level scalar key is one unit; a child's whole value subtree is one leaf. SEQUENCES defer to the byte tier: any unit whose subtree contains an array becomes a content-INDEPENDENT reduced-fidelity 'seq' marker (order is meaning the key-tree algebra cannot honestly claim — pretending would knot CI-step edits the token merge composes today). DETERMINISM: raw scalar LEXEMES (as-written is meaning, mirrors ts-essence's literal discipline; 1.0 ≠ 1); map key ORDER is not meaning (canonical sort — a pure reorder is the empty delta); the KEY PATH and FILE PATH are folded into the body (documented exception to labels-never-hashed: for structured data the key path IS the contract and the file location IS meaning; cost: cfg file rename reads as retire+born). Essence tag cfg-v1 (own content-address namespace, never colliding with TS CCNF). FAIL-CLOSED: unparseable / duplicate-key / non-map-root / multi-document / anchor-alias-tag/merge-key YAML / oversize (>1MiB) files fall to the byte tier with a single VISIBLE reduced-fidelity 'unliftable' marker unit — never silent-empty, never a false verdict. JSON is parsed by a strict local scanner with JSONC comforts (comments + trailing commas — tsconfig reality; comments are prose, never hashed) and raw-lexeme + duplicate-key fidelity JSON.parse cannot provide; YAML via the `yaml` package, plain core schema only. Lockfiles are excluded entirely (#derived-artifacts). File enumeration is delegated to #lens-walk, which prunes the shared baseline (node_modules/.git/.warpline/.loom/dist/build/.build/.next/coverage — the fabric never lifts itself; .loom is the Loom-era engine's state dir, same rule, prior name, T-2026-07-17-007: worktree absorbs were lifting thousands of #cfg:.loom/states/* symbols into every verdict) AND applies the repo's own .warplineignore/.gitignore; this lens adds only .paradigm (machine-managed state). Before that delegation existed this lens was the single largest source of junk in the universe — every JSON key under Swift's .build/ became a symbol (14,168 of 25,341 in a WORKTREE absorb — 55.9% of what `status`, `diff` and worktree-mode absorbs saw; the git-ref seal path was never affected), with ABSOLUTE machine paths in the ids. Measured again on an Expo-shaped fixture, where the field test is headed: 3,673 symbols without ignore-awareness vs 13 with it, and the junk (ios/Pods, .expo) is reachable ONLY through .gitignore — no baseline denylist would have caught it.

derived-artifacts.name: Derived Artifacts
derived-artifacts.description: The DERIVED-ARTIFACT rule (P3 GAP-1). Lockfiles (package-lock.json, npm-shrinkwrap.json, yarn.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml, bun.lockb/.lock, deno.lock, Cargo.lock, composer.lock, Gemfile.lock, poetry.lock, Pipfile.lock, flake.lock) are machine-generated projections of the manifests beside them — derived, never meaning. isDerivedArtifact(relPath) matches by explicit BASENAME set (no glob — fail-open here would silently wrong-merge a file we pretended to understand). Consumers: #cfg-lens never lifts them; #materialize never knots them (both-sides-divergent → take OURS wholesale + a STALE marker in MergePlan.derivedStale — regeneration from the merged manifests is the consumer's step, recorded not performed in v1); #honesty labels them 'derived'.

honesty.name: Honesty
honesty.description: Per-path merge HONESTY labels (P3 GAP-1) — "what fraction of this merge did meaning govern?" classifyMergePaths(paths, states) labels every touched path exactly one of: meaning-decided (a lens lifted REAL units from the file — TS code-units, cfg key units, .purpose symbols; cfg MARKER units never claim coverage), derived (#derived-artifacts), or byte-decided (everything else — README, unparseable configs, sequence-valued keys). Returns sorted perPath + aggregate counts {meaningDecided, byteDecided, derived}. G1-ADDITIVE presentation data, never a verdict input: attached as AdmitResult.coverage (on a materialized CLEAN admit, classified against proposed/selvage/merged states) and OracleRecord.coverage (over changedPaths(base,A) ∪ (base,B), real refs only; schemaVersion unchanged).

lift-code-units.name: Lift Code Units
lift-code-units.description: The absorb-side bridge (stage 3a, spec §9 sub-phase 2 / §4.1). liftCodeUnits(rootDir) runs every REGISTERED lens over a read-only worktree root and collects the union of CodeUnits (re-sorted by symbol for deterministic injection order). injectCodeUnits(index, units) turns each CodeUnit into a synthetic SymbolEntry (kind 'component' + componentType 'code-unit'; DETERMINISTIC id = sha256('code:'+symbol), NOT a uuid; source 'premise'; references = the distinct LOCAL targets in first-appearance order so liftEdges yields code->localTarget edges into buildEssenceGraph.adj and Tarjan detects code cycles) and splices it into the live SymbolIndex (entries + byType + bySource) BEFORE computeEssences runs — same universe, never a parallel graph. The identity-bearing payload travels on entry.data: codeEssence (body with positional f:idx slots), codeLocalTargets (the ordered distinct local target symbols the f:N slots substitute against), and essenceTag = CCNF_ALGO_VERSION+":ts"+TS_LENS_VERSION (e.g. "v1.1:ts5.9.3" — the algorithm- and compiler-pinned version namespace §5.2, so essence-hash never imports the lens — the tag travels with the node). P3 GAP-1: a unit may OVERRIDE the tag per-unit (CodeUnit.essenceTag — #cfg-lens stamps cfg-v1) and carry a cfgMarker discriminator into entry.data for the #honesty classifier.

absorb.name: Absorb
absorb.description: absorb(gitRef) -> WarpState. Materializes the ref's tree via `git archive | tar` into a temp dir (NO worktree, no .git/worktrees lock — concurrency-safe, T-2026-06-23-003), loadLiveGraph on it, lifts every symbol, builds the WarpState, releaseTree in a finally. The literal WORKTREE ref absorbs the live cwd uncommitted state. STAGE 3a: after loadLiveGraph and before buildWarpState (both the ref and WORKTREE paths), liftCodeUnits + injectCodeUnits splice TS/TSX code-units into the index as synthetic nodes so code essences flow through the same WARP. The lens only READS the worktree/cwd — the read-only invariant holds. DETERMINISM INVARIANT: absorbing the same ref twice is byte-identical (stateId + every per-symbol contentId + repo-relative filePath), so diff(absorb(HEAD), absorb(HEAD)) is provably ZERO. Rests on (a) the absorb root being passed to buildWarpState for repo-relative filePaths, (b) deterministic .purpose/portal file-discovery order in premise-core's aggregator, and (c) the lens's sorted file enumeration + deterministic synthetic ids (duplicate-symbol resolution + Merkle essences are stable across parses regardless of filesystem order or temp-dir prefix).

hazard.name: Hazard
hazard.description: THE CLEAN-HAZARD ADVISORY (T-2026-06-24-015, founder-gated pre-field-test). An ADVISORY, never a gate: it cannot raise a refusal, cannot enter knots/dangling, cannot move status or sealed. evaluateHazards returns [] for any status other than CLEAN, so it is structurally incapable of riding a contested verdict — which matters because the founder DELIBERATELY declined the over-block fix in favour of measuring the real false-KNOT rate in the field (TD-2026-08-11-663), making the contested denominator the headline instrument of the whole value-prop proof. A feature that could add to it would corrupt the number everything rests on. WHAT IT ACTUALLY CATCHES, which is narrower than the task title suggests. The recorded canonical example (A lowers a limit 100->50, B adds a retry loop assuming the old one) is NOT the live defect: essences are Merkle-by-target and TRANSITIVE, so if B's symbol references A's, the edit ripples into a shared key and the verdict is already a conflicting-slot KNOT — an over-block, i.e. #essence-hash's problem, not this one. The residual class is changes whose transitive closures are DISJOINT in the lifted graph but coupled through a channel the graph does not represent. The sharpest instance is guaranteed rather than probable: #cfg-lens emits references: [] on every config node, so a config value and the code reading it are ALWAYS graph islands, and any (config-value x code) pair is necessarily a symbol-disjoint independent CLEAN that auto-weaves with zero review. On an Expo app that is app.json / eas.json / package.json versus the code reading them. There is no safety net under it either: #grade's trust floor needs K_MIN_GRADED=3 graded outcomes and readGradeSidecar returns [] on a missing sidecar, so HELD cannot fire on a fresh repo at all. THE RULE. On CLEAN — for BOTH confidence values, because the 'linked' prior is inverted for the born-caller case and restricting to 'independent' would miss it — take each side's LOCALLY-CHANGED units, extract the value tokens that entered or left the essence (free:/str:/num:/tmpl: for code, canonical JSON scalars for cfg), intersect across sides, and weight by CORPUS RARITY computed in one pass over the base state. Rarity is the whole noise control and needs no break-history, which is essential because a new repo has none: num:0 and free:useState score ~0; num:8500 and str:"rate_limit" score high. Danger signals (a portal gate, high fan-in) are a SEVERITY MULTIPLIER on an already-triggered hazard, never the trigger. A token whose participants are the same symbol on both sides is dropped — the graph saw that one. WHAT IT DOES NOT CATCH, pinned as an executable assertion in test/hazard-advisory.test.ts rather than left in prose: the canonical case itself (zero shared tokens), invariants expressed only in comments (excluded from the essence), anything in unlifted files (.js/.mjs/native — and Expo ships babel.config.js, metro.config.js, app.config.js), and cross-process or temporal invariants with no shared literal. It also produces false positives by construction. An empty hazard list is NOT an all-clear, and nothing in the surface may license the sentence "Warpline catches invariant conflicts" — the CLI says LEXICAL and states the blind spot in the same breath. WHERE IT LIVES: additive `hazards?` on #admit's result, attached by ONE shared helper (hazardAdvisory) that both the git-era and native paths call, because two copies of a rule is exactly how #refusal diverged; a .warpline/hazards.jsonl sidecar (G5 pattern, suppressed under shadow); an additive capped field on the #shadow row; and a #warpline-health line ADJACENT TO but never folded into `contested`. `mode: 'hold'` is DECLARED AND UNIMPLEMENTED — it folds to 'advise' — so it cannot quietly become a gate mid-measurement. ALSO ON THE FORECAST (T-2026-08-11-016): the same evaluateHazards signal now rides #oracle's OracleRecord and #weave's `weave --preview` (additive `hazards?`, via oracle.forecastHazards / forecastHazardsFromRefs), so a preview is never MORE optimistic than the admit it forecasts — a jointly-wrong (config x code) pair used to preview as an unqualified CLEAN while admit surfaced the coupling. Gated on the MEANING-CLEAN forecast (no knots/dangling — the admit-CLEAN equivalent) and honours `mode: off`. The forecast writes NO sidecar (a preview is ephemeral); it is still advisory-only and moves no verdict, no mergeClean, no convergence.

sem-delta.name: Sem Delta
sem-delta.description: The SemDelta and diff(base, branch), keyed by stableKey (SymbolEntry.id, so rename survives). contentId-equal short-circuits to no-delta; a pure rename/move is the EMPTY delta. MOVE RECONCILIATION (T-2026-08-11) makes that last sentence true for CODE UNITS, which it never was. The contentId-equal rename branch only runs for a key present on BOTH sides, and a code-unit's stableKey is an opaque HASH while its SYMBOL embeds the file path — so moving a file produced two unrelated entries (retired at the old path, born at the new) and the rename branch was unreachable by construction. The delta reported a refactor as destruction. MEASURED COST on a 40-seal run: 12 of 42 strands graded `overturned`, calibratedConfidence 0.8 -> 0.35, every one of them a file move whose body never changed — #grade overturns a strand whose symbols a later strand RETIRES, so routine reorganisation was silently corrupting the per-codebase calibration signal (the moat). After the fix the same run grades 0 overturned / 29 survived / 0 retirements / 10 renamed-noop. reconcileMovedCodeUnits pairs a retired with a born carrying the IDENTICAL contentId AND the identical qualified-name suffix, and re-emits the pair as one zero-weight rename. CONSERVATIVE BY CONSTRUCTION, because a wrong pairing erases a real retirement: `#code:` only (a `#cfg:` file rename stays retire+born — that is the RATIFIED trade in #cfg-lens, where the file path is deliberately folded into the body because for structured data the location IS meaning); the suffix is taken from the SYMBOL after its FIRST `::`, kept whole so `Cls::method` never collides with a free function of the same leaf name; and pairing is STRICTLY 1:1 — an ambiguous key (two identical bodies under one name) pairs nothing and is pinned as such in test/code-diff.test.ts. Classifies changed contract slots and edge add/remove. A symbol-born delta carries an edgesAdded-only changeset (ALL of the born object's outgoing edges) so a new symbol's outgoing edges feed the dangle pass the same way a gained edge does (born-consumer → retired-target). STAGE 3b: ContractChangeset gains a bodyChanged flag → a 'body' slot in changedSlotsOf. classify sets bodyChanged when either side is a code-unit: classify runs ONLY when contentIds already differ, and a code-unit's identity IS its body (incl. inline-substituted local refs), so a differing code-unit contentId means the body moved. 'body' is the body-INTERNAL analog of 'steps' (a literal/operator change with no call change fires 'body' but not 'edges'; a call add/remove still fires 'edges' via the existing path — both correct). This closes the TD-806 "0 deltas on a .ts-only change" gap. RANKING SIGNAL (T-2026-07-03-002, additive): each delta also carries localChanged — TRUE iff THIS side changed the symbol's OWN content (born/retired existence, a name-keyed slot/edge, a scalar contract field, or a code-unit's raw codeEssence/codeLocalTargets), FALSE = a pure RIPPLE re-address (contentId moved only via edge-target essence transitivity, Merkle-by-target). Never consulted by knot/dangle/autoClean semantics — presentation+ranking data only.

predict.name: Predict
predict.description: predict(ΔA, ΔB) -> {autoClean, knots[], dangling[]}. The commute / knot / dangle decision procedure. Dangle wins precedence so the score is a true partition; same-key identical-essence is convergent (autoClean). STAGE 3b: 'body' joins the scalar-conflict-slot list (componentType|kind|steps|body) so two branches that edit the SAME code-unit's body to DIFFERENT essences are a KNOT with conflictingSlots ['body'] (git may auto-merge textually-distant edits Warpline flags at function granularity); a call to a code-unit the other branch retired surfaces as a DANGLE via the unchanged edge pass. RIPPLE-GATE (stage 2, TD-2026-08-12-831): the 'body' slot is a genuine conflict only when BOTH sides contest it — bodyContested(d) = (d.localChanged ?? true) || (d.rippleFromContract ?? true). A callee const/body ripple that re-addresses the caller's inlined body but COMMUTES (signature held) leaves that side uncontested → CLEAN, killing the measured 3/3 over-block false-KNOTs while direct×direct and signature-bearing-ripple×edit stay contested → KNOT preserved. Consults #sem-delta.rippleFromContract/localChanged. RANKING (T-2026-07-03-002, additive): Knot.direct / Dangle.direct = TRUE iff ≥1 side's delta has localChanged (own-content edit); FALSE = a ripple-only knot (both essences shifted transitively — the 48-176-symbol avalanche class ground truth proved 0% churn-validated). Absent flags default direct (surfaced, never silently collapsed). The knot/dangle DECISIONS themselves are unchanged. RULE LABELS (refusal:v1 SP1a, TD-2026-07-21-766): every emitted Knot and Dangle carries KnotRule — which of the five branches fired (retire-vs-edit | born-divergent | both-retype | conflicting-slot | dangle-retire). The former boolean isKnot predicate became knotRuleOf, returning WHICH branch fired instead of merely THAT one did (non-null is exactly the old true), so the partition is byte-identical: this labels control flow, it does not steer it. The label is what lets a cold agent (falsifier F4) branch on WHY without parsing prose — retire-vs-edit is a keep-or-drop decision, conflicting-slot is a merge-the-slot decision, born-divergent is a pick-one decision: same verdict class, different work. OPTIONAL on the interface so hand-built Prediction fixtures and pre-rule persisted shapes stay valid; absent means UNLABELLED, never a guessed label (#refusal reports it as null). Consumed by #refusal's contested index.

justification.name: Justification
justification.description: The v0 Justification — actor/intent from the branch tip's git log, computedRipple via getReferencesTo over changed symbols, danglingRefs, and a reserved signature field (unsigned:sha256 stub). P2.3 (forge-spec §3b, ADDITIVE): an optional claimId POINTER to the author's pre-declared #claim sidecar — present only when the change was proposed under a claim (absent ⇒ byte-identical to the pre-claim schema); the claim body and its grading never ride inline (G5).

strand.name: Strand
strand.description: A Strand — one PICK sealed into the fabric. Two deliberately-separated identities: stateId (the REPRODUCIBLE content-address of the meaning it lands on, from #warp-state) and pickId (the EVENT identity, including actor + time + intent, so attribution/provenance lives here). Carries a compact StrandDelta (born/retired/contractChanged names + renamedNoop count), an objectCount, git coexistence provenance (ref/treeSha/gitCommit), and calibratedConfidence — RESERVED (null until graded), the one field a git-backed history can't carry and the seed of the non-portable moat. computePickId null-normalizes the body (canonical rejects null) for the ADDRESS only; stored JSON keeps real nulls. SCHEMA v2 (TD-2026-07-01-721, the pickId identity contract): schemaVersion widens 1→(1|2). A v2 pickId is pick:v2:sha256 and folds INTO the address the chain link (parentPickId = the ledger tip's pickId, so reorder/forge breaks the chain, A1), the byte binding (binding.treeId, so a bait-and-switch binding is caught without a signature — Aegis C2), agent attribution (authoredBy.agentId; sessionKey EXCLUDED), and on a merge the second DAG parent (mergeParentPickId = the base strand) + the pinned merge algo (MergeRecipe.algo 'warpline-merge3-v1', restored per Judge). Still EXCLUDED from both rules: calibratedConfidence, binding.gitOid, merge.{base,ours,theirs,result} — and binding.treeSemantics (T-2026-07-18-005: the additive tree-semantics tag, 'worktree:v1' on new bindings, absent = legacy-git; rides OUTSIDE the preimage in BOTH epochs, so no signed identity moved). strand.byteOnly (T-2026-07-18-002, the byte-custody flag on a meaning-NOOP + tree-advanced seal) is additive and rides INTO the v2 preimage via the rest spread (new strands only; derivable: empty delta + stateId === parent's + binding advanced). The v1 rule (pick:v0) is byte-for-byte preserved so historical strands re-verify. LEGACY (§7, TD-2026-07-01-202): the on-disk fabric was sealed under two retired rules and #grade overwrote a hashed field for the oldest strands; computePickIdWholeBody + reproducesUnderKnownRule try the finite set of known rules, and the graded-over residue is grandfathered by pickId in .warpline/fabric-legacy.json. M1b — the byte seam: #pick/#admit/#seal stamp binding on every seal (snapshotState = snapshotDir for worktree, snapshotRef for a git ref); a CLEAN merge stamps the compositional result (A2 — base tree via cat-file + the merge's byte changes, never the git-archive dir). SCHEMA v3 (V3.1, docs/specs/warpline-v3-identity.md §1, founder-signed §9): schemaVersion widens to (1|2|3). A v3 pickId is pick:v3:H(parents + content) — NO ledger position, EVER: seq/parentStateId/merged/parentPickId/ mergeParentPickId are GONE from the strand (position/merged-ness are DERIVED, #fabric-dag); parents: string[] is the ORDERED multi-parent chain link (IN the hash — ancestry is identity, so reseal-on-retry mints a NEW id, §1.3); the merge recipe folds WHOLE (closes MED-D structurally); binding.treeId folds in and is MANDATORY at seal (buildStrandV3 refuses unbound — the HIGH-A class dies at the schema level); calibratedConfidence does not exist on a v3 strand AT ALL (§7 R4 — grades.jsonl sidecar is authoritative); recordedAt stays IN (§9.5); sessionKey stays OUT. The v3 preimage is built EXPLICITLY (no rest-spread) so a stray positional field can never move a v3 identity. buildStrandV3(input) is the only v3 constructor (pure — the default seal-path cutover is V3.3). A sealed v3 strand has ZERO post-seal-mutable fields. SIGNING (M3-lite I3, TD-2026-08-23-136): an optional `sig` {keyId, sigBase64, principal, schemaVersion:'strandSig:v1'} rides on agent-class strands sealed after the signing-epoch boundary (#seal signStrandForSeal; Ed25519 over the domain-separated pickId, #keys). sig is EXCLUDED from the pickId preimage in BOTH sealing epochs of NECESSITY (the signature is over the pickId — folding it in is circular): the v2 rule destructures it out of the `...rest` spread; the explicit v3 preimage never picks it up. The retired v1 rule and computeLegacyBodyHash deliberately do NOT exclude it — no v1/grandfathered strand can carry one (pre-epoch by construction), so a grafted sig fails CLOSED (pickId-mismatch / legacy-body-mismatch). Regression: test/strand-sig-preimage.test.ts pins all three postures both ways. UNDER-GRANT (M3-lite I6): optional `underGrant: grantId` on a resolves-strand whose ACTING principal was an agent admitted through an active #grants row (threaded from the gate — authoredBy names the CONTESTED agent and can never discriminate who acted).
