INSIDE the pickId preimage in BOTH epochs, the exact opposite posture to sig: on v2 it rides the `...rest` spread; the explicit v3 preimage lists it conditionally (absent = absent, old identities hold), and buildStrandV3 refuses underGrant without resolves. Regression: test/m3-grants.test.ts.

seal.name: Seal
seal.description: The single place a pre-absorbed WarpState becomes a fabric #strand and the selvage advances. sealState(root, store, state, input) — shared by #pick, #admit (merge seal), and #resolve (KNOT-council seal) — owns the strand schema, the seq, the delta summary (summarizeDelta computed BEFORE putState so the dedup case where current.stateId === parent.stateId doesn't diff against itself), and the optional `resolves` envelope, so there is ONE writer of fabric history. Publishes ledger-first then a CAS'd selvage advance (only if the tip is still the parent the decision was based on) — defense-in-depth under #fabric-lock so a lost-update can never silently write a wrong tip. REFS MODE (V3.2): once a repo has run the one-time `warpline refs migrate`, seal DUAL-WRITES — the legacy stateId selvage AND refs/heads/selvage (the tip pickId) advance together via #fabric-refs writeRef per-ref CAS; drifted tip pointers refuse the seal fail-closed. Unmigrated repos are byte-for-byte untouched (seal never creates refs/heads as a side effect). SEAL-TIME AGENT SIGNING (M3-lite I3): signStrandForSeal(root, strand) — called on the fully-built strand immediately before append by sealState AND by the three v3 seal sites in #native-write-path (propose/weave/ resolve — the daemon's write path, which does NOT flow through sealState). Human-class strands (no authoredBy.agentId) pass through UNSIGNED (the procedural boundary, TD-2026-08-23-136 Q1); epoch-less repos (no signed-from row, #keys hasSignedFrom) pass through byte-for-byte as before; an agent-class seal with a pinned epoch is post-boundary BY CONSTRUCTION and MUST sign — the principal's key loads fail-closed (#keys loadAgentKey) and an unresolvable key REFUSES the seal with a refusal:v1 AUTH whose next[] is the human's `key.mint` escalation (never an unsigned agent seal past the boundary). sig is outside the pickId preimage, so attaching it never perturbs the computed identity. Tests: test/seal-sig.test.ts.

grade.name: Grade
grade.description: The calibration grader (Loid's MOAT — the one thing a git-backed history can't carry). admit SEEDS strand.calibratedConfidence from the gate rule; gradeFabric grades it against real OUTCOME, mirroring the classroom certify→outcome loop. A strand's AUTHORED symbols (delta.born ∪ contractChanged) are OVERTURNED when a DAG-DESCENDANT strand RETIRES one (or a #resolve names it in resolves.contended) → confidence ↓; SURVIVED when they hold across a window of DESCENDANTS → ↑; PENDING when too recent. Survival/overturn is DAG-REACHABILITY-scoped, NOT ledger-linear (M2.5 branch-safety, TD-2026-08-12-813): "later" means a strand that actually builds on this one (dag.ts children reachability, buildDag once per run), never fabric.jsonl arrival order. This is the prerequisite for branching — all branches append to one fabric.jsonl, so slice(i+1) would mix concurrent branches and a doomed branch's revert would overturn a survivor on the integration line. A retire/contend on a CONCURRENT (non-descendant) branch is not an overturn; an ABANDONED branch (never merged → never a descendant of the integration head) contributes ZERO — it falls out of reachability with no dead-branch check. Unlinked v1 strands (parentsOf → []) have no resolvable descendants and grade PENDING rather than off arrival order. applyGrades updates calibratedConfidence in the ledger (pickId EXCLUDES the field, so the content-address is unchanged) and appends the trajectory to .warpline/grades.jsonl, under #fabric-lock. The report buckets survival by gate-rule prior class — the falsifiable 'does linked beat independent?' moat experiment. V3 (v3-identity §7, R4): a v3 strand carries NO calibratedConfidence at all — applyGrades never rewrites a v3 strand; its grade trajectory lives ONLY in grades.jsonl (the sidecar becomes fully authoritative at V3.4, when rewriteFabric is deleted). P3 LANE A2 (forge-spec §1d): grades are additionally KEYED by WHO and WHAT — every StrandGrade (and thus every grades.jsonl row) carries authoredBy.agentId + the authoredSymbols set, and GradeReport gains byAgent/bySymbol buckets (per-symbol outcome is conservative: a non-overturned symbol on an OVERTURNED strand is not graded, never silently 'survived'). The module also hosts the sidecar's FIRST CONSUMER: readGradeSidecar → symbolSurvivalIndex (latest row per pickId wins — the sidecar is a trajectory) → evaluateEscalation, a PURE function of (decision, sidecar snapshot) implementing the one trust-floor rule for #admit's HELD verdict; constants K_MIN_GRADED=3 / SURVIVAL_FLOOR=0.5 are exported STARTING GUESSES, calibration-pending (TD-2026-07-16-426 organic arm — moved only by graded outcome data, never hand-tuned). Accepted-risk overrides append to .warpline/grades-escalations.jsonl (G5 sidecar; recordGradeEscalation/listGradeEscalations).

fabric-lock.name: Fabric Lock
fabric-lock.description: A cross-process advisory lock around the fabric's read-decide-write critical section (Reviewer C1). admit/pick/resolve — and the post-commit auto-seal hook which BACKGROUNDS its seal — can otherwise interleave readSelvage→…→writeSelvage and lose a write (a strand appended that isn't the tip, two strands sharing a seq). withFabricLock (acquireFabricLock/releaseFabricLock) acquires an O_EXCL lockfile under .warpline/refs/.lock (atomic create = acquire), bounded retry with backoff, and steals a stale lock (crashed holder) after a TTL. OWNERSHIP (M2 item 4, Judge): the lockfile carries an OWNER TOKEN (pid+random) written at acquire; release unlinks ONLY if the on-disk token is still ours — after a steal the old holder's release leaves the new holder's lock alone (no cascading multi-holder); the steal CLAIMS the stale file by atomic rename-aside (exactly one stealer wins; never a blind unlink). The in-process #repo-lock only guards the git merge-tree fallback; this is the on-disk lock the hook's cross-process seals need. Paired with #fabric's rewriteFabric LOST-UPDATE CAS: the on-disk ledger must still be pick-for-pick the one the rewrite was derived from, else throw — racing an append never drops a strand. D-C (audit 2026-07-31): staleness WAS a 30s wall clock stamped once at acquire, so a merely-slow holder was presumed crashed and silently robbed — the enabling condition for the two CRITICAL multi-writer findings. It is now a three-tier liveness predicate (lockHolderPresumedGone, the one place the policy is decided): (1) an UNREF'd heartbeat refreshes mtime every HEARTBEAT_MS so mtime means "last seen alive" and a crashed holder stops beating with its own event loop; (2) a PID LIVENESS probe — because the critical section is largely SYNCHRONOUS (restoreTree) and a sync block STARVES the timer, measured at zero beats landed across 11s of blocking, so heartbeat alone would still rob the exact holder D-C is about — a same-host holder that answers process.kill(pid,0) is NEVER presumed crashed and a provably dead one is stolen IMMEDIATELY; (3) HARD_STALE_MS=600_000, the un-wedge ceiling that steals regardless of liveness so a recycled pid can never hold the fabric forever. A foreign-host holder is unprobeable and falls back to tiers 1+3 (i.e. the pre-fix predicate). THE VICTIM IS TOLD: fabricLockIsHeld is a timer-free synchronous token re-read, withFabricLock throws rather than returning work done under a stolen lock, and assertFabricLockHeld is exported so a section may refuse BEFORE its write. OPEN (not fixed here — native.ts is out of this module's ownership): restoreTree runs INSIDE the lock while touching only the agent's private worktree, never the fabric; moving it out would shorten the critical section materially (native.ts:711).

resolve.name: Resolve
resolve.description: The KNOT council. resolveKnot(root, {agentId, resolvedRef, reason, decidedBy, oursRef?}) seals a HUMAN resolution of a genuine conflict #admit refused to auto-merge: it absorbs the resolved state, records a #strand `resolves` envelope (decidedBy, reason, the contended symbols, the symbols changed vs the tip, and knotPayloadId — the EXACT join to the #knot-payload this resolution settles), seals via #seal, advances the selvage, and clears the scratch. The reasoning git's merge commit can't keep lives natively in the fabric. I-1 (2026-08-11): the knotPayloadId join + the precise contended set now bind UNCONDITIONALLY — findKnotPayloadForResolve pins the (ours, theirs) contested stateId PAIR (theirs = the selvage being resolved), so a proposal re-admitted against a moved selvage binds the RIGHT payload deterministically; --ours only SHARPENS the ours-side key, it is no longer the switch. The join is now the precise contended set's source (the payload's classified units); it degrades to the resolved-symbols fallback only when no payload persisted, and the PRESENCE of knotPayloadId is the honest precise/fallback marker. A native `pick:` scratch value flowing into this git-era path now REFUSES loudly (the C-9 mirror), never recording a non-stateId into resolves.base. P2.2: also accepts a #knot-payload resolution proposal — proposalToResolveOptions maps a verified knotResolutionProposal:v1 (enveloped reason, resolvedRef, decidedBy) 1:1 onto ResolveOptions; sealing stays behind this verb (G4).

fabric.name: Fabric
fabric.description: See the #fabric component (and siblings) in packages/warpline/.purpose for the full per-module documentation.

fabric-verify.name: Fabric Verify
fabric-verify.description: warpline fabric verify — authenticate the whole PICK-DAG (verifyFabric(root) -> FabricVerifyReport), read-only. Per strand in seq order: (1) INTEGRITY — recompute pickId trying the finite set of known hashing rules (§7.1: the v2 rule, or for v1 the current-exclusion rule OR the retired whole-body rule) and accept on any match; (2) CHAIN (v2) — parentPickId == the immediately-preceding strand's pickId (null at a v2 genesis, the v1 TIP at the boundary), else chain-break; (3) MERGE (v2) — mergeParentPickId resolves to an earlier strand, else merge-parent-unresolved; (4) BINDING — every tree/blob reachable from binding.treeId RE-HASHES to its content-address (recompute via the store's verified reads, NOT mere presence — MEDIUM-1; memoized so shared subtrees hash once; a self-consistent DANGLING binding is the backstop for a re-forged pickId), else missing-binding / corrupt-object / binding-mismatch; (5) MERGE RECIPE (the OQ-D compensating control — recipe fields are EXCLUDED from the pickId by design, so verify is the authority): all four recipe trees ({base,ours,theirs,result}) exist AND recompute, and merge.result === binding.treeId, else merge-recipe-invalid. Classification (§7.3 + HIGH-2 containment): known-rule match -> OK; no match + a V1 strand grandfathered AND matching its PINNED bodyHash -> legacy-unverifiable (SOFT, exit 0); a grandfathered strand whose BODY moved -> legacy-body-mismatch (HARD — the clause exempts the retired pickId rule, never the body); no match + not grandfathered -> pickId-mismatch (HARD) — how a real forgery still surfaces. MANIFEST SANITY: every fabric-legacy.json entry must correspond to an existing v1 strand; an unknown entry or a v2 pickId in the list -> legacy-manifest- invalid (HARD, seq -1). Report carries v1Prefix{count,selfHashOk}, v2Chain{count,ok}, boundaryAnchored, legacyUnverifiable{count,pickIds}, failures[]. Exit 0 intact / 1 tamper / 2 I/O error. Distinct from `objects verify` (loose-object self-consistency). Spec docs/specs/warpline-fabric-schema-v2.md (+ the 2026-07-01 amendment). V3 DAG WALK (V3.1, v3-identity §3.1–4): v3 strands skip the linear chain check and get (3.2) CLOSURE — every parents[] entry resolves in-fabric, else parent-unresolved (HARD, truncation/forgery evidence); (3.3) CAUSALITY — parent line-index < child line-index (the causal-append invariant), else causality-violation; (3.4) acyclicity (dag-cycle — impossible under honest hashing, so forgery evidence) + at most one parentless genesis (multiple-genesis) + MANDATORY binding (missing-binding — no unbound v3 strand is legal). Report adds v3Dag{count,ok}. REFS (V3.2, §3.5): every refs/heads/* entry resolves to a present strand else ref-unresolved (HARD); headless tips no ref names land in report.abandonedHeads (REPORTED, never a failure); in refs mode the legacy selvage is cross-checked against the selvage REF's strand (not the physical tip). A v3 failure's `seq` is the LINE INDEX (v3 stores no seq). The §3.7 nested-epoch anchor walk is V3.3. STAKE-JOURNAL CROSS-CHECK (step 7c — audit C-6, the ONLY check here that speaks to how much history SHOULD be present). Every other check reads the ledger and asks whether it is internally consistent, which is exactly why cutting 59% of a replica of the live fabric off the TAIL and rolling the selvage back verified "all intact", exit 0: the survivors agreed perfectly. verify now consults #stake-journal — every pickId a COMPLETED checkpoint attests must still be present, else stake-journal-orphan (HARD, seq -1), surfaced in report.stakeJournal{present, attested, missing[]} and printed as "stakes N checkpoint(s) cross-checked". HARD by symmetry with the ref-unresolved rule directly above it ("a ref naming a missing strand is truncation evidence") — a STAKE naming a missing strand is the same evidence with STRONGER provenance (a git commit, pushable off-machine, vs a one-line local file), so it cannot be the weaker verdict; and a warning that leaves exit 0 would be deniable, which is precisely C-6's harm. Its OWN kind, never folded into chain-break: "a strand that was here is gone" is a different fact, with a different remedy, than "the strands present disagree". ADVISORY IN, HARD OUT: the attestation set is empty whenever the journal is absent, unreadable, disabled or fresh, and an empty set can never fail a verification — absence of evidence is not evidence of truncation, and a check that failed on every repo not running the valve would be unshippable. Regression: test/stake-journal-truncation.test.ts (the reproduction + the three negative cases). SIGNATURES (step 5c — M3-lite I4): once a signing epoch is pinned (#keys signed-from), every AGENT-CLASS strand strictly AFTER the boundary (boundary resolved ONCE by line index; a null signedFromPickId = genesis pin, everything post-boundary) must carry a valid sig: absent → sig-missing; malformed or cryptographically wrong under the REGISTRY public key (NEVER the key file — a swapped key file signs with a keyId the registry does not hold) → sig-invalid; keyId not a registry agent-key row for that principal (ANY row for the principal counts — re-mint appends, rotation must not un-sign history) → sig-key-unknown; sig.principal != authoredBy.agentId → sig-principal-mismatch. A signed-from row naming a pickId absent from the fabric → registry-invalid (HARD, seq -1; per-strand checks stand down rather than guess a boundary). EXEMPT permanently: strands at-or-before the boundary (grandfathered, the v1-anchor shape), human-class strands (procedural boundary, TD-2026-08-23-136 Q1), and EVERYTHING on an epoch-less repo (the pre-M3 world — zero behavior change). Report adds signing{epochPinned, signedFromPickId, signed, exempt, failed}; the CLI prints "signing epoch: none" on unpinned repos. Tests: test/verify-sig.test.ts. GRANTS (step 5d — M3-lite I6): a strand carrying `underGrant` claims its resolution was agent-acted under a named #grants row — checked: the grant must have been ACTIVE (issued, unexpired — strict — and unrevoked AT the strand's recordedAt, scope-matched) else grant-violation; underGrant on a non-resolves strand is grant-violation too (grants cover RESOLVE only). A resolves-strand WITHOUT underGrant is presumed human-resolved (accepted residue, TD-2026-08-23-136 — no check invented for the absence); zero underGrant strands = the grant store is never even read. Tests: test/m3-falsifier.test.ts.

fabric-fsck.name: Fabric Fsck
fabric-fsck.description: warpline fsck — THE INTEGRITY UMBRELLA (M3-lite I5, m3-integrity-design §3+§6): runFsck(root, {store?}) -> FsckReport, ONE read-only pass aggregating every custody check the individual verbs already run into five sections {ok, findings[{level: warn|fail, kind, message}], notes[]}. REUSE-ONLY by rule — fsck adds aggregation + sectioning, never new verification machinery: (1) FABRIC — verifyFabric verbatim (integrity + chain + DAG + bindings + anchor + the I4 signature walk); notes carry the strand counts and the signing summary ("signing epoch: none" on unpinned repos — the fabric-verify CLI vocabulary). (2) OBJECTS — ObjectStore.verify() verbatim (the `objects verify` loose-object re-hash); each corrupt id a corrupt-object FAIL. (3) REFS — the checks verifyFabric already exposes, re-sectioned: ref-unresolved failures route here (FAIL) and abandonedHeads become abandoned-head WARNINGS (legal, surfaced with the `refs set` recovery line); selvage-tip drift stays in the fabric section (verify reports it as chain-break — existing vocabulary, not re-classified). (4) REGISTRY — readKeyRegistry / listKeySummaries diagnostics: a malformed row is a FAIL (registry-malformed-row — a garbled line in an append-only registry is tamper/corruption evidence; every reader already skips it fail-closed, fsck makes it non-deniable); a LATEST-row key FILE missing is a WARNING only (key-file-missing — a verifier box may hold no private keys; verification uses REGISTRY public keys, never key files); extra signed-from rows are WARNINGS (signed-from-duplicate — ignored by design, the first pin is authoritative forever); a signed-from naming a pickId absent from the fabric is a FAIL (verifyFabric's registry-invalid, ROUTED here so the registry section — not fabric — fails). (5) STAKES — the C-6 cross-check verifyFabric already ran (stake-journal-orphan routed here); a grades↔fabric cross-check is deliberately ABSENT (no exported check exists — gradeFabric is a scoring report) and the absence is SAID in the section notes, not silent. Overall ok = every section ok; warnings never fail. CLI `warpline fsck` [--json]: per-section PASS/WARN/FAIL + finding lines (✗ fail / ⚠ warn); exit 0 iff ok IN BOTH RENDER MODES (fsck's own contract — stricter than the fabric-verify --json idiom), 1 on any failed section, 2 on a usage/I/O error (the §4.3 split). NO daemon/descriptor skin: adding a daemon verb grows DAEMON_VERBS and moves the FG-3-frozen descriptorsId (descriptors-frozen.test.ts pins the content address + totality) — founder-gated territory, so fsck is CLI-only at M3-lite. NO daemon startup hook either (no startup health framework exists to hang it on; not invented). Tests: test/fsck.test.ts (healthy signed fabric; per-section tamper routing incl. chain byte-flip, sig strip, loose-object flip, garbled registry row, missing key file WARN-only, unknown signed-from; epoch-less repo; CLI exit codes + --json).

fabric-repair.name: Fabric Repair
fabric-repair.description: THE REPAIR PATH (audit C-13 + the P1 entry "detection without repair is a dead end a real crash will find"). Warpline detected nearly everything and repaired nothing; the documented recovery from a torn ledger line was hand-editing JSONL in a text editor — precisely what source control must never require. Two verbs, both under #fabric-lock, both re-reading INSIDE the lock (the plan was computed outside it and a seal may have landed). `warpline fabric repair` [--confirm] [--json] — repairFabric(root, {confirm, now}). C-13 is reachable WITHOUT a crash: a real `pick` on a full disk committed a 142-byte partial line, after which log/selvage/restore/pick AND `fabric verify` all failed; the live fabric's largest line is 307,905 bytes, so the window is wide. Four design calls, all deliberate: (1) TAIL TEARS ONLY — a malformed line with well-formed strands AFTER it REFUSES (RepairRefusal), naming how many good strands truncation would have cost, because "truncate to the last well-formed strand" applied mid-ledger makes repair the data-loss event; (2) DRY RUN BY DEFAULT — --confirm is required to write anything, since a verb that quietly shortens history the first time it is run in a panic is worse than the corruption; (3) QUARANTINE FIRST, DURABLY — the pre-repair bytes go to .warpline/repair/fabric.jsonl.<iso>.bak through #warp-durable BEFORE the ledger is shortened (the torn bytes are evidence, and a crash mid-repair must not leave neither copy); (4) VERBATIM PREFIX — the retained bytes are a raw Buffer slice, never re-serialized. The result itemizes EXACTLY what was dropped (line, offset, bytes, parse error, and a bounded control-character-escaped excerpt — a torn line is attacker-influenceable content headed for a terminal). Repair does NOT touch the tip pointers: in the crash shape the append tore so the selvage/ref publish never ran and both still name the last good strand; where they DO disagree that is C-4/C-12 with its own detectors, and re-pointing heads would be meaning-level surgery under a byte-level name. It also does not PREVENT the tear — fsync makes a write durable, not atomic — it makes one recoverable; a genuinely atomic append needs a different on-disk shape (length-prefixed records / write-ahead intent / segment store) and is out of scope. `warpline refs set <name> <pickId>` [--force] — setFabricRef(root, name, pickId, {force}). The actionable half of verify's "⚠ abandoned head(s) — no ref names": recovering one used to require hand-editing .warpline/refs/heads/. Two guards: a pickId ABSENT from the fabric refuses (a repair verb that can mint the ref-unresolved corruption verify catches is not a repair verb), and an EXISTING ref is never clobbered without --force (overwriting a head is how sealed work becomes abandoned). Same value ⇒ idempotent no-op. Reads via scanFabric, not readFabric, so a torn ledger does not block ref repair — the two verbs must work in either order. Write is #fabric-refs writeRef with expectedOld = what was read under the lock (per-ref CAS). Regression: test/fabric-repair.test.ts.

fabric-dag.name: Fabric Dag
fabric-dag.description: The DERIVED DAG index over the fabric ledger (V3.1, v3-identity §1.2 + §4). fabric.jsonl is an ARRIVAL LOG (a local receipt), not the authority on order — the DAG in the strands is. parentsOf() unifies the epochs (v3 parents[]; v2 parentPickId+mergeParentPickId; v1 none). buildDag(strands) → byPickId, children, the deterministic topological ORDER (ties between concurrent strands broken by (recordedAt, pickId) ascending — deterministic across machines GIVEN THE SAME STRAND SET, the correct promise), positionOf, heads (tips with no children), roots, missingParents (closure holes — verify makes them HARD; the index still orders the remainder for display), and cycle (unorderable strands — forgery evidence under honest hashing). Duplicate appends dedup (content- addressed, §1.3 idempotence). A derived position may be SHOWN (the @N selector sugar) but is never persisted and never a durable selector across exchange.

fabric-refs.name: Fabric Refs
fabric-refs.description: pickId refs + per-ref CAS (V3.2, v3-identity §2, founder-signed §9.1: refs hold PICKIDS, not stateIds — a stateId is many-to-one and cannot name a history position). .warpline/refs/heads/<name> each hold an event identity; readRef/writeRef (atomic tmp+rename; CAS refuses when the on-disk ref moved — verbatim the writeSelvage mechanics re-scoped per ref; a losing writer reseal- retries or publishes under its own ref and weaves later, jj/darcs posture), listRefs, heads() — the API new code writes against instead of assuming a unique tip (spec §6.3; legacy fallback = the single ledger tip). Ref names are single-segment validated fail-closed (spliced into a filesystem path — no traversal). migrateSelvageToRefs is the ONE-TIME founder-visible migration: resolves the legacy stateId selvage via the highest-seq hack for the LAST time, writes refs/heads/selvage, idempotent, fails closed on a corrupt tip — NEVER automatic (unmigrated repos, including the live dogfood fabric until its own step, stay untouched). The O_EXCL #fabric-lock survives as the short critical-section guard for append+ref-write. DURABLE + COLLISION-FREE PUBLISH (soundness audit C-7 + C-15): writeRef goes through #warp-durable, so the ref bytes are fsynced BEFORE the rename and refs/heads/ AFTER it, and the staging file is `<ref>.tmp.<pid>.<n>` instead of a shared `<ref>.tmp` that let a racing writer publish another writer's value underneath the CAS. REF NAMES vs STAGING RESIDUE (C-15, the second half): REF_NAME permits dots — legitimately, `v1.0` is a ref — and that is exactly how a crashed writer's `refs/heads/selvage.tmp` became a REF: it matched, listRefs returned it despite its own comment saying "tmp files / strays are not refs", and heads() reported a PERMANENT phantom second head that `fabric verify` called intact. Unique staging names do NOT fix this on their own (`selvage.tmp.123.0` matches REF_NAME just as well). The fix is the composed predicate isRefName = REF_NAME ∧ no `..` ∧ !isTmpResidue, applied on BOTH sides: listRefs never READS residue as a ref and writeRef never MINTS one. Symmetry is the point — an asymmetric filter would be the mirror bug, a ref you can create and never see.

head.name: Head
head.description: The CURRENT-BRANCH pointer (the git HEAD analog), M2.5 branching foundation (TD-2026-08-12-813, Arky's design) — head.ts. #fabric-refs already NAME history positions; what did not exist is a pointer saying WHICH ref the next seal advances. `.warpline/HEAD` is a SYMREF with exactly two shapes (git's, honestly borrowed): `ref: refs/heads/<name>` (attached to a branch) or a bare `pick:<id>` (DETACHED at an event identity). readHead → {kind:'branch',branch} | {kind:'detached',pickId} | null (absent); writeHead publishes it atomically + durably via #warp-durable atomicWriteSync; resolveHeadTip(root, wdir) follows the symref to its ref tip (readRef) or returns the detached pickId. DEFAULT: an ABSENT HEAD is treated as refs/heads/selvage (DEFAULT_BRANCH) so a fabric that never branched behaves exactly as before HEAD existed — the pre-branching world is "always on selvage"; readHead reports absence faithfully (null) and resolveHeadTip applies the default. The branch name is validated through the SHARED #fabric-refs isRefName predicate (now exported) — the same fail-closed grammar that guards a ref filename, because a symref target is spliced into refs/heads/<name> and read back as a path; no second grammar can drift from the first. Fails closed: a HEAD that exists but is unreadable or malformed throws rather than masquerading as absent. Structurally a sibling of #fabric-refs. Pinned by test/branch-foundation.test.ts.

mergebase.name: Mergebase
mergebase.description: The MERGE-BASE (lowest common ancestor) over the fabric DAG, M2.5 branching foundation (TD-2026-08-12-813, Arky's design) — mergebase.ts. The one genuinely new algorithm branching needs: given two heads, find the history position they last shared, so a three-way merge (base × ours × theirs) has its base. ancestorSet(byPick, tip) is the inclusive BFS over the unified DAG parents (#fabric-dag parentsOf) — the same walk #native-write-path does over the selvage tip, generalized and EXPORTED here so branching does not re-derive it. mergeBase(byPick, a, b): I = ancestors(a) ∩ ancestors(b); the base is the element of I that is a proper ancestor of NO other element of I (the lowest common ancestor, closest to a and b). CRISS-CROSS FAILS CLOSED: when the history criss-crosses (a diamond whose two merge strands cross), I has MORE THAN ONE minimal element and there is no single base — returns {ambiguous:[…]} rather than silently choosing one (Arky's v1 decision: a wrong base is a silently-wrong merge, the exact class Warpline refuses). DISJOINT roots → null (I empty; the record is suspect, the caller escalates). DETERMINISTIC + CLOCK-FREE: the ambiguous list is ordered by the derived topological position (#fabric-dag buildDag), pickId as the tiebreak, so two machines with the same strand set report the same base(s) in the same order. Pure — no clock, no I/O, no git. Pinned by test/branch-foundation.test.ts.

branch.name: Branch
branch.description: The BRANCH VERBS (M2.5 increment 2, TD-2026-08-12-813, Arky's design) — branch.ts. The human/agent layer OVER the increment-1 foundation (#head symref, #fabric-refs CAS, #mergebase, a bare branch name as a #restore selector): create / list / delete a named line, and SWITCH the worktree between them. A branch is nothing new underneath — a `refs/heads/<name>` holding a pickId, exactly like `selvage` (the default trunk / #head DEFAULT_BRANCH); this module only mints, enumerates, retires, and MOVES-TO those refs, wiring primitives rather than adding a ref grammar or a worktree-writer. createBranch(root, name, {from?}): resolve the source tip (from HEAD via resolveHeadTip when omitted/`HEAD` — the CURRENT branch, not select.ts's legacy selvage-alias; else resolveSelector, a `tree:` selector refused), then writeRef with CAS-null (must-not-exist — a concurrent create loses cleanly, a branch is never silently re-pointed). listBranches(root): listRefs sorted, each annotated `current` (HEAD's branch; absent HEAD ≡ selvage, detached ≡ none — the '*' marker). deleteBranch(root, name): UNLINK the ref only — the strand survives in append-only fabric.jsonl as an abandoned head (`fabric verify` reports it, `refs set` recovers it); refuses `selvage` (the trunk) and the current HEAD branch. switchBranch(root, worktree, name, {force?}): resolve the branch tip → treeId (A4-refuses an unbound strand, exactly as #restore does), write those bytes into the worktree through the SHARED guarded byte-writer (guardedRestoreTree — refuse-dirty by default, a path whose bytes are in no object refuses; `--force` overrides, git-parity), THEN writeHead — the restore precedes the HEAD move, so a dirty refusal leaves both worktree and HEAD untouched. Switch OVERLAYS the tip tree (#restore semantics reused verbatim): it writes the target's paths and leaves unrelated files in place, and does not prune paths absent from the target — so switching BETWEEN branches whose tracked content diverges needs `--force` (the guard has no index/baseline to know the current bytes are captured in the other branch's tree). branch/switch are AGENT-CLASS verbs (opening/moving lanes is the concurrency the fabric adjudicates) — deliberately NOT in the HUMAN_ONLY set. CLI: `warpline branch [<name>] [--from <sel>] [-l|--list] [-d|--delete]`, `warpline switch <name> [--force]` (alias `checkout`). Library code: no console output. Pinned by test/branch-verbs.test.ts.

graph.name: Graph
graph.description: MULTI-BRANCH HISTORY presentation (M2.5 increment 6, TD-2026-08-12-813; closes M2 history-nav T-2026-07-01-013) — graph.ts. READ-ONLY: nothing here changes a verdict, a seal, or a ref. It CONSUMES the layers increments 1–5 built — the derived pick-DAG (#fabric-dag), the ref layer (#fabric-refs), HEAD (#head), and the native object store (#warp-store) — to present history ACROSS branches, exactly as `git log --all` / `git diff A..B` / `git show` present git's object graph without mutating it. branchGraph(fabric, refs, head): the whole DAG order (buildDag.order) reversed to NEWEST-FIRST, each node annotated with the ref names that point at its pickId (inverted ref map; a tip may carry several), whether HEAD resolves to it, and the HEAD branch name — where an ABSENT HEAD ≡ the selvage trunk (the same DEFAULT_BRANCH default resolveHeadTip applies). ancestorsOf(fabric, tip): the INCLUSIVE ancestry line of a branch tip, the #mergebase ancestorSet presented in DAG topo order newest-first (reuses the unified-parent walk — no second walker). diffTrees(store, A, B): the byte diff between two native trees — flattens BOTH through #materialize flattenNativeTree and compares {mode,id} per path via the SAME nativeDiffers the native merge decides changed-ness with (a rename reads as delete+add; an unchanged file is exactly id-equal) → added / removed / modified. CONSUMED by the CLI: `warpline log [<branch>]` (multi-branch annotated by default; `<branch>` = that branch's ancestry line), `warpline diff <A>..<B>` (byte diff between two branch/rev tips — resolveSelector each side → treeId → diffTrees), and `warpline show <selector>` (extended beyond KNOT payloads: an ordinary strand renders its meaning delta + intent + author + DAG parents + byte paths changed vs its primary parent). Library code: no console output — the CLI prints. Pinned by test/branch-history.test.ts.

merge.name: Merge
merge.description: The BRANCH-MERGE verb (M2.5 increment 4 — the acceptance-gate increment; TD-2026-08-12-813 spine, TD-2026-08-12-351 fail-closed rule; Arky's design, Jinx's gate) — merge.ts. mergeBranch(root, {into, from}) folds `from` (OURS — the branch being merged) into `into` (THEIRS/selvage role — the integration line advanced). base = #mergebase LCA of (from-tip, into-tip): a CRISS-CROSS ({ambiguous}) fails closed UNSUPPORTED (v1 has no recursive merge — a wrong base is a silently-wrong merge), disjoint roots (null) fail closed INTEGRITY_BROKEN. FAST-FORWARD when into ∈ ancestors(from): advance into's ref to from-tip, no weave strand (mirrors #admit FAST_ADMIT); ALREADY-UP-TO-DATE when from ∈ ancestors(into); an UNBORN into genesis-es at from. Otherwise it calls the SHARED seal core #native-write-path weaveTips with ours=from, theirs=into, base=LCA, targetBranch=into — the SAME engine #admit runs, so disjoint meaning auto-folds CLEAN, same-symbol contradiction KNOTs, and a byte-conflict downgrades to KNOT, all inherited verbatim. THE FAIL-CLOSED RULE (the whole point): merge passes holdOnByteDecided=true, which #admit NEVER sets — after a CLEAN weave that would auto-seal, if ANY changed path is BYTE-DECIDED (#honesty classifyMergePaths — no lens lifted it: a `.js`/cfg config value, a scalar `export const LIMIT=100→50` invariant carrier), the merge does NOT seal. It surfaces a MEANING-BLIND HOLD: status HELD, sealed false, the target ref UNMOVED, meaningBlind.bytePaths names the paths, and the refusal (GATE_REFUSED / verdict HELD / retry-with-override) escalates to a human `--confirm` (acceptMeaningBlind) — human-class to clear, exactly like a KNOT. DERIVED (take-either lockfiles) are deliberately NOT held. This makes merge STRICTLY SAFER than git (git auto-merges disjoint config×code silently). The hold is MERGE-TIME only — #admit's linear path is byte-identical (increment 3 preserved it; weaveTips computes coverage one line earlier now, identical inputs). Attribution: a branch merge has no scratch, so `from` stands in as the ours-side principal (clearScratch of a branch name is a harmless no-op absent a same-named live agent). CLI: `warpline merge <from> [--into <branch>] [--confirm] [--no-restore]` — default into = the current HEAD branch (detached fails closed); verdict-keyed exit. THE ACCEPTANCE GATE: test/merge-falsifier.test.ts drives the two canonical §8 breaks across a real branch merge — (a) config×code and (b) no-shared-token const HOLD; (c) two disjoint lifted functions auto-fold (no over-hold); (d) same-symbol KNOTs. Library code: no console output.

protected.name: Protected
protected.description: The PROTECTED-BRANCH registry and the AGENT-CLASS LANDING GATE (M2.5 security, TD-2026-08-12-813 — Aegis's own finding) — protected.ts. THE THREAT it closes: with branches, an agent can isolate work on a private feature branch — GUARANTEED CLEAN, because it is alone there, so the KNOT/resolve gate never trips — then clean-MERGE that branch into the integration line with NO human. That laundering route bypasses the human gate that is the entire safety model. THE FIX: name the integration line PROTECTED; refuse an AGENT-class admit/merge that LANDS onto it (feature branches stay agent-writable, main is a human/policy act). THE REGISTRY: `.warpline/protected.json`, a JSON string[] of branch names. ABSENT ⇒ the DEFAULT set — the trunk `selvage` (#head DEFAULT_BRANCH), plus `main` iff a branch by that name exists (git-parity alias) — so a fresh `warpline init` protects its trunk with NO file written. Once a human writes the file (protect/unprotect), it is AUTHORITATIVE (the default no longer applies, so `unprotect selvage` genuinely removes protection). Reads fail CLOSED (a corrupt / non-array registry throws, never "nothing protected" — mirrors #head / #fabric-refs). isProtected / listProtected / protectBranch / unprotectBranch (pure mutators; idempotent). THE GATE (protectedLandingRefusal): refuses when THREE things all hold — the principal is AGENT-class, the target branch is PROTECTED, and BRANCHING IS IN USE (branchingInUse = listRefs > 1). THE DEFAULT-PROTECTION POLICY, chosen to preserve the baseline: `selvage` protected by default, but the third clause keeps the SINGLE-LINE world byte-identical — with only the trunk, there is no feature branch to launder FROM, so an agent admits onto the trunk exactly as before (the daemon genesis cycle + every pre-branch test stay green); the gate ENGAGES the instant a feature branch opens. A merge inherently needs ≥2 named lines, so an agent merge into protected is always gated. PRINCIPAL SOURCE (no new vocabulary — Aegis §2.2): 'human'|'agent' is the SAME class the daemon token kind and #refusal next[] speak. The CLI derives it from `$WARPLINE_AGENT_ID` (#agent-shell — possession of an UNMARKED shell is the human credential); an ABSENT principal is human, so agent-class is OPT-IN and every existing engine caller is unaffected. The refusal is FORBIDDEN / retriable 'never' with next[] naming the human path (escalate, never self-retry). ENFORCEMENT POINTS: the merge gate in #merge mergeBranch (before any tip read — the ref never moves) and the admit gate in #native-write-path admitNative (on the resolved targetBranch). protect / unprotect is a HUMAN-class act (an agent must never decide what is protected FROM agents) — CLI `warpline branch --protect/--unprotect <name>`, guarded by the same #agent-shell credential; the daemon exposes NO protect verb (#warplined-protocol PROTECTED_BRANCH_HUMAN_ONLY documents both surfaces). Library code: no console output. Pinned by test/protected-branch.test.ts.

anchor.name: Anchor
anchor.description: The v1-prefix EPOCH ANCHOR (docs/specs/warpline-v1-anchor.md) — closes the HIGH-A / HIGH-B / MED-C live exploits (the v2 chain was authenticated, the v1 prefix was not). computePrefixDigest folds the FULL v1 strands (bodies, bindings, pickIds all included) domain-separated + length-prefixed; the anchor is a NORMAL v2 strand carrying an `attests` block (EpochAnchor) that rides into its pickId via computePickId's ...rest spread — so the attestation is itself chain-protected. `warpline fabric attest` (attestFabric) is the ONE-TIME verb: refuse-if-attested → precondition verify (coverage suppressed) → corroborate the working prefix+manifest against git history of .warpline/fabric.jsonl (record the matching commit) → seal a meaning-no-op anchor at the tip. No re-attest/force/ repair verb exists (a re-attest path = tamper-then-re-attest). fabric-verify then authenticates the prefix against the anchor (anchor-missing/mismatch/manifest- mismatch/duplicate/malformed, v1-out-of-prefix; + the §6.7 selvage/tip cross-check) and REQUIRES coverage as a code constant. assertV1Covered is the cheap restore gate. Residual (stated honestly): a full re-chain by an in-loop writer stays possible — tamper-EVIDENT, not trustworthy; signatures are M3.

backfill.name: Backfill
backfill.description: `warpline objects backfill` (backfillV1Bindings) — stamp a native byte binding onto every v1 strand lacking one, from its provenance.gitCommit tree (snapshotRef), so the v1 prefix has all the bindings it will EVER have BEFORE the epoch anchor freezes it. gitOid:null deliberately (MED-E — a backfilled native tree is ignore-filtered, so the git sha would be a lie; the check is vacuous for self-produced values). Binding is EXCLUDED from the v1 pickId, so a stamp is legal pre-anchor. A strand whose gitCommit is null/unreachable stays UNBOUND forever (restore refuses permanently, A4). PRE-ATTESTATION ONLY: refuses once an anchor exists (findAnchor) — the same one-way freeze gate #fabric's rewriteFabric keys off. Ordering trap: backfill → git commit → attest must not be reordered. DELTA-NATIVE (T-2026-07-04-003): snapshots CHAIN — each strand anchors on the previous one just computed, so a long v1 prefix costs N diffs, not N universes.

restore.name: Restore
restore.description: The layer→VCS THRESHOLD (M1c, T-2026-07-01-012) — reconstruct a working tree from the NATIVE object store with git ABSENT. Two modules + a hardened writer: select.ts (resolveSelector(wdir, selector) → treeId): omitted|HEAD|selvage → the tip strand — refs mode (V3.2) resolves the EXACT pickId at refs/heads/selvage (no stateId ambiguity); legacy mode keeps the latest-arrival-on-stateId disambiguation (grandfathered until migration); N|@N → stored seq === N, falling back to the DERIVED topo position (#fabric-dag) when the fabric carries position-free v3 strands (local sugar, never durable); pick:<id> → that pickId; state:<id> → the most-recent-arrival strand on that stateId (§3 many-to-one); tree:<id> → that treeId DIRECTLY (no strand). <branch> → a BARE BRANCH NAME (an existing refs/heads/<name>, M2.5 branching) resolves to that ref's tip strand — checked LAST so it never shadows the reserved forms, and only when a ref actually holds the name (an unknown name still errors; `selvage` resolves via the tip branch to the identical strand). A4 (cutover-refuse-on-missing-binding): a resolved strand with no binding.treeId (sealed pre-M1b) is REFUSED loudly — never silently restored empty. restore.ts (restore(root, {selector, to, force})): the DIRTY-DEST GUARD refuses a non-empty dest without --force; --force OVERLAYS (overwrites colliding regular files, leaves unrelated files, never wipes). The byte writer restoreTree (#warp-store, snapshot.ts) is PATH-HARDENED (Aegis C3, CVE-2021-21300 class): it FAILS CLOSED (throws, aborting the whole restore) on a forged/corrupt entry name — assertSafeEntryName rejects empty/./../slash/backslash/NUL/absolute/drive-letter and the reserved .git/.warpline; the parent dir must be a real (non-symlink) directory; and it never writes THROUGH a pre-existing symlink (traversal escape). Byte-faithful modes preserved (100644/100755/120000/40000/160000). Proof: rm -rf .git && warpline restore HEAD reproduces the exact tree (external), and snapshot(restore(x)) == x.binding.treeId (internal round-trip).

pick.name: Pick
pick.description: The single-writer WRITE PATH (Phase 2). recordPick(root, opts) absorbs the working tree (or a ref) to a WarpState, and — using the DIFF vs the parent selvage as the source of truth for "did meaning change?" (NOT stateId equality, which hashes the DEDUPED essence set and so misses a born symbol whose essence equals an existing one) — decides NOOP vs seal, then seals a #strand via #seal (the single fabric writer) under #fabric-lock (so a backgrounded post-commit auto-seal can't race it). BYTE CUSTODY (T-2026-07-18-002): NOOP ⟺ empty deltas AND empty renames AND tree unchanged (vs the tip strand's binding, under the canonical worktree semantics — T-2026-07-18-005); a meaning-NOOP whose TREE advanced seals a BYTE-CUSTODY strand instead (strand.byteOnly:true additive, IN the v2 pickId via the rest spread; stateId naturally equals the parent's; the binding advances) so doc/lore/config-only commits keep durable native custody (git-absent restorable; auto-stake counts them). Byte-only is always FAST/no-gate: a NOOP verdict never refuses, even agent-attributed under gate:'real'. New bindings are stamped binding.treeSemantics:'worktree:v1'. Genesis (no selvage) records seq 0 with an empty delta; objectCount is the headline. FAIL-CLOSED (T-029): a SET selvage whose parent state cannot be loaded now THROWS rather than falling through to seal (which would orphan history) — symmetric with the #admit guard. SCHEMA v2: RecordPickOptions gains agentId/sessionKey; the seal stamps authoredBy (agentId IN the pickId, sessionKey excluded). No agentId (the hook/human path) → authoredBy.agentId null. The single-writer daily-driver path — the multi-writer protocol is #admit. DELTA-NATIVE (T-2026-07-04-003): a REF pick's seal snapshot anchors on the tip strand's verified binding (strandSnapshotAnchor) — the post-commit hook seal costs one commit's diff, not the whole tree; worktree picks keep the full snapshotDir walk, unchanged. NATIVE-FIRST R1: when #warpline-config sets shadowGate:true, every pick ALSO records the #shadow-gate observe-only verdict of the just-lifted state vs the PRE-seal selvage (reusing the absorb — pure compute). FAIL-SAFE: shadow is telemetry; a shadow failure never blocks or fails the seal. NATIVE-FIRST R2 (T-2026-07-18-001, loid-loops.md R2 "mixed mode"): gate.agentWrites:'real' makes an AGENT-ATTRIBUTED pick (agentId present — --agent / $WARPLINE_AGENT_ID, incl. the auto-seal hook forwarding it) ENFORCE that same verdict: would-not-seal (KNOT/DANGLE/HELD/non-materializable CLEAN) REFUSES the seal (PickGateRefusal; row records gate:'real'), override = `pick --accept-risk` (row records overridden:true — never silent). FAIL-CLOSED for agents (an enforced gate that crashes, or a config too corrupt to read, refuses); humans/unattributed picks stay byte-identical (two doors, one fabric). After a successful non-noop seal the R2 auto-stake cadence (#stake maybeAutoStakeOnSeal) runs best-effort, outside the fabric lock. REFUSAL (refusal:v1 SP1c, ADDITIVE): PickGateRefusal now carries a `.refusal` — the machine-readable #refusal beside the human `message`. The would-not-seal refusal re-homes the UNDERLYING #admit refusal (from the shadow pipeline) to gate:'pick', keeping its code, ranked contested index, pointers and override door, and rewrites next[] for the pick surface — because the verb that retries HERE is `pick`, not `admit`. Its ladder omits knot.show by design: the gate's verdict comes from #shadow-gate, which builds a #knot-payload as pipeline proof and never persists it, so there is no selector to hand out; the durable artifact is the VERDICT ROW, read back via shadow.tail. D-10 (F4 instrument panel, 2026-07-31): the ladder's `resolve` step advertised ['resolvedRef','reason','decidedBy'] — the exact phantom list PW-3a had already removed from #admit's meaningNextSteps, left unfixed one file over. It OMITTED resolve's REQUIRED agentId and named two params the verb has never accepted (decidedBy is SERVER-STAMPED identity; resolvedRef was never a daemon param), so a human following it verbatim BAD_REQUESTed. It now mirrors meaningNextSteps exactly: the target agent rides in params (copy-paste ready), requires is [worktree, reason]. pickGateRefusal is EXPORTED so PW-4 (test/refusal-vocabulary-totality.test.ts) can exercise this file's REAL builder — the defect survived an era because a test cannot cover a builder it cannot call. The two fail-CLOSED throws are labelled too — a corrupt config yields code ENGINE with retriable 'never' and an EMPTY next[] (the machine-readable way to say "no call recovers this; escalate"), while a failed verdict pipeline yields ENGINE with 'retry-identical' (the request was well-formed; lock contention is the common cause). Constructor arg is optional so external callers still compile; every throw site here populates it. C-9 (soundness audit 2026-07-31, closed-as-diagnosed 2026-08-01) — THE GATE'S BASE, and the two defects around it. #pick has NO fork step BY DESIGN: it is the SINGLE-WRITER git-coexistence door, and the multi-writer cycle is fork→propose→admit (#native-write-path). So the R2 verdict is a real RE-BASE judgment only when a SCRATCH ref already pins this agent's base — `warpline scratch <agentId>` (#scratch forkScratch, a `state:` base). With none, #admit falls back to the selvage, base === selvage, and admitDecision returns FAST_ADMIT UNCONDITIONALLY: KNOT/CLEAN/DANGLE/HELD are unreachable BY CONSTRUCTION, not for want of contention. That is how all 42 live verdict rows (27 FAST_ADMIT, 15 NOOP) were produced. The audit concluded from this that the gate was DEAD; it is not — with a base it produces genuine KNOTs, demonstrated end-to-end against the #f4-seed engine functions in test/pick-gate-contested.test.ts and pinned since R2 in test/r2-agent-gate.test.ts. It is UNDISCOVERABLE, not dead: nothing in #pick, in `pick --help`, or in the R2 record named the base prerequisite, and `scratch` is on NO taught surface (it is not a DaemonVerb, so it is absent from VERB_DESCRIPTORS, the MCP tool set and CLI_VERB_MAP). Whether an AGENT should be able to reach this gate is therefore an OPEN FOUNDER DECISION — see #warpline-descriptors — and was deliberately not decided here, because adding a verb to the agent surface moves descriptorsId. (2) The gate's fail-closed catch used to overwrite EVERY pipeline failure with ENGINE/'retry-identical'. That is right for a transient (lock contention) and is the pre-PW-2 dead-end for a DETERMINISTIC prerequisite refusal: it discards a working 'retry-corrected' ladder and instructs an infinite losing retry. A thrown RefusedError is now re-homed to gate:'pick' via pickPipelineRefusal with its code, retriability and ladder intact; only an UNTYPED throw still becomes ENGINE/'retry-identical'.

scratch.name: Scratch
scratch.description: A per-agent ephemeral view (the read side of multi-writer). forkScratch(agentId) pins the stateId the agent works against (its optimistic base) under .warpline/refs/scratch/<agentId>; N agents fork the SAME selvage concurrently with zero contention — what git's single shared working-tree/index/HEAD cannot do. Forking is O(1), no working-tree lock. readScratch/clearScratch round it out. NATIVE-FIRST (phase 0, I9): the same file doubles as the native SCRATCH REF — writeScratchRef stores a PICKID (`warpline fork` mints it at the selvage tip; #native-write-path propose advances it per sealed scratch strand). Consumers dispatch on the pick:/state: prefix; a mismatch fails closed, never coerces. C-9 (2026-08-01): that contract had exactly ONE conforming direction. #native-write-path refused a `state:` scratch (UNSUPPORTED/retry-corrected/ fork) from PW-2 onward; the GIT-ERA #admit did neither — it handed a `pick:` value straight to store.loadState, read the null as "base cannot be loaded", and reported a corrupt states cache with an instruction to repair .warpline/. Wrong diagnosis, untyped throw, and (through the R2 gate's catch) an ENGINE/'retry-identical' ladder — reached by an agent that had done nothing but follow `status` → `fork`, since `fork` is the ONLY scratch-minting verb on the agent surface. Now symmetric: UNSUPPORTED/ retry-corrected naming the other path's admit, on both sides. CAS (PW-10, optional `expect` param): a conditional write throws on current≠expected instead of silently clobbering — the loud-failure half of the fork clobber guard (two same-principal sessions could orphan each other's sealed proposal with no error anywhere). DURABLE + COLLISION-FREE (soundness audit C-7 + C-15): both writers now go through #warp-durable. writeScratchRef's shared `<agentId>.tmp` sat DIRECTLY beneath the CAS above — the CAS runs before the write, so two writers that both passed it raced on one staging path and one could publish the other's value while returning success. forkScratch was worse still: a bare truncate-then-write, the one ref writer with no staging file at all.

admit.name: Admit
admit.description: The multi-writer WRITE side (Phase C v1, DECISION-level). admitDecision(base, proposed, selvage) is the pure verdict: NOOP (no meaning change — decided by diff(base, proposed) being empty, NOT stateId equality, same rule as #pick: stateId hashes the DEDUPED essence set and misses a change whose before/after essences both pre-exist elsewhere); FAST_ADMIT (selvage unadvanced since base → admit directly); CLEAN (selvage advanced but predict(agentΔ, otherΔ) is autoClean — the concurrent edits commute in MEANING, the case git CONFLICTS on for textually-adjacent edits — carrying a GATE-RULE confidence: 'linked' when the two changed-sets are dependency-adjacent in-graph (Merkle would surface a real conflict, so autoClean is trustworthy) vs 'independent' when disjoint (autoClean may HIDE a cross-symbol semantic conflict per the false-AUTOFOLD gate)); KNOT (same symbol, contradictory meaning → human DECIDE, never silently merged); DANGLE (edge into a retired symbol). v2: admit() now PERFORMS the merge — on FAST_ADMIT it seals the proposed state; on CLEAN it calls #materialize to produce the merged tree, seals it, advances selvage, and clears the scratch (if materialization finds a byte conflict the meaning layer missed, it downgrades to KNOT — never a silent wrong-merge). Materialization needs git refs for ours/base/theirs (the strands' provenance.gitCommit anchors); a WORKTREE proposal returns CLEAN unsealed. A CLEAN re-base onto a MERGE strand also fails CLOSED (unsealed): a merge strand's gitCommit is ONE parent and lacks the merged bytes, so re-basing off it would mis-materialize a 3rd-gen merge (H1). SCHEMA v2: all three seal calls pass authoredBy {agentId: opts.agentId}; the CLEAN merge seal also passes mergeParentPickId = the base strand's pickId (the SECOND DAG parent), folded with merge.algo into the authenticated v2 pickId. DELTA-NATIVE (T-2026-07-04-003): every seal-time snapshot is ANCHORED where verifiable — FAST_ADMIT anchors on the tip strand (selvage === base there), the CLEAN capture anchors base on the base strand's verified binding (ours/ theirs then diff off the base tree), and the H1-relaxed native path anchors each git-ref side on its strand binding — so a warm admit on the full monorepo runs in single-digit SECONDS (was >2min; bench/bench-admit.mts). Anchors are verified by #warp-store's strandSnapshotAnchor and fail OPEN to the full snapshot; verdict semantics are untouched (decision before bytes). P2.2 (forge-spec §3a): a meaning-level KNOT/DANGLE verdict additionally durably snapshots the unsealed proposal's bytes, builds the machine-readable #knot-payload, persists it to .warpline/knots/, and returns knotPayloadId — a POINTER on AdmitResult (G1-additive; never the payload inline). Payload construction is derived evidence: a build failure degrades to a verdict without a pointer, never a crash. The verdict itself remains a pure function of STRUCTURAL inputs — prose never reaches admitDecision (the poisoned-prose invariant, test/injection-envelope.test.ts). P2.3 (forge-spec §3b): admit optionally judges the admission against a pre-declared #claim (AdmitOptions.claim = a claimId from the propose API) — the CLAIM GATE runs strictly BEFORE any seal: a breach (computed touched ⊄ claimed, per #claim's documented excess rule) returns the CLAIM-BREACH verdict class (G1-additive to AdmitStatus; never returned by admitDecision itself) — HELD, unsealed, with the exact excess/missing sets and the underlying verdict on AdmitResult.claim. FAIL-SAFE not fail-hard: acceptBreach is the explicit override that seals the underlying verdict while recording the breach fact. Every judgment (breach or not, sealed or not) appends a row to .warpline/claims/evaluations.jsonl (the calibration-probe stream, G5). Claims are OPT-IN: an admit without a claim is byte-identical to pre-claim behavior (tested), and no claim ever narrows what admit computes (the perf hint is recorded-only). Strand/pickId identity is UNTOUCHED — the claim pointer lives in sidecars and the Justification, never the signed strand. P3 GAP-1 (G1-additive): a materialized CLEAN admit also attaches AdmitResult.coverage — the #honesty per-path labels (meaning-decided / byte-decided / derived) + aggregate counts over the merge plan's changed paths. Presentation data, never a verdict input. P3 LANE A2 (forge-spec §1d — the permission model IS the scrutiny policy): the TRUST-FLOOR gate, the grades sidecar's first consumer. After the claim gate (claims judge honesty before trust is), an independent-confidence CLEAN — the autoClean class the false-AUTOFOLD gate proved blind — touching a symbol whose GRADED survival (#grade's symbolSurvivalIndex over grades.jsonl; ≥ K_MIN_GRADED graded outcomes, MIN across touched symbols) is below SURVIVAL_FLOOR returns the HELD verdict class (G1-additive to AdmitStatus; never returned by admitDecision): refused, unsealed, selvage unmoved, with AdmitResult.escalation naming the symbol + survival + n. Same fail-safe mechanics as CLAIM-BREACH: acceptRisk is the explicit override — it seals the underlying CLEAN and records the override row in .warpline/grades-escalations.jsonl (G5; never silent). The escalation decision is PURE over (decision, sidecar snapshot); the sidecar is read ONLY on the independent-CLEAN path, so a repo with no grades data — and every other verdict path — behaves byte-identically to before the rule (regression-guarded in test/trust-escalation.test.ts). NATIVE-FIRST R1 (AdmitOptions.shadow, #shadow-gate): shadow mode runs this whole pipeline — claim gate, verdict, escalation, coverage (read-only plan), knot-payload BUILD — and swaps every write (seal, snapshot, sidecar rows, payload persist) for a plain return; AdmitOptions.proposedState lets #pick reuse its own absorb. The decision function is untouched. NATIVE-FIRST R2 (T-2026-07-18-001): a SEALED, NON-SHADOW admission triggers the config-gated auto-stake cadence (#stake maybeAutoStakeOnSeal) best-effort at the single wrap point — never blocking the admission. SCHEMA STAMP (refusal:v1 SP0): AdmitResult carries schemaVersion 'admitResult:v1' (G1) — the result crosses the daemon wire and lands in forge/GUI consumers verbatim (G3), so it names its own shape instead of being duck-typed. The stamp is applied EXACTLY ONCE at the public boundary (admit(); admitNative() mirrors it) over an internal AdmitResultBody, so no builder can forget or forge it and every internal return site is unchanged. REFUSAL (refusal:v1 SP1c, ADDITIVE): every REFUSING return additionally carries AdmitResult.refusal — the machine-readable #refusal. CLAIM-BREACH raises code CLAIM_BREACH at gate 'claim' (pointers.symbols = the excess set, override acceptBreach); the trust floor raises TRUST_HELD at gate 'trust' with an honestly EMPTY contested set (the verdict was CLEAN — what refused is the floor, so pointers.symbols names the below-floor symbol); KNOT/DANGLE raise GATE_REFUSED at gate 'meaning' pointing at the persisted #knot-payload, with next[] = knot.show then resolve (human-class per Aegis §2.2). The byte-conflict DOWNGRADES (meaning said CLEAN, bytes overlapped) raise the same GATE_REFUSED with contestedTotal 0 — which is the honest report that no MEANING unit is contested and the conflict lies below this layer — because a refusal must never be ABSENT on a refusing verdict, or a cold agent learns it cannot rely on the field (F4). Under SHADOW the knot-payload id is deliberately withheld from pointers: the payload is built as pipeline proof but never persisted, and a pointer that fails to dereference is worse than no pointer. Every pre-existing field (status, sealed, claim, escalation, knotPayloadId) is unchanged and remains the authority — #refusal restates them in one shape an agent can act on. The refusal BUILDERS (meaningRefusal / claimRefusal / trustRefusal) are exported and shared with #native-write-path (T-2026-07-21-007): both paths raise the SAME objects, differing only in the ladder's admit params ({ref} git-era, {native:'true'} native) so next[] is copy-paste runnable on the surface that raised it. gitSides (ADDITIVE, 2026-08-10): AdmitResult carries {ours, theirs} — the two GIT commits the verdict's two meaning-sides correspond to. `ours` is the agent's ref (fixed above the lock); `theirs` is the commit of the strand the SELVAGE named, resolved INSIDE the fabric lock at the same expression that decides `baseFrom`, for the identical reason: the selvage can move the instant the lock releases, so a consumer that re-read it would measure against a tip this verdict never judged. Its one consumer is #git-counterfactual, and a counterfactual measured against the wrong pair is worse than none. The ledger read is try/caught — an unreadable ledger yields theirs:null (surfacing downstream as an explicit 'no-two-refs') rather than making a NOOP admission start throwing where it succeeded before. Git-era path only; #native-write-path is git-absent by definition.

claim.name: Claim
claim.description: The claim-scoped propose API, claim:v1 (P2.3, forge-spec §3b, T-2026-06-24-018). A claim is the author's PRE-DECLARATION — agentId, claimedSymbols, optional taskRef (a structured id/URL, not prose), optional claimedContractDelta (the engine's SemDelta shape VERBATIM, G3 — recorded for the future grade stream, not evaluated in v1), optional confidence, and an ENVELOPED intent (#prose-envelope, §3d) — content-addressed at creation (claimId = claim:v1:sha256(canonical body); createClaim is the only constructor; verifyClaim recomputes the address + the intent envelope, and persist/read fail CLOSED on tamper). The claim schema IS the future OFFER metadata (§3b). Triple duty: (1) HONESTY CHECK — evaluateClaim(decision, claim) compares claimed vs COMPUTED symbol sets: excess = changed-but- unclaimed symbols that are DIRECT (SemDelta.localChanged) or ripple-only- but-KNOTTING (a ripple-only non-knotting symbol is exempt — charging authors for Merkle avalanches would make honest claims impossible; no agentDelta ⇒ all treated direct, conservative). The knotting carve-out excludes PROVEN body-internal ripples (localChanged false AND rippleFromContract false, the #sem-delta stage-1 bit — T-2026-07-21-008): the essence inlines callee bodies into callers, so an honest single-symbol edit re-addresses every caller and can knot them against a concurrent writer; charging the claim for that engine artifact converted accurate self-reporting into a breach (the documented trust-erosion path — the CLI's remediation taught agents --accept-breach as routine). Exemption exactly as narrow as the proof: rippleFromContract absent or true keeps the knot counting (fail closed); missing = claimed-but-untouched, recorded NEVER a breach; breach = excess nonempty → #admit's CLAIM-BREACH verdict. (2) CALIBRATION PROBE — every evaluation appends {claimId, pickId?, agentId, breach, excess, missing, acceptedBreach?, ts} to .warpline/claims/evaluations.jsonl (G5 sidecar; the per-agent claimed-vs- computed honesty signal for the grade layer). (3) PERF HINT — recorded so a later layer CAN scope by claim; deliberately not implemented (no decision function reads a claim to narrow computation). evaluateClaim reads NO prose (the poisoned-prose invariant extends to claim fields). Sidecar persistence under .warpline/claims/ keyed by claimId (G2: no ledger positions). Surfaced via `warpline propose --agent <id> --claim <file|json>` (returns claimId) and `warpline admit … --claim <claimId> [--accept-breach]`.

prose-envelope.name: Prose Envelope
prose-envelope.description: The injection-safety envelope (P2.4 minimum slice, forge-spec §3d, T-2026-06-24-013). Agent-authored prose (intents, resolution reasons, proposal rationales) is UNTRUSTED INPUT to any reading agent/surface: every free-text field crossing an agent or rendering boundary is wrapped at creation as {kind:'untrusted-prose', contentAddress, body} — born content-addressed ('prose:v1:'+sha256), kind tag unforgeable in the shape (a body CONTAINING a serialized envelope stays a string). verifyProse recomputes the address (tamper ⇒ false); frameProse is the ONLY legal human rendering — Warpline authors the frame, control/ANSI bytes are escaped, every body line is guttered so no body content can pose as a frame boundary, and a tampered envelope refuses to render (fail closed). The third layer — the PURE-FUNCTION CONTRACT (gate/verdict decisions read only structural inputs, never prose) — is a TESTED invariant: the poisoned-prose suite asserts byte-identical verdicts under an adversarial corpus in every prose field.

knot-payload.name: Knot Payload
knot-payload.description: The machine-readable KNOT payload, knotPayload:v1 (P2.2 / R3, forge-spec §3a — the forge's issue AND the agent's work order, ONE shape). buildKnotPayload turns a KNOT/DANGLE decision + the three states into a SELF-SUFFICIENT document: per contested unit both sides' MEANING bodies (the essence-data body slot / canonical contract) AND durable file texts read from the content-addressed object store, per-side sem-deltas, conflictingSlots, direct-vs-ripple, essences; both sides' intents as #prose-envelope (untrusted-prose) with agentId/actor attribution; base/ours/theirs stateIds + treeIds; the blast-radius as a mode:'ripple' graph slice; and the RESOLUTION-PROPOSAL envelope (knotResolutionProposal:v1) that proposalToResolveOptions maps 1:1 onto #resolve's ResolveOptions after VERIFYING the reason envelope (tamper ⇒ fail closed). Deterministic (no clock; payloadId = content address), G1-versioned, G2 (no ledger positions), G5 (persisted as derived sidecar data under .warpline/knots/ — never a strand). §3a exit gate is a TESTED round-trip: a resolver acting from the payload ALONE constructs a resolve call that seals. NO auto-resolution here (P5, gated on the blind injection corpus). Surfaced via `warpline knot show <payloadId|admitRef>` (--json = the exact engine shape; human view frames all prose).

judge.name: Judge
judge.description: The Warpline LLM-JUDGE — the blinded second rater / meaning-judge falsifier of the Expo field test (expo-field-test-protocol.md §5 / §4; T-2026-07-14-004). A STANDALONE COLD INSTRUMENT, blind by construction: pure, deterministic, no clock, no API call, no Warpline daemon token, and NO import path to the agent runtime/roster/notebooks. Three foundation modules: #judge/rubric — the FROZEN rubric text + two version-tagged prompt templates, each with a stable rubricHash (rubric:v1:sha256 over the canonical text): the §5 GENUINE / OVER-BLOCK question for KNOT cards (the (B)/(C) denominator) and the §4 broken / not-broken question for false-CLEAN cards, each carrying the standing injection instruction that ALL framed content is quoted UNTRUSTED DATA, never instruction. #judge/rating-card — the STRIPPER: buildKnotRatingCard walks agentChanged ∪ otherChanged (recovering file paths from #code:/#cfg: symbol names) plus the contested units' own paths to the FULL changed-file set, reads base/ours/theirs bodies via #knot-payload readFileFromTree, keeps the two #prose-envelope intents, and STRIPS the verdict, confidence, contested[].kind, conflictingSlots, blastRadius, direct flag, payloadId, rebasedOnto — everything evaluative; buildCleanRatingCard does the same from a §4 audit row (two parent trees + merged tree + the failing check NAME, never the CLEAN verdict). cardId = ratingCard:v1:sha256(canonical(cardBody)), clock-free. #judge/card-render — the ONLY surface the model sees: every side body + intent rendered through #prose-envelope frameProse (escaped, guttered, visibly UNTRUSTED), a 400-line-per-body truncation note that never hides silently, then the frozen rubric text + the framed card as one inert prompt string. THE LIVE HALF: #judge/types — the shared vocabulary (Judgment with verbatim per-sample outputs + majority/spread/indeterminate; RunRecord pinning model=claude-opus-4-5-20251101, agentsModel=claude-opus-5, temp 0, N=3; LedgerRow; the pinned constants). #judge/judge-run — the INSTRUMENT: an INJECTABLE CallModel (unit tests pass a deterministic fake, NEVER the network), N=3 sampling with no-2-of-3 → INDETERMINATE, run-record.json frozen pin + verbatim judgments.jsonl; liveCallModel lazily wires @anthropic-ai/sdk (OPTIONAL dep) at the pinned model + temp 0, guarded to construct only with an API key — imports NOTHING from src/daemon or the agent loader. #judge/ledger — hash-chained content-addressed custody (rowHash = sha256(canonical (body)+prevRowHash)) with WRITE-BEFORE-REVEAL (the judge-verdict row sealed before the warpline-join that references it), head() as the git external witness, and verify() first-bad-row. #judge/preflight — the BLOCKING gate: the per-card twin-invariant (a card whose verdict moves under a comment/prose-neutralized twin is VOID) plus the blind injection corpus (a judge that tracks a planted payload is DISQUALIFIED for the whole run). #judge/scoring — the falsifier harness: Cohen's kappa, confusion tables, the §4 objective-non-vetoable false-CLEAN confirmation JOIN, seeded-control precision/recall vs the ~29% prior, before/after pre-fix scoring against the fixed judge label, the §7A two-denominator bounds (objective vs subjective, rule-of-three each, NEVER blended), and the INDETERMINATE fraction against the contested floor. #judge/judge-runner — the ENFORCING run path that wires the three together so the foundation gates actually fire: runJudgeEnforced runs #judge/preflight FIRST and HARD-REFUSES (JudgeRefusedError / hard-fail result) if the judge is disqualified — nothing real scores past an unvalidated judge; only twin-PASSING eligibleCards are sampled (verbatim run-record.json + judgments.jsonl kept as the §5 raw-output AUDIT artifact) and each MAJORITY verdict is SEALED into the hash-chained #judge/ledger via sealJudgeVerdict — the LEDGER, not the plaintext log, is the AUTHORITATIVE denominator, and a later Warpline join goes through joinWarplineVerdict (write-before-reveal). At each BLOCK BOUNDARY it writes ledger.head() to a git-tracked witness file (default <outDir>/.warpline-judge/expo-field-audit.head) and surfaces it via the return value / injected logger: committing (or GPG-signing) that head into git is a REQUIRED run-procedure step (§3 A13) — the code writes and surfaces the head, the OPERATOR commits it, so git's independent history externally witnesses the chain. CARD HARDENING (§5, §3d): #judge/card-render routes EVERY filePath and failingCheck — the bare `file:` lines, the changed-files list, the failingCheck line, AND the frameProse LABEL (which frameProse does NOT escape) — through sanitizeField (escapeProseBody + newline/tab collapse), so an agent-controlled filename carrying newlines/control bytes can no longer forge a column-0 narration line or a frame edge; #judge/preflight's benign twin ALSO neutralizes filePath/failingCheck (defense in depth — the differential COVERS those channels). INSTRUMENT HARDENING (T-2026-08-23-002, B1–B6): (B1) MULTI-BATCH CONTINUITY — runJudgeEnforced LOADS + VERIFIES an existing <outDir>/expo-field-audit.jsonl (LedgerContinuityError on a broken chain, nothing sealed) and APPENDS; JudgeLedger.persist/appendPersist is append-only (never truncates a prefix, refuses divergence); runJudge appends judgments.jsonl and verifies+MERGES run-record.json (cardIds union, batches[] per call; RunRecordMismatchError if model/promptHash/rubricHash/samplesPerCard change mid-run); the result carries previousHead + ledgerHead and every batch head is appended to <witness>.log. (B2) every judge-verdict row carries judgmentHash = judgment:v1:sha256(canonical(Judgment)) over the FULL verbatim Judgment (judgmentHashOf / verifyJudgmentBinding) plus the §4 RECORDING Provenance (source, planted/seededControl/auditSample, groundTruth, coveredClass, objectiveRegression, strand/pick/agents/parents/mergedTree ids, oracle outcomes) sealed write-time- immutable into the LEDGER ONLY — never the card or the prompt (blindness asserted byte-for-byte); excludedFromDenominator / denominatorRows drop planted, seeded and corpus rows. (B3) confirmCleanFalse never rounds favorably: indeterminate and pending are their OWN CleanVerdicts; scoreCleanAudits reports them separately and nSubjective = true-clean + confirmed-false-clean only (subjectiveBoundInputs). (B4) preflight runs gate (b) FIRST (a disqualified judge sees ZERO real cards — realCardsSampled: 0), classifies card/twin/corpus at N=SAMPLES_PER_CARD with the instrument's own resolveMajority and compares MAJORITY labels (spreads recorded), and an EMPTY corpus is DISQUALIFIED (allowEmptyCorpus is a TEST-ONLY hatch, threaded through runJudgeEnforced, default false). (B5) beatsPriorPrecision is the one-sided 95% Wilson LOWER bound (wilsonLowerBound) vs the ~29% prior — a point estimate alone never beats it; seededControlPrecisionRecall reports genuinePrecisionLowerBound95 / overBlockRecallLowerBound95. (B6) indeterminateFraction excludes seeds/planted/corpus (exclude predicate or provenance map) and reports genuineAfterDrain (the §3 floor is GENUINE-only; meetsContestedFloor(…, 20)) and overBlockAfterDrain separately — contestedAfterDrain is gone.

refusal.name: Refusal
refusal.description: refusal:v1 — the MACHINE-READABLE REFUSAL every gate hands back (founder constraint TD-2026-07-21-766; pre-registered falsifier F4 "cold-agent legibility"). THE CONSTRAINT: an agent of ANY provider, with no Warpline in its weights and no Warpline docs in context, must complete propose → admit → KNOT → resolve using ONLY tool descriptions and the returned refusal objects. Git is easy for models because git is MEMORIZED; Warpline never will be, so runtime self-description is the only mechanism — and this object is its load-bearing carrier. THE BINDING RULE: no human sentences in a verdict, ever. Every field is an id, an enum, a pointer or a count; human prose stays OUTSIDE the verdict (the thrown Error's message, CLI rendering) or ENVELOPED as #prose-envelope untrusted-prose. Fields: code (12-value closed enum — GATE_REFUSED / CLAIM_BREACH / TRUST_HELD / STALE_BASE / INTEGRITY_BROKEN / AUTH / FORBIDDEN / BAD_REQUEST / UNKNOWN_VERB / NOT_FOUND / UNSUPPORTED / ENGINE), verdict (the AdmitStatus behind it, null for transport/usage), gate (meaning|claim|trust|pick| transport|usage — WHICH layer refused), retriable (retry-identical | retry-after-rebase | retry-after-resolve | retry-with-override | never), contested[] (the RANKED index — stableKey, symbol, #predict KnotRule, conflictingSlots, direct-vs-ripple rank), contestedTotal, pointers (knotPayloadId / proposedStateId / rebasedOnto / claimId / symbols — G2: never a ledger position), next[] (THE F4 field: verb + already-determined params + the arg NAMES still required + principal agent|human, so an agent seeing principal:'human' ESCALATES rather than attempts), and an optional human-class override door (acceptBreach|acceptRisk). refuse() is the SINGLE constructor — no other module builds a Refusal literal, which is what makes the cap, the total, the ranking and the code tables INVARIANTS rather than per-site conventions. TRUNCATION HONESTY: contested is capped at MAX_CONTESTED (32) so an essence-transitivity avalanche cannot blow a tool-result budget, contestedTotal always carries the FULL count (a truncated list without a total is a lie), and the survivors are the direct-contested ones (#rank) so the cap never eats the signal. Every pointer must DEREFERENCE: a shadow-built knot payload is never persisted, so its id is deliberately withheld rather than advertised as a dead knot.show selector. exitCodeFor maps each code to the shell-legible exit contract (1 refuse / 2 bad request / 3 claim breach / 4 trust held / 5 stale base), is TOTAL by construction, and fails CLOSED (1) on an unknown code — a refusal must never exit success. exitCodeForResult(result) is the whole-OUTCOME form every skin consumes (T-2026-07-21-006: exitCodeFor was exported-and-unconsumed, so `admit --native` exited 0 on an unsealed CLAIM-BREACH — a silent failure indistinguishable from success): the refusal's mapped code when one is present, else 0 — the exit is derived from the result's OWN refusal object, never a re-derived vocabulary (G3). Deterministic, pure, G1-versioned, G5 (derived data — never a signed strand field). refusalOf(value) is the SINGLE ACCESSOR — the counterpart to refuse() being the single constructor: no consumer re-derives WHERE a refusal can live. Two legal depths: the engine shape's own `.refusal`, and an ENVELOPE that nests the engine shape under `.result` (the shadow gate's {shadow, row, result}). Added for audit C-16 (Jinx J-12): #warplined's PW-8 audit probe and #warpline-mcp's isError probe each tested `'refusal' in result` on the OUTER object, so a SHADOW CLAIM_BREACH / TRUST_HELD / KNOT reached the MCP host as isError:false and audited with no resultCode — the exact masking PW-8 claims to close, reopened by an envelope, and a corruption of the #shadow-gate verdict stream that the R2 gate-promotion argument rests on. Shape-checked (schemaVersion + code), so an unversioned look-alike is never mistaken for a verdict, and DELIBERATELY BOUNDED at one envelope level — a deep search would find refusals that are not the caller's outcome (an archived knot verdict, a tail of shadow rows) and turn reads into errors. A third depth, if one is ever introduced, is named HERE. Regression: test/shadow-refusal-mask.test.ts. PW-1 (mcp-skin-spec §4): retriability gains 'retry-corrected' ("a corrected or prerequisite call succeeds — follow next[], then retry"); BAD_REQUEST/UNKNOWN_VERB/NOT_FOUND default to it ('never' on a fixable call taught cold agents to abandon instead of correct); AUTH/FORBIDDEN stay 'never' (escalation is the door, carried by next[]). RefusedError (PW-2 shell) is the THROWN refusal: engine prerequisite boundaries throw it carrying a typed refusal:v1, and every skin's catch-all (CLI fail(), daemon boundary) detects it and emits the carried refusal verbatim instead of collapsing to ENGINE/retry-identical/empty-next — the machine hint that instructed an infinite losing retry. D-6a (F4 instrument panel, 2026-07-31) — THE PHANTOM-PARAM RULE, now tested rather than remembered: a next[] step's params/requires must name params that EXIST on the verb they call. The CLAIM_BREACH ladder's propose step required 'claimedSymbols', which is a param of NO skin — it lives one level DOWN, inside `claim` — and the MCP skin's filterToSchema drops unknown keys SILENTLY, so a cold agent following the ladder verbatim sealed a proposal with no claim on it, met the identical breach, and (the other step being principal:'human') had no agent-runnable recovery left in the ladder at all. It now requires [intent, worktree, claim], and the honest recovery is to widen `claim` until it COVERS pointers.symbols; the retry of the refused verb stays implicit, as in every other ladder here (agent prerequisites, then the human door). PW-4 (test/refusal-vocabulary-totality.test.ts) enforces BOTH halves of the class across every ladder-bearing builder: an OMITTED required param (coverage — now checked on human-class steps too, the skip that hid #pick's D-10) and an INVENTED one (membership — with the human override door exempted, since it is a CLI act carrying --native/--ref and the accept* flags that are deliberately absent from the MCP schema).

rank.name: Rank
rank.description: The DIRECT-CONTESTED vs RIPPLE-ONLY ranking rule, as an engine function (T-2026-07-03-002; lifted out of #warpline-cli in the refusal:v1 build). rankOf(x) reads #predict's own-content-changed flag — DIRECT iff ≥1 side edited the unit's OWN content, RIPPLE iff the essence moved only via edge-target transitivity (Merkle-by-target); an ABSENT flag reads as DIRECT, so unknown is surfaced and never silently collapsed into the bucket consumers are entitled to hide. rankVerdicts(knots) partitions a knot set, preserving input order within each bucket.
