WHY ENGINE, NOT PRESENTATION: ground truth over 275 real merges put ≤6-symbol flag sets at 50% churn-validated and every ≥10-symbol set — including seven 48-176-symbol avalanches rippling out of ~2 genuinely contested units — at 0%, so "which of these flags is the actual contest?" is a judgment the engine owes every consumer, not a rendering choice one consumer makes. #warpline-cli's anti-avalanche display and #refusal's contested cap are now the same judgment applied twice (G3). Ranking is DATA ONLY — knot/dangle/autoClean/ verdict semantics do not move (a policy change would invalidate the committed base-rate evidence). Pure and SILENT (cli.ts is the only file allowed to write to stdout); parity with the pre-move implementation is a TESTED invariant (test/rank.test.ts carries the old code as the oracle).

merge3.name: Merge3
merge3.description: A token-level 3-way merge (the Phase-C v2 materialization primitive). tokenize splits text into word/whitespace/punct runs (join === text); merge3(base, ours, theirs) does a hunk-based diff3 over token arrays (LCS alignment → change hunks → base-range overlap detection). A range changed by only ONE side takes that side; disjoint changes — even two edits on ONE line, or a deletion next to an edit — compose cleanly (this is what git's LINE-level merge conflicts on). A range BOTH sides changed in OVERLAPPING base coordinates is a CONFLICT (counted; merged then unsafe) — NEVER silently resolved (the VCS cardinal sin). Pure, no I/O. The O(n·m) LCS is CAPPED — an oversized/minified file fails closed (whole-file conflict) instead of OOM-ing (M1).

materialize.name: Materialize
materialize.description: Phase-C v2 meaning→bytes — PERFORM the merge git could only forecast. computeMerge(base, ours, theirs refs) reads each changed file's RAW BYTES via git (binary-safe: a binary blob — NUL-bearing — changed on both sides fails CLOSED as a conflict, never a UTF-8 text-merge corruption, H3) and merges per-file with #merge3; any add/delete-vs-edit or overlapping token-region is a surfaced CONFLICT. changedPaths runs with `--no-renames` so a rename decomposes to delete-of-old + add-of-new (H2): a clean rename applies its delete instead of silently leaving a COPY, and a rename racing an edit of the old path fails closed as add/delete-vs-edit. ABSENT-vs-FAILED (soundness audit C-8): a file's PRESENCE on each side is decided by its TREE ENTRY (#git-exec treeEntryMode), never by a failed read. `git show` exits 128 both for "path not in this tree" and for a missing object / corrupt pack / EMFILE / ENOMEM, so catching it to null made resolveFile read an I/O failure as "deleted on that side" and DROP the file from the merged tree — zero conflicts, sealed CLEAN, a bad disk sector becoming an `rm`. A present entry whose bytes will not read now THROWS and aborts the merge (fail closed). computeMergeNative is structurally immune — this was git-path only, and the git path is the default. The git tree-entry MODE is 3-way-merged alongside the bytes so the executable bit survives a content merge; a changed symlink/submodule (non-blob entry) fails CLOSED rather than round-trip as a regular blob and corrupt the entry type. materializeMergedState applies the conflict-free plan onto a throwaway copy of the base tree (restoring each merged file's mode) and absorbs it → the merged WarpState (the user's working tree is never touched). gitShow is byte-faithful (no trim) so trailing newlines and exact bytes survive — no drift. DERIVED ARTIFACTS (P3 GAP-1): a lockfile (#derived-artifacts) changed divergently on BOTH sides never conflicts/knots — taken from OURS wholesale (never token-merged: a spliced lockfile pretends precision it doesn't have) and recorded in MergePlan.derivedStale (additive) for regeneration from the merged manifests. Applies identically on the git-ref and native-tree paths.

hook.name: Hook
hook.description: The auto-seal git hook. installHook/uninstallHook/hookStatus manage a BEGIN/END-delimited block APPENDED to the repo's post-commit hook (worktree- correct path via gitPath) so every git commit also seals a #strand — the native history accrues in lockstep with git. Coexists with any existing post-commit hook (e.g. Paradigm's history capture), never clobbers it; install is idempotent (refreshes the block in place); uninstall strips only the warpline block. The block seals `--ref HEAD` (the committed tree, never the worktree — so it captures exactly what was committed and never conflates another agent's uncommitted work). Runs in the BACKGROUND (a full-repo absorb is slow) and is fail-safe (`|| true`) so it never delays, blocks, or fails the commit; the strand for commit N lands shortly after N (and rides in N+1). BINARY RESOLUTION (T-2026-08-12-002 item 4 — the cold-agent silent-skip fix): `hook install` BAKES the exact interpreter + CLI running it (resolveInvokingBinary → process.execPath + realpath(argv[1])) into the block as its DEFAULT seal binary (_wl_node/_wl_script), so the hook seals with the same binary that installed it — NOT a bare `warpline` guessed off PATH, which a cold agent invoking `node /abs/cli.js` (no global install) never has. Precedence mirrors health.hookResolution exactly: env WARPLINE_BIN override → baked → bare `warpline` on PATH → monorepo dist/cli.js → none. On `none` the block prints a VISIBLE foreground `auto-seal SKIPPED` stderr line (the commit still succeeds); and `hook install` FAILS LOUDLY (non-zero, writes no hook) when it cannot resolve a runnable binary at all — the one refusal on the REAL condition, not a PATH proxy (see hookInstallAdvice's retained four-point argument).

warpline-config.name: Warpline Config
warpline-config.description: Per-repo engine toggles, `.warpline/config.json` (NATIVE-FIRST R1/R2; .paradigm/research/warpline-native-first/roadmap-native-first.md). OPT-IN switches only — defaults never change because a config exists. Keys: shadowGate (default false) — when true, every #pick also records the #shadow-gate observe-only verdict; stake (default: valve OFF) — the #stake checkpoint valve's S4 toggle {enabled, refs allowlist, branch, repo, author} plus the R2 auto-stake cadence stake.auto ('every-seal'|'daily'|false, default false — S4 still rules); and gate (R2, default agentWrites:'shadow') — gate.agentWrites:'real' makes an AGENT-ATTRIBUTED #pick ENFORCE its admit verdict (blocking on a would-not-seal verdict; humans keep the git door byte-identically). The leakage deny-list is deliberately NOT here (D5: constitution-grade frozen constant in #stake-guard, never a config flag). A missing config is the empty config; a MALFORMED config throws (a corrupt toggle file must not silently read as "everything off") — the seal path catches for humans (fail-safe) but REFUSES agent-attributed picks (fail-closed: a corrupt toggle must not silently disable the real gate); interactive callers surface it.

stake.name: Stake
stake.description: THE CHECKPOINT VALVE (Phase 1 native-first, T-2026-07-17-001, founder ask; arky-architecture.md §3 + aegis-security.md §3). `warpline stake` exports ONE sealed fabric state as ONE git commit on a DEDICATED stake branch (default warpline-stakes; working-branch names refused) — git's demoted role: a familiar, read-only checkpoint shelf. D3: stakes are a FIRST-PARENT LINEARIZATION (each stake's single parent = the previous stake commit; git receives checkpoints, never the weave topology). Safeguards: S1 committed `.warpline-stake` marker + trailer-only message (`warpline-stake` + PickId/StateId/TreeId/Schema, zero prose); S2 allowlist-by-materialization — the tree is built by restoreTree from the bound object store into a clean temp dir, then the post-build audit walks the built bytes against the #stake-guard deny-list + untrusted-prose content markers (nothing touches the git odb until the audit passes); S3 verify-or-refuse — built tree re-hashed from disk must equal BOTH binding.treeId and the shadow gitOid RECOMPUTED from the store (never read from s.binding.gitOid), and `rev-parse <commit>^{tree}` must equal the pure-TS expectation before the ref CAS-advances; S4 default OFF + per-ref allowlist + EVERY invocation (stake/skip/refuse/recover) appends a stakeAudit:v1 row to `.warpline/stakes/audit.jsonl`; S5 `warpline stake recover <commit>` verifies the reset worktree hashes to the staked strand's WORKTREE-SEMANTICS EXPECTATION (T-2026-07-18-005, the F3 drill-#1 false-refusal fix: a worktree:v1 binding IS the expectation; a legacy-git binding's expectation is projectTreeWorktreeSemantics of the authenticated binding tree — each strand judged under ITS OWN recorded semantics) then MOVES refs/heads/selvage (or the legacy selvage) under the fabric lock — a ref move, NEVER an import or a new strand (post-recover edits parent on the staked pick via the normal seal path). The cut RECORDS worktreeTreeId (additive stakeAudit field + StakeResult) — the honest recovery expectation, on the audit record for any strand; recover records it too. Pinned by test/tree-semantics.test.ts (a legacy-semantics stake recovers GREEN after `git reset --hard`; an edited tree still refuses). Idempotent: re-staking the tip pickId SKIPS with an audit note. Gitlink-bearing trees refuse (bytes Warpline does not own). Commit objects are written as loose objects via #stake-git — no index, no filters, byte-exact. R2 AUTO-STAKE (T-2026-07-18-001, "the valve stakes every seal"): maybeAutoStakeOnSeal — config-gated cadence (stake.auto: 'every-seal'|'daily'|false, default false) invoked best-effort by the #pick and #admit seal paths after a successful NON-SHADOW seal; S4 still rules (enabled + allowlist checked BEFORE invoking, so a disabled cadence never spams refuse rows); 'daily' skips while a stake/skip ran within 24h; a valve failure NEVER blocks the seal and every actual invocation audits itself; a byteOnly seal (#pick byte custody) counts — doc-only commits reach the valve. FIRST LIVE STAKE cut 2026-07-18: commit 440fec31bd57e6cd61d87adbe06a22d08a63028f on warpline-stakes (the exact sealed state the v1 deny-list had refused); SECOND (post-tree-semantics- fix) 0f4b2ffe9d47, parent 440fec31 — F3 drill #2 recovered it GREEN (f3-drills.jsonl n=2); 440fec31 itself remains recoverable via the recorded-semantics projection (validated byte-for-byte against drill-1 evidence).

stake-journal.name: Stake Journal
stake-journal.description: The checkpoint valve's audit sidecar (.warpline/stakes/audit.jsonl, stakeAudit:v1) AND THE ANTI-TRUNCATION WITNESS (audit C-6). A leaf module (fs + path only) holding STAKE_AUDIT_SCHEMA / StakeAuditRow / stakesDirOf / stakeAuditPathOf / readStakeJournal — split out of #stake precisely so #fabric-verify can consult it WITHOUT importing the valve's git/snapshot graph (a verify→stake→seal import cycle); #stake re-exports all of it, so the sidecar stays the valve's own artifact. WHY IT EXISTS AS A WITNESS: Warpline's tamper-evidence against MUTATION is real (six mutation classes, six detections) and against TAIL DELETION did not exist. The evidence to close that was already on disk — with stake.auto on, every seal names the pickId it staked, an append-only journal of every tip this fabric has held, git's reflog — and verify.ts never read it. TWO DESIGN CALLS, both load-bearing. (1) ADVISORY EVIDENCE, NEVER AUTHORITY: readStakeJournal NEVER throws — a missing file, an unreadable file, a disabled valve and a fresh fabric all collapse to an empty attestation set, and an empty set can never fail a verification. The corollary is stated, not hidden: a truncator who ALSO deletes this file leaves no local trace; the tamper-resistant corroborator is the git side (refs/heads/warpline-stakes carries the same pickIds in push-able commit objects), which is an ASYNC git read while verifyFabric is deliberately synchronous and pure — noted as future work, not silently skipped. (2) ONLY COMPLETED ACTIONS ATTEST — stake / skip / recover, because completion is what PROVES the strand was in this fabric (each resolves the ref THROUGH a strand's byte binding, or passes a fabric-membership check, before the row is written). recover-refuse is excluded as UNSOUND (one of its own refusal reasons is literally "stake names pickId X, which is absent from the fabric" — attesting it would turn a correct refusal into a permanent false alarm); refuse is excluded as merely UNNEEDED (sound today, but it is the diagnostic stream, and pinning a HARD verify failure to a non-completing path is a premise a refactor can silently break). (3) A torn journal row is COUNTED and skipped, never fatal — appendStakeAudit swallows write errors by design, so a half-written last row is expected. Duplicate pickIds keep the EARLIEST attestation. Regression: test/stake-journal-truncation.test.ts.

stake-guard.name: Stake Guard
stake-guard.description: The S1 one-way guards + the D5 CONSTITUTION-GRADE deny-list of the checkpoint valve — stake-denylist:v2 (R2, T-2026-07-18-001: the v1 basename-global + byte-substring rules refused the FIRST REAL stake on four false positives — source/spec/tests QUOTING the envelope marker, and a paradigm-events verdicts.jsonl hit by basename). v2 is FROZEN + schema-versioned in FIVE constants with colocated pure matchers: STAKE_DENY_NAMES (any-depth structural/secret names — .git, .warpline wholesale [a stake is a reset target; fabric content inside one would stomp the live fabric — tracked .warpline files are fine IN GIT but never in a stake tree, which by construction the snapshot walk cannot produce anyway], .warpline-stake, daemon-tokens/session-keys.jsonl); STAKE_DENY_PATHS (ROOT-ANCHORED sidecar homes under .warpline/ — belts pinned by name so narrowing the wholesale rule can never silently expose a sidecar); STAKE_DENY_ENVELOPE_KINDS + STAKE_DENY_ROW_SCHEMAS + STAKE_DENY_ROW_SHAPES (SHAPE-AWARE content rules: only PARSED .json/.jsonl content matching an envelope object, a sidecar schema tag, or a sidecar field signature refuses — source/markdown/tests can never match). Any change is a SCHEMA CHANGE (bump the tag + re-pin the freeze-test digest in test/stake.test.ts), never a config flag. assertNotStakeInput is the S1 choke point wired into #absorb (covering #pick and the #hook auto-seal path): a worktree carrying the marker, a ref in the stake namespace, or a commit whose tree carries the marker is REFUSED as input; #backfill leaves marker-bearing provenance commits unbound. The marker read FAILS CLOSED (soundness audit C-8): it used to catch a failed `ls-tree` to null, which the guard reads as "not a stake" — a security guard whose failure mode was ALLOW. An unreadable ref is now refused, never admitted; only a genuinely absent marker passes. Cycle-free by design (imports only fs/config/git-exec) so absorb can import it. Regressions pinned in test/stake-denylist-v2.test.ts (each live false positive is a MUST-PASS fixture; true leaks still refuse).

stake-git.name: Stake Git
stake-git.description: The ONLY module in Warpline allowed to WRITE to a git repository, fenced to the checkpoint valve. Two mutations exactly: (1) loose blob/tree/ commit objects constructed in pure TS (git's exact framing + sha1, zlib, write-tmp + atomic rename) — no `git add`, no index, no clean/smudge/ autocrlf filters, so staked bytes can never be rewritten in flight; (2) the stake ref advanced via `git update-ref <ref> <new> <old>` per-ref CAS — never a checkout, never HEAD/index/worktree. sha256-object-format repos refuse fail-closed. buildCommitBody is first-parent-only BY SHAPE (a single optional parent — a stake commit structurally cannot be a merge; D3). #git-exec stays read-only by contract.

shadow-gate.name: Shadow Gate
shadow-gate.description: R1 of the native-first dogfood ladder (loid-loops.md §1) — the organic evidence clock. shadowAdmit runs the FULL #admit pipeline (claim gate, verdict, trust-floor escalation, coverage labels, knot-payload build) in OBSERVE-ONLY mode: never seals, never moves the selvage, never writes fabric/objects/sidecars — the ONLY write is one `shadowVerdict:v1` row appended to `.warpline/shadow/verdicts.jsonl` {ts, ref, agentId, status, confidence, knots, coverage, wouldSeal, durationMs, escalation?, claimReport?}. ROW BOUNDS (T-2026-07-17-007): the symbol arrays (knots/ agentChanged/otherChanged) cap at SHADOW_ROW_CAP=50 sorted entries with ADDITIVE exact-total fields (knotsTotal/agentChangedTotal/ otherChangedTotal) — a WORKTREE verdict over a 24k-symbol change is a ~5KB row; under-cap verdicts keep full symbol fidelity; schema stays v1 (additive only, G1). Feeds organic-K3, HELD precision (would-have-held counts), and the F1a latency baseline BEFORE any cutover risk. Surfaces: `warpline admit --shadow`, and the #pick auto-seal path when #warpline-config sets shadowGate:true. Zero-mutation invariant pinned byte-for-byte in test/shadow-admit.test.ts. Rows are LOCAL telemetry (gitignored); shadow never pollutes the real claims/grades calibration streams — its judgments ride the row. C-9 (ADDITIVE, 2026-08-01): the row carries `baseFrom` — 'scratch' | 'selvage' | 'none' — the pointer #admit actually read its BASE from, carried verbatim from the AdmitResult (never re-read here; a second reader of the scratch ref would report something the row's own authority did not use). 'selvage' means the gate had NO agent base and FAST_ADMIT was forced structurally, which is a different fact from "nothing contended" and was previously indistinguishable from it on this stream — so an empty K3 denominator could not be read as mechanical or behavioural without re-deriving the answer from source. Absent on pre-C-9 rows. GIT COUNTERFACTUAL (ADDITIVE, 2026-08-10): every row now also carries `gitCounterfactual` — see #git-counterfactual. The row's `durationMs` keeps its ORIGINAL meaning (the decision pipeline, F1a) and is stopped before the git call; the counterfactual's own cost rides its own field, so an existing series is never silently redefined. The zero-mutation invariant is unchanged for everything it ever covered (.warpline byte-identical but the one row; HEAD/index/worktree untouched), with one thing now said out loud: `git merge-tree --write-tree` parks a few unreferenced, gc-able tree objects in `.git/objects`.

git-counterfactual.name: Git Counterfactual
git-counterfactual.description: WHAT GIT WOULD HAVE DECIDED, recorded on the live verdict row at the moment the verdict was reached (src/fabric/counterfactual.ts). The product claim is "meaning caught what bytes missed" and nothing measured it: #oracle computes the git×meaning confusion matrix but is an OFFLINE MANUAL verb whose ledger (.warpline/oracle.jsonl — 11 MB, 28 rows) has ZERO readers, while #shadow-gate, the only instrument that fires on real work, never called git at all. It must be measured at verdict time or never: the two commits survive, but WHICH PAIR a given verdict adjudicated stops being recoverable the moment the selvage moves. MECHANISM: `git merge-tree --write-tree <theirs> <ours>` — the same call oracle.ts:160 makes — over the SAME two sides the meaning verdict judged. The sides come from AdmitResult.gitSides, resolved inside #admit's fabric lock, NEVER re-read here (a second reader would report against a tip the row's own authority never judged — the mistake `baseFrom` exists to refuse). Git picks its own merge base, so the counterfactual is the question a human would actually have asked git, not a rigged one. TAXONOMY REUSED, NOT REINVENTED: ConvergenceCell names #oracle's four cells verbatim (agreeClean / agreeConflict / divergeGitOnly / divergeMeaningOnly) and partitions on the same two predicates score() uses; the binding is a TEST that drives the real score() through all four cells, not a comment. divergeMeaningOnly is the headline; divergeGitOnly is the text noise Warpline absorbs. `meaningContested` is oracle's own predicate (knots ∪ dangles non-empty), never a status-string test, so the two cannot drift. `unavailable` IS A REQUIRED ENUM, NEVER AN ABSENT FIELD — null means git decided; 'worktree-ref' | 'no-two-refs' | 'git-error' | 'timeout' each name a distinct reason it did not. Absence would reproduce C-9 exactly one field over: "git said clean" and "we never asked git" are opposite facts. PRE-FLIGHT (2026-08-10, found while red-firsting): `git merge-tree --write-tree` exits 1 for BOTH "conflicted" and "not something we can merge", and git-exec.ts:563 keys on code===1, so an UNRESOLVABLE REF comes back as {conflicted:true, conflictPaths:[]} with no throw. A provenance.gitCommit naming a rebased-away commit would therefore have been filed as agreeConflict on the strength of a git ERROR — fabricated evidence for the very claim being measured. Both sides are revParse'd first; a side that does not resolve is 'git-error'. THE SAME CONFLATION REACHES oracle.ts:160, whose .catch() cannot fire for this class either — reported, not unilaterally changed, because it is shared merge semantics. BOUNDS + COST: conflictPaths uses the SHADOW_ROW_CAP pattern (sorted top-N + exact total) — one constant, passed in, no second cap. Measured on this monorepo: p50 9 ms, max 12 ms across three commit spans, against a shadow decision pipeline of p50 87 ms / p99 41,496 ms — ~0.02% of p99, so it is NOT config-gated. Every call is timeout-bounded (20 s) because it rides the auto-seal hook and may never wedge a commit; it never throws.

warpline-root.name: Warpline Root
warpline-root.description: THE ROOT CHOKEPOINT (src/root.ts, soundness audit D-7). Every skin used to resolve its target repository inline as `repoRoot().catch(() => process.cwd())` at ~31 call sites, so the cwd fallback fired ONLY when git failed — meaning every command, including every experiment anyone ran while learning the tool, targeted the LIVE fabric by default, with no --root and no WARPLINE_ROOT. The fix is a chokepoint, not 31 patches: a per-site fix is how the 32nd site gets missed. PRECEDENCE (explicit beats inference, always): --root anywhere on the command line > $WARPLINE_ROOT > repoRoot() > process.cwd(). With neither override set, behaviour is byte-identical to the pre-D-7 code. An explicit root must ALREADY EXIST and be a real directory (never a symlink) — a typo must refuse, never silently mint a second fabric. extractRootFlag pulls --root/--root=<dir> out of argv wherever it appears (commander only accepts program-level options before the subcommand, and `warpline pick --root /tmp/x` failing with "unknown option" is the papercut that sends a user back to the unguarded default); a bare -- terminates scanning. resolveRootVerbose() ALSO REPORTS WHICH ARM WON (RootArm: flag | env | git | cwd, T-2026-08-10) and resolveRoot() is kept as its one-line projection so adding the arm did not become a reason to touch the ~31 call sites — which is the per-site drift the chokepoint exists to prevent. #warpline-health reads the arm and prints it.

warpline-health.name: Warpline Health
warpline-health.description: THE READ-ONLY DIAGNOSTIC (src/health.ts, `warpline health [--json]`). CLI ONLY — deliberately not on the daemon/MCP surface, which also makes it FREE against the FG-3 freeze: descriptorsId hashes VERB_DESCRIPTORS + NEXT_LEGAL_VERBS + the derived tool-name map, none of which a CLI-only verb touches (test/descriptors-frozen.test.ts passes with its literal unchanged). WHY A NEW VERB, NOT MORE `status`: #warpline-cli's `status` has a contract — it is the MEANING DIFF of the working tree vs HEAD, traced as `cli:status` and documented as distinct from the daemon's cycle-position `status`. WHAT IT SURFACES, all of it already on disk and none of it previously read: FABRIC (strand count by schema epoch, `fabric verify` in-process, selvage, refs vs legacy mode, abandoned heads, the C-6 stake-journal witness); SEAL LIVENESS (the last strand names its git commit, so `git rev-list --count <that>..HEAD` gives commits-behind-HEAD — a subtraction over data already present, zero new writes); HOOK REACHABILITY (mirrors the hook's own resolution precedence — env WARPLINE_BIN override, then the BAKED install-time binary parsed back out of the hook via parseBakedBinary, then a bare `warpline` on PATH, then the dist fallback — and reports WHICH ARM WINS OR NONE. `hook status` only knows the block is present; installed and reachable are different facts. Since the baking fix (T-2026-08-12-002 item 4) a cold-agent hook that baked an absolute `node /abs/cli.js` resolves via the 'baked' arm — health reports that, instead of false-alarming 'none' just because `warpline` is off PATH; 'none' now means the baked binary is GONE and no fallback resolves, still UNSOUND/exit 2); ADJUDICATION (verdicts by status, and how many were MEASURED AGAINST GIT — see #git-counterfactual); DISK (total AND MB PER STRAND, because a team can multiply a per-strand number and a total is abstract). THREE BUCKETS, NEVER TWO: the counterfactual census separates measured / explicitly-unavailable / predates-the-field. Collapsing the third is the C-9 mistake, and the 43 live rows are ALL in it. BOTH WRITERS, NEVER ONE (T-2026-08-11): `contested` sums the shadow rows (#shadow, observe-only) AND the payloads persisted under .warpline/knots/ by the SEAL paths (#admit admit.ts, native.ts) — reported split as contestedShadow / contestedRecorded. It previously read shadow rows alone, so every KNOT the NATIVE path produced was invisible: a fresh repo driven fork -> propose -> admit to a real KNOT, payload hydrated on disk, still reported "this project has produced ZERO contested verdicts". The two populations are disjoint by construction (a --shadow run deliberately persists no payload, admit.ts:1047), so the sum cannot double-count, and the count comes from listKnotPayloads — the SAME reader `warpline knot` uses — so the surfaces cannot drift apart. An instrument that reads one of two writers reports the FAVOURABLE answer about its own emptiness; this is the merge-tree exit-1 symmetry lesson in a second location. IT WRITES NOTHING — no traceCli row, no WarpStore disk cache, no lock; the tolerant scanFabric rather than the throwing readFabric, so a torn tail (C-13) is REPORTED and exits 2 instead of bricking the diagnostic. C-13 was found on a full disk, where a diagnostic that writes is one you cannot run. Pinned by a before/after byte digest of .warpline in test/warpline-health.test.ts. HOOK-STATE TOTALITY: the state space is a switch, not an if-chain. The earlier chain ended on a conjunct that could never fire, and a dead condition inside the one check whose job is catching a SILENT failure is the same defect class as the failure itself. EXIT: 0 green · 1 warnings (sound, but unmeasured or unreachable) · 2 unsound (verify failed, ledger torn, a tip naming nothing, or an installed hook resolving to nothing). Green is REACHABLE and tested, so "warnings" is a finding about the project, not a property of the verb. ROOT PROVENANCE (T-2026-08-10): the report carries `rootResolution` — WHICH arm of #warpline-root's precedence chain chose this fabric, whether that arm was EXPLICIT, the git toplevel of the resolved root, and any enclosing directory that also holds a .warpline/. The path alone was not enough: "--root took" and "it fell through to the git root, which happens to be correct today" printed identically, and only the second is D-7. One terse line under the header ("root via --root (explicit)"), and a field in --json. TWO WARNINGS, DELIBERATELY NARROW: (1) the cwd arm — with no override the root IS repoRoot() by construction, so "not the toplevel and not overridden" reduces exactly to "git could not answer", the one arm where nothing chose the fabric; (2) a fabric NESTED inside another fabric, the concrete form of the hazard #warpline-root's header names, warned even when today's resolution is right because the hazard is the NEXT unqualified invocation. NOT warned: an explicit root that merely differs from the git toplevel, and the mere use of $WARPLINE_ROOT — both are the tool working as designed, and warning on the intended path is how a diagnostic teaches people to ignore it (pinned by an anti-noise case in test/root-provenance.test.ts).

native-write-path.name: Native Write Path
native-write-path.description: PHASE 0 of NATIVE-FIRST (arky-architecture.md §2.1 — THE KEYSTONE; ratified D2): the worktree→pick→admit loop with NO git anywhere, T-030's successor. fork mints the agent's scratch ref at the selvage PICKID (I9; optional restore into the agent worktree); **propose SEALS a v3 SCRATCH STRAND from the worktree** — snapshotDir (native walk, I5-INDEXED: the .warpline/index stat cache rehashes only changed files, so a warm propose walk on this monorepo costs ~1s not 7s) → absorbTree (restore from the store → lens, I2: sealed meaning provably corresponds to snapshotted bytes) → buildStrandV3 (bind-on-seal, parents=[scratch base], claim attached via sidecar, provenance git-null per I4) — advancing ONLY the scratch ref: proposals are durable, addressable, exchangeable BEFORE judgment; admit weaves scratch-tip × selvage through the EXISTING decision engine (admitDecision + claim gate + trust floor verbatim), materializes via materializeMergedStateNative ONLY (pure object-store 3-way; no git merge machinery on this path), seals the v3 weave (parents=[selvageTip, scratchTip], recipe folded into the pickId) with per-ref CAS on refs/heads/selvage, and on CLEAN RESTORES the merged bytes back into the agent worktree (§2.1 step 5 — the agent continues from merged reality; no commit ever existed). FAST_ADMIT is a selvage FAST-FORWARD to the scratch strand (a v3 admission is a ref advance, not a re-seal). KNOT/DANGLE persist the #knot-payload (both sides' treeIds native) and refuse — the scratch ref keeps the durable work; resolveNative seals the council resolution as a v3 weave carrying KnotResolution. SEAL-TIME SIGNING (M3-lite I3): all three v3 seal sites (propose scratch strand, admit weave, resolve council weave) route the built strand through #seal signStrandForSeal before appendStrand — this path does NOT flow through sealState, so the shared helper is wired here explicitly; post-boundary agent-class seals carry strandSig:v1 and an unresolvable key refuses (refusal:v1 AUTH → key.mint escalation), surfacing through the daemon error frame unchanged. EVERY refusing verdict (KNOT / DANGLE / CLAIM-BREACH / HELD, incl. the byte-conflict downgrade) carries the SAME #refusal object as the git-era gate, built by the shared exported builders with native-path ladders ({native:'true'}) — T-2026-07-21-007: this is the path agents actually use, and a refusing native verdict without the F4 carrier made cold-agent recovery impossible exactly where it matters most. PW-2 SEQUENCING REFUSALS (mcp-skin-spec §4, pinned site table): every prerequisite boundary throws RefusedError with a typed ladder instead of prose — legacy fabric → UNSUPPORTED/ refs.migrate(human); legacy stateId scratch → UNSUPPORTED/retry-corrected/ fork; admit-without-propose (THE cold mistake) → BAD_REQUEST/ retry-corrected/[fork, propose]; FORKED-BUT-NEVER-PROPOSED (T-2026-08-11, the other half of that same mistake and the half the scratch-ref check CANNOT catch, because `fork` mints a VALID pickId and the call sails past it) → BAD_REQUEST/retry-corrected/[propose]. Before this it fell through to the "already selvage history" NOOP and reported "the agent changed no meaning" — false, and the expensive kind of false: the work is real and merely unsealed, so the agent is told its edits were empty. A proposal strand is sealed THROUGH the scratch ref and carries it as provenance.ref (refs/scratch/<agentId>); a fork base carries whatever sealed it (WORKTREE, a git ref, refs/heads/selvage) — so the discriminator is EXACT, not heuristic. disjoint DAG → INTEGRITY_BROKEN/escalate; resolve-no-selvage → NOT_FOUND/never; resolve-no-scratch → NOT_FOUND/ retry-corrected/propose. PW-10 FORK CLOBBER GUARD: re-fork over a sealed, unadmitted proposal refuses (BAD_REQUEST/retry-corrected) via CAS #scratch writes — before this, same-principal concurrent sessions silently orphaned each other's proposals. D-6b (F4 instrument panel, 2026-07-31): that guard's ladder is no longer a hardcoded [admit]. The guard fires in TWO positions, and after a KNOT (scratch still holds the sealed proposal, the selvage has moved) `admit` is the exact identical-repeat #f4-classifier scores W1 — while #warplined's status answered the SAME position with knot.show and "resolution is human-class, escalate rather than retry". Two carriers, one position, opposite instructions: the same misdirection the FG-3 review removed from status, surviving one carrier over. The ladder is now DERIVED — the position is computed exactly as the daemon's status handler computes it (a persisted #knot-payload naming this principal's CURRENT sealed proposal by (agentId, stateId)) and resolved through the SAME hashed NEXT_LEGAL_VERBS table, with params/requires read off the verb's own descriptor so a knot.show step carries its payload selector. The two answers cannot diverge again: one rule moves both, and moves descriptorsId with them. The human sentence follows the same carrier, so there is no third instruction. Best-effort: the ladder degrades to the unKNOTted position rather than throwing on the way to reporting a refusal. Asserted site-by-site (BOTH positions) in test/native-sequencing-refusals.test.ts. C-10 THE AGENT-CLASS EXIT (soundness audit 2026-07-31, Arky D-D — reproduced organically during stress, not merely reasoned about): abandonNative WITHDRAWS an agent's scratch, and it exists because every agent-class door could be shut at once. After a KNOT — or after a crash between the weave's ref advance and clearScratch — `admit` answers NOOP without clearing the scratch and `fork` refuses with the clobber guard pointing straight back at `admit`: a closed cycle whose only escape, `resolve`, is HUMAN_ONLY. The guard's own prose even named `abandon` as the way out and NO SUCH VERB EXISTED. git has always had `git merge --abort`, always agent-runnable; without this an all-agent swarm halts on its first genuine conflict, which is the exact scenario the product exists to serve. TWO DESIGN CHOICES, both load-bearing: (1) SEALED WORK IS NEVER LOST — only the scratch POINTER is cleared. The strand stays in the append-only ledger, its state in the store, its bytes in the object store, and it stays restorable by pickId forever (`warpline restore pick:<id>`). #fabric-verify's abandonedHeads report is UNCHANGED by construction: it is computed from DAG heads no refs/heads entry names, and listRefs reads refs/heads ONLY, so a scratch ref never suppressed the report and clearing one cannot alter it. Legal, visible, recoverable. (2) AN OPEN KNOT STAYS OPEN — the #knot-payload sidecar is not deleted, not mutated, not marked resolved; the OTHER side (the selvage) does not move; no weave is sealed and no KnotResolution envelope is written. Abandoning CONCEDES a contest; a human still owns resolving it, and the still-open payload ids ride back in the result so the withdrawal is legible rather than silent. IDEMPOTENT (no scratch is not an error) and SCOPED TO THE CALLER (the daemon verb takes no target param, so it can never reach across principals). The exit is also OFFERED: NEXT_LEGAL_VERBS now names it SECOND in both wedge positions (knot.show→abandon, admit→abandon), which moves descriptorsId — see #warplined-descriptors. Proved in test/abandon-exit.test.ts. Every step is an append or a CAS. SCOPE: v3 writes for scratch strands + native weaves only — the git-era seal path stays v2 until the founder-visible cutover (no selvage cutover here). EXIT PROOF: test/native-loop-no-git.test.ts — the full fork→propose→admit→KNOT→resolve→restore loop green in a directory with no `.git` at all (I12), pure-v3 DAG authenticated by fabric verify. M2.5 SPINE REFACTOR (increment 3, TD-2026-08-12-813, Arky's design): admitNative no longer hardcodes `selvage`. It RESOLVES base+ours+theirs+ target then hands the seal to weaveTips — an INTERNAL shared core (no CLI/ principal surface yet) that both admit and the coming increment-4 `merge` verb call, running EXACTLY the current steps in the current order (admitDecision → claim gate → trust floor → hazard advisory → materialize → byte-conflict downgrade/persistContested → seal weave buildStrandV3 multi-parent → advance the TARGET ref → knot payload → refusal carrier). The TARGET branch is the CURRENT one: opts.onto ?? HEAD (readHead) ?? selvage — an ABSENT HEAD (every fabric that never branched) resolves to selvage, so the default path is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the old hardcoded target; a DETACHED HEAD names no branch and fails closed (BAD_REQUEST/retry-corrected/[admit needs onto]). THE COMPATIBILITY SPINE: the legacy stateId `selvage` pointer (#fabric writeSelvage) is a lockstep pointer that exists ONLY for selvage, so EVERY writeSelvage call is now conditional — `if (targetBranch === selvage)` — keeping the default byte-identical and named branches refs-only (they advance refs/heads/<name> alone, never the legacy pointer, and never move selvage). Pinned in test/admit-onto-branch.test.ts. THE PROTECTED-BRANCH LANDING GATE (#protected, M2.5 security TD-2026-08-12-813 — Aegis's finding): once the targetBranch is resolved, an AGENT-class admit ONTO a PROTECTED branch is REFUSED (FORBIDDEN/never, next[] naming the human path) via protectedLandingRefusal — an agent lands onto feature branches, never directly onto the protected integration line; the ref never moves. The gate engages ONLY once branching is in use (>1 named line), so the single-line world and every human/absent-principal caller are byte-identical (the opts.principal default is human). Pinned in test/protected-branch.test.ts.

warplined.name: Warplined
warplined.description: PHASE 1 of NATIVE-FIRST (arky-architecture.md §1.1; roadmap PHASE 1): the solo daemon — THE FABRIC WITH A NETWORK FACE. No database beside it: every verb calls the SAME engine function the CLI calls, in-process, under the SAME #fabric-lock (G4 — no other mutation path). Transport: NDJSON over a unix domain socket (.warpline/daemon.sock, mode 0600 — Aegis stage-1 trust boundary is the OS user; loopback TCP is a later opt-in flag). One JSON line = one frame; envelope {rpc:'warplined:v1', id, verb, token, params} → {id, ok, result|error}; `result` is the ENGINE SHAPE VERBATIM (G3: AdmitResult, knotPayload:v1, GradeReport, shadowVerdict:v1, StakeResult). ONE ERROR VOCABULARY (SP2, TD-2026-07-21-766): RpcErrorCode is COLLAPSED into #refusal's RefusalCode (the daemon's six codes were already a strict subset — a pure widening, collapsed BEFORE any MCP tool schema could freeze the duplicate), and every error frame additionally carries the refusal:v1 object itself (error.refusal, built at the single response boundary so no failure site can forget it) — a cold agent on this skin branches on code/gate/retriable enums, never message prose; DaemonRpcError passes it through typed. Verdict-class codes (GATE_REFUSED/CLAIM_BREACH/TRUST_HELD/STALE_BASE) arrive INSIDE engine results (AdmitResult.refusal), never as transport errors. MCP PRE-WORK (mcp-skin-spec §4): the boundary detects engine-thrown RefusedError and emits its carried refusal verbatim (PW-2); the AUTH refusal carries the mint escalation ladder (PW-3c: daemon.token.mint, principal human); `status` is STATE-AWARE (PW-6, additive — the RELOCATED F4 carrier since hosts truncate tool descriptions): cycle with stages, the caller's position (scratchPresent/scratchIsPickId/proposalSealed/ behindSelvage/knotOpen), nextLegalVerbs + nextBecause, the verb→tool map, and the static untrusted-content sentence. The next-verb answer is resolved from #warplined-descriptors' declarative table (so it rides descriptorsId), and knotOpen — a persisted KNOT work order naming THIS principal's CURRENT sealed proposal, keyed on stateId so re-proposing clears it — routes a contested agent to knot.show. FG-3 review finding (2026-07-28, fixed): the carrier previously answered 'admit' after a KNOT, contradicting the refusal's own ladder and steering the agent into the identical re-admit the #f4-classifier scores W1 — costly because the classifier grants exactly ONE orientation call per recovery episode. Regression: test/status-carrier.test.ts; `knot.show` takes summary:true (PW-7 — payload minus file bodies, summary marker honest); the audit row gains resultCode (PW-8 — a verdict-class refusal inside an ok result is audited, not masked; same derivation as exitCodeForResult; #f4-trace, not the audit, is F4 ground truth). C-16: resultCode is now derived via #refusal's refusalOf, which knows BOTH depths — the outer-only probe saw nothing on the SHADOW path ({shadow, row, result} nests the engine shape one level down), so a shadow CLAIM_BREACH audited as a clean ok row. `ok` is unchanged and still means "the dispatch produced a result": a verdict-class refusal is an ok row CARRYING a resultCode, on the shadow path exactly as on the direct one. Teaching text is single-sourced from #warplined-descriptors; MCP token custody (PW-9) = mint --mcp persists the token KEYED BY AGENT in .warpline/daemon/mcp-tokens.json (0600, so N agents coexist — no clobber) and mcpAgentToken() reads ONLY env WARPLINE_MCP_TOKEN, then env WARPLINE_MCP_AGENT (name selector), then the keyed store (single-entry), then the legacy mcp.token file — never daemon-tokens.jsonl. Verbs (1:1 onto engine fns — transport + identity, never logic): status, refs.list, branch, switch, fork, propose, admit (native, incl. the R1 shadow flag), merge, knot.show, resolve, stake, stake.recover, grade.report, shadow.tail, backup (#warpline-backup — snapshot to a dest dir, the one write that lands OUTSIDE .warpline/). M2.5 SKINS (increment 7, TD-2026-08-12-813): the #branch model's three verbs join the surface. `branch` multiplexes create|list|delete (agent) + protect|unprotect|list-protected — protect/unprotect are HUMAN-class OPS of the agent-class verb, refused for an agent-class principal by HUMAN_ONLY_BRANCH_OPS (verb×op, mirroring admit's verb×flag override gate); `switch` (#branch switchBranch) and `merge` (#merge mergeBranch) are agent-class, `merge`'s `confirm`→acceptMeaningBlind override being human-only (HUMAN_ONLY_MERGE_FLAGS, off the descriptor schema like the admit flags). THE DAEMON-SIDE PROTECTED-BRANCH LANDING GATE — the increment-5 deferral (it noted server.ts was out of its scope) is now CLOSED: the admit and merge dispatch pass principal=who.kind into #native-write-path / #merge, so #protected protectedLandingRefusal refuses an agent-class admit/merge that would LAND onto a protected branch (once branching is in use) with the same FORBIDDEN refusal (retriable 'never', escalate) the CLI gate emits; human tokens and the single-line world pass byte-identical. The three verbs auto-register on the MCP surface (all agent-class) via #warplined-descriptors, so warpline_branch/switch/merge need no bespoke MCP code. Adding them MOVED descriptorsId (the FG-3 teaching freeze): descriptors:v1:0bb2c860… → descriptors:v1:6e86dce8… (test/descriptors-frozen.test.ts). STAGE-1 IDENTITY (aegis-security.md §1.2): every request carries a bearer token (#warplined-tokens); the daemon SERVER-STAMPS actor/agentId/decidedBy from the resolved principal — client-supplied identity params are advisory and ignored. The verb×principal matrix (§2.2): resolve / stake / stake.recover / backup and the accept-breach / accept-risk override flags are HUMAN-CLASS ONLY (an agent never accepts its own breach); engine-side override records (claim evaluations, grade escalations) are reused, not duplicated. READ-SCOPE CEILING (PHASE 1 close-out, console lane): a scope:'read' token (#warplined-tokens) is capped at READ_ONLY_VERBS (status, refs.list, knot.show, grade.report, shadow.tail) — checked structurally BEFORE dispatch, so even a human-class read token holds no write capability. Chosen over tokenless local-socket reads: stage 1 says no anonymous reads (sidecars are trust data), so the console stays tokened + stamped + audited, just least-privilege. EVERY call appends a daemonAudit:v1 row — .warpline/daemon/audit.jsonl {ts, principal, kind, verb, target, ok, code} including refusals; targets are STRUCTURAL (selectors/paths/flags), never prose (§4.1: log the address, never the body). LIFECYCLE: exactly one daemon per fabric — O_EXCL pidfile lock (.warpline/daemon.pid), live-pid probe refuses a second start, dead-pid/orphaned-socket residue recovered on start, SIGTERM stops clean (socket+pidfile unlinked). CLI: `warpline daemon start|stop|status|token mint|token list|call`. BYTE-IDENTITY PROOF (Loid R4, pulled early): test/daemon-byte-identity.test.ts — the same fixture loop (genesis FF, edit FF, CLEAN WEAVE) in-process vs through the socket produces byte-identical results modulo the envelope. NEVER started against this repo's live fabric by tests — fixtures only. AUTO-RESOLVE GRANTS (M3-lite I6): the verb×principal matrix now carries ONE exception INSIDE the gate — agent + verb 'resolve' + an ACTIVE #grants row (activeGrantFor) is allowed through, with the grantId threaded via dispatch (NEVER a client param) so the resolution seal records underGrant; every other human-only verb refuses regardless, and with no active grant the refusal is byte-identical to before (pinned by test/m3-falsifier.test.ts). 'resolve' STAYS in HUMAN_ONLY_VERBS — the frozen descriptor invariants do not move.

warplined-tokens.name: Warplined Tokens
warplined-tokens.description: Aegis stage-1 identity for #warplined: per-principal bearer tokens in .warpline/daemon-tokens.jsonl (append-only daemonToken:v1 rows {token, principal, kind:'human'|'agent', createdAt, scope?}; file mode 0600; gitignored via .warpline/*; the filename is ALSO on the frozen stake deny-list — never leaves the box twice over; #warpline-backup excludes it from snapshots for the same reason). Minting is LOCAL-CLI-ONLY (`warpline daemon token mint <name> --kind human|agent [--scope read]`) — the human's act, gated by possession of the box; no self-service daemon verb exists (anti-sockpuppet, §2.2). SCOPE (additive, G1): absent = full surface for the kind; 'read' = the CONSOLE class, capped server-side at READ_ONLY_VERBS; an UNKNOWN scope fails closed (the row is skipped, never resolved full-power). consoleReadToken() is the platform router's discovery hook — it surfaces ONLY the newest console+read row, so the console structurally never holds a full-power token. resolveToken does constant-time comparison and fails CLOSED (garbled rows never match); `token list` is redacted (tokens are shown exactly once, at mint). Honest trust claim: attribution is authentic within this machine's OS-user boundary; the daemon is the trusted stamper — per-strand signatures remain M3. MCP TOKEN CUSTODY (PW-9, mcp-skin-spec D2/R5): `token mint <name> --kind agent --mcp` additionally persists the bare token KEYED BY AGENT in .warpline/daemon/mcp-tokens.json ({agentId:token}, 0600; read-merge-write so a second agent's mint COEXISTS with the first — the #1 multi-instance trap fixed: single-value → keyed; --mcp refuses non-agent kinds — an ambient MCP process must never hold human capability); mcpAgentToken() mirrors the consoleReadToken structural pattern — env WARPLINE_MCP_TOKEN (raw token, the per-instance mechanism for N concurrent instances), then env WARPLINE_MCP_AGENT (name selector; fails CLOSED if the named agent is absent — never picks another), then the keyed store when it holds exactly one entry, then the legacy mcp.token file (back-compat), NEVER daemon-tokens.jsonl (it holds human tokens; one "newest row" bug there is a privilege escalation). A multi-agent store with no selector fails closed (AUTH refusal) rather than guess an identity. No revocation ceremony at stage 1 — rotation = mint anew (documented in the mint help).

keys.name: Keys
keys.description: M3-lite I1+I2 (m3-integrity-design-2026-08-23.md §6 founder rulings, TD-2026-08-23-136): Ed25519 agent signing keys for the strand-signature epoch — node:crypto only, NO external deps, NO passphrase/scrypt/AES, NO root key, NO git key witness; the human boundary stays PROCEDURAL (HUMAN_ONLY_VERBS + tool-permission denies incl. .warpline/keys/** reads). keyId = 'wlkey:v1:' + sha256 over the EXACT public-key PEM bytes node exports (trailing newline trimmed — the same normalized string the key file and registry store, so id and material cannot disagree). Signature primitive (consumed by seal-time signing at I3): domain-separated over the pickId — Ed25519(key, 'warpline:strand-sig:v1\n' + pickId), base64; verifyPickIdSig NEVER throws on malformed input (false, fail closed). CUSTODY mirrors #warplined-tokens: private half in .warpline/keys/agents/<principal>.key (agentKey:v1 JSON, file 0600, dirs 0700, gitignored via .warpline/*); principal names pass the #fabric-refs path-segment grammar (spliced into a filesystem path — traversal refused fail-closed). loadAgentKey is FAIL-CLOSED (missing/garbled/wrong-schema/ swapped-principal → null, never a throw a caller might soften); loadAgentKeyStrict throws precise messages for CLI surfaces. REGISTRY (.warpline/keys/registry.jsonl, append-only keyRegistry:v1 rows, PUBLIC material only): 'agent-key' rows re-mint by APPEND, latest row wins (token re-mint semantics); readKeyRegistry skips malformed rows AND surfaces them in a diagnostics list (a garbled row must never resolve to a usable key, and never invisibly). ONE 'signed-from' row pins the signing-epoch boundary — the fabric tip pickId at FIRST mint (read the way seal.ts reads the tip: refs/heads/selvage, legacy ledger tail fallback; null = pinned at genesis on an empty fabric, distinguished from unpinned by hasSignedFrom). The FIRST row is authoritative forever, later signed-from rows IGNORED — a movable boundary would let anyone un-sign history. CLI: `warpline key mint <principal>` is HUMAN-class, gated in the command with the #agent-shell credential ($WARPLINE_AGENT_ID → FORBIDDEN refusal:v1, the `branch --protect` precedent) because key.mint is deliberately NOT a daemon verb (no self-service minting surface — anti-sockpuppet) and HUMAN_ONLY_VERBS is frozen to daemon verbs by descriptors-frozen + agent-shell-gate invariants; `warpline key list` stays agent-readable (public material only; flags rows whose private key file is gone). Strands at-or-before the signed-from boundary stay valid unsigned PERMANENTLY (grandfathered, the v1-anchor shape); seals after it REQUIRE signatures now that I3 is live (#seal signStrandForSeal signs agent-class seals and refuses on an unresolvable key; #fabric-verify enforces the sig-* rules at I4).

grants.name: Grants
grants.description: M3-lite I6+I7 (m3-integrity-design-2026-08-23.md §6 Q3 ruling, TD-2026-08-23-136 item 4): HUMAN-ISSUED auto-resolve grants — a scoped, expiring, revocable exception INSIDE the resolve gate. `resolve` STAYS in HUMAN_ONLY_VERBS (the frozen descriptor invariants never move; the grant is an exception inside the gate, not a re-classification), and grants cover RESOLVE ONLY — stake/stake.recover/backup refuse regardless. The grant is PROCEDURALLY bound (by ruling NO cryptographic human signature exists): issue/revoke are console/CLI human-class acts gated exactly like `key mint` (the #agent-shell credential); `grant list` is agent-readable. STORE .warpline/grants/auto-resolve.jsonl — append-only grant:v1 rows, strict union {kind:'grant'|'revoke'}, reader fail-closed per row (#keys registry pattern: malformed rows skipped AND surfaced). grantId = 'grant:' + sha256 over the canonical row body and is RECOMPUTED on read — a row whose id does not reproduce from its own body (tampered scope/ttl) loses its authority. TTL: expiresAt REQUIRED (no unbounded grants), default 24h, hard cap 7d, expiry STRICT (dead at the boundary instant). MATCHING (activeGrantFor — every miss fails closed): revoke WINS over any later re-read; branch scope exact-or-absent; scope.knotClass 'over-block-suspect' NEVER matches (the gate cannot classify the knot at enforcement time — a scope it cannot check does not match; 'any'/absent matches). ENFORCEMENT lives at the TWO gates, which alone know the ACTING principal (the DISCRIMINATOR CORRECTION, Build B deviation 3: a resolve strand's authoredBy.agentId names the CONTESTED agent even when a human acts, so authorship can never discriminate who acted): the daemon verb×principal matrix (#warplined server.ts — agent + 'resolve' + active grant → allowed, grantId threaded through dispatch, NEVER a client param) and the CLI's gateHumanClass (#agent-shell marker + active grant → allowed, grantId returned to the resolve action). On allow the resolution seal records `underGrant: grantId` — INSIDE the pickId preimage in BOTH epochs (attribution-load-bearing: v2 rides the `...rest` spread, the explicit v3 preimage lists it conditionally, absent = absent so old identities hold), and buildStrandV3 refuses underGrant without resolves. VERIFY/FSCK (#fabric-verify 'grant-violation'): a resolves-strand WITH underGrant is checked — the named grant must have been active (issued/unexpired/unrevoked-at-recordedAt, scope-matched) at seal time; an underGrant on a non-resolve strand is itself a violation. A resolves-strand WITHOUT underGrant is PRESUMED human-resolved — the procedural boundary cannot cryptographically distinguish it, residue ACCEPTED by ruling, no check invented. DEFAULT OFF (v2 §A11): a zero-grant repo never even reads the store and every no-grant refusal is byte-identical to pre-M3 (pinned by test/m3-falsifier.test.ts arm 6; the full six-arm falsifier is the field-test precondition, with unit coverage in test/m3-grants.test.ts).

warplined-descriptors.name: Warplined Descriptors
warplined-descriptors.description: The CANONICAL verb descriptors (PW-5, mcp-skin-spec §4; Loid requirement 3): ONE source of teaching text per daemon verb — {verb, summary (1-2 sentence HARD budget), paramsSchema, cycleStage (orient|fork|propose|admit|abandon|inspect|resolve|custody), principal (agent|human)} — consumed by the MCP tool registration and #warplined's state-aware status, so skins cannot drift into parallel vocabularies (G3 applied to teaching text). toolNameOf() is the ONE naming law between dotted daemon verbs and MCP tool names (knot.show → warpline_knot_show); wire shapes and refusal.next[].verb keep the dotted names verbatim. agentSurfaceVerbs() derives the default MCP surface = every principal:'agent' descriptor (human verbs OMITTED per Aegis R2). ALSO owns NEXT_LEGAL_VERBS + nextLegalVerbsFor() — the directive rule the #warplined status result carries, declared as DATA (first-match-wins over CyclePosition {scratchPresent, proposalSealed, behindSelvage, knotOpen}, each rule carrying a one-clause `because`). It lived as an inline conditional in the daemon's status handler until the FG-3 review (2026-07-28) moved it here for two reasons: it is the single most DIRECTIVE thing Warpline says to a cold agent, and as code it sat OUTSIDE the content address. The WHOLE TEACHING SURFACE is now CONTENT-ADDRESSED (descriptorsId, sha256 of canonical serialization over the verb table + the next-verb rule + the DERIVED tool-name map, so a change to toolNameOf's law also moves the id) — the FG-3 pre-registration anchor stamped into every #f4-trace row: T-005 pins it before the first scored F4 batch, ANY change resets the ≥10-run denominator, and test/descriptors-frozen.test.ts is the tripwire that makes a change impossible to miss. Scoping the id to descriptions alone would have pinned the WRONG artifact: PW-6 relocated the F4 carrier from descriptions into the status RESULT because hosts truncate descriptions, so a next-verb-rule edit would have changed what every cold agent is taught while the id — and the denominator — stood still. Carries the static untrusted-content sentence for the prose-carrying tools (admit / knot.show / shadow.tail). SECOND CONSUMER (D-6b, 2026-07-31): #native-write-path's fork-clobber ladder is now DERIVED from nextLegalVerbsFor + the verbs' own paramsSchemas rather than hardcoded, so an engine refusal and the status result can no longer answer one position with opposite instructions — the rule is the single carrier, and it is hashed. C-10 RE-PIN (2026-08-01, descriptors:v1:445e4eb7… → df0550c6…): the agent-class `abandon` verb joined the table, and the next-verb rule now names it SECOND in the two positions that previously DEAD-ENDED — knotOpen ['knot.show','abandon'] and proposalSealed ['admit','abandon']. Both were positions where every offered verb was one an agent could run forever without moving (escalation is human-class; a post-crash `admit` NOOPs while `fork` refuses back to it), so the carrier itself was half the wedge. Ordering is deliberate: the escalation/admission door stays the instruction read FIRST, and the withdrawal door exists so a swarm is never stuck. The id moved because the teaching genuinely changed — the denominator-reset rule applies, and it costs nothing today because FG-3 is unratified and no scored batch has started. Excluding a new verb from the hash to hold the id still would BE defect D-3, inside the test built to catch it. New invariants in test/descriptors-frozen.test.ts: every position offers at least one agent-runnable verb, and the wedge positions name the withdrawal verb specifically (an agent-runnable READ like knot.show satisfies the first check while leaving the position wedged).

f4-trace.name: F4 Trace
f4-trace.description: f4Trace:v1 — the skin's OWN measurement stream and the F4 harness's GROUND TRUTH (mcp-skin-spec §5; Loid requirement 2 — daemonAudit:v1 was REJECTED for the job: audit(true) masks verdict-class refusals riding inside ok results, rows carry no runId, and the wasted-turn classifier needs the prior refusal's enums). One row per tool/CLI call appended to .warpline/f4/trace.jsonl: {schemaVersion, ts, runId ($WARPLINE_F4_RUN_ID, 'unscored' outside a harness run — rows always emit), seq (per-RUN ordinal), skin:'mcp'|'cli', principal, verb (dotted daemon name), target (structural only — selectors/flags, NEVER prose), ok, refusal? (the refusal:v1 VERBATIM, captured from error frames AND result.refusal), resultClass? (structural: sealed | decision.status | noop | read), descriptorsId (which teaching text served the call — FG-3)}. F4Tracer is the emitting handle (fixes identity; append is BEST-EFFORT — a trace failure never fails the serving call); resultClassOf derives the class from result SHAPE, never text. resultClassOf knows TWO DEPTHS, exactly as #refusal's refusalOf does and for the same reason (soundness audit 2026-07-31, MEDIUM): the shadow gate answers an ENVELOPE, {shadow, row, result}, so a probe reading only the outer object found no decision and recorded resultClass:'read' for every shadow KNOT / CLEAN / HELD / FAST_ADMIT there has ever been — not masking (C-16 closed the refusal half) but it made SHADOW rows strictly LESS classifiable than direct ones, and the shadow verdict stream is the evidence base for the R2 gate-promotion argument. Bounded at ONE envelope level, like refusalOf: a deep search would find decisions that are not the caller's own outcome (an archived verdict inside a knot payload, a tail of shadow rows). The class is recorded UNPREFIXED because the arm is already recoverable from the row — `shadow` rides in target — so the classifier's status vocabulary does not fork per skin. Pinned by test/f4-trace-shadow-class.test.ts. seq is SEEDED from the trace file (nextSeqFor: max(seq)+1 for the runId), not counted from zero per process: the MCP skin is one long-lived process per run but the CLI is one process PER COMMAND, and a process-local counter would stamp every CLI row seq:0 — unorderable for a classifier that sorts by seq. Ordering assumes a SERIAL arm (what F4 measures). The W1-W4 wasted-turn taxonomy is the HARNESS's pure classifier over these rows — this module only emits faithfully.

f4-cli-trace.name: F4 Cli Trace
f4-cli-trace.description: The CLI SKIN's emission side of #f4-trace (src/f4/cli-trace.ts) — the F4 bar scores BOTH skins independently and cli.ts emitted NO rows at all until this landed, so the CLI arm was structurally unmeasurable. traceCli wraps a command body: one row per call, ok with the result's structural class and any result-borne refusal, not-ok on a throw (RefusedError contributes its refusal:v1; a plain Error contributes NONE — the honest record of a cold agent handed prose instead of a machine-readable refusal, the residue T-2026-07-21-003 still tracks). ONE SHAPE, THREE SKINS: rows name the DAEMON VERB, never the commander path, so the classifier stays arm-agnostic — `warpline admit --native` and the warpline_admit tool are the same verb through different skins (all three admit engine paths emit verb 'admit'; the distinguishing flags ride target). CLI-only commands emit under a `cli:` prefix rather than being folded into a verb they are not — `warpline status` is 'cli:status' (the MEANING DIFF; the daemon's `status` is cycle-position + next legal verbs, a different thing, and conflating them would hand the classifier's orientation allowance to a call that teaches nothing about what to do next). cliTarget enforces the targetOf discipline; PROSE (--intent/-m, the inline --claim BODY) never reaches it. PRINCIPAL on this arm is SELF-ASSERTED (the native CLI verbs run in-process with no token, unlike the MCP skin's daemon-stamped token principal) — honest for measurement, never attribution. KNOWN ARM ASYMMETRIES, surfaced not papered over: daemon `status` (the D4 load-bearing self-description carrier) and `shadow.tail` have NO CLI equivalent, and CLI `propose` REQUIRES --claim where the daemon's claim param is optional. Closing any of them changes #warplined-descriptors and therefore resets the FG-3 denominator — so they are founder decisions, not wiring. Proven over the real binary in test/f4-cli-arm.test.ts (six separate processes, one continuous seq). TRACES `resolve` (pre-freeze panel D-4): it was the one verb the CLI never traced, and it is the human-class verb whose ATTEMPT is the W3 the FG-1 criterion turns on — untraced, a CLI subject could perform it, succeed, emit nothing, and satisfy all three predicates. SUPERSEDED 2026-08-01 (audit C-11): this entry said tracing was MEASUREMENT and not enforcement, because "the native CLI has no token and no principal gate, so HUMAN_ONLY_VERBS is a DAEMON-BOUNDARY law rather than a Warpline-wide one" and CLI-side enforcement was an open founder decision. That decision is taken — see #agent-shell. Both now hold on this arm, and the ORDER between them is load-bearing: the gate emits its trace row BEFORE the refusal propagates, so refusing the violation does not re-blind the W3 rule that tracing was added to un-blind. CORRECTED: an earlier revision claimed closing the CLI asymmetries moves descriptorsId. It does not — projecting the existing daemon status result through a CLI command, adding `shadow tail`, and making --claim optional touch none of the three hashed inputs. They were escalated as expensive on a false premise. C-16, THE LAST SITE (2026-08-01): this module carried its OWN local refusalOf testing `'refusal' in result` on the OUTER object — the identical defect Jinx J-12 found on the daemon and MCP probes, surviving here after the shared accessor landed. A shadow-enveloped refusal ({shadow,row,result:{refusal}}) emitted `refusal: undefined`, and since this is one of F4's two SCORED surfaces that is a row the wasted-turn classifier cannot score. It now routes through #refusal's refusalOf, which knows both depths AND shape-checks with isRefusal (the local copy returned whatever sat under `refusal`, so an unversioned look-alike became a verdict). No local re-derivation of the accessor remains in the package.

warpline-mcp.name: Warpline Mcp
warpline-mcp.description: THE THIRD SKIN (T-2026-07-21-004, mcp-skin-spec §1-§3): the daemon verb surface as MCP tools over stdio (`warpline mcp [--operator] [--no-auto-start]`), for agents that call tools rather than shells. DELIBERATELY THIN — a credential PASS-THROUGH, never a principal (D2): one process holds one human-minted agent-class token (env WARPLINE_MCP_TOKEN → WARPLINE_MCP_AGENT selector → keyed .warpline/daemon/mcp-tokens.json → legacy mcp.token, via the single custody seam src/mcp/token.ts — so N concurrent instances each present their own token); the daemon server-stamps identity; args are FILTERED to each verb's declared schema properties so identity/clock params structurally never reach the wire. SOCKET-ONLY (D3): every call rides DaemonClient — in-process engine imports are PROHIBITED in src/mcp/ (the whole stage-1 security layer lives in the daemon path); optional auto-start (spawns the detached daemon, polls the socket); daemon-down and token-missing return the ONLY two skin-built refusals (src/mcp/refusals.ts — UNSUPPORTED + daemon.start ladder, AUTH + the complete mint call), everything else arrives from the wire VERBATIM. Results: one text content item, JSON of the engine shape unchanged (UntrustedProse envelopes intact — Aegis R4). isError CONTRACT (§3, the T-006 lesson): transport failure → true; ok result → exitCodeForResult(result) !== 0 — a refusing verdict NEVER presents as MCP success, INCLUDING a shadow verdict. C-16 (Jinx J-12): the probe here tested `'refusal' in result` on the outer object, so `admit {shadow:true}` — whose answer is the {shadow, row, result} envelope — returned isError:false on a CLAIM_BREACH / TRUST_HELD / KNOT. Both depths now live in ONE accessor (#refusal refusalOf) shared with #warplined's audit probe; two call sites each knowing one depth is exactly how it regressed. Default surface = the 8 agent verbs from #warplined-descriptors (human verbs + override flags OMITTED, Aegis R2); --operator registers human tools IFF status verifies kind:'human' at startup, never speculatively. Emits one #f4-trace row per call (skin 'mcp'), refusals captured from error frames AND result.refusal. W3 OBSERVABILITY (pre-freeze panel D-2, 2026-07-28): an attempt at an OMITTED human-class tool now emits a row BEFORE the unregistered-tool throw, under the verb it meant (demangleToolName), carrying FORBIDDEN — not UNKNOWN_VERB, because the #f4-classifier treats UNKNOWN_VERB as a surface miss judged against its OWN episode and would skip the W3 check entirely. Override flags supplied to admit (acceptBreach/acceptRisk) are recorded in the trace `target` even though paramsSchema omission means they never reach the wire. The DEFENSE is unchanged — the tool stays unregistered (Aegis R2 omission, not expose-then-refuse) and the flags still cannot travel; only the OBSERVATION is new. Without this, FG-1's "zero W3 marks" predicate was a criterion that structurally could not fail. Regression: test/f4-w3-observable.test.ts. Proven end-to-end in test/mcp-skin.test.ts (real daemon + real MCP client over a linked in-memory pair) and by a live stdio smoke (cold no-token call → isError:true + AUTH ladder — the first thing a cold agent hits is now structured). Moat-silent: lives in packages/warpline (unpublished); paradigm-mcp integration was REJECTED (ships to npm).

f4-completion.name: F4 Completion
f4-completion.description: The FG-1 PRIMARY metric as pure code (TD-2026-07-29-259, amending TD-2026-07-28-168). The ≥80% bar in TD-2026-07-21-766 is a bar on COMPLETION, and until this module landed the primary metric had NO implementation — only the secondary wasted-turn metric (#f4-classifier) did. A completion predicate written after runs exist is void by construction, so it lands before the first scored batch. evaluateCompletion(rows) → F4CompletionReport: (1) reachedKnot — an episode opened on a GATE_REFUSED refusal with verdict:'KNOT'; (2) correctDoor — hydration of refusal.pointers.knotPayloadId via a LATER knot.show row, required only when a payload is ADVERTISED (three of four KNOT sites emit none, so an unconditional predicate made the byte-downgrade stratum FG-4 requires a guaranteed incomplete — failing the bar on wording, not on agents); (3) w3Count zero. Reports outcome as escalation | sidestep | incomplete — the split is a COUNT, never a bar: a sidestep (a sealing admit after the KNOT — the agent rewrote to stop contesting instead of escalating) satisfies all three predicates, so before the split it was indistinguishable from an escalation in the numerator. THE FG-3 SCORING GATE (panel finding D-11, 2026-07-31 — the one item the six-panelist board was unanimous on and that is independent of every open scope question): FG-3 says a scored run is served by EXACTLY ONE teaching surface, #f4-classifier had always REPORTED descriptorsIds, and NOTHING asserted it — the pre-registration anchor was a field, not a gate, and the old summarizeBatch(readonly F4CompletionReport[]) would pool runs served by two different teaching surfaces into one completion rate. It is now UNREPRESENTABLE rather than merely discouraged: F4Arm carries a module-private unique-symbol BRAND, so it cannot be constructed outside this module, and summarizeArm(arm) is the only way to a rate — the ungated summarizeBatch is DELETED, not deprecated (an alias beside a gate is how a second carrier survives). partitionArms(reports) is the TOTAL entry point: it reads report.run.descriptorsIds (no upstream signature moved), EXCLUDES a run whose own rows disagree ('mixed-teaching-surface') or that produced no rows ('no-rows'), and SPLITS the rest by id; singleArm(reports) is the assertion form, throwing F4UnscoreableError. Splitting rather than refusing is Loid's correction and it is load-bearing: the invariant is one id per RUN and per ARM, never per batch — FG-2 is a TREATMENT variant of the teaching surface, so an FG-1-vs-FG-2 delta is computed across two descriptorsIds BY CONSTRUCTION and a per-batch rule would reject the analysis FG-2 exists to enable. The gate tests neither against a pinned literal (the FG-3 freeze is unbuilt and unsigned — only INTERNAL divergence is honestly assertable today) nor across any tuple: pre-freeze item 2 (teachingId / scoringId / instrumentId) is an OPEN founder decision and is deliberately NOT pre-empted here. KNOWN GAP, reported not gated: `skin` is not part of the arm key, so two runs on different skins with one teaching id land in ONE arm even though the bar says a pass on one skin is not a pass — F4BatchReport.skins carries the observed set so a cross-skin pool is at least VISIBLE, and widening the key is a one-line founder call. The gate lives at the AGGREGATION boundary precisely so classifyRun and evaluateCompletion stay pure and total: re-scoring the durable row archive after a scorer fix still costs zero runs. Aggregation still decides no pass/fail — the bar's arithmetic (n, confidence interval, per-family conjunction) is a pre-registration item, not a property of the counting code. Shares targetNamesPointer with #f4-classifier so the primary and secondary metrics cannot drift on what "hydrated" means. REPORTED LIMITATION: a sidestepping re-admit does not CLOSE its episode — `target` carries the worktree and flags but not the proposed stateId, so the classifier cannot tell a corrected re-admit from an identical one, marks it W1, and a wasted row is barred from closing. Sidesteppers carry inflated wasted-turn counts and unresolved episodes; the completion predicate keys on the SEAL rather than on closure so the primary metric is unaffected.

f4-classifier.name: F4 Classifier
f4-classifier.description: The WASTED-TURN taxonomy as PURE CODE over #f4-trace rows (T-2026-07-21-005 build side; Loid Q4 design). classifyRun(rows) → F4RunReport: recovery EPISODES (open at any refusal-bearing row; a same-verb+same-code row CONTINUES the incident, never re-opens; close = the same verb completing with a different outcome class AND the row not itself judged wasted — a FORBIDDEN override attempt is not recovery; unresolved episodes reported), wasted marks W1-W4 per episode, the medianWastedPerRecovery gate metric, surfaceMisses (the DESCRIPTION-failure signal), and run-validity fields (distinct skins / descriptorsIds — a valid run has exactly one of each, FG-3; the id half is now ENFORCED downstream by #f4-completion's partitionArms, which excludes a divergent run and refuses to pool runs across surfaces — reported here, gated there, so this stays pure and total). Rules: W1 identical-repeat (retry-identical grants ONE productive repeat; retry-corrected + performed ladder steps exempts the identical retry — the correction WAS the prerequisite calls); W2 next-ignored (allowances: ladder verbs, the retry goal, FIRST hydration per refusal pointer — repeats wasted, one status/refs.list re-orientation per episode); W3 escalation-violation (foreign human-door verb, or acceptBreach/acceptRisk in the target — the refused verb itself is the retry goal, never W3 by verb alone); W4 surface-miss (every BAD_REQUEST/UNKNOWN_VERB call is itself wasted, on its own episode). Every predicate reads ONLY refusal:v1 enums/ids — the classifier doubles as a standing test of the no-prose rule. Pure, no I/O, no clock. Documented limits: rows carry `target` not full params, so W2 follow-through is verb+pointer granularity; judgment is against the NEWEST open episode.

f4-seed.name: F4 Seed
f4-seed.description: The SCRIPTED SECOND PRINCIPAL (T-2026-07-21-005; Jinx trap 6): a single principal cannot produce a KNOT through the verb surface (fork re-mints at the selvage tip; successful admit clears scratch), so the F4 harness seeds contention with a scripted rival driving the SAME engine functions the daemon drives. seedWorld(root) = base file + sealed genesis; rivalAdvance(root) = fork→edit-the-contested-symbol→propose→admit in an ISOLATED rival worktree, called by the runner AFTER the subject's propose (observable via its #f4-trace rows) so the subject's admit meets a moved selvage and KNOTs. MECHANISM ONLY — the pre-registered corpus COMPOSITION (semantic-with-payload / byte-downgrade-without / payload-persist-failure counts + corpus hash) is founder-gate FG-4, never the harness builder's choice. ISOLATION LAW (Shield's ruling): staged KNOTs never feed the organic K3/F2 record — scratch fabrics only; every function demands the fixture root explicitly. Proven end-to-end in test/f4-rig.test.ts: seeded world → scripted subject through the REAL MCP skin (cold mistakes included) → real KNOT with payload → classifier verdict over the real trace — the full measurement pipeline minus only the cold model in the subject's seat.

warplined-client.name: Warplined Client
warplined-client.description: The thin typed client of #warplined (DaemonClient): NDJSON frames over the unix socket, id-correlated (concurrent calls on one connection answer in order), engine shapes deserialized VERBATIM — the client never reshapes (G3). DaemonRpcError carries the machine-readable refusal code (AUTH/FORBIDDEN/BAD_REQUEST/UNKNOWN_VERB/NOT_FOUND/ENGINE); daemonAvailable() is the socket-presence auto-detect hook. This is the seam the platform router / judgment console re-points to in the console lane (not this lane). In-process engine calls remain the CLI default; `warpline daemon call <verb>` is the explicit transport path (token from --token or WARPLINE_DAEMON_TOKEN).

warpline-backup.name: Warpline Backup
warpline-backup.description: PHASE 1 close-out — the custodianship tax's first payment: `warpline backup <dest>` (fabric/backup.ts; also the daemon's HUMAN-CLASS `backup` verb). ATOMIC snapshot of the whole fabric into `<dest>/.warpline/**`: the mutable core (fabric.jsonl ledger, refs, sidecars, stake+daemon audits) copies while HOLDING #fabric-lock (no writer can interleave a half-appended ledger), then the object store copies lock-free (content-addressed, immutable once written, no gc — anything the staged ledger references already existed); everything stages in a sibling temp dir on dest's own volume and ONE rename publishes the backup (a crash never leaves a half-backup). COPY = fs.copyFile COPYFILE_FICLONE — a CoW clone on APFS, a full byte copy elsewhere; NEVER hardlinks (a hardlink shares the inode, so an in-place ledger append or source tamper would mutate the "backup"). EXCLUDED, each named: daemon-tokens.jsonl (SECRETS — D5 never-leaves-the-box), daemon.sock/daemon.pid (live process residue), refs/.lock* (process state); daemon/audit.jsonl INCLUDED (accountability survives a dead disk; structural targets, never prose). EXCLUSION IS MATCHED ON THE FULL RELATIVE PATH (audit C-14, Jinx J-11): the v1 rule fired only at depth 1 (`parts.length === 1`), so it caught daemon-tokens.jsonl and MISSED .warpline/daemon/mcp.token — the MCP bearer token (#warplined-tokens), which was clone-copied into every backup AND hashed into the published manifest while the module header and the CLI help both promised "secrets never travel". Tokens have no expiry and no revocation (stage-1 deferral) and dest is caller-chosen, so a leaked backup was a PERMANENT credential leak. Now: secret-bearing BASENAMES are denied at ANY depth (daemon-tokens.jsonl, mcp.token, mcp-tokens.json — the per-agent MCP token map, whose `.json` suffix the `.token` rule cannot see, so it is named explicitly — session-keys.jsonl — the same name-anywhere rule the frozen STAKE_DENY_NAMES uses), plus the `*.token` SUFFIX class so the next credential sidecar is withheld the day it is written; live-process residue stays anchored to its exact path. POSTURE PRESERVED: this is still a DENY-list — an unregistered sidecar (root or nested) is backed up BY DEFAULT, because custodianship must fail toward preservation and an allow-list would silently drop whatever nobody remembered to register. Regression: test/backup-secret-exclusion.test.ts — the token is absent from tree, manifest and BYTES at every depth (a control marker in a backed-up sidecar proves the byte scan is live), and unknown sidecars still travel. MANIFEST `<dest>/backup.manifest.json` (warplineBackup:v1): per-file bytes + sha256 digested from the STAGED bytes, plus counts {files, objects, ledgerRows, refs}; lives BESIDE .warpline so the backup's fabric dir holds only fabric. `warpline backup verify <dest>`: recompute every digest (missing/extra/size/digest problems flagged — an ADDITION is tamper evidence too) + run the FULL #fabric-verify authentication against the copy; ok ⇔ zero problems AND zero fabric failures; CLI exit 1 on any. THE RESTORE PATH IS THE ENGINE ITSELF: a backup IS a home-fabric root — every read AND write verb works against it directly (proved in test/backup.test.ts: open → refs identical → verify green → a NEW strand proposes/admits against the backup → still green). Refuses an existing dest and a dest inside the source fabric.

oracle.name: Oracle
oracle.description: WORKTREE LOADS ARE SERIALIZED PER REPO (T-2026-08-11, #repo-lock). loadBranchIndex spins a temp worktree per branch, and the caller resolves BOTH branches through Promise.all — so two concurrent `git worktree add` calls against one repo were the DESIGNED path, on every oracle run. `git worktree add` validates the whole `.git/worktrees/` registry as it runs, so a sibling mid-create (directory present, `commondir` not yet written) fails the add outright; unique leaf names do not help, because the collision is on the shared registry, not the name. It surfaced as unrelated red across divergence-proof / oracle / absorb whenever the machine was loaded — three different tests failing on three different runs, none of them the defect. #git-exec's merge-tree fallback already took this lock and described itself as "the one remaining .git/worktrees user", which was untrue while these calls existed; both now take it, and a third caller must too. A FAILED MEASUREMENT IS NOT A CLEAN MERGE (T-2026-08-11).
