The git-reality step used to swallow EVERY failure into `conflicted: false`, and that is not a neutral default: score() gates the confusion matrix on it, so an unmeasurable merge was scored as "git merged clean" — precisely the cell that FLATTERS the headline claim ("meaning caught what bytes missed"). The instrument that measures our own claim was failing toward the favourable answer, the exact asymmetry the merge-tree exit-1 conflation already taught once. #git-counterfactual learned it one field over and says so in its header: "git said clean" and "we never asked git" are opposite facts. Now a PRE-FLIGHT rev-parses both sides (mirroring counterfactual.ts) so a ref git cannot resolve never reaches merge-tree — `git merge-tree --write-tree` exits 1 for BOTH "conflicted" and "not something we can merge", so git-exec reports an unresolvable ref as a CONFLICT — and any merge-tree failure THROWS rather than scoring. Deliberately contained to the oracle: the shared merge semantics every other caller (#admit, #weave, #git-counterfactual) depends on are untouched. The oracle FAILS LOUD rather than carrying an `unavailable` state, because unlike a shadow row (one observation among many, which must survive a hole) an OracleRecord IS the scored verdict — a record whose git side was never measured has nothing to score, and emitting one would put a fabricated cell into the only evidence base for the claim. oracle(branchA, branchB) — merge-base → absorb base/A/B → diff → predict → git merge-tree reality (read-only) → score the confusion matrix (agreeClean/agreeConflict/divergeGitOnly/divergeMeaningOnly/score/verdict) → append an OracleRecord to .warpline/oracle.jsonl. The two divergence cells are the experimental result. Conflict paths map to symbols at .purpose-dir level; a git conflict in a NON-SYMBOL file (or an unresolvable merge) becomes gitConflictUnmapped — a git-only divergence that gates the verdict, so the oracle NEVER reads CONVERGENT over a real git conflict (T-2026-06-25-001). The ACTIONABLE answer is a separate mergeClean flag (no knots ∧ no dangling ∧ no git conflict); convergence measures meaning⟷git AGREEMENT, so a contested merge both sides predict scores 'convergent agreement' but is NOT mergeClean — read mergeClean for "is it safe to weave?" (T-2026-06-25-005). KNOT-SIZE RANKING (T-2026-07-03-002, additive fields — verdict/score untouched, so the committed base-rate evidence stays valid): convergence also partitions divergeMeaningOnly into directContested[] (own content changed on ≥1 side) vs rippleOnly[] (flagged only via essence transitivity) + knotSize (=|directContested|, the ranking/threshold key) and flagCount. Ground truth: ≤6-symbol flag sets were 50% churn-validated, every ≥10-symbol avalanche 0% — small knots ARE the product; the CLI names direct symbols and collapses ripple to a count line. P3 GAP-1 (G1-additive, schemaVersion unchanged): the record also carries coverage — the #honesty per-path labels over every path either side touched (real refs only) + aggregate counts. A coverage failure never fails the oracle.

weave.name: Weave
weave.description: The pre-merge MEANING forecast + the semantic-diff report — READ-ONLY and, unlike #oracle, never writes .warpline/. forecast(A, B) reuses the Oracle pipeline up through predict() (mergeBase → absorb base/A/B → diff → predict) and surfaces it as pre-merge UX: a CLEAN-vs-DECISIONS verdict, autoClean count, knots (symbol + contending sides), dangling (from→target, retiredBy). An optional vsGit flag also runs the full Oracle (git merge-tree) read-only for the meaning-vs-bytes divergence comparison. semanticDiff(refA, refB) groups the SemDeltas (born / retired / contract-changed-with-slots / renamed-noop) so the "rename/move is the EMPTY delta" property is visible on real refs. The `weave` WRITE verb is RESERVED, not implemented in Phase 1.

consolidate.name: Consolidate
consolidate.description: The N-way fold FORECAST (read-only) — the N-branch generalization of #weave's forecast(). consolidate(refs[], {base?}) absorbs a common base + N refs IN PARALLEL (concurrency-safe via git-archive materialization, T-2026-06-23-003), diffs each against base, and runs the proven 2-way #predict PAIRWISE across every (i<j), aggregating by symbol: an N-way knot is the union of the pairwise knots on a stableKey (sides = the refs in tension), a dangle is an edge one ref added into a symbol another ref retired, autoFolded = touched keys with no decision. decisions (K_human) = knots + dangles. NO git merge, NO ledger write. The engine behind the falsifiable multi-agent claim (T-2026-06-24-012): a meaning-preserving edit (reorder, local rename) carries ZERO delta and auto-folds where git textually conflicts, so human labor tracks GENUINE meaning-collisions, not branch count. Engine only — no CLI verb wired yet.

lifeline.name: Lifeline
lifeline.description: Meaning-aware blame — lifeline(symbol, {maxCommits}) traces a symbol's ESSENCE through the commits that touched its file (git log --follow, so the thread survives the renames/moves git blame resets on), attributing each essence-change to the commit that INTRODUCED it (newest-first) with the author + INTENT (the commit subject git blame can't show). Resolves the symbol at HEAD, absorbs up to maxCommits of the file history IN PARALLEL (concurrency-safe per T-2026-06-23-003), and emits ONLY genuine meaning changes — a commit that touched the file but not the symbol's meaning is NOT an event. Read-only. MVP: tracks by the ::qualified suffix (rename-stable across file moves; a same-suffix collision elsewhere is a known limitation).

agent-shell.name: Agent Shell
agent-shell.description: THE CLI HALF OF THE HUMAN-CLASS LAW (soundness audit 2026-07-31 C-11 / Aegis S3; pre-freeze panel D-4; Aegis M-1). HUMAN_ONLY_VERBS and HUMAN_ONLY_ADMIT_FLAGS were enforced at exactly ONE place — #warplined's verb × principal matrix. The native CLI has no token, no principal and no gate, so `warpline resolve` sailed past authorization and failed only on a missing argument, and resolve / stake / stake.recover / backup / --accept-breach / --accept-risk all sat on the top-level help with no credential. Not tidiness: FG-1's ratified completion criterion rests on `resolve` being the act the security law FORBIDS, and that law held for an agent on the MCP skin and evaporated for an agent with a shell — which every coding agent has. THE NAIVE FIX IS INCOHERENT (possession of the shell IS the human credential under the stage-1 model, #daemon-tokens — there is no CLI principal to gate on), so this uses the product's OWN precedent: `$WARPLINE_AGENT_ID` is the established "this shell is an agent shell" marker (#pick attributes by it, and #pick's R2 gate already refuses an agent-attributed CLI write under gate.agentWrites:'real'). When it is set, the human-class verbs and flags are refused with a real refusal:v1 — never a bare Error — carrying the DAEMON'S OWN ANSWER VERBATIM: FORBIDDEN, gate 'transport', retriable 'never', EMPTY next[]. Empty means exactly one thing in #refusal: no call recovers this, ESCALATE; naming the human verb in next[] would invite the retry that IS the W3 violation. BOUND, NEVER RE-LISTED: the gated sets are DERIVED from the daemon's two constants (cliPathOf: dots are CLI subcommand separators exactly as toolNameOf mangles them for MCP, so stake.recover → `stake recover`; longFlagOf: camelCase → --kebab), so a fourth divergent copy of the law cannot appear and adding a verb to HUMAN_ONLY_VERBS gates its CLI command in the same edit. ORDERING (the MCP skin's D-2 lesson): the attempt is TRACED before the refusal propagates — a violation that is refused but unrecorded makes "zero W3 marks" unfailable, which is the blindness tracing `resolve` was added to remove. INVISIBILITY IS A REQUIREMENT, not a side effect: an UNMARKED shell returns from the gate having done nothing — no row, no throw — so the founder's shell and the F4 harness's scripted human-resolve leg (which runs unmarked, in its own shell) are byte-identical to before. HONEST SCOPE: $WARPLINE_AGENT_ID is UNSIGNED self-assertion exactly as it is for pick attribution — an agent that unsets it is unmarked. This raises the cost of the violation from zero to deliberate; it is not authentication, and M3 signatures still close that gap. Gated sites: resolve, stake, stake recover, backup, admit --accept-breach/--accept-risk, and pick --accept-risk (the R2 override door, which #pick's own ladder already marks principal:'human'). `daemon token mint` is deliberately NOT gated — it is not in HUMAN_ONLY_VERBS, and widening the set is a founder call, not a wiring one. Proved in test/agent-shell-gate.test.ts. AUTO-RESOLVE GRANTS (M3-lite I6): the CLI resolve gate (cli.ts gateHumanClass) consults #grants the same way the daemon matrix does — a MARKED shell attempting `resolve` (verb only, never the override flags) under an ACTIVE grant is allowed through and the grantId is returned so the seal records underGrant; no grant → the identical refusal as before, byte for byte.

warpline-cli.name: Warpline Cli
warpline-cli.description: COLD-AGENT LEGIBILITY (F4, TD-2026-07-21-766 — an agent of ANY provider must use Warpline as easily as git, and since Warpline is unpublished and in no model's weights, runtime self-description is the ONLY mechanism). fork / propose / admit each NAME THEIR CYCLE POSITION in --help ("CYCLE STEP 1|2|3"), matching the daemon/MCP descriptors which always numbered them. Two CLI-only defects made the write path unreachable from --help alone, both found by driving a fresh repo end to end: (1) `propose` marked --claim REQUIRED while the ENGINE requires `intent` and treats `claim` as optional (native.ts), so an agent had to author `#code:<file>::<name>` symbol-id syntax — which the CLI never teaches — before it could capture ANY work; --claim is now optional with --native, required only in claim-only mode, and intent is enforced with the I3 reason. (2) `admit` after fork-without-propose reported NOOP "the agent changed no meaning" — false, and expensively so: the work is real and merely unsealed (see #admit for the engine-side refusal). Also: `fail()` no longer prints `warpline: warpline:` on engine errors, which is precisely the text an agent reads when it is already lost. Pinned in test/cli-cold-agent-cycle.test.ts, which drives the REAL binary because the defects lived in option wiring and prose that no library-level test can see. The warpline command line (commander). `warpline oracle <a> <b> [--json]`, `warpline absorb <ref> [--json]`, `warpline weave --preview <a> <b> [--vs-git] [--json]` (the pre-merge forecast; the bare `weave` write verb is reserved and refuses with a read-only notice), `warpline consolidate <refs...> [--base R] [--json]` (the N-way fold forecast — CLEAN-to-fold vs N decisions, knots with per-ref sides, dangling, auto-fold count), and `warpline diff [refA] [refB] [--json]` (semantic diff; no args = WORKTREE vs HEAD, one arg = ref vs HEAD, two args = refA vs refB). Plus `warpline status [--json]` (the working tree's MEANING vs HEAD — the named, discoverable form of diff-no-args) and `warpline lifeline <symbol> [--max N] [--json]` (meaning-aware blame — who changed a symbol's meaning, when, why; survives renames). ONBOARDING + NATIVE STATUS (T-2026-08-12-002, cold-agent dogfood): `warpline init [dir] [--json]` (#warpline-init) is the discoverable onboarding verb — it seals the genesis fabric via the native path (proposeNative → admitNative), writes a starter `.warpignore` (commented examples so the syntax is visible), keeps `.warpline/`+`.warpline-judge/` out of git (.gitignore append-or-create, idempotent), and prints the fork→propose→admit→resolve next-steps; it is idempotent (a second run seals no genesis, duplicates no line). `status`/`diff` take a NATIVE path (#native-status: nativeStatus — worktree MEANING vs the SELVAGE, snapshotDir+absorbTree, no git) when `HEAD` is not git-reachable, so the FIRST thing an agent runs no longer dies `git … not a repository` in a native project; git present ⇒ the git path is unchanged. Both also carry a BYTE-HONESTY layer (DiskHonesty {filesChanged, byteOnly}): a byte-only or scalar-only change that lifts to NO meaning delta prints "0 meaning changes, but N files changed on disk (byte-only / not lifted into meaning)" instead of a bare "clean", so an agent never mistakes real work for a no-op — surface strings only, never a verdict input. A bare `warpline` (no command) prints help pointing at init then status; the legacy `.warplineignore` earns a one-time stderr deprecation notice on these surfaces when `.warpignore` is absent. Pinned by test/init-status-native.test.ts. Phase-2 WRITE PATH: `warpline pick [-m <intent>] [--as <actor>] [--confidence <n>] [--ref <ref>] [--quiet] [--json]` seals meaning into the fabric (no-op when unchanged; with `--ref <commit>` and no -m, intent + actor are derived from the commit), `warpline log [--max N] [--json]` shows this project's native meaning-history (the strands, newest first, with the git coexistence anchor), `warpline selvage [--json]` shows the current fabric tip + the strand that sealed it, and `warpline hook <install|uninstall|status>` manages the post-commit auto-seal, `warpline scratch <agentId>` forks a per-agent multi-writer base, `warpline admit <agentId> [--ref <ref>] [--json]` runs the admission protocol (FAST_ADMIT / CLEAN+confidence / KNOT / DANGLE) — its exit code is VERDICT-KEYED off the result's #refusal via exitCodeForResult on both the git-era and --native paths (0 sealed/NOOP, 1 GATE_REFUSED, 3 CLAIM_BREACH, 4 TRUST_HELD, 5 STALE_BASE — T-2026-07-21-006: a refusing verdict must never exit 0; --shadow stays exit 0 by contract, observe-only), and `warpline resolve <agentId> --ref <resolvedRef> -m <reason> [--by <who>] [--ours <ref>]` seals a KNOT-council resolution, and `warpline abandon <agentId> [--json]` is THE AGENT-CLASS EXIT (audit C-10) — it withdraws the agent's scratch pointer and nothing else, so the sealed proposal survives as a restorable abandoned head and an open KNOT stays open (see #native-write-path for the two design choices); it is idempotent, and it is what makes `git merge --abort`'s always-available escape hatch exist here, and `warpline grade [--window N] [--dry] [--json]` grades strand confidence against real survive/overturn outcome (the moat), and `warpline fabric verify [--json]` authenticates the whole PICK-DAG (integrity + v2 chain + binding re-derivation; exit 0 intact / 1 tamper / 2 I/O), and `warpline restore [selector] [--to <dir>] [--force] [--json]` reconstructs a working tree from the native object store with git ABSENT (the layer→VCS threshold — selector HEAD|selvage|N|@N|pick:|state:|tree:, path-hardened, A4-refuses an unbound strand, dirty-dest guarded), and `warpline refs <migrate|list> [--json]` (V3.2 pickId refs: `migrate` is the ONE-TIME founder-visible stateId→pickId selvage conversion; `list` shows refs/heads/* + the head set — legacy repos show the single ledger tip). `fabric verify` additionally reports the v3 DAG segment, abandoned heads and the C-6 stake-journal cross-check ("stakes N checkpoint(s) cross-checked"). THE REPAIR PATH (#fabric-repair — audit C-13/P1): `warpline fabric repair [--confirm] [--json]` salvages a torn TAIL line (dry run by default — itemizes the dropped line, its bytes, its parse error and a bounded escaped excerpt; --confirm quarantines the original under .warpline/repair/ FIRST, then republishes the well-formed prefix verbatim; refuses mid-ledger damage), and `warpline refs set <name> <pickId> [--force] [--json]` re-points a head — the actionable half of the abandoned-head warning, which the verify output now names inline. Both refuse rather than improvise; neither writes silently. `warpline health [--json]` (2026-08-10) is the READ-ONLY diagnostic — #warpline-health. It is ADDITIVE, never an overload of `status`: `status` is the meaning diff and is traced as `cli:status`, a different thing from the daemon's cycle-position `status`. `health` is CLI-ONLY (so the FG-3 descriptor freeze is untouched — descriptorsId hashes nothing a CLI verb reaches), is NOT wrapped in traceCli because that would WRITE, and exits 0/1/2 for green/warnings/unsound so CI can gate on `--json`. `warpline fsck [--json]` (M3-lite I5, #fabric-fsck) is the INTEGRITY umbrella — fabric + objects + refs + registry + stakes in one read-only pass (each check reused verbatim, nothing new); per-section PASS/WARN/FAIL lines, exit 0 iff every section ok (warnings never fail; --json included — fsck's own contract), 1 on a failed section, 2 on usage/I/O. CLI-only for the same FG-3 reason as `health`. The only module allowed to write stdout; library code stays quiet.

field-harness.name: Field Harness
field-harness.description: The expo-field-test-protocol RUN HARNESS, increment 1 of 2 (§B7, T-2026-08-23-003) — src/field/*, standalone from src/daemon by rule, and writing under .warpline/field/ only. THREE PIECES. (1) #field-oracle: the §4 CLEAN-seal oracle AUTOMATION. discoverAuditTargets walks the fabric for MergeRecipe strands (a real merge: two parents + result) AND single-parent CLEAN/FAST_ADMIT seals — every field READ off the strand or its parents, null where unrecorded, never invented (v3 strands carry no seq → seq:null). auditOne restores result (+ ours/theirs for merges) trees via the native restoreTree into scratch dirs and runs the DECLARED green-gate (.warpline/field/greengate.json — loaded, never hardcoded; an ABSENT config records every check 'absent' and the row says so: the default is not a pass) through an INJECTED CheckRunner (unit tests fake exec; the CLI injects execFile+timeout, no shell). ESTABLISHING POWER (§4): every check — and every frozen behavioral assertion, run as `script <assertion>` through the same runner — runs on BOTH parents first; red on either parent alone → recorded 'excluded-parent-red' (proves nothing); green-both-parents ∧ red-on-merge → objectiveRegression (non-vetoable) → verdict 'candidate-false-clean'. Single-parent seals: mode:'single-parent', result-only run, objectiveRegression structurally false (no merge to regress). coveredClass comes from #field-blind-class over the seal's changed paths (merge: union of both sides' diffs vs base via #graph diffTrees; single-parent: diff vs the bound parent; underivable ⇒ null ⇒ coveredClass false — ignorance is not coverage); a blind-only seal is 'blind-untested', NEVER 'true-clean'. Rows land hash-chained in .warpline/field/expo-field-oracle.jsonl (rowHash = fieldOracleRow:v1: sha256(canonical(body)+prev), the #judge-ledger idiom); verifyAuditLedger recomputes the chain; runFieldOracle is idempotent by strandId (already-audited seals skipped). (2) #field-cards: habit (ii) capture, SCAN-based (no admit-path hook in increment 1) — every persisted KNOT payload (.warpline/knots/) becomes a blinded §5 rating card via the EXISTING #judge stripper buildKnotRatingCard, written idempotently by content-addressed cardId to .warpline/field/cards/; the card on disk carries NO verdict/confidence/founder label (blindness re-asserted on the serialized bytes in test). The B-3 gap — a byte-downgrade KNOT whose refusal advertises no knotPayloadId (git-path downgrade sites; evidence trail = .warpline/f4/trace.jsonl, read DIRECTLY with a narrow local type because field modules may not import src/daemon) — is RECORDED card-less in cards/byte-downgrades.jsonl (idempotent by recorded identity), never faked into a card: a card needs sides, and building one from MergeRecipe trees alone is increment-2 work. (3) #field-fallback: habit (iii) — every reach for the git fallback appended to .warpline/field/git-fallback.jsonl {ts, actor, message, knotId?, admitRef?}: plain JSONL by design (the protocol asks a LOG, not custody); an empty message refuses (a silent fallback is the exact flattering-direction error (C) measures). CLI: `warpline field oracle [--since <seq>] [--greengate <path>]` / `warpline field cards` / `warpline field fallback -m <msg> [--knot] [--admit] | --list`, all with --json. INCREMENT 2 (T-2026-08-23-003, §5/§3/§7/§9): FOUR MORE PIECES. (4) #field-interleave: the §5 card stream. selectAuditSample = the §4 rule VERBATIM (every 5th true-clean by LEDGER order among dismissed CLEANs, floor 15 per block, planted excluded — the fraction never re-tunes to the observed count). buildCleanCardFromOracleRow bridges an OracleRow to the #judge stripper's CleanAuditRow (sides from the strand's OWN MergeRecipe trees for the CHANGED paths the row recorded; intents from the parent strands; oracle-flagged carries the failing check NAME, audit-sample carries the F3c sentinel 'none-declared' — the rubric fix is FOUNDER-GATED, so the leak is carried as the LOUD AUDIT_SAMPLE_LEAK_CAVEAT in the run manifest + §9 report, never silently fixed). interleave = deterministic Fisher–Yates keyed by sha256(seed‖index), seed COMMITTED to .warpline/field/judge/ shuffle-seed before the first batch (a different later seed REFUSES). loadSeedCards reads .warpline/field/seeds/{planted,genuine,over-block, corpus}/ — manifest.json seals ground truth + per-file sha256; cardId re-verified against content; any mismatch/unsealed file refuses; absent dirs → empty sets (the run then refuses on empty corpus). (5) #field-judge-run: `warpline field judge` — assembles KNOT cards + oracle-flagged + audit-sample + seeds → interleaves with the committed seed → #judge-runner runJudgeEnforced (pre-flight FIRST, §4 provenance sealed per row, LEDGER-FILE PAIRING: the judge custody ledger keeps the protocol name expo-field-audit.jsonl under .warpline/field/judge/, the oracle ledger stays expo-field-oracle.jsonl — module-header notes in each name the other). Idempotent by cardId; --batch-limit defers to continuity; --fake = deterministic by-kind dry-run (measures nothing); default requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY → liveCallModel. Writes field-judge-manifest.json (counts + seed + the F3c caveat). (6) #field-join: `warpline field join` — §3 A13 PRECONDITION with NO escape hatch: `git show HEAD:<witness>` must equal SOME chain row's rowHash or NOTHING joins (git absent / uncommitted / matching no row each refuse precisely; rows after the witnessed head are the only permitted un-witnessed tail). CLEAN cards join the oracle-row verdict via provenance pickId; KNOT cards join 'KNOT' ('KNOT:resolved' when a fabric strand's resolves.knotPayloadId names the payload); planted/ seeded/corpus rows are calibration and are skipped, counted, never guessed. A verdict row sealed AFTER the witnessed ordinal is NOT joined this pass (reported awaitingWitness with an operator commit-first instruction) — only a head witnessed BEFORE the answer counts. Idempotent; after joining the NEW head is re-witnessed and the VERBATIM commit reminder printed. (7) #field-score: `warpline field score` — PURE over recorded artifacts. §7A twoDenominatorBounds (objective over covered CLEANs, subjective via subjectiveBoundInputs over the JOINED audits — a rating is 'pending' until its warpline-join row exists in the chain, rated-but-unjoined never enters n_subjective; NEVER blended, no combined field exists). Audit-sample floor: applied GLOBALLY, equivalent to §4's per-block rule below 100 admissions (caveat stated in the module + report; per-block flooring needed for multi-block runs). §7B byte-baseline column per audited merge target (fabric/merge3 mergeText over base/ours/theirs bodies; unrecorded recipe → computable:false, never guessed); meaning-decisive = CLEAN ∧ byte-conflicted ∧ oracle true-clean COUNTED; the silent-mismerge class emitted as CATCH-CANDIDATES requiring oracle confirmation, NOT claimed (honest increment-2 scope). §7C intervention rate (KNOTs + logged fallbacks over admissions; --admissions override) + K2 flag. Seeded-control precision/recall + Wilson-LB beats-prior gate; indeterminate fraction with GENUINE-only floor; genuine reported BOTH uncorrected and naive-precision-corrected, labeled 'correction formula pending pre-registration v2' (F3d founder-gated). Report → .warpline/field/ report.md + report.json with every §9 mandatory element: the correlated-priors ≠-branch caveat VERBATIM (agents claude-opus-5 vs judge claude-opus-4-5-20251101, version-only separation, discount at the STRONGER end), the pre-fix baseline framing, the audit-sample leak caveat, blind-class exclusions, kappa honestly reported as NOT COMPUTABLE (founder primary labels not captured), and VOID/not-tested defaults (planted control absent/uncaught → '(A) not tested'; genuine<20 → (B)/(C) INCONCLUSIVE). Reviewer follow-ons folded in: ByteDowngradeEntry.strandId renamed stateRef (a byte-downgrade never sealed a strand; legacy key still read for idempotency), and appendAuditRow's O(n²) tail re-read replaced by a per-path head cache (verify-on-load kept — first append per process verifies the whole chain).

field-seed-authoring.name: Field Seed Authoring
field-seed-authoring.description: The PRE-APP KIT PRODUCER (field-test freeze-checklist items that don't need the subject app yet; expo-field-test-protocol-v2 §4/§5/§A6/§A9, runbook §0) — src/field/seed-authoring.ts + src/field/corpus-payloads.ts. It BUILDS the sealed seed/corpus card sets that #field-interleave.loadSeedCards (the RUN'S OWN loader) then consumes VERBATIM; the seal formula (recomputeCardId) and manifest shape (SeedManifestEntry: file, cardId, sha256, groundTruth/ steeredLabel) are byte-identical to the consumer's, and the producer→consumer round-trip is asserted in test/seed-authoring.test.ts (a card the loader rejects is a failure). THREE PURE PRODUCERS. (1) sealCardSet(dir, cards) writes each RatingCard to <dir>/seed-NNN.json (deterministic index filenames), sha256 over the EXACT bytes, and manifest.json — returning the manifest sha256 the operator commits to git (§C). (2) buildInjectionCorpusCards (§A9): PUBLIC prompt-injection payload strings (corpus-payloads.ts — STARTER_INJECTION_PAYLOADS, 10 generic well-known patterns tagged with the steeredLabel each pushes, provenance stated as externally-authored-not-tuned) embedded VERBATIM in the untrusted-prose intent channel of a well-formed knot RatingCard; because the payload rides framed prose, buildBenignTwin neutralizes it and the twin differs (the §5 differential injection gate's signal). (3) buildPlantedControlCard (§4/A6 canonical false-CLEAN): takes the two operator-supplied side file maps (limit-100→50 vs retry-loop-assuming-100 by DEFAULT SYNTHETIC pair — swap real subject files at seal time), materializes ours/theirs/merged into durable trees via snapshotDir, assembles the CleanAuditRow, and runs the SAME #judge stripper buildCleanRatingCard the run uses; groundTruth 'broken'. CLI (under the existing `field` group): `warpline field seed corpus|planted|classify|verify` — corpus seals the starter public corpus; planted seals one control from --ours/--theirs (or the synthetic pair, with a LOUD replace-before-run warning); classify seals already-captured KNOT cards (from `field cards`) as KNOWN-GENUINE/KNOWN-OVER-BLOCK with operator ground truth (authored AFTER contested cards exist, §A6); verify (the money verb) loads all four sealed dirs through the run's own loader and reports counts + any seal failure (proves §C condition (c) BEFORE the freeze). Each seal verb refuses to overwrite a non-empty sealed dir unless --force.

field-subject-bootstrap.name: Field Subject Bootstrap
field-subject-bootstrap.description: The PRE-APP KIT SUBJECT ONBOARDING (expo-field-test-protocol-v2 §A2/§A3, runbook §0) — src/field/subject-bootstrap.ts + `warpline field init-subject [dir]`. It SCAFFOLDS and INSTRUCTS; it does NOT act. It writes, under the subject repo's .warpline/field/: (1) a starter greengate.json = the §A3 declared gate {checks:[typecheck: npx tsc --noEmit, bundle: npx expo export], behavioral:{script:'', assertions:[]}} that readGreenGate parses (asserted in test); (2) a behavioral-checklist.template.md stub the operator fills (its assertions enumerate the config×code couplings — a coupling not listed is BLIND, not passed). It PRINTS the ordered runbook §0 pre-run checklist, each item tagged auto (a tool step) or manual (a human decision/act), plus the load-bearing reminder that agent keys must be MINTED BEFORE agents propose (Build-D fixture finding: an unkeyed proposal is refused). It deliberately does NOT run `warpline init` and does NOT mint keys — both are human acts. Idempotent: refuses to clobber an existing greengate.json unless --force.

Returns fixed classifier strings safe for logs / telemetry / LLM context. aggregator.description: #aggregator: Combines multiple .purpose files. Exports DEFAULT_PURPOSE_IGNORE (7.13.0) — the discovery ignore list findPurposeFiles uses.

symbol-index.name: Symbol Index
symbol-index.description: #symbol-index: In-memory symbol index. Also home of the ONE shared anchor-string parser (7.12.0, D9): parseAnchorString (aggregator path; section anchors first, then the pre-7.12 line semantics byte-identical — "file.ts:15-20" still yields exactly {path, lines:[15,20], raw}), parseAnchor (same section-first fallthrough), parseSectionAnchor (Obsidian-compatible docs/x.md#Heading Text → kind heading, docs/x.md#^block-id → kind block, lines 0 = unresolved; the path part must end in a file extension so src/c#/x.cs:10 stays a line anchor, and a fragment containing '/' or ending in :N / :N-M is rejected so dir.name#x/Foo.ts:10 stays a line anchor) and resolveSectionAnchorLines (content + key → current 1-based inclusive range or null; heading = through the next same-or-higher heading, fenced pseudo-headings ignored, exact then case-insensitive match; block = contiguous paragraph ending at the inline caret-id or preceding a standalone caret-id line). SourceType gained 'frontmatter' (no exhaustive switches exist; bySource is an open Map).

frontmatter-parser.name: Frontmatter Parser
frontmatter-parser.description: #frontmatter-parser: src/frontmatter.ts — the ONE YAML-frontmatter splitter (7.12.0, D8). parseFrontmatter(raw, {mode}) → {data, body, hasFrontmatter, error?} over FRONTMATTER_RE (LF + CRLF, closing fence then newline or EOF). lenient (default) never throws: no block → whole input is body; malformed YAML / non-mapping → data {} + error, body after the fence. strict throws FrontmatterError(reason missing|yaml|not-mapping) with CONTRACT messages "missing YAML frontmatter (--- … ---)", "frontmatter is not a YAML mapping", or the YAML parser message verbatim (surfaced unchanged by #skill-loader). Consumers: #native-memory-scan (lenient), #skill-loader splitFrontmatter (strict), docs-loader (lenient → null adapter). Follow-up: university-core loader + doctor agent-audit still hand-roll.

search-engine.name: Search Engine
search-engine.description: #search-engine: Symbol search functionality (searchSymbols in src/symbol-index.ts). Since 7.13.0 per-entry lowercased haystacks (symbol, description, tags, componentType, joined multi-token string) are memoized in a WeakMap keyed by SymbolIndex and revalidated against the entry source fields, so repeated searches over a cached #live-index index skip re-lowercasing. Substring semantics and ranking are unchanged.

symbol-integrity.name: Symbol Integrity
symbol-integrity.description: #symbol-integrity (7.15.0, TD-2026-10-13-661 Phase 1): canonical symbol identity. aggregator.ts canonicalizeSymbols merges every contributor of one symbol string into ONE entry (portal wins for gates; real declarations beat reference stubs; ties keep last-wins), records all contributors in SymbolEntry.sources, and marks reference-only stubs declared:false. resolveReferences scans the winner AND every donor's data (dropping `anchors` and `referencedFrom`), so no edge is lost in the merge; portal gates now reference the prize signals they award. symbol-index.ts adds bySymbol/byNameLower maps, resolveSymbol (exact -> case-insensitive -> unambiguous bare name, else candidates), addSymbolEntry and sourcesOf; getSymbol is O(1). src/integrity.ts exports findDuplicateDeclarations (a portal+purpose pair is exempt; a second .purpose declaration is flagged) and findDanglingReferences. Fixes ripple reporting 0 dependents for portal gates referenced from .purpose.

live-index.name: Live Index
live-index.description: #live-index: src/live-index.ts (7.13.0) — incremental in-process cache of the LIVE SymbolIndex. getLiveIndex(rootDir) globs .purpose (purpose-core findPurposeFiles) + portal.yaml (portal-core findGateFiles), stats every file, and returns the SAME cached index when the ordered (path, mtimeMs, size) lists are unchanged; otherwise re-parses only changed .purpose files via #purpose-parse-cache and re-aggregates the FULL set in discovery order through aggregateFromDirectory's AggregateOptions loader seams, so output equals a cold parse (order + duplicate last-write-wins, T-2026-06-13-011). Concurrent callers share one in-flight refresh. Files with mtime within 2s of now also carry a content sha1 in their stamp (same-size edits inside one mtime tick). At most LIVE_INDEX_MAX_ROOTS (8) roots are cached, LRU-evicted. invalidateLiveIndex(rootDir?) drops a root (paradigm_reindex calls it). Returned index/entry data are shared — read-only. Bench (report only): scripts/bench-live-index.mjs.

graph-slice-projector.name: Graph Slice Projector
graph-slice-projector.description: #graph-slice-projector: Projects a BOUNDED, deterministic slice of the symbol graph centered on one symbol (src/graph-slice.ts). Shared by the `paradigm graph slice` CLI + `paradigm_graph_slice` MCP tool. Sources neighbors from a LIVE SymbolIndex (aggregateFromDirectory + buildSymbolIndex — the SAME live-parse pipeline `paradigm ripple` uses), NOT the stale scan-index/flow-index, so flow membership (e.g. #cockpit-view → $$fleet-switch) always surfaces. Unioned edges: getReferencesFrom → uses/gated-by/in-flow, getReferencesTo → used-by, flow membership → in-flow, flow co-members (flow mode) → uses. BFS to radius (1, max 3), DEGREE_CAP 8 with +N-more collapse, deterministic sort, fail-loud did-you-mean. Freshness is the live-parse timestamp, stale always false (sidesteps the scan-index determinism wart). Since 7.13.0 loadLiveGraph delegates to #live-index and memoizes the LiveGraph per SymbolIndex (buildLiveGraph), so a warm call does no parsing.

classroom-metrics.name: Classroom Metrics
classroom-metrics.description: #classroom-metrics: The ONE canonical repeat-failure-rate rollup for the Classroom (TD-2026-06-19-007), src/classroom-metrics.ts. Both the paradigm_classroom_status MCP tool and `paradigm doctor` consume it (the CLI does NOT depend on paradigm-mcp; both depend on premise-core), so the formula lives here ONCE to avoid drift. computeRepeatFailureRate(certs) → overall + per-agent { resolved, overturned, rate } where rate = overturned/resolved (3dp), null until a cert resolves (survived|overturned; pending excluded). readClassroomCertifications/readFieldFailures read .paradigm/events/*.jsonl tolerantly (skip corrupt lines, never throw), mirroring graph-slice's .paradigm file access. The cert WRITER stays in paradigm-mcp/utils/field-failures.ts — only the read+rollup is shared.

purpose-parse-cache.name: Purpose Parse Cache
purpose-parse-cache.description: #purpose-parse-cache: src/parse-cache.ts (7.13.0) — PurposeParseCache, a per-file memo keyed by absolute path → {mtimeMs, size, sha1, data, errors}. stat fast path (mtime+size equal and mtime older than RECENT_MTIME_WINDOW_MS=2s → cached parse, no read; recent files are always hashed so same-size edits in one mtime tick are caught); on a stamp change the file is read + sha1-hashed and the parse reused when the bytes are identical, else re-parsed with parseRawPurposeFileContent (the exact post-read pipeline of parsePurposeFileDetailed). prune/invalidate drop entries. parsePurposeFilesCached / getAllPurposeFilesCached keep the input (findPurposeFiles) order — the cache never reorders. Returned data is shared and read-only. Consumer: #live-index in premise-core.

brain-mcp.name: Brain Mcp
brain-mcp.description: 7.14 paradigm_brain({op: status|search|stale}) — ON-DEMAND family listed ONLY while some brain has agent_access metadata (families.ts requires: brain-agent-access; config enable / tool_activate cannot override). Thin adapter over utils/brain: openBrainView(agent) only, metadata-only output (id, relpath, folder, kind, title, topics), headings wrapped as <untrusted_document_text>, every response through view.respond() (egress-logged, leak-checked; BrainLeakError → generic blocked). No confirm/write op; not mixed into paradigm_search. Every document-derived string (title, topics, relpath, folder, headings, cross-link relpath/target, brain name) is wrapped; stripEnvelope removes envelope-like tags case-/whitespace-/zero-width-/NFKC-tolerantly until stable; not-exported reason → unknown for agents.

CaptainTools.description: 3 MCP tools for Cid (the Captain agent) — paradigm_captain_brief (pre-task context discovery pipeline: search + navigate + ripple + wisdom + protocol + lore → Context Brief injected into every agent prompt), paradigm_captain_debrief (post-task coverage audit: .purpose stub creation, pending-review queueing, lore recording, .cid-briefed stop hook marker, sessionInsights object handed off to Loid; v7 §3 adds a postflight-liveness check that self-heals — runs runPostflightLearning itself when the settlement-liveness probe shows no postflight ran, and on self-heal failure proposes an ADVISE block, never guard), and paradigm_captain_board (#captain-board — Cid's owned run-DAG read+write artifact: read assembles the live orchestration DAG from non-terminal epic tasks + their stage-children ordered by stage/dependsOn, plus ripple-ranked unclaimed open tasks and a summary; claim writes a task claimant keeping status open with a human/peer-over-archetype override guard; advance records a Cid-owned blocked_on reason without changing status — v7.0 has no blocked status). Core-tier always loaded. Cid closes navigation; Loid closes learning. Ownership boundary: Cid writes claimant/blocked_on (present tense); Loid writes settledAt (past tense) — they never co-write a field.

captain-board.name: Captain Board
captain-board.description: v7 §3 — paradigm_captain_board, Cid's owned run-DAG artifact (read|claim|advance). read assembles the live orchestration DAG from non-terminal epic tasks + their stage children (ordered by stage/dependsOn) plus ripple-ranked unclaimed open tasks; claim writes a task claimant keeping status open (human/peer override archetype); advance records a Cid-owned blocked_on reason. Session-open proposes claimants (a real per-session mutation, replacing the anonymous task dump); session-close debrief reads the settlement-liveness probe and self-heals (runs postflight itself, advise-not-guard). Resolves the audit's inert-Captain finding.

team-invocation-gates.name: Team Invocation Gates

injects a decision-time orchestration directive into model context, once
per TTL window, telemetry on every match) and team-gate (PreToolUse
Write|Edit; one-time stderr advisory before source edits in unresolved

the PARADIGM_TEAM_GATE=off kill switch. Markers expire by AGE
(PARADIGM_GATE_TTL_HOURS, default 4h) — never stop-cleared, because Stop

check-14-remediation-gate.name: Check 14 Remediation Gate

v6.1 Sprint 1 Wave 2 — Stop hook Check 14. Iterates the cached
_REMEDIATIONS_JSON (sourced from `paradigm internal active-remediations
--json`). severity=guard adds to VIOLATIONS (blocks); advise/auto-author
route to ADVISORY. Honors PARADIGM_OVERRIDE comma-list to skip ids and
append an audit row to .paradigm/events/overrides.jsonl with mechanism=env.
Iteration uses temp-file + redirect (NOT pipe) for POSIX subshell-safe
VIOLATION_COUNT propagation.

check-15-memory-hygiene-nudge.name: Check 15 Memory Hygiene Nudge

Memory Steward A3 (TD-2026-09-19-110) — Stop hook Check 15. Advisory-only
cheap heuristic that nudges `paradigm memory review` when native Claude
Code memory (outside the repo at $HOME/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/)
looks due. Metadata only (entry count > 25, MEMORY.md bytes > 32768, days
since .paradigm/.memory-last-review > 30, or never-reviewed + entries > 15)
— NO LLM, NO scan, NO content reads. Appends at most one line to ADVISORY;
NEVER touches VIOLATIONS. Fail-open on missing HOME/dir/stat: emits nothing.

memory-steward-types.name: Memory Steward Types

memory-steward-score.name: Memory Steward Score
memory-steward-score.description: scoreEntry composes a 0..1 staleness score from age (mtimeMs, normalized to a 90d horizon), per-type decay weight (project fast, feedback/reference/user slow), and graph-validity penalty. deriveFinding maps a score to a suggested action (provably-stale→prune, feedback→route:habits, project→route:task, reference+decision→route:decisions, near-dup→merge, durable→pin). Age/window constants re-defined locally to avoid a paradigm-mcp dependency.

memory-steward-cluster.name: Memory Steward Cluster

memory-steward-sync.name: Memory Steward Sync
memory-steward-sync.description: B2 sync engine (advisory + strictly guarded, reworked 2026-09-20 after a dry-run against a real hand-curated MEMORY.md false-flagged active sections). computeSync (read-only) leans the native MEMORY.md and reports what WOULD change. DEMOTION is drastically narrowed: a block is demotable ONLY if it is a LEAF at heading level ≥3 (never a # title or ## section, never a node with child subsections) AND provably graph-stale (cites symbols, all dead vs the live graph) AND carries NO active-signal marker (⭐, START HERE, ACTIVE, IN PROGRESS, live, current, next, TODO, WIP, ⚠, or any date within 180d of now, case-insensitive) AND has no active-marked ancestor (protection inherits down the subtree). The old shipped+dated-old heuristic is REMOVED. PROJECTION is OFF by default (opts.project) — a plain sync only leans; when opted in the managed block (<!-- PARADIGM:BEGIN/END -->) is COMPACT (one terse `- [kind] title` line each, ≤80 chars), CAPPED at 8 items, and DEDUPED against the current file (skip any item whose id/title already appears — kills the circular re-injection case); 0 survivors → no block at all. Dedup of exact-duplicate leaf blocks (keep first) is unchanged. writeSyncResult is the ONLY mutator: backup-to-.bak FIRST, then atomic temp+rename, fail-open on any error (original untouched). Deterministic (no timestamps in the managed block) → two syncs over unchanged inputs are byte-identical. Includes a dependency-free unified-ish line diff for the advisory preview.
