Owns no storage; mutation stays on the write router.

TasksWriteRouter.name: TasksWriteRouter
TasksWriteRouter.description: /api/tasks/* WRITE verbs — POST /:id/{claim,start,done,block,unblock} each PROXY the enforced updateTask state machine (no bypass), plus POST /sync (inbound two-way GitHub reconcile through the same writers). Verbs fire a best-effort outbound GitHub projection; a done settle broadcasts a live agent:annotate. portal.yaml ^write-capable.

WarplineRouter.name: WarplineRouter
WarplineRouter.description: /api/warpline/* — READ-ONLY HTTP over the @a-company/warpline engine (the Convergence/Divergence Oracle), imported in-process (never shells the CLI). GET /ledger (reads .warpline/oracle.jsonl, version-guarded on schemaVersion, newest-first), GET /refs (local branches + HEAD), POST /forecast (ephemeral meaning forecast, no ledger write), POST /oracle (full Oracle, appends ledger), POST /diff (semantic diff), GET /absorb/:ref (serialized WarpState). An in-process concurrency semaphore (cap 2) guards every absorb-spawning handler; a per-ref WarpState cache reuses deterministic absorbs. fs.watch the ledger → !oracle-record-appended over the WS bus. NO git-write/weave path (HEAD/index/worktree untouched), but POST /oracle APPENDS to .warpline/oracle.jsonl — a state mutation declared in portal.yaml as ^write-capable while the reads + ephemeral computes are ^read-only. User refs pass an allowlist validator (REF_RE) and the engine interposes --end-of-options (git-exec) so a leading-dash ref can't be an arg-injection. FABRIC-NATIVE CONSOLE LANE (PHASE 1 re-point, native-first) — five GET-only fabric views, DAEMON-BACKED when warplined serves this fabric — GET /fabric/status (tip + transport mode + daemon status), GET /fabric/refs (native refs/heads + head pickIds), GET /fabric/shadow-tail?n=, GET /fabric/knot/:selector (SELECTOR_RE allowlisted; 404 when none), GET /fabric/grade-report?window=. Transport swap, not a redesign — when .warpline/daemon.sock exists AND the human has minted the read-SCOPED console token (`warpline daemon token mint console --kind human --scope read`, auto-discovered via consoleReadToken which structurally never returns a full-power row), responses ride DaemonClient and are the engine shapes VERBATIM (G3), byte-identical to the in-process fallback (tests/platform-warpline-router.test.ts); no daemon / no token / transport failure falls back in-process (zero breakage; a DaemonRpcError NOT_FOUND is authoritative → 404). Read-only stays LAW at three layers — GET-only route registrations, the read-scoped token, and the daemon's server-side READ_ONLY_VERBS ceiling.

AcademyRouter.name: AcademyRouter
AcademyRouter.description: /api/academy/* — READ-ONLY HTTP over @a-company/university-core (7.11.0, replaces the deleted /api/university router that read JSON course files). GET /packs (discoverPacks + an implicit project pack when .paradigm/university has content but no pack.yaml; per-type counts, sections, skillCount), /packs/:packId/paths, /paths/:id (steps resolved to note/quiz titles), /notes/:id ({frontmatter, body}), /quizzes/:id (WITH answers — the client grades), /skills (#skill-loader listPackSkills; trust always external, never script bodies or dirs), /search?q=&type=&pack=. :packId must match a discovered pack (404); ids must match ^[A-Za-z0-9-]+$ (400); bodies load by id through the core loader with the discovered packRoot — input is never path-joined; no absolute paths leave the server. Engine imports are lazy; a throw becomes 500 { error }. portal.yaml ^local-only + ^read-only. GET /search rejects q longer than 200 characters with 400.

MemoryRouter.name: MemoryRouter
MemoryRouter.description: /api/memory/* — READ-ONLY HTTP over the Memory Steward engines (Phase C1, TD-2026-09-20-669). GET /review calls buildDigest DIRECTLY (never reviewCommand, which writes remediations + a review stamp) → returns the advisory hygiene digest verbatim { root, scanned, pinned, items: DigestItem[] }. GET /sync?projection=true|false calls computeSync (PURE — the only mutator writeSyncResult is not reachable here) + unifiedDiff → returns the lean-rewrite PREVIEW { root, memoryFile, existed, changed, bytesBefore/After, linesBefore/After, demoted[], deduped[], projectionEnabled, projectionItems[], diff } — the full before/after bodies are intentionally WITHHELD (only the diff string). Owns no storage; NO write endpoints (apply/write verbs arrive in C2/C3). Every handler is fail-open — an engine throw becomes 500 { error }, never crashes the server. portal.yaml ^local-only + ^read-only.

MemoryWriteRouter.name: MemoryWriteRouter
MemoryWriteRouter.description: /api/memory/* WRITE verbs (Phase C2/C3, TD-2026-09-20-669) — POST /:id/prune, /:id/route { to }, /merge { ids[] }, /:id/pin each PROXY the SAME return-shaped appliers the CLI wrappers call (applyPrune/applyRoute/applyMerge/applyPin from commands/memory), so ALL path-safety (isInsideMemoryDir), archive-not-delete, and fail-open discipline live in ONE place — a browser POST is just another caller of the enforced core. Validation mirrors tasks-write (bad id → 404; bad route target or merge < 2 ids → 400; other applier failure → 409). POST /sync/write { projection? } is the GATED lean-rewrite apply — computeSync then, only when existed && changed, writeSyncResult (backup-then-atomic on MEMORY.md; original left byte-for-byte intact on any error) → { wrote:true, backupPath, bytesAfter } else { wrote:false }. On a successful mutation best-effort broadcasts memory:changed so an open ledger refreshes live. Owns no storage of its own. portal.yaml ^local-only + ^write-capable.

ClassroomRouter.name: ClassroomRouter
ClassroomRouter.description: /api/classroom/* — READ-ONLY HTTP over the Academy (Classroom) gated-learning artifacts (TD-2026-06-19-007). GET /status (bootstrapped flag = curriculum dir has ≥1 *.syllabus; per-agent syllabi w/ status + certified/provisional counts; cert rollup w/ the HONEST repeatFailureRate = overturned/(survived+overturned), null when 0 resolved), GET /staged (the REAL staged candidates = study-hall JOURNAL entries from the ENROLLED agents only — those with a syllabus — read from each agent's GLOBAL journal ~/.paradigm/agents/<agent>/journal/*.yaml, one item per entry {agent, insight, confidence, trust, source, ts} newest-first; EXCLUDES entries already promoted to the notebook (promoted_to_notebook set) — once an entry graduates it is no longer a staged candidate (T-007); deliberately does NOT read the legacy Ambient nominations firehose — the Academy is the GATED-truth counterpart to Ambient), GET /certifications (cert rows from classroom-certifications.jsonl, each with a derived loop:'gated'|'legacy' from certifiedBy — gate→legacy, peer|quorum→gated, newest-first), GET /refinements (field-failure rows, newest-first), GET /rapsheet (per-certified-entry learning lineage joining the three loop spines — born=cert.ts ⋈ applied=notebook-refs.jsonl by entryId ⋈ broke=field-failures by entryId; each row {entryId, agent, concepts, certifiedBy, loop, outcome, bornTs, appliedCount, lastAppliedAt, breaks[]}; `breaks: []` means UNTESTED, never "passed"; sorted overturned→applied-pending→never-applied), GET /locker (Agent Locker — per-agent notebook vetting scoped to the PROJECT roster = enrolled agents ∪ agents with a project notebook, NOT the whole installed library; each agent's entries read from GLOBAL ~/.paradigm/notebooks/<agent> overlaid with PROJECT .paradigm/notebooks/<agent> deduped by id project-wins; per entry {id, title, source, trust, scope, confidence, appliedCount, brokeCount, publishable, vetted}; trust defaults to 'provisional' when unset so legacy auto-promoted entries read as BACKLOG not VETTED; vetted = trust 'certified'; sorted most-applied-first). Owns no storage; NO write endpoints. Every loader degrades to []/empty rollup on missing/malformed files (never throws on cold start). portal.yaml ^read-only.

BrainRouter.name: BrainRouter
BrainRouter.description: /api/brain/* READ surface for the Platform Brain section (7.14.0). Every handler goes through the single #brain-view choke point openBrainView(rootHash, 'owner') — never the index or brain.yaml directly. GET /overview (brains list; badge from egressSummary — nothingLeft/count/bytes/last; recent egress rows as counts only; map = counts by type / size band / recency band over VISIBLE files; locked zones as {folder, gate, count} only — never filenames; banner = tamper copy when brain.yaml changed outside Paradigm, else null; paused = suggestions auto-paused; sets the HttpOnly SameSite=Strict brain_owner cookie — the owner token is never in a body), GET /health (computeHealth over the owner view → brokenLinks / looseNotes / sameName as plain {id,title,path} rows; links into hidden files are never 'broken'), GET /suggestions (paused flag + nextSuggestions — next ≤10 folder-first with a plain rationale string; also logs the batch to suggestions.jsonl like the CLI), GET /find?q= (view.search over title/heading/path/topic; q > 200 chars → 400; repeated q → 400; the query is NOT echoed back — reflection surface). ?brain=<rootHash> optional (invalid → 400, unknown → 404, default first brain). brainLocalGuard requires a loopback Host, an Origin (when present) EXACTLY equal to the Platform's own origin (Host port == socket port; other localhost ports refused), and Sec-Fetch-Site same-origin|none when present, on EVERY request including GETs; corsMiddleware sets ACAO on /api/brain only for the own origin. portal.yaml ^local-only + ^read-only + ^brain-default-deny.

BrainWriteRouter.name: BrainWriteRouter
BrainWriteRouter.description: /api/brain/verdict WRITE (7.14.0) — POST { suggestionId, verdict: accept|reject|skip, brain? } proxies the SAME recordVerdict the CLI `paradigm brain confirm` calls (accept → declared.yaml backup + atomic write; stale → 409; unknown id → 404). ^brain-owner-write: requires the brain_owner cookie equal (timing-safe) to the per-process owner token AND an Origin exactly equal to the Platform's own origin — otherwise 403 before the body is validated. Also exports brainLocalGuard + isSameOriginBrainRequest + setBrainOwnerCookie + pickBrain + getBrainOwnerToken shared with BrainRouter. Best-effort broadcasts brain:changed. portal.yaml ^local-only + ^write-capable + ^brain-owner-write + ^brain-default-deny.

PlatformWebSocket.name: PlatformWebSocket
PlatformWebSocket.description: WebSocket server with per-client channel subscriptions — broadcast() is channel-routed (channel = the segment before ':' in a message type; a client sends {type:'subscribe',channels:[...]} to narrow, default = all channels for backward compat), plus client tracking and reconnect handling

AgentPresenceManager.name: AgentPresenceManager
AgentPresenceManager.description: Tracks connected agents by ID, auto-prunes after 2min idle, deterministic color assignment

UserStateTracker.name: UserStateTracker
UserStateTracker.description: Accumulates user section/symbol/theme state and highlight/annotation state for observe tool

SymbolPage.name: SymbolPage
SymbolPage.description: Symbol detail page with badge, metadata row, flow steps, related symbols, and source path

FlowPage.name: FlowPage
FlowPage.description: Flow detail page with step timeline, symbol links, and involved symbols grid

PortalPage.name: PortalPage
PortalPage.description: Portal reference with gate cards and HTTP method-colored route table

CategoryListPage.name: CategoryListPage
CategoryListPage.description: Category index page with card grid showing all symbols in a category

ContentPage.name: ContentPage
ContentPage.description: Markdown renderer for handwritten docs pages — headings, code blocks with language headers, tables, inline code, bold, links

help-view.name: Help View
help-view.description: In-app help system with 9-section guide covering Conductor capabilities, menus, shortcuts, and known limitations. Accessible via ? button.

agent-decision.name: Agent Decision
agent-decision.description: Model for a host-rendered branching CHOICE the agent offers the human ($decision-exchange), parsed from a conductor-decision fenced block (#fenced-block-parser). Carries question + 2-5 DecisionOptions (label/description/★recommended/▸visualId/affectedSymbols) + multiSelect/allowOther + an optional top-level `symbols` array (the real graph symbols the decision is about) + an optional settled DecisionAnswer. symbols/affectedSymbols default [] (schema-tolerant) and drive the hover-to-spotlight binding into the LIGHTBOX graph. composeReply() builds the human-readable user turn. Lives on ConversationMessage (additive).

agent-visual.name: Agent Visual
agent-visual.description: Model for a host-rendered DIAGRAM, COMPARISON or GRAPH ($decision-exchange), parsed from a conductor-visual envelope or a bare mermaid/svg fence (#fenced-block-parser). kind flow|comparison|graph render in v1 (LIGHTBOX); graph carries a GraphPayload (root/nodes/edges/truncated/freshness) drawn by #atrium-graph-view; wireframe|diff are decode-tolerant v2 placeholders. Rendered as a ▸ launcher chip — never auto-opens.

atrium-decision-card.name: Atrium Decision Card
atrium-decision-card.description: Inline card rendering an #agent-decision in the ATRIUM thread. PENDING = question + stacked radio/checkbox option cards + Other… field (when allowOther) + escape affordances, AMBER leading rail (Mika's temperature law); on pick calls onAnswer → ClaudeStreamSession.answerDecision. ANSWERED = collapsed teal ✓ you chose <label> with a change/reopen affordance. ★ marks a recommended lean; ▸ view opens a linked visual in the LIGHTBOX. Hovering an option row fires onHoverSymbols(option.affectedSymbols) (empty on hover-out) → spotlights those symbols in the LIGHTBOX graph (#atrium-graph-view); READ-ONLY — clicking is still the only commit path.

atrium-visual-canvas.name: Atrium Visual Canvas
atrium-visual-canvas.description: THE LIGHTBOX — a 380pt right slide-out hosting one #agent-visual. Shares the right zone with the CHORUS rail and renders OVER it (chorus stays mounted; PUSH-consistent layout, conversation column narrows). Switches on kind: flow → MermaidWebView (sandboxed offline WKWebView, vendored mermaid.min.js, NO network, ATRIUM-recolored); comparison → native SwiftUI table (ATRIUM styling); graph → #atrium-graph-view (❖ header glyph); wireframe/diff → v2 placeholder. Takes a plain `highlightedSymbols: Set<String>` (NOT folded into the Equatable #agent-visual) and forwards it to #atrium-graph-view for the decision-option hover spotlight — kept separate so hover only redraws the Canvas, never re-identifies the LIGHTBOX.

atrium-graph-view.name: Atrium Graph View
atrium-graph-view.description: Native SwiftUI Canvas render of a bounded symbol ego-graph (#agent-visual kind == .graph) inside THE LIGHTBOX. STATIC closed-form RING layout: root (focus) at center with a soft halo, other nodes evenly on a ring (angle 2π·i/count, radius shrunk to fit 380pt). Edges draw under nodes as center→ring lines. Node shapes encode GraphSymbolKind via Mika's accent mapping (component→ink rounded rect, flow→user stadium, gate→amber diamond, signal→teal circle, aspect→violet dashed). Labels = symbol id, scaled off atriumFontScale. Footer shows +N-more (truncated) + stale-index. HOVER SPOTLIGHT (Phase-2c): a plain `highlightedSymbols: Set<String>` (driven by decision-option hover) lights matching nodes at full saturation + a brighter amber ring and DIMS all others to ~40% (edges between two lit nodes draw amber); an animated dimPhase eases the room dim in/out over ~150ms on hover-in/out. READ-ONLY — never selects/commits; an empty set renders at rest. NO force sim, drag, or zoom.

mermaid-web-view.name: Mermaid Web View
mermaid-web-view.description: Sandboxed WKWebView that renders a mermaid diagram OFFLINE from a vendored mermaid.min.js (Resources/, loaded via #conductor-resources to dodge the SwiftTerm Bundle.module collision). nil baseURL, navigation blocked except the in-memory load, ATRIUM dark theme. Degrades to a source dump if the script is missing from the bundle.

AcademySection.name: AcademySection
AcademySection.description: Academy section in the Platform UI (7.11.0, T-2026-09-26-003) — the home of University content packs, replacing the retired standalone University UI. Three columns: pack list, then the selected pack's learning paths (or one path's steps) plus its pack-skills table, then a reading pane that renders a note or runs a quiz. Read-only: nothing is written server-side.

PackList.name: PackList
PackList.description: Clickable list of discovered packs with id, tenant kind, per-type content counts and skill count.

PathView.name: PathView
PathView.description: PathList (a pack's learning paths) and PathView (one path's ordered steps, resolved to note/quiz titles; notes and quizzes open in the reading pane; plsat/missing steps are shown but not openable; local quiz results inline).

NoteView.name: NoteView
NoteView.description: Renders a note's markdown body with the Platform's shared renderMarkdown (sections/docs/renderMarkdown.ts; HTML-escaped first; code fences + lists supported).

QuizRunner.name: QuizRunner
QuizRunner.description: Client-side quiz runner. Weighted score vs the quiz passThreshold, shows the right answers + explanations after submit, supports retry. Results are recorded through academyStore.recordResult (localStorage only).

PackSkills.name: PackSkills
PackSkills.description: Read-only table of skills a pack ships (/api/academy/packs/:packId/skills), labelled "external — not active" with the `paradigm skill import` hint; notes when a project/global copy shadows the pack skill.

academyStore.name: AcademyStore
academyStore.description: Zustand store for the Academy (mirrors memoryStore's fetch/abort pattern). Mirrors the /api/academy shapes: packs, selected pack's paths + skills, the open path, and the reading pane (note | quiz). Quiz results keyed `${packId}:${quizId}` persist to localStorage (`paradigm-academy-results`), every read/write wrapped in try/catch.

BrainSection.name: BrainSection
BrainSection.description: Brain section in the Platform UI (7.14.0, T-2026-09-29-002). Header shows the folder name, last-looked time, a brain picker when there is more than one, and the PrivacyBadge. Two-column body: Map + Private & Locked on the left; Find, Suggestions and Health on the right. Empty state when no brain exists: "Run `paradigm brain init <folder>` to get started". Never shows symbol sigils, gate ids or config words — every internal term goes through labels.ts. Live refresh on brain:changed (forwarded as a brain-ws CustomEvent by useAgentEffects, debounced); never resets a suggestion batch in progress. Paused-vs-off suggestions copy via suggestionsOffCopy.

PrivacyBadge.name: PrivacyBadge
PrivacyBadge.description: "Nothing has left this Mac" (green) or "N things shared → see what left" (amber) which expands the recent egress rows (when, how many notes, to whom, bytes — never file names).

BrainMapPanel.name: BrainMapPanel
BrainMapPanel.description: Counts of browsable files by type, size band and last-changed band, with proportional bars.

LockedPanel.name: LockedPanel
LockedPanel.description: Private & Locked — a lock icon plus a count per locked folder and a plain kind label (Health records / Money & taxes / Other people's messages / Passwords & keys). Never filenames; the server only sends {folder, gate, count}.

HealthPanel.name: HealthPanel
HealthPanel.description: Three collapsible buckets — Broken links, Loose notes, Same-name notes — off /api/brain/health.

SuggestionsPanel.name: SuggestionsPanel
SuggestionsPanel.description: Batched (≤10) suggested labels with the rationale beside each. Keyboard triage: A keep, R dismiss, S skip, ↑/↓ or j/k to move (ignored while typing). Each verdict POSTs /api/brain/verdict with the owner token and advances to the next undecided row; shows past acceptance when known.

FindPanel.name: FindPanel
FindPanel.description: Search box (≤200 chars) over titles, headings, locations and topics of browsable notes via /api/brain/find; shows which field matched.

brain-labels.name: Brain Labels
brain-labels.description: labels.ts — React-free plain-language label tables (gate → kind label, type/size/recency/match labels, badge text, plainText sigil stripper). Tested in labels.test.ts, which also scans the section's JSX text for sigils / config words.

brainStore.name: BrainStore
brainStore.description: Zustand store for the Brain section (mirrors academyStore's getJson pattern). load(brain?) → GET /api/brain/overview (remembered brain in localStorage `paradigm-brain-selected`, try/catch wrapped; falls back to the default when the remembered one is gone), then health + suggestions. decide(verdict) POSTs /api/brain/verdict with credentials same-origin — the owner token rides only in the HttpOnly brain_owner cookie set by GET /overview (never readable from script). Overview carries banner (tamper copy or null) and paused. find(q) aborts the previous search and caps q at 200 chars.

DocsSection.name: DocsSection
DocsSection.description: Documentation browser in Platform UI — sidebar navigation, symbol pages, flow diagrams, portal reference

renderMarkdown.name: RenderMarkdown
renderMarkdown.description: Shared escape-first markdown renderer (renderMarkdown.ts, React-free; re-exported from DocsCustomPage) used by Docs pages and the Academy NoteView. Escapes & < > before emitting any tag and never builds attributes or links. v7.11 adds fenced ``` code blocks (<pre><code>, verbatim, no language attribute), - / * bullet lists and 1. numbered lists. Tested in renderMarkdown.test.ts (incl. <script> inside a code block stays escaped).

MemorySection.name: MemorySection
MemorySection.description: Memory Steward ledger section in the Platform UI (Phase C1 + C2/C3, TD-2026-09-20-669). Header band shows scanned/pinned/findings counts off the /api/memory/review digest. Two-column body: a Ledger (the advisory hygiene digest grouped by suggestion in the CLI's heading order — prune / merge / route:habits / route:task / route:decisions / route:lore / pin) beside the SyncPreviewPanel. fetchReview on mount. Surfaces the store's single last actionError as a dismissible inline banner above the ledger. Rows carry one-click apply buttons (C2) and the sync panel carries the gated --write apply (C3).

LedgerGroup.name: LedgerGroup
LedgerGroup.description: One suggestion bucket in the ledger. Renders the CLI's SUGGESTION_HEADINGS label (reused verbatim so the web ledger reads identically to `paradigm memory review`) + a count, then a column of LedgerRows. Self-hides when the bucket is empty.

LedgerRow.name: LedgerRow
LedgerRow.description: A single memory-entry finding — name, staleness score (0–1, color-ramped), graph-validity verdict, rationale, the equivalent applyCommand as a code chip, and (C2) a one-click apply button driven by the row's suggestion (prune → prune; route:* → route with the matching to; merge → merge the whole cluster; pin → pin) via store.applyRow. Prune confirms first (it archives a file). While any row action is in flight all buttons disable.

SyncPreviewPanel.name: SyncPreviewPanel
SyncPreviewPanel.description: The lean-rewrite PREVIEW off /api/memory/sync (computeSync is pure — no write). Shows bytesBefore→bytesAfter, lines, changed/already-lean status, demoted[] leaf entries (heading + reason + applyHint), deduped[] blocks, a projection checkbox that refetches with projection=true and lists projectionItems[], and the unified diff in a monospace scroll box. (C3) When the preview would change MEMORY.md it exposes an explicit "Apply sync (--write)" button that confirms, POSTs /api/memory/sync/write with the current projection toggle, and on success shows the backupPath + refetches the preview. Makes clear it writes MEMORY.md (backed up first).

memoryStore.name: MemoryStore
memoryStore.description: Zustand store for the Memory section (mirrors tasksStore's fetch/abort + runAction pattern). Holds the review digest + the sync preview (each with its own AbortController + loading/error state) and the projection toggle. fetchReview → GET /api/memory/review; fetchSync(projection) → GET /api/memory/sync?projection=. (C2/C3) applyRow(item) maps the suggestion → the matching write endpoint (prune/route/merge/pin), POSTs, and on success re-fetches BOTH review + sync; actionPendingId/actionError drive per-row pending + inline error. applySyncWrite() POSTs /api/memory/sync/write and holds syncWriting + syncWriteResult{ wrote, backupPath, bytesAfter }.

TasksSection.name: TasksSection
TasksSection.description: Tasks section shell in Platform UI — header band (title + live "{n} open · {n} in-flight · {n} unclaimed" stat off board.summary) and a Board|List|Inbox ViewSwitcher. Defaults to Board. The Board renders a four-tab sub-tab bar (BoardTabs: State | Claimant | Symbol/Flow | Calibration, State default). The three lane tabs render the FilterBar + BoardView (grouped by boardTab) with the lanes filling full viewport height; the Calibration tab renders the full-area calibration grid (CalibrationStrip variant='tab') with NO FilterBar and NO lanes. List renders the ListView; Inbox the InboxView. 10s section-guarded poll drives fetchTasks + fetchBoard + fetchCalibration. Also subscribes to the `tasks-ws` CustomEvent (forwarded from the central WS hub useAgentEffects, which relays tasks:* server broadcasts) — on tasks:synced / tasks:sync-conflict it refreshes fetchBoard()+fetchTasks()(+inbox) so poll-driven reconciliations appear live without a user click.

TaskCard.name: TaskCard
TaskCard.description: Card cloning the lore-card structure — priority + status chips, line-clamped title, the prominent CalibrationBlock, a claimant chip colored via the shared AGENT_COLORS map, a fragile/symbol tag row, and a GitHub badge when external_ref.provider is github. When a card has no actual claimant but carries a proposedClaimant (Cid's suggested owner on unclaimed tasks), it renders a subtle dashed "→ {ref}" hint in that claimant's color — distinct from a real claim chip. Round D — clickable (onClick → store.openDetail(id), keyboard-accessible), an optional elevated `hero` variant for the Inbox, and live agent-effect registration via useTaskAgentEffect (symbol-matched pulse/color/label + badge stamps; keyed by taskId so the 10s poll re-render doesn't detach the highlight).

CalibrationBlock.name: CalibrationBlock
CalibrationBlock.description: The calibration moat made visible. SIZE tracks confidence — learned estimates lead with a big (32px) green Fibonacci story-point + a green LEARNED badge (◆ + n{count}); prior cold-start guesses LEAD with the dimmed italic ~prior~ label and demote the number to a recessed ~17px secondary value so a guess never out-shouts a learned band. Both render the raw token band plus a small muted cell caption (claimant-archetype × taskType, e.g. "builder×feature") mapping the estimate back to the calibration grid.

tasksStore.name: TasksStore
tasksStore.description: Zustand store for the Tasks section (mirrors loreStore). Holds list, board, calibration, inbox, detail, filter, boardTab and dep-cache state, each fetch with its own AbortController; default view is board. boardTab is the Board's sub-tab ('state' default | 'claimant' | 'symbol' | 'calibration'), persisted to localStorage key paradigm.tasks.boardTab with graceful migration from the legacy paradigm.tasks.laneMode key; setBoardTab updates it. BoardView derives its laneMode from boardTab for the three lane tabs. Read fetches hit the /api/tasks read routes; Task/BoardNode/BoardUnclaimed carry the computed estimate + taskType. The UI's ONLY write verbs live here — claimTask, startTask, doneTask, blockTask, unblockTask all POST the enforced /api/tasks/:id action endpoints (which proxy the updateTask state machine), and syncGitHub posts /api/tasks/sync for two-way reconcile; each refreshes board/list/inbox on success and surfaces a transient actionError/sync summary. BoardData also carries the three optional Cid/Loid governance detections (integrity, settlementDebt, staleClaims) passed through to BoardHealth.

TaskActions.name: TaskActions
TaskActions.description: Shared status-aware write-verb row rendered by both the InboxView hero and the TaskDetailPanel header — the single mutation surface in the Tasks UI. Respects the v7 task state machine so it never offers a verb that would 409 — open → [Start] + [Claim to me] (shown only when unclaimed or already held by the viewer; passes the human ref from /whoami, kind:'human') + [Done] + [Block]; in-progress → [Done] + [Block]; done/shelved are terminal (no verbs); blocked_on set → a reason banner + [Unblock] (orthogonal to status). Block opens a window.prompt for the reason. Wires each button to the matching tasksStore action and renders store.actionError as a dismissable inline error (e.g. the 409 "cannot displace a human/peer claim"). Buttons disable while an action is in flight.

storyPoints.name: StoryPoints
storyPoints.description: Pure helper tokenBandToPoints({min,max}) → Fibonacci story point (1/2/3/5/8/13/21) by mapping the band midpoint through tunable token thresholds (POINT_THRESHOLDS), to be re-fit against real actuals later.

board-utils.name: Board Utils
board-utils.description: Board helpers — AGENT_COLORS (verbatim from TeamSection) + claimantColor() which resolves a claimant ref to its Team color via a CLAIMANT_ALIAS map (cid→architect, forge→builder, compliance→security; role words map to themselves) so a claimant's lane color === their Team color, with a widened hashed-fallback (S/L jitter) keeping unknown refs mutually distinct; claimantArchetype() exposes the same ref→archetype resolution for calibration-cell matching. Plus deriveSymbols()/firstSymbol() (tags + blurb-parsed

BoardView.name: BoardView
BoardView.description: Horizontally-scrollable row of SwimLanes off /api/tasks/board, filling full viewport height (each lane's card column scrolls internally). The lane mode is derived from the active board sub-tab (boardTab): laneMode='state' (the default tab) = open/in-progress/done/shelved kanban; 'claimant' = one lane per claimant.ref + trailing Unclaimed lane (hidden entirely when 0 cards) + collapsed Done lane; 'symbol' = grouped by each card's first derived symbol. Honors store status/priority/search + calibrationFilter — the cell filter matches the task's real taskType field against the cell column and the claimant's resolved archetype against the cell row; a 0-match cell click shows a specific "No {taskType} tasks claimed by {archetype} yet" empty state. Renders the BoardHealth advisory banner above the lanes — it self-hides when the board carries no governance detections. The lane sub-tab bar lives in TasksSection (BoardTabs), not here.

BoardHealth.name: BoardHealth
BoardHealth.description: Compact collapsible ADVISORY banner at the top of BoardView surfacing the three Cid/Loid governance detections the backend attaches to the board — integrity (DAG defects: self-parent / dangling / cycle), settlementDebt (children all terminal but the epic never settled), and staleClaims (archetype-claimed open tasks past 7 days). Amber, never error-red, never blocking. Self-hides entirely when the board is healthy. Collapsed by default to a count summary (persisted to localStorage); expanded it lists each detection grouped by kind, and clicking a row with a taskId opens that task's detail panel.

SwimLane.name: SwimLane
SwimLane.description: Single vertical board lane — colored header (label + presence dot + card count + SUMMED story points) using AGENT_COLORS, a scrollable column of TaskCards sorted in-progress-first then priority-desc, collapsible via chevron with per-lane localStorage persistence.

BoardTabs.name: BoardTabs
BoardTabs.description: The Board's sub-tab bar — four tabs in order State | Claimant | Symbol/Flow | Calibration (State is the default), styled with the shared segmented .view-tab idiom. Active tab = store.boardTab; clicking sets boardTab via setBoardTab. Replaces the old LaneModeToggle pill.

FilterBar.name: FilterBar
FilterBar.description: Tasks filter bar lifted from lore's pattern — status dropdown, priority dropdown, search-blurb input wired to store filter state, plus a clearable active-filter chip surfacing the calibrationFilter (archetype×taskType) when set.

CalibrationStrip.name: CalibrationStrip
CalibrationStrip.description: The calibration moat surface off /api/tasks/calibration, with two rendering modes via a variant prop. variant='tab' (the Calibration sub-tab, current usage): a coverage header ("{pct}% calibrated cells · {graduated} of {total} graduated") + the full CellGrid filling the available height (scrolls when tall), with no collapse chrome; on cold-start it shows a "learning in progress" badge + the "Run `paradigm calibrate`…" CTA. Clicking a cell sets the calibrationFilter AND switches boardTab to 'state' so the filtered lanes show. variant='strip' (legacy) is the default-ON collapsible hero strip above the board — coverage StatCard + CellGrid, collapse persisted to localStorage with a glanceable collapsed summary, force-expanded on full cold-start so the differentiated artifact never starts hidden.

CellGrid.name: CellGrid
CellGrid.description: Calibration matrix — archetype rows × taskType columns. Learned cells render solid + agent-color tint + a ● dot + compact band ("3–13" n24); PRIOR cells encode progress-to-graduation (a cell graduates at n>=8) as a live ramp — fill width + cell opacity + border tint ramp by min(n,8)/8 toward the archetype color, and an in-cell "{n}/8" tick reads the sample count directly, so a cell accumulating actuals (n=5) looks visibly closer to graduating than an empty one (n=0). The grid answers "where is the team about to learn something," not just "nothing yet." Clicking a cell toggles the store calibrationFilter that BoardView honors and FilterBar surfaces as a chip; an optional onCellSelect callback fires when a cell is selected (used by the Calibration tab to switch back to the State lanes).

InboxView.name: InboxView
InboxView.description: The Inbox tab — the AGENT FACE. A claimant pill-row (a "Me" pill resolved via /api/tasks/whoami + one AGENT_COLORS-tinted pill per distinct board claimant) selects whose inbox to focus via fetchInbox(kind, ref). The focused column shows a rolled-up calibration header ("calibration {pct}% · n={total}", share of source==='learned') — suppressed to "—" for human claimants, whose learned bands are archetype-keyed so a % would be a category error, a NEXT-ACTIONABLE hero card (highest-priority in-progress-or-open, not blocked) elevated on top, a DependsChain ribbon under the hero (●done → ●this → ○next) that resolves each dependsOn id first from the loaded board/inbox pool (now incl. board.loose) and, for cross-run ids not in that pool, lazily via store.resolveDep → GET /api/tasks/:id (deduped + cached in store.depCache; a cached null = a genuine 404) so deps render "unknown" only after a fetch truly fails rather than for any out-of-pool id, then the rest as a queued list of TaskCards. Cold-start default landing is the human's ("Me") inbox; empty claimants render "inbox zero". Round E renders a TaskActions row directly under the hero card so the valid write verbs (start/claim/done/block) act from the agent face.

GitHubSyncStrip.name: GitHubSyncStrip
GitHubSyncStrip.description: Persistent Board-tab footer. Aggregates external_ref state across visible board tasks — synced (provider==='github' && url) and push-pending (github && no url), both derived from real external_ref state (the always-0 "drifted" placeholder was dropped as less honest than its absence). The PRIMARY action is now a REAL two-way Sync button (Round F) — on click it calls store.syncGitHub() → POST /api/tasks/sync (no client body; the server pulls each linked GitHub issue and reconciles it back through the enforced state machine, 100% server-side) and disables with a spinner ("Syncing…") while in flight. On return it renders a transient inline summary off store.lastSyncSummary in one of three tones — success ("✓ Synced N · M unchanged" in green; a quiet "Up to date" on a 0-change result); CONFLICT (amber --p-accent-amber, never error-red — conflict means local won and a human should look — with the conflicted task ids as clickable chips → store.openDetail(id)); OFFLINE (calm "GitHub not available — `gh auth login` to enable sync" hint when every verdict is offline/skipped or the request failed, NOT a red failure). After a sync that applied changes the store re-runs fetchBoard()+fetchTasks()(+fetchInbox if a claimant is focused) so changes show immediately. A small "via CLI" SECONDARY affordance remains — opens a popover that clipboard-copies `paradigm task sync` as a fallback for users without the server. The client never sends task/remote state.

TaskDetailPanel.name: TaskDetailPanel
TaskDetailPanel.description: Right-slide detail panel cloning lore's .detail-overlay/.detail-panel. Opened by clicking any TaskCard (store.openDetail(id)); fetches GET /api/tasks/:id (seeded instantly from the already-loaded board/inbox/list pool). Shows full blurb, the dependsOn DAG (ids + resolved states), the estimate breakdown (token band + LEARNED/prior provenance + n), fragileSymbols/tags chips, a GitHub section (ref + link when url present), and related_lore ids. Round E renders a TaskActions row in the header area so the write verbs work from any view (board/list click → detail → act); the panel re-seeds its local task from the refreshed store pool after a verb so the status-aware action row updates without a manual refetch. Closes on backdrop click / Esc.

useTaskAgentEffect.name: UseTaskAgentEffect
useTaskAgentEffect.description: Hook consuming the shared agentStore the SAME way the platform's agent-effect protocol works — matched by SYMBOL (not taskId). A card registers its derived symbols (board.deriveSymbols) and intersects them against agentStore.highlights[].symbols (pulse + color + label) and agentStore.annotations of type 'badge' (symbol-targeted badge stamps). Mute clears agentStore, so a muted session yields no card effects for free.

WarplineSection.name: WarplineSection
WarplineSection.description: Warpline section shell (sub-phase 2) — the Oracle Divergence Viewer. Lays out the OracleLedgerRail (left) beside the OracleDivergenceViewer (right). On mount fetches GET /api/warpline/ledger?limit=200 (selecting the newest row) and GET /api/warpline/refs (for the picker). Run posts /api/warpline/oracle (records → prepends + selects) and Preview posts /api/warpline/forecast {vsGit:true} (ephemeral, adapted via forecastToRecord, never added to the rail). Subscribes to the `warpline-ws` CustomEvent (forwarded by useAgentEffects from the `warpline:*` server broadcast) — on `warpline:oracle-record-appended` it prepends the new record (deduped by rowKey) so a live run repaints without a poll. All read-only; the UI never constructs a write/weave call.

OracleLedgerRail.name: OracleLedgerRail

Each row shows branchA→branchB (ledgerRowLabel) · verdict · ts; DIVERGENT rows (isDivergentRow) carry a seam-violet dot. Clicking a row selects it (rowKey identity) → drives the viewer. Run is disabled until two distinct branches are picked.

OracleDivergenceViewer.name: OracleDivergenceViewer
OracleDivergenceViewer.description: THE screen where "git sees bytes, Warpline sees meaning" is the whole page. Composes RunHeader (branchA ◀ weave ▶ branchB + mergeBase + ts), MeaningVsBytesSplit (the hero — a hard 50/50 split: LEFT bytes/git monospace with a CLEAN ✓ / CONFLICT chip off gitReality.conflicted; a 1px center violet SEAM that pulses on headline divergence; RIGHT meaning/warp serif with a DIVERGENT/CLEAN chip off convergence.verdict + knot/dangle tally), ConfusionMatrix (a literal 2×2 git×meaning whose 4 cells bind convergence.{agreeClean,divergeGitOnly,divergeMeaningOnly,agreeConflict}; each cell clickable to expand its real symbol keys; the divergeMeaningOnly cell is the ★, the only cell that glows — static box-shadow, never animated, no count-up), VerdictCard (verdict + score ALWAYS beside the raw agree/git-only/ meaning-only counts + a templated consequence line from dangling[0] or knots[0]) and DivergencePanel (a KnotRender per prediction.knots — two intent threads A=--warp/B=--weft cinching a knot glyph, conflictingSlots incl. the code-lens 'body' slot; a DangleRender per prediction.dangling — a severed thread drifting into a dashed violet void labeled danglingTargetSymbol + retiredBy). CONVERGENT/empty renders the calm "No knots. No dangles. The weave is clean." Includes a basic DrillDown slide-over (knot essenceA/essenceB + slots, or dangle from→target). All four hero states are chosen purely from real OracleRecord fields (heroState).

warpline-viewer-state.name: Warpline Viewer State
warpline-viewer-state.description: The React-free PURE binding layer (viewerState.ts). Maps real OracleRecord fields onto UI decisions: heroState (the 4-state mood), isHeadlineDivergence (divergeMeaningOnly>0 — lights the ★ + pulses the seam), gitChip/meaningChip, matrixCells (the literal 2×2 with per-cell symbol keys + the ★ flag), rawCounts, consequenceLine (dangle-first templated line), isCalm + CALM_DIVERGENCE_COPY, ledgerRowLabel/isDivergentRow/rowKey, knotDrill/dangleDrill, and forecastToRecord (adapts a vsGit Forecast to an ephemeral OracleRecord for Preview). Unit-tested in a node env (viewerState.test.ts) against a DIVERGENT and a CONVERGENT sample — keeps "the number can't lie" falsifiability a pure asserted function.

voice-turn.name: Voice Turn
voice-turn.description: One spoken turn (spec §14.2). User side: AudioIO frames, then the PTT held span or a VAD segment, then the gates (attached, mode within the ceiling, outside every playback window plus 750 ms), then STT, then speaker verification, then log.append voice.turn.user{turnId, speakerId, speakerEnrolled, forwarded, mode, aec, aecTransport, t0, t1, text}, then session.send content [{text}] for enrolled speakers only. Unknown speakers are logged with no text. A refusal is shown and never retried. Agent side: log.read follow, then the speakable rows the kernel writes (voice.turn.agent{source: kernel-speakable, turnSeq, items}), then Kokoro one sentence at a time, then play, then voice.turn.agent{t0, t1, textPlanned, textSpoken}. Barge-in: speech past the barge-in threshold (configured), or the talk key, stops playback and drops the rest of the reply. Live words (B1): while a segment is heard, anchored tail-window decodes (decodeAsync, one in flight, busy ticks skipped) fold into LocalAgreement-2; after a provisional speaker match on the first 1.5 s they ride hearing / transcribing capture reports as text{committed, tail}, shown only in the GUI ghost line (gui credential); they never reach log.append, voice.turn.user or session.send, and the turn's text stays the full-segment decode.

daemon-lifecycle.name: Daemon Lifecycle
daemon-lifecycle.description: $daemon-lifecycle (spec §2.4; PR-5 core of M1.9). (1) client activation — `gnomon daemon --detach` re-execs gnomond with the clean env and home in argv, then waits for its ready line (item 3 below); (2) one per user — home 0700 read back, endpoint path chosen (never /tmp), O_EXCL daemonPid:v1 pidfile acquired (live holder refuses with daemon.lock.refused, dead holder reclaimed; Aegis L2: an EPERM holder — another user's pid — is residue and reclaimed, and a same-user live holder is `already-running` only if a kernel answers hello on OUR socket within 2 s, else `holder-silent`, transient, pidfile left alone — a silent holder may be a racer — UNLESS its `ps -o lstart=` start witness (TZ=UTC) lies more than a 2 s tolerance (HOLDER_START_TOLERANCE_MS, a configured bound) after the pidfile's startedAt: a recycled pid after a crash or reboot, so the pidfile is reclaimed (pid+startedAt+inode re-checked, at most once, daemon.lock.reclaimed emitted; T-2026-10-19-017); no witness or an unparseable startedAt stays holder-silent); (3) #kernel-log opened with the kernel key (M1.4 seam: a supplied or ephemeral in-memory software Ed25519 key, custody partial; keystore item is M1.3) and the root authority (default unprovisioned), #socket listens at 0600 with the hello/auth dispatcher, daemon.start is emitted AND logged (daemon.exit logged at shutdown, then the log is closed before the lock is released); (4) idle exit — no open connections for idleMs (default 10 min) ⇒ daemon.exit{reason: 'idle'}, socket closed, pidfile and socket released only if still ours; SIGTERM/SIGINT take the same path with reason 'signal'. Since M1.4 slice 2 every log.read{follow} subscription is an idle holder ('subscriber') and the hub is closed first at shutdown. Not yet built: sessions/timers as holders, mod stop, orphan sweep, the Windows pipe. M1.4: the #web-endpoint is started by requestWebLaunch, its WebSocket connections are idle holders, and it is stopped (child ended) before the socket closes at shutdown. M1.9: (5) home — the daemon takes its home only from --home (daemonHomeOf; GNOMON_HOME is a client-side test seam it never reads — both gnomond paths, foreground and detaching; only `gnomon` client commands honour the seam); (6) orphan sweep at start, before the socket listens — every KERNEL-written session.spawned with no session.exited/orphaned is recorded session.orphaned{probe, action} BEFORE any signal, and its group is signalled only when the row's boot session (log/boot.ts) equals this boot AND the live leader's start-time witness (process-control.ts: macOS ps lstart, Linux /proc stat field 22, read with TZ=UTC before any await at track; ps forks — never on a hot path; win32 = parity phase, never signalled) equals the recorded one — else probe stale-boot | unattributable, action none; orphans stopped in parallel, counted only when gone (G-DMN-04); (7) supervised children (DaemonChildren: session, local-runner, mod) — intend() writes session.spawned{phase:'intent'} before the fork, track() writes {phase:'running', pid, pgid, boot, startTime} and refuses a session child that does not lead its own group; sessions write session.exited and hold idle ('session'); mods never hold, and have no spawn/exit kinds in §9.1, so a crash-orphaned mod is not swept (residual); stop = SIGTERM → grace → SIGKILL, then group members outliving the leader are SIGKILLed and counted; every shutdown (idle included) stops the scheduler, then stops and AWAITS every child (mod.stopped{reason}) and the web transport child (socket.web.stop{reason:'idle'|'daemon-exit'}) BEFORE daemon.exit {reason, liveChildren} is written — the falsifier "daemon exits with a live child"; (8) idle holders are connections, subscribers (log.read follow AND open GUI WebSockets), sessions and #scheduler timers due inside 10 min. Not yet built: the session runner and mod host that call children.track (M1.7/M1.8/M1.11), the Windows pipe, job object and owner-only DACL read-back (G-WIN-02, parity phase P8-D78). T-2026-10-18-030 (1): the clean re-exec passes exactly one node flag, --disable-sigusr1 (env.ts DISABLE_SIGUSR1 / reexecArgs), and runForeground refuses to start without it in execArgv ([sigusr1-enabled]) — a same-user kill -USR1 would otherwise open the V8 inspector in the key-holding process; a JS SIGUSR1 listener never counts. Both bins use `#!/usr/bin/env -S node --disable-sigusr1`. Falsifier: a running gnomond receiving SIGUSR1 opens no inspector and keeps running (test/daemon-lifecycle.test.ts, control arm proves the detector). A SEA must bake the flag into sea-config execArgv. T-2026-10-19-009 item 1 (descendant sweep): before the first signal a session / local-runner stop takes an ASYNC process-table snapshot from the kernel (process-control snapshot(): `ps -A -o pid=,ppid=,pgid=,lstart=`, TZ=UTC, execFile — never spawnSync on the event loop), collects the leader's descendants (ppid walk) and group members with their lstart witnesses, SIGTERMs out-of-group ones with the group, and after the grace SIGKILLs only pids whose witness still matches (a recycled pid is never signalled). session.exited{tree} = exited | alive | unverifiable (no snapshot / failed re-check / win32 ⇒ unverifiable, never folded). Residual: a descendant reparented to init before the stop began is unreachable; lstart is 1 s resolution. A leader already gone at snapshot time with no group member left ⇒ unverifiable + treeDetail 'leader-gone-before-stop', never exited. stopAll takes ONE snapshot for all its children (T-2026-10-19-011), not one `ps` per child; a single stop takes its own. T-2026-10-19-009 item 3 (readiness handshake, Orca Adopt 3): the activator (lifecycle/ready.ts launchDaemon, used by `gnomon daemon --detach` and plain gnomond) spawns the kernel with an inherited ready pipe (`--ready-fd 3`) and a bounded stderr tail (8 KiB; after an exit the tail is judged once stderr ends, waiting at most 250 ms); the kernel writes one gnomonReady:v1 {pid, startedAt, socketPath, kernelPrincipal} line once it holds the lock and serves, then stops writing events to the activator's stderr (EPIPE swallowed). No socket polling. A child that exits superseded (lost lock race) or transient before ready makes the activator wait for the winner's socket and report `attached` (exit 0, no error); no ready line on a live child (Windows fallback) = socket probing until the GLOBAL deadline. Probes are a 1 s `hello` RPC (not a bare connect) and every probe loop stops once the launch settles. Our own live child owning the socket (pidfile names it) at the deadline = timeout, never attached. The ready line is capped at 4 KiB and must name the child pid AND the expected socketPath, else it is rejected (noted in the tail). kernelPrincipal from it is an unauthenticated hint, never pinned (only M1.4 mutual auth authenticates). gnomond seals the inherited ready fd first thing (sealReadyFd: re-open via /proc/self/fd or /dev/fd with O_CLOEXEC, close the inheritable one; unsealable => closed) so the identity helper and web child cannot forge it. Linux (libuv's stdio pipe is a socketpair /proc/self/fd cannot re-open) uses the 'fifo' channel instead (T-2026-10-19-011): a private 0600 FIFO in a fresh 0700 mkdtemp dir, read end opened by the activator before the spawn, only its path passed (`--ready-fifo`), the kernel opens the write end O_CLOEXEC (FIFO/owner/mode/inode checked, its parent dir ours and 0700 (Aegis L2), O_NOFOLLOW) and unlinks the name first thing, the activator removes the dir at settle; mkfifo runs by absolute path (/usr/bin, then /bin, never PATH); a FIFO failure passes NO ready channel (never the unsealable fd, Aegis L1): the tail and the attached outcome's readyDowngrade record `ready fifo unavailable: <code>; probing the socket` and the socket is probed until the global deadline. macOS keeps the sealed fd (kqueue never reports the FIFO writer's close, losing the no-ready-line fallback). Residual: win32 handle inheritance; pid + socketPath pin applies on every channel. `gnomon daemon status` PINS (T-2026-10-19-016(a)): an unpinned hello learns only the CLAIMED serverKeyId; the pin is read from the home (root-signed registry kernel row, else keys/kernel-pub.jsonl = pinSource home-kernel-pub, same-user custody partial) and a fresh pinned hello must verify, then `running:true, serverVerified:true, pinSource`. A key the home does not know prints `running:null, answering:true, serverVerified:false` with clientApi/serverKeyId only under `unverified` (exit 0); a known key whose serverSig fails is refused (exit 1). Never running:true on an unverified hello. Aegis L4: KernelLog.open runs after the pidfile lock and BEFORE the socket is published (the sweep, dispatcher and pre-auth rows need the log first; a refused open must not leave a served endpoint). Its exclusivity rests on the pidfile lock, which assumes same uid and same pid namespace for every contender; a home shared across pid namespaces is unsupported (a holder there can look dead and be reclaimed). Exit codes are defined ONLY in lifecycle/exit-codes.ts: 0 ok, 4 superseded, 64 usage, 70 internal, 75 transient, 78 config; config/superseded never restart, transient and internal restart with backoff. Every LifecycleRefusalReason is classified by a Record (a new reason is a compile error until it is). Tests: test/daemon-ready.test.ts (POSIX, registry row), test/daemon-exit-codes.test.ts (every platform).

The lens only reads the tree — the Phase-1 read-only invariant holds.

computeEssences over the merged .purpose+code universe (code-units take the <algo>:ts<exact> tag, e.g. v1.1:ts5.9.3; .purpose stays v0)
buildWarpState stamps each object's contentId and derives the stateId; remove the worktree in a finally

Absorb the working tree, diff against the parent selvage (the source of truth for change), no-op on an empty diff, else seal a #strand, persist the snapshot, append to the #fabric ledger, and advance the selvage atomically. Writes .warpline/ only — git is read for provenance (HEAD sha, user.name) and never mutated.

steps.name: Lift the working tree (or a ref) to a WarpState of MEANING
readSelvage — the parent tip (null at genesis)
diff(parent, current) — empty ⇒ no-op; else summarize born/retired/contract-changed/renamed
putState — durably persist the snapshot under .warpline/states/
Seal the #strand (attribution + reserved confidence + git-HEAD anchor); appendStrand; writeSelvage (atomic publish)

offer-accept.name: Offer Accept

setup-token.name: Setup Token
setup-token.description: Gnomon setup mode one-shot token (spec §11.2 rule 11, T-2026-10-19-005). The #setup-endpoint mints ONE 32-byte token per endpoint, 60 s TTL, single use, carried only in the URL fragment (#setup=<tok>&k=<spki>) on the TTY line or the Gnomon.app wrapper channel pipe; never argv, env, files or logs. The setup WebSocket (exact Origin, Host 127.0.0.1:<port>) is refused every gnomon-setup:v1 call before auth {setupToken}; a second connection is refused, and a reuse inside the TTL aborts provisioning and journals setup.token-reuse without the token. No gnomon-rpc verb is reachable on this endpoint.

unprovisioned-only.name: Unprovisioned Only
unprovisioned-only.description: Gnomon first-run provisions only a home with NO keys/identity.json (spec §2.4 rule 9). An existing identity is shown (createdAt, root keyId) and never adopted or replaced; a malformed one is shown, never touched; a dev or symlinked home is refused. The writes allowed on a provisioned home are the I10 completion of a missing device registry row (the saved, already root-signed row; no new signature) and setup.purge of a leftover, non-live key generation the checks listed (behind a presence prompt; the live and GNOMON_HOME generations are protected). Enforced by gnomon setup, bare gnomon, up --wrapper routing and the #setup-endpoint setup.begin / setup.complete.

subscription-only.name: Subscription Only
subscription-only.description: ^subscription-only (spec §10 law 7, D35): no kernel-spawned Claude process bills API credits — #budget-fuse refuses permit.reserve {session.spawn|turn, claude-code} BILLING_REFUSED on any API-billing path the law-7 scan finds; the only API path is the per-use root-signed api-token card of #approval-broker, injected into exactly one child, with the API CREDITS ACTIVE indicator and billing.api.active rows. M1.7 slice 1: #session-runner scans every layer the child reads per spawn cwd before any permit, #supervisor refuses claude without a law-7-scanned claude-code spawn permit and watches the layers mid-session (G-SUB-01, G-SUB-05).

api-authenticated.name: Api Authenticated

voice-armed.name: Voice Armed
voice-armed.description: Gnomon voice arm is live (spec §14.7, P8-D58–D62): voice intents may decide cards only inside an armed window (hard minutes, maxDecisions per arm class, headphones + handle + challenge). Reserved in M1.1; no route yet — enforced by #approval-broker in Move 4.

brain-default-deny.name: Brain Default Deny
brain-default-deny.description: Paradigm Brain default-deny. Every Brain read goes through the single #brain-view choke point (openBrainView). Files are private unless a human shares them; sensitive zones (medical, financial, third-party-data, quarantined) are never listed — the owner sees only {folder, gate, count}. Filtering happens BEFORE any matching, so search/health/suggestions never see hidden records. Brain routes additionally require a loopback Host on GET (DNS-rebinding guard for private metadata).

write-capable.name: Write Capable

local-only.name: Local Only

Enforced two ways — the socket binds loopback by default, AND the #local-guard request middleware rejects 403 any state-changing (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) /api request whose Host is non-loopback or whose (present) Origin is non-loopback (CSRF + DNS-rebinding guard). CORS reflects only loopback origins (never wildcard). GET/HEAD reads are not gated.

brain-owner-write.name: Brain Owner Write

POST /api/brain/verdict requires the per-process owner token in the HttpOnly SameSite=Strict `brain_owner` cookie (set by a same-origin GET /api/brain/overview, never in a response body) AND an Origin exactly equal to the Platform's own origin. Other localhost ports get no ACAO and a 403 on every /api/brain request.

PR-4 covers the label and read-projection halves; M1.12 slice 3 adds the honesty CI (§9.7: G-HON-02, 03, 05, 06, 07; test/honesty.test.ts) and the status-number declarations (src/kernel/socket/status-numbers.ts); retention/TTL pruning (§9.4) and the remaining §9.6 metrics follow.

read-only.name: Read Only
read-only.description: THE GIT-SAFETY INVARIANT (Phase-1 read-only; PRESERVED by the Phase-2 write path) — Warpline NEVER mutates the user's git HEAD/index/worktree. A ref is read by materializing its tree via `git archive` into a throwaway temp dir (no worktree, no .git/worktrees lock); the cold git<2.38 merge-tree fallback uses a detached worktree torn down in a finally. The ONLY disk Warpline writes is under .warpline/ — the content-addressed store, the oracle.jsonl ledger, AND the Phase-2 native history (#fabric: refs/selvage + fabric.jsonl + states/). The write path is a write to Warpline's OWN store, NOT to git: git is read for provenance (HEAD sha, user.name) only. Lifting a ref, or the WORKTREE pseudo-ref, only READS files — the code-lens included.

determinism.name: Determinism
determinism.description: THE THESIS — absorbing the same ref twice is byte-identical (stateId + every per-symbol contentId + repo-relative filePath), so diff(absorb(HEAD), absorb(HEAD)) is provably ZERO and two machines on the same source agree. No timestamps/paths/positions/prose/embeddings enter the hashed byte stream; every set is sorted+deduped; strict canonical JSON; sorted file enumeration; deterministic synthetic code-unit ids; the TS compiler is exact-pinned and stamped, WITH the CCNF algorithm version, into the code essence tag (essence:<algo>:ts<exact>, e.g. essence:v1.1:ts5.9.3) so a different compiler OR serialization algorithm is a different content-address namespace, never a silent collision.

meaning-coverage.name: Meaning Coverage
meaning-coverage.description: THE TD-806 HONESTY METRIC — Warpline reports WHERE it has meaning versus where it degrades to opaque bytes (the 3-tier fidelity model). A code-unit the TS lens cannot soundly lift (unresolved refs, unsupported forms) is flagged reducedFidelity — never silently empty; coverage is surfaced, not assumed. Honest about its own blind spots so the meaning layer's thickness is legible.

suite-gated.name: Suite Gated
suite-gated.description: THE CI GATE (panel item 0 / blocker B-1, 2026-07-31). Until this landed, packages/warpline/test/ — 83 files, 687 tests — RAN NOWHERE in CI: root `npm test` chained only to @a-company/paradigm, whose vitest config includes src/**, tests/** and platform-ui/src/sections/warpline/** and does not reach this package; the only warpline-touching workflow (warpline-guard.yml) is continue-on-error and runs the Guard ACTION, not vitest. Consequence: test/descriptors-frozen.test.ts — the FG-3 freeze tripwire — was wired to nothing, and every "green CI extension of PW-4" exit criterion was unsatisfiable. Now root `npm test` = `test:cli && test:warpline`, and ci.yml carries a dedicated BLOCKING `warpline` job (Node 20, NOT continue-on-error) that runs `npm run test:warpline`. TWO DELIBERATE PROPERTIES. (1) `test:warpline` BUILDS dist before running: four tests (f4-cli-arm, pick-agentid-env, two in stake-denylist-v2) are `it.skipIf(!existsSync(dist/cli.js))`, so an absent or STALE dist makes them evaporate silently while the run still reports green — building immediately before the run is what makes the CLI arm observable at all, and @a-company/warpline is now also in root `build:packages` (it was absent). This narrows but does NOT close D-12: the arm still cannot OBSERVE cross-image divergence, it merely no longer manufactures it. (2) The gate covers TEST EXECUTION ONLY, NOT TEST TYPECHECKING — tsconfig.json includes src/**/* alone, so test/ is never typechecked, and wiring it in comes up RED today (pre-existing errors in backup.test.ts, bind-on-seal.test.ts, code-diff.test.ts, knot-payload.test.ts, knot-rule.test.ts). Do not mistake one for the other.

completion-confirmation.name: Completion Confirmation
completion-confirmation.description: Agent spawner validates relay output before accepting success — builders must write files, all agents must produce artifacts/decisions/handoff. Failures downgrade to partial with logged message.

audit-log-yaml-per-orchestration.name: Audit Log Yaml Per Orchestration
audit-log-yaml-per-orchestration.description: Audit logs are stored as YAML files in .paradigm/orchestrations/ with date-prefixed filenames; each file contains full agent details, token counts, costs, and artifacts

background-accept-reject-workflow.name: Background Accept Reject Workflow
background-accept-reject-workflow.description: Background orchestrations follow a pending/running/completed/accepted/rejected lifecycle; only completed orchestrations can be accepted or rejected, rejection can optionally clean up created files

habits-loader.name: Habits Loader
habits-loader.description: Habits engine — 5-step merge loader (seeds → global yaml → global .habit → project yaml → project .habit), validation, and individual .habit file support

habits-types.name: Habits Types
habits-types.description: Habit type definitions — HabitDefinition, HabitCheck, HabitCategory, HabitTrigger, HabitSeverity, check type enums

stop-hook-8-compliance-checks.name: Stop Hook 8 Compliance Checks
stop-hook-8-compliance-checks.description:
Stop hook blocks agent completion unless 8 checks pass:
(1) source files modified without .purpose updates (threshold 2+),
(2) modified directories missing .purpose files entirely,
(3) route patterns added without portal.yaml,
(4) aspect anchor files that no longer exist,
(5) per-directory .purpose freshness via .pending-review,
(6) aspect coverage advisory,
(7) lore entry expected for 3+ source file sessions,
(8) blocking habits not satisfied

pre-tool-use-auto-reindex.name: Pre Tool Use Auto Reindex
pre-tool-use-auto-reindex.description: PreToolUse hook intercepts Bash calls matching git commit patterns and automatically runs paradigm reindex before the commit proceeds; never blocks the tool call

post-tool-use-advisory.name: Post Tool Use Advisory
post-tool-use-advisory.description: PostToolUse hook fires after Edit/Write tool calls and emits an advisory reminder when source files are edited without nearby .purpose coverage; advisory only, never blocks

human-gated-transfer.name: Human Gated Transfer
human-gated-transfer.description: File transfers always require explicit human approval (unless auto-approved in trust config)

hard-deny-list.name: Hard Deny List
hard-deny-list.description: Certain file patterns (.env, *.key, *.pem, credentials) are always blocked regardless of approval

adapter-section-ordering.name: Adapter Section Ordering
adapter-section-ordering.description: All IDE adapters emit sections in a shared order — header, overview, symbol system, terminal guidance, navigation, MCP tools, workflow protocol, session recovery, checkpoints, logging rules, conventions, commit convention, update rules, scan protocol, footer; sections are only included if the config has relevant data

provider-api-key-requirements.name: Provider Api Key Requirements
provider-api-key-requirements.description: Each provider has specific environment detection — claude requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, claude-code requires CLAUDE_CODE=1 or TERM_PROGRAM=claude, cursor-cli requires Cursor IDE environment, claude-cli checks claude command in PATH

manual-always-available-fallback.name: Manual Always Available Fallback
manual-always-available-fallback.description: Manual provider is always available (isAvailable returns true unconditionally) and creates file-based handoff tasks in .paradigm/handoffs/ and .paradigm/tasks/ for human execution

session-isolation.name: Session Isolation
session-isolation.description: Each ClaudeStreamSession is fully self-contained (own Process/Pipes/off-main LineFramer/SessionTranscript/@Published state); the FleetStore composes them and never introduces shared mutable session state. Background (non-active) sessions keep streaming into their own state because ingest is instance-bound.
